\paragraph{Direction of the continuation.}
Version~V4 completed the three diagonal leading stocks
\(A_1,A_2,A_3\).  They are retained verbatim and are not used to guess an
old/fine cross coefficient.  The remaining finite transport target is a
law-aligned mixed covariance.  Version~V4 asked for the signed outer
expectation, the two actual marginal normalizations, and the selected root.
The present continuation proves that this is more information than the
Schur-residual target itself requires.  For real source writers, one
nonnegative three-replica area writer and two nonnegative pair-difference
writers determine the complete normalized Schur residual exactly.  One
additional signed pair-difference writer is required only when the orientation
of the old/fine line, rather than its singular value or residual, is part of
the target.

The same calculation reveals an exact positive decomposition of the mixed
residual.  Its first summand is the already constructed two-link centre-fibre
innovation, and its second summand is the residual of the centre-orbit
conditional mean against the chosen old line.  This prevents the local
centre-fibre birth and the remaining outer misalignment from being charged
twice.  A new finite support audit shows that the native fan meets exactly
\(416\) plaquettes.  Since one \(\SU(3)\) Wilson plaquette action lies in
\([0,3/2]\), every bounded selected-root subsequence has a uniform absolute
native variance floor and hence a uniform absolute centre-fibre stock.  The
stock is carried by a gauge-invariant writer supported at physical
\(\ell^\infty\)-radius at most \(2a_N\).  Thus the bounded weak-facing branch
now returns a typed, non-gauge, contact-scale cutoff innovation rather than an
unresolved mixed row.

The attached selected-shell margin report is used only as an interface
constraint.  Its exact reduced-fibre gap is not inserted as a boundary
coefficient.  The centre-fibre writer can land on the rooted transverse
momentum--colour carrier only through an actually supplied same-law mode-score
map; the Ward calculation below shows that such a landing annihilates coarse
gauge directions.  The Wilson-specific signed symbol margin remains a
separate YM--A acquisition.

\section{The law-aligned native mixed card}
\label{sec:V5-mixed-card}

Retain the native real fan \(f_N\), the two-link order-three centre rotation
\(\tau\), the complete blocked-record sigma-algebra \(\mathscr B_N\), and the
\(\tau\)-invariant sigma-algebra \(\mathscr Q_N\) from Version~V3.  Thus
\(\mathscr B_N\subseteq\mathscr Q_N\), and on the actual finite Wilson law
\(\mu_{N,\beta}\),
\begin{equation}
 M_{N,\beta}
 :=\mathbb E_{\mu_{N,\beta}}[f_N\mid\mathscr Q_N]
 =\operatorname{Re}(b_\beta Z_N),
 \qquad
 \xi_{N,\beta}:=f_N-M_{N,\beta}.
 \label{eq:V5-centre-residual}
\end{equation}
The explicit local tilt \(b_\beta\), complex fan \(Z_N\), and ten charged
plaquettes are unchanged.  In particular, no new conditional law is fitted.

Let \(G\in L^2(\mu_{N,\beta};\R)\) be any nonconstant
\(\mathscr B_N\)-measurable old column after its actual law alignment.  This
includes a natural-law Radon--Nikodym lift whenever that lift is part of the
frozen physical incidence.  Put
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_F^2=\operatorname{Var}(f_N),\qquad
 \sigma_G^2=\operatorname{Var}(G),\qquad
 c_{FG}=\operatorname{Cov}(f_N,G),
 \label{eq:V5-covariances}
\end{equation}
and define the unnormalized covariance determinant and normalized fine-over-
old Schur residual by
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak D(f_N,G)
 :=\sigma_F^2\sigma_G^2-c_{FG}^2,
 \qquad
 \mathbb R(f_N\mid G)
 :=\frac{\mathfrak D(f_N,G)}{\sigma_F^2\sigma_G^2}.
 \label{eq:V5-Schur-def}
\end{equation}
Both variances are strictly positive on every admitted card.  Positivity of
\(\sigma_F^2\) was proved in Version~V3; positivity of \(\sigma_G^2\) is the
nonconstant-column domain condition and is checked rather than inferred from
a label.

\begin{theorem}[Exact centre-fibre/outer Schur decomposition]
\label{thm:V5-Schur-split}
For every law-aligned card above,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak D(f_N,G)
 ={}&\sigma_G^2\,\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2\\
 &+\Bigl(
   \operatorname{Var}(M_{N,\beta})\sigma_G^2
   -\operatorname{Cov}(M_{N,\beta},G)^2
  \Bigr).
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V5-Schur-split}
\end{equation}
The two terms on the right are nonnegative.  After normalization,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R(f_N\mid G)
 =\underbrace{\frac{\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2}{\sigma_F^2}}
              _{\mathbb R_{\rm cf}}
 +\underbrace{
   \frac{
   \operatorname{Var}(M_{N,\beta})\sigma_G^2
   -\operatorname{Cov}(M_{N,\beta},G)^2}
   {\sigma_F^2\sigma_G^2}}
              _{\mathbb R_{\rm out}}.}
 \label{eq:V5-normalized-Schur-split}
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathbb R_{\rm cf}\) is the centre-fibre source birth and
\(\mathbb R_{\rm out}\) is the remaining outer alignment residual.  No
signed cancellation between them is possible.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(F^\circ=f_N-\mathbb Ef_N\),
\(M^\circ=M_{N,\beta}-\mathbb Ef_N\), and \(G^\circ=G-\mathbb EG\).
Conditional expectation preserves the mean, so
\(F^\circ=M^\circ+\xi_{N,\beta}\).  By construction,
\(\xi_{N,\beta}\) is orthogonal to all
\(\mathscr Q_N\)-measurable functions.  In particular it is orthogonal to
\(M^\circ\), to \(G^\circ\), and to the constants.  Hence
\[
 \sigma_F^2=\|M^\circ\|_2^2+\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 c_{FG}=\langle M^\circ,G^\circ\rangle.
\]
Substitution in \eqref{eq:V5-Schur-def} gives
\eqref{eq:V5-Schur-split}.  The second summand is the determinant of the
\(2\times2\) covariance Gram of \((M_{N,\beta},G)\), hence is nonnegative.
Division by the positive diagonal variances gives
\eqref{eq:V5-normalized-Schur-split}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Native and dilated columns occupy different summands]
\label{cor:V5-native-dilated}
For the native fine fan, Version~V3 gives
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{\rm cf}
 =\frac{\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2}{\sigma_F^2}
 \ge d(\beta)
 :=\frac{9}{5+4\cosh(15\beta)}>0.}
 \label{eq:V5-native-relative-floor}
\end{equation}
For a literally dilated old fan
\(f_N^{\rm dil}=f_{N/2}\circ B_{N\to N/2}\), one instead has
\(\xi^{\rm dil}=0\).  If its old normalization is taken in the induced
coarse law, then also \(\mathbb R_{\rm out}=0\), so the complete residual is
zero.  Thus the native positive residual cannot be transferred to a dilated
column by matching its fan label, leading Haar norm, or diagonal stock.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is the exact Version~V3 centre-orbit variance theorem,
inserted into the first summand of
\eqref{eq:V5-normalized-Schur-split}.  A dilated writer is measurable with
respect to \(\mathscr B_N\subseteq\mathscr Q_N\), so its centre-fibre
residual vanishes.  Under the induced-law normalization, the dilated fine
writer and the old pullback are the same centered normalized vector; their
outer covariance Gram has rank one and zero determinant.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[No-double-charging consequence]
\label{ass:V5-no-double-charge}
The local conditional writer \(M_{N,\beta}=\operatorname{Re}(b_\beta Z_N)\)
does not replace the native source by a second source.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V5-normalized-Schur-split} is an orthogonal Pythagoras: first retain
the source born inside the centre fibre, then test only the remaining
conditional mean against the old line.  Adding a separately computed
``native residual'' and a full old/fine Schur residual would count the first
summand twice.
\end{assessment}

\section{A target-minimal positive three-replica Read}
\label{sec:V5-replica}

Let \((F_i,G_i)\), \(i=1,2,3\), be three independent copies of the same
law-aligned pair \((f_N,G)\).  These are product preparations of one frozen
common-cylinder law, not three unrelated marginal tables.  Define the
nonnegative pair-difference writers
\begin{equation}
 A_F:=\mathbb E(F_1-F_2)^2,
 \qquad
 A_G:=\mathbb E(G_1-G_2)^2,
 \label{eq:V5-pair-reads}
\end{equation}
and the oriented three-point area
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{123}
 :=(F_1-F_3)(G_2-G_3)-(F_2-F_3)(G_1-G_3).
 \label{eq:V5-area}
\end{equation}
Its square gives the positive Read
\begin{equation}
 C_\triangle:=\mathbb E\Delta_{123}^2\ge0.
 \label{eq:V5-area-read}
\end{equation}
For optional orientation recovery, define the signed two-copy Read
\begin{equation}
 D_\times:=\mathbb E[(F_1-F_2)(G_1-G_2)].
 \label{eq:V5-signed-read}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact replica determinant identities]
\label{thm:V5-replica-identities}
For every real square-integrable pair \((F,G)\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_F=2\operatorname{Var}(F),\qquad
 A_G=2\operatorname{Var}(G),\qquad
 D_\times=2\operatorname{Cov}(F,G),}
 \label{eq:V5-two-replica-identities}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 C_\triangle
 =6\Bigl(
   \operatorname{Var}(F)\operatorname{Var}(G)
   -\operatorname{Cov}(F,G)^2
  \Bigr).}
 \label{eq:V5-three-replica-identity}
\end{equation}
Consequently, whenever \(A_F,A_G>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R(F\mid G)
 =\frac{2C_\triangle}{3A_FA_G},
 \qquad
 \alpha(F,G)
 =\frac{D_\times}{\sqrt{A_FA_G}},}
 \label{eq:V5-replica-Schur-alpha}
\end{equation}
where \(\alpha\) is the signed normalized covariance.  The four readings
obey the exact held-out identity
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_\times^2+\frac23C_\triangle=A_FA_G.}
 \label{eq:V5-heldout-identity}
\end{equation}
Thus \(A_F,A_G,C_\triangle\) determine the singular value magnitude and the
complete Schur residual without either marginal mean and without a signed
mixed expectation.  The single extra Read \(D_\times\) determines the
orientation and supplies an independent consistency check.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All four writers are unchanged if constants are subtracted from \(F\) and
\(G\), so assume both are centered.  The two-copy identities follow by
expansion and independence.  Put
\[
 D_{ij}=F_iG_j-G_iF_j.
\]
Then
\(\Delta_{123}=D_{12}-D_{13}+D_{23}\).  For \(i\ne j\), independence gives
\[
 \mathbb ED_{ij}^2
 =2\bigl(\mathbb EF^2\mathbb EG^2-(\mathbb EFG)^2\bigr).
\]
Every cross term between two different \(D_{ij}\)'s has expectation zero.
For example, conditional on the shared first copy, \(D_{12}\) and
\(D_{13}\) are independent and have conditional mean zero; the other two
cases are identical.  Hence the expectation of \(\Delta_{123}^2\) is three
times the displayed value, proving
\eqref{eq:V5-three-replica-identity}.  Substitution of
\eqref{eq:V5-two-replica-identities} gives
\eqref{eq:V5-replica-Schur-alpha}, and adding the covariance square to the
determinant gives \eqref{eq:V5-heldout-identity}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Replica decomposition of the centre-fibre stock]
\label{cor:V5-replica-split}
For the native fine fan and every old-record column \(G\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 C_\triangle
 ={}&6\sigma_G^2\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2\\
 &+6\Bigl(
   \operatorname{Var}(M_{N,\beta})\sigma_G^2
   -\operatorname{Cov}(M_{N,\beta},G)^2
  \Bigr).
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V5-replica-centre-split}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{C_\triangle\ge6\sigma_G^2\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2.}
 \label{eq:V5-area-centre-floor}
\end{equation}
The positive three-replica area therefore sees the centre-fibre source stock
without requiring its phase or an arbitrary source basis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Multiply \eqref{eq:V5-Schur-split} by six and use
\eqref{eq:V5-three-replica-identity}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Outward interval compiler for the positive replica card]
\label{thm:V5-replica-interval}
Suppose certified rational intervals satisfy
\begin{equation}
 0<a_-\le A_F\le a_+,
 \qquad
 0<b_-\le A_G\le b_+,
 \qquad
 0\le c_-\le C_\triangle\le c_+.
 \label{eq:V5-moment-intervals}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \max\left\{0,\frac{2c_-}{3a_+b_+}\right\}
 \le\mathbb R(F\mid G)\le
 \min\left\{1,\frac{2c_+}{3a_-b_-}\right\}.}
 \label{eq:V5-residual-interval}
\end{equation}
The corresponding squared-overlap interval is obtained by subtracting the
endpoints from one.  If an interval for \(D_\times\) is also supplied, its
sign orients the line, while interval inconsistency with
\eqref{eq:V5-heldout-identity} rejects the card as ill typed rather than
returning a physical obstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The rational function \(2C_\triangle/(3A_FA_G)\) is increasing in its
nonnegative numerator and decreasing in its two positive denominators.
This proves the outward endpoints.  A covariance Gram is positive, so the
exact residual lies in \([0,1]\), which gives the truncations.  The final
statement follows because \eqref{eq:V5-heldout-identity} is an exact identity
for every common product law.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[What the replica replacement does and does not remove]
\label{fire:V5-replica-scope}
The positive area Read is target minimal for the Schur residual and singular
value magnitude.  It does not determine the oriented old/fine transport
without \(D_\times\), and it does not prove that three purported replica
marginals arise from one independently repeated physical cylinder.  Product
preparation or an equivalent three-copy glued query remains an occurrence
row.  Conversely, marginal means are not charged merely to decide the
centered covariance determinant.
\end{firewall}

\section{A uniform absolute native stock at bounded coupling}
\label{sec:V5-absolute-stock}

The Version~V3 residual lower bound is relative to the actual native variance.
To decide whether a bounded-root sequence can hide the residual by collapsing
the entire source norm, one further local estimate is required.

\begin{lemma}[Exact range of one \(\SU(3)\) Wilson plaquette action]
\label{lem:V5-SU3-range}
For every \(U\in\SU(3)\),
\begin{equation}
 -\frac32\le\operatorname{Re}\Tr U\le3.
 \label{eq:V5-trace-range}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 0\le1-\frac13\operatorname{Re}\Tr U\le\frac32.
 \label{eq:V5-action-range}
\end{equation}
Both endpoints are attained, at the identity and at either nontrivial centre
element respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write the eigenvalues as
\(e^{ix},e^{iy},e^{-i(x+y)}\).  The real trace is the smooth function
\[
 h(x,y)=\cos x+\cos y+\cos(x+y)
\]
on the compact two-torus.  At a critical point,
\(\sin x=\sin y=-\sin(x+y)\).  If \(x\equiv y\), then
\(\sin x(1+2\cos x)=0\), giving values \(3,-1,-3/2\).  If
\(x\equiv\pi-y\), the critical equations give only values at least \(-1\).
Thus the minimum is \(-3/2\) and the maximum is \(3\).  The nontrivial centre
has all three eigenvalues equal to \(e^{\pm2\pi i/3}\), so it attains the
minimum.  Equation \eqref{eq:V5-action-range} follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Exact native support and incident-face count]
\label{prop:V5-support-count}
Let \(S_F\) be the positive-edge support of the exact factored native fan of
Version~V3.  Let \(\mathcal P(S_F)\) be the set of plaquettes containing at
least one edge of \(S_F\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{|S_F|=100,\qquad|\mathcal P(S_F)|=416.}
 \label{eq:V5-support-count}
\end{equation}
The union of \(S_F\) with the boundaries of the ten charged plaquettes has
exactly \(120\) links and bounding box
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{[-2,2]\times[-2,2]\times[-1,1]\times[-1,1]}
 \label{eq:V5-reader-box}
\end{equation}
in coordinates relative to the even centre.  Hence the local conditional
writer \(M_{N,\beta}\), the residual \(\xi_{N,\beta}\), and all pointwise
centre-orbit quantities have physical \(\ell^\infty\)-radius at most
\(2a_N\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Insert the forty explicitly displayed three-edge staple paths and the four
two-edge corner paths from Version~V3, canonicalize every unoriented positive
edge, and take their finite union.  For each resulting edge \((x,\mu)\), add
the six canonically oriented plaquettes with bases \(x\) and
\(x-e_\nu\), \(\nu\ne\mu\), and take the union again.  Exact integer set
reduction gives \(100\) edges and \(416\) plaquettes.  Adding the edge
boundaries of the ten already certified charged plaquettes gives \(120\)
edges and does not enlarge the displayed bounding box.  This finite
calculation is replayed independently by the Version~V5 certificate; it uses
no floating arithmetic and does not enumerate the \(5^8\) fan loops.
Multiplication by the lattice spacing gives the physical-radius statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform local density comparison]
\label{lem:V5-local-density}
Let \(S\) be a finite link set in a finite Wilson lattice, and let
\(n_S\) be the number of plaquettes meeting \(S\).  Conditional on every link
outside \(S\), the density \(q_{S,\beta}\) of the links in \(S\) relative to
product Haar obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 e^{-\frac32n_S\beta}
 \le q_{S,\beta}\le
 e^{\frac32n_S\beta}.}
 \label{eq:V5-local-density-bound}
\end{equation}
Therefore every real \(H\in L^2\) depending only on \(S\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mu_{N,\beta}}(H)
 \ge e^{-\frac32n_S\beta}
       \operatorname{Var}_{m_S}(H),}
 \label{eq:V5-local-variance-comparison}
\end{equation}
where \(m_S\) is product Haar on the selected links.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
After the exterior links are fixed, only the \(n_S\) incident plaquette terms
vary.  By \Cref{lem:V5-SU3-range}, their sum has oscillation at most
\(3n_S/2\).  If its minimum and maximum are \(a\le b\), the normalized
conditional density is
\(e^{-\beta A_S}/\int e^{-\beta A_S}\,\dd m_S\).  Its numerator is at least
\(e^{-\beta b}\), while the denominator is at most \(e^{-\beta a}\); this
gives the lower bound.  Interchanging the two extrema gives the upper bound.
For each fixed exterior configuration,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{q_{S,\beta}m_S}(H)
 =\inf_{c\in\R}\int(H-c)^2q_{S,\beta}\,\dd m_S
 \ge e^{-\frac32n_S\beta}\operatorname{Var}_{m_S}(H).
\]
The total-variance identity and averaging over the exterior give
\eqref{eq:V5-local-variance-comparison}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute centre-fibre stock and local old-orthogonal witness]
\label{thm:V5-absolute-contact-stock}
For the native fan at every finite \(\beta\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sigma_F^2\ge e^{-624\beta},
 \qquad
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 \ge\eta(\beta)
 :=e^{-624\beta}\frac9{5+4\cosh(15\beta)}.}
 \label{eq:V5-absolute-stock}
\end{equation}
Moreover \(\xi_{N,\beta}\) is centered, gauge invariant, supported at
physical radius at most \(2a_N\), and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\xi_{N,\beta},H\rangle=0
 \quad\text{for every }H\in L^2(\mathscr B_N).}
 \label{eq:V5-old-orthogonality}
\end{equation}
Thus
\(\xi_{N,\beta}/\|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2\) is an explicit local normalized
physical old-orthogonal source witness, not merely a lower bound on an
unidentified Schur complement.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use \Cref{prop:V5-support-count,lem:V5-local-density} with
\(S=S_F\) and \(n_S=416\).  The imported product-Haar identities are
\(m_S(f_N)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_{m_S}(f_N)=1\), hence
\(\sigma_F^2\ge e^{-(3/2)416\beta}=e^{-624\beta}\).
Version~V3 gives
\[
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 \ge d(\beta)\,\mathbb E f_N^2
 \ge d(\beta)\sigma_F^2,
\]
which proves the second bound.  Conditional expectation makes \(\xi\)
centered and orthogonal to \(L^2(\mathscr Q_N)\), hence to the old record.
Gauge invariance follows because \(f_N\), all ten plaquette traces, their
Wilson weights, and \(M_{N,\beta}=\operatorname{Re}(b_\beta Z_N)\) are gauge
invariant.  The support statement is \Cref{prop:V5-support-count}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Positive replica signal at bounded coupling]
\label{cor:V5-area-signal}
If \(0\le\beta\le B<\infty\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R(f_N\mid G)\ge d(B),
 \qquad
 C_\triangle\ge6\sigma_G^2\eta(B).}
 \label{eq:V5-bounded-area-signal}
\end{equation}
In particular, for an actual-law unit-variance old column,
\(C_\triangle\ge6\eta(B)>0\).  For centered unit-variance versions of both
columns, \(C_\triangle=6\mathbb R\ge6d(B)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The function \(d\) and the exponential factor in \(\eta\) decrease on
\([0,\infty)\).  Apply
\Cref{cor:V5-native-dilated,cor:V5-replica-split,thm:V5-absolute-contact-stock}.
\end{proof}

\section{Selected weak-facing roots: escape or a contact-scale cutoff birth}
\label{sec:V5-selected-roots}

\begin{importedresult}[Weak-facing response selector]
\label{imp:V5-weak-facing}
The attached dedicated renormalized Yang--Mills programme fixes, before any
boundary or symbol datum is inspected, the weak-facing root
\(\beta_{M_r}^{\rm wf}\) as the last stable down-crossing of the same four-loop
response at the frozen value \(u_*\).  It proves that this is a canonical
response-only selector at every dyadic cutoff \(M_r=2^rM\).  It also proves
that any failure of \(\beta_{M_r}^{\rm wf}\to\infty\) has a cofinal bounded
subsequence.  No root is retuned here.
\end{importedresult}

Put
\begin{equation}
 \beta_r:=\beta_{M_r}^{\rm wf},
 \qquad
 a_r:=\frac{L}{M_r},
 \qquad
 F_r:=f_{M_r},
 \qquad
 \xi_r:=\xi_{M_r,\beta_r}.
 \label{eq:V5-selected-native-sequence}
\end{equation}
Use the native fine column and the actual dyadic old record on each card.

\begin{theorem}[Selected-root native alternative]
\label{thm:V5-selected-alternative}
Exactly one of the following branches holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item \textbf{Escaping weak-facing branch:}
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{\beta_r\longrightarrow\infty.}
       \label{eq:V5-root-escape}
      \end{equation}
      The local lower bounds \(d(\beta_r)\) and \(\eta(\beta_r)\) then tend
      to zero and do not decide the selected-root mixed card.  Its first
      target-minimal acquisition is the positive replica packet
      \((A_{F,r},A_{G,r},C_{\triangle,r})\), together with
      \(D_{\times,r}\) only if oriented transport is required.
\item \textbf{Bounded-root contact-birth branch:} there are
      \(r_j\to\infty\) and \(B<\infty\) such that \(\beta_{r_j}\le B\).
      On this actual selected-root subsequence,
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \begin{gathered}
       \|\xi_{r_j}\|_2^2\ge\eta(B)>0,
       \qquad
       \supp\xi_{r_j}\subseteq
       B_{\ell^\infty}(c_{r_j},2a_{r_j}),\\
       \xi_{r_j}\perp L^2(\mathscr B_{M_{r_j}}),
       \qquad
       \mathbb R(F_{r_j}\mid G_{r_j})\ge d(B)>0
       \end{gathered}}
       \label{eq:V5-contact-birth-packet}
      \end{equation}
      for every admitted nonconstant old-record column \(G_{r_j}\).  Hence
      the native source has a uniformly noncollapsed, gauge-invariant,
      contact-scale cutoff innovation and cannot be an exact transported old
      line on that subsequence.
\end{enumerate}
The second branch is a typed obstruction to perfect native old/fine
attachment.  It is not a positive-physical-range source: its radius tends to
zero.  It is also not the earlier radial-message condition
\(q_{N,R}^{\square}\to1\), which remains a separate shell-direction query.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every positive real sequence either tends to infinity or has a bounded
subsequence; apply this to the already selected \(\beta_r\).  On the bounded
subsequence, \Cref{thm:V5-absolute-contact-stock} gives the absolute stock,
support and old-record orthogonality, and
\Cref{cor:V5-native-dilated} gives the normalized Schur floor.  Since

\section{The only gauge-compatible mode-card landing}
\label{sec:V5-mode-landing}

The selected-shell margin report works on a reduced-fibre mode score
\(s_h\) and the signed Hessian card
\(\mathbb E K-\operatorname{Cov}(s)\).  A boundary residual does not enter
that card by itself.  The following statement identifies the exact first
possible landing if the common score experiment is supplied.

\begin{theorem}[Ward-compatible landing of the contact covariance]
\label{thm:V5-Ward-landing}
Let \(\nu\propto e^{-\mathcal S}\,\dd m\) be one finite reduced-fibre Wilson
law on which the contact writer \(\xi\) and the actual centered coarse mode
scores \(s_h\) are jointly defined.  Suppose the score of a coarse gauge
direction \(h_\zeta=d_0^{\rm c}\zeta\) has the exact gauge-orbit form
\begin{equation}
 s_{h_\zeta}=\dd\mathcal S(X_\zeta),
 \label{eq:V5-gauge-score}
\end{equation}
where \(X_\zeta\) is the divergence-free infinitesimal residual gauge action.
If \(\xi\) is gauge invariant, then the contact response functional
\begin{equation}
 \ell_\xi(h):=\langle\xi,s_h\rangle_{L^2(\nu)}
 \label{eq:V5-contact-functional}
\end{equation}
obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\ell_\xi(d_0^{\rm c}\zeta)=0.}
 \label{eq:V5-contact-Ward}
\end{equation}
Consequently the positive rank-one form
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb C_\xi(h,k)
 :=\frac{\overline{\ell_\xi(h)}\ell_\xi(k)}{\|\xi\|_2^2}
 \label{eq:V5-contact-form}
\end{equation}
has the coarse gauge subspace in its kernel and descends to the rooted
transverse momentum--colour quotient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Gauge invariance gives \(X_\zeta\xi=0\).  Since the gauge action preserves
product Haar, \(X_\zeta\) is divergence free.  Weighted integration by parts
gives, for every smooth \(H\),
\[
 \int H\,\dd\mathcal S(X_\zeta)e^{-\mathcal S}\,\dd m
 =\int X_\zeta H\,e^{-\mathcal S}\,\dd m.
\]
Take \(H=\xi\) and use \eqref{eq:V5-gauge-score}; the right side vanishes.
The rank-one form therefore annihilates every gauge direction in either
slot and factors through the quotient.
\end{proof}

scores are physically supplied.  Neither the three diagonal boundary stocks,
the positive replica residual, nor the exact flat reduced-fibre gap
\(\lambda_*\) constructs \(\ell_\xi\).  Even after
\(\mathbb C_\xi\) is acquired, it is one source-visible covariance form, not
the complete signed symbol
\(\widehat H=\mathbb E K-\operatorname{Cov}(j)\).  The YM--A small-field and
large-field residual rows and their \(|p|^2\)-Schur normalization remain

\end{firewall}

\section{A certified local action gap from microscopic plaquette flatness}
\label{sec:V6-local-gap}
% =============================================================================

Retain the Version~V3 centre element $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}$, the order-three
rotation $\tau$, the ten charged plaquettes $\mathscr D$, their nonzero
charges $q_p\in\{1,2\}$, and
\begin{equation}
 d(V):=1-\frac13\operatorname{Re}\Tr V.
 \label{eq:V6-defect}
\end{equation}
For one fine configuration put
\begin{equation}
 S_j(U):=\sum_{p\in\mathscr D}d(\zeta^{jq_p}U_p),
 \qquad 0\le j\le2.
 \label{eq:V6-local-actions}
\end{equation}
Thus the three centre-orbit weights are proportional to
$e^{-\beta S_j(U)}$.  The unrotated local defect is $S_0$.

\begin{lemma}[One-plaquette centre-rotation inequality]
\label{lem:V6-centre-defect}
For every $V\in\SU(3)$ and $q\in\{1,2\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d(\zeta^qV)
 \ge
 \frac32-\frac12d(V)-\sqrt{\frac32d(V)}.}
 \label{eq:V6-centre-defect-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Put $z=\Tr(V)/3=x+\mathrm i y$.  Since $V$ is unitary,
$|z|\le1$, while $x=1-d(V)$.  For either nontrivial centre power,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}(\zeta^qz)
 =-\frac12x\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}y.
\]
Therefore
\[
 d(\zeta^qV)
 \ge1+\frac12x-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}|y|
 =\frac32-\frac12d(V)-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}|y|.
\]
Finally,
\[
 |y|^2\le1-x^2
 =1-(1-d(V))^2
 =2d(V)-d(V)^2\le2d(V),
\]
which gives \eqref{eq:V6-centre-defect-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Ten-plaquette centre-orbit energy separation]
\label{lem:V6-orbit-gap}
For $0<\varepsilon$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, the implication
\begin{equation}
 S_0(U)\le\varepsilon
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 S_j(U)-S_0(U)\ge\Delta(\varepsilon)
 \label{eq:V6-gap-implication}
\end{equation}
holds with
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta(\varepsilon)
 :=15-\frac32\varepsilon-\sqrt{15\varepsilon}.}
 \label{eq:V6-gap-function}
\end{equation}
In particular, at the fixed threshold $\varepsilon=1$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \delta_*:=\Delta(1)=\frac{27}{2}-\sqrt{15}>0.}
 \label{eq:V6-delta-star}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{lem:V6-centre-defect} to every charged plaquette.  Since there are
exactly ten of them,
\[
 S_j
 \ge15-\frac12S_0
       -\sqrt{\frac32}\sum_{p\in\mathscr D}\sqrt{d(U_p)}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \sum_{p\in\mathscr D}\sqrt{d(U_p)}
 \le\sqrt{10S_0}.
\]
Subtracting $S_0$ proves
\[
 S_j-S_0\ge15-\frac32S_0-\sqrt{15S_0}.
\]
The right side decreases with $S_0>0$, giving
\eqref{eq:V6-gap-implication}.  Equation \eqref{eq:V6-delta-star} is the
special case $\varepsilon=1$; positivity follows from
$27/2>\sqrt{15}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why the direction of the estimate matters]
\label{rem:V6-gap-direction}
Version~V3 used the global orbit oscillation to obtain a finite-$\beta$
\emph{lower} bound on conditional variance.  The present estimate uses
microscopic plaquette flatness to show that the actually sampled orbit
representative has much lower local action than its two nontrivial centre
rotates.  It therefore gives an \emph{upper} bound on the same conditional
variance at large $\beta$.  The two inequalities apply on complementary
trajectory regimes and do not contradict one another.
\end{remark}

\section{Ultraviolet extinction of the absolute centre-fibre source}
\label{sec:V6-extinction}
% =============================================================================

The complex fan satisfies
\begin{equation}
 Z_N(U)=\frac{\sqrt{18}}{3\,5^4}
       \sum_{\eta\in\mathcal N^8}\Tr U_{\Gamma_\eta},
 \qquad f_N=\operatorname{Re}Z_N.
 \label{eq:V6-fan-recall}
\end{equation}
Since there are $5^8$ summands and $|\Tr V|\le3$ on $\SU(3)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |f_N|\le K_{\rm fan}:=\sqrt{18}\,5^4,
 \qquad K_{\rm fan}^2=18\,5^8=7031250.}
 \label{eq:V6-fan-sup}
\end{equation}
For a periodic card define the average charged-plaquette defect
\begin{equation}
 \bar p_{N,\mathscr D}(\beta)
 :=\frac1{10}\sum_{p\in\mathscr D}
   \mathbb E_{\mu_{N,\beta}}d(U_p).
 \label{eq:V6-charged-mean}
\end{equation}
By translation and hypercubic symmetry it equals the elementary plaquette
mean $p_N(\beta)$ used in the imported trajectory theorem.

\begin{lemma}[Orbitwise conditional-variance upper bound]
\label{lem:V6-orbit-variance-upper}
Let
\begin{equation}
 v_j(U)=\operatorname{Re}(\zeta^jZ_N(U)),
 \qquad
 w_j(U)=\frac{e^{-\beta S_j(U)}}{\sum_{k=0}^2e^{-\beta S_k(U)}},
 \label{eq:V6-values-weights}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 V_{\rm orb}(U)
 :=\sum_{j=0}^2w_j(U)
   \left(v_j(U)-\sum_{k=0}^2w_k(U)v_k(U)\right)^2.
 \label{eq:V6-orbit-variance}
\end{equation}
For every threshold $\varepsilon>0$ with $\Delta(\varepsilon)>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 S_0\le\varepsilon
 &\Longrightarrow
 V_{\rm orb}\le8K_{\rm fan}^2e^{-\beta\Delta(\varepsilon)},\\
 S_0>\varepsilon
 &\Longrightarrow
 V_{\rm orb}\le K_{\rm fan}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V6-orbit-variance-two-regime}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On $\{S_0\le\varepsilon\}$,
\Cref{lem:V6-orbit-gap} gives, for $j=1,2$,
\[
 \frac{w_j}{w_0}=e^{-\beta(S_j-S_0)}
 \le e^{-\beta\Delta(\varepsilon)}.
\]
Hence $w_1+w_2\le2e^{-\beta\Delta(\varepsilon)}$.  Conditional variance is
the minimum weighted squared distance to a constant, so using the candidate
constant $v_0$ and \eqref{eq:V6-fan-sup},
\[
 V_{\rm orb}
 \le\sum_jw_j(v_j-v_0)^2
 \le4K_{\rm fan}^2(w_1+w_2)
 \le8K_{\rm fan}^2e^{-\beta\Delta(\varepsilon)}.
\]
On the complementary event,
$V_{\rm orb}\le\sum_jw_jv_j^2\le K_{\rm fan}^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-card upper bound for the centre-fibre stock]
\label{thm:V6-centre-stock-upper}
For every declared nonwrapping periodic native-fan Wilson card and every
$\beta\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 \le K_{\rm fan}^2
 \inf_{\substack{\varepsilon>0\\\Delta(\varepsilon)>0}}
 \left\{
  \frac{10\bar p_{N,\mathscr D}(\beta)}{\varepsilon}
  +8e^{-\beta\Delta(\varepsilon)}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V6-centre-stock-optimized}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 \le18\,5^8
 \left(
  10p_N(\beta)+8e^{-\delta_*\beta}
 \right),
 \qquad
 \delta_*=\frac{27}{2}-\sqrt{15}.}
 \label{eq:V6-centre-stock-explicit}
\end{equation}
The estimate is independent of the number of links and plaquettes outside the
fixed centre-orbit reader.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Version~V3 orbit conditional-expectation formula gives
\begin{equation}
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 =\mathbb E_{\mu_{N,\beta}}V_{\rm orb}(U).
 \label{eq:V6-xi-orbit-identity}
\end{equation}
Split this expectation according to $S_0\le\varepsilon$.  By
\Cref{lem:V6-orbit-variance-upper},
\[
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 \le K_{\rm fan}^2\Pr(S_0>\varepsilon)
     +8K_{\rm fan}^2e^{-\beta\Delta(\varepsilon)}.
\]
Markov's inequality and \eqref{eq:V6-charged-mean} give
\[
 \Pr(S_0>\varepsilon)
 \le\frac{\mathbb ES_0}{\varepsilon}
 =\frac{10\bar p_{N,\mathscr D}(\beta)}{\varepsilon}.
\]
Taking the infimum proves \eqref{eq:V6-centre-stock-optimized}.  On a
periodic card, set $\varepsilon=1$ and use
$\bar p_{N,\mathscr D}=p_N$ and
\Cref{lem:V6-orbit-gap} to obtain
\eqref{eq:V6-centre-stock-explicit}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform extinction on every escaping weak-facing sequence]
\label{cor:V6-centre-extinction}
There is a deterministic function
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak e_{\rm cf}(\beta)
 :=18\,5^8\left(
  10C_{\rm pl}\frac{1+\log\beta}{\beta}
  +8e^{-\delta_*\beta}
 \right)
 \label{eq:V6-extinction-rate}
\end{equation}
defined for $\beta\ge\beta_{\rm pl}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{N:\,\text{native stencil nonwrapping}}
 \|\xi_{N,\beta}\|_2^2
 \le\mathfrak e_{\rm cf}(\beta)
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad(\beta\to\infty).}
 \label{eq:V6-uniform-extinction}
\end{equation}
Consequently, if the frozen weak-facing roots escape,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta_r=\beta_{M_r}^{\rm wf}\longrightarrow\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|\xi_r\|_2\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V6-selected-extinction}
\end{equation}
Thus the V5 centre-fibre source is an absolute source only on the bounded-root
branch.  It is not a noncollapsed ultraviolet source on an escaping branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Insert the volume-uniform plaquette estimate
\eqref{eq:V6-imported-plaquette} into
\eqref{eq:V6-centre-stock-explicit}.  Both terms in
\eqref{eq:V6-extinction-rate} tend to zero.  The selected-root statement is
obtained by substituting $N=M_r$ and $\beta=\beta_r$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Absolute extinction does not by itself determine a normalized
angle]
\label{fire:V6-absolute-not-relative}
The conclusion $\|\xi_r\|_2\to0$ does not imply
$\mathbb R_{{\rm cf},r}\to0$ unless the native variance has a positive lower
bound.  The denominator $\operatorname{Var}(f_{M_r})$ may vanish on the same
sequence.  Such a vanishing denominator is a source-visibility failure and
must not be hidden by whitening.  The next section keeps both the absolute
centre stock and the total native stock in the card.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The exact outer replica card after centre-fibre shorting}
\label{sec:V6-outer-card}
% =============================================================================

Retain one actual-law old-record writer $G$ and write
\begin{equation}
 F=f_N=M+\xi,
 \qquad
 M=\mathbb E[F\mid\mathscr Q_N],
 \qquad
 \xi=F-M.
 \label{eq:V6-F-M-xi}
\end{equation}
Thus $\xi$ is centered and orthogonal to both $M$ and $G$.  On three
independent replicas define
\begin{align}
 A_M&:=\mathbb E(M_1-M_2)^2,
 &A_\xi&:=\mathbb E(\xi_1-\xi_2)^2,
 \label{eq:V6-separated-pair-reads}\\
 A_G&:=\mathbb E(G_1-G_2)^2,
 \label{eq:V6-separated-old-read}\\
 \Delta^{\rm out}_{123}
 &:= (M_1-M_3)(G_2-G_3)
     -(M_2-M_3)(G_1-G_3),
 \label{eq:V6-outer-area}\\
 C_{\rm out}&:=\mathbb E(\Delta^{\rm out}_{123})^2,
 &D_{\rm out}&:=\mathbb E[(M_1-M_2)(G_1-G_2)].
 \label{eq:V6-outer-reads}
\end{align}
All these writers are pointwise executable from the same $120$-link local
centre-orbit reader and the frozen old column.  The conditional writer $M$
is a projection of the occurring source, not a second source occurrence.

\begin{theorem}[Separated positive replica identities]
\label{thm:V6-separated-replica}
Let $A_F,C_\triangle,D_\times$ be the Version~V5 readings for $(F,G)$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_F=A_M+A_\xi,
 \qquad
 A_\xi=2\|\xi\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_\times=D_{\rm out},}
 \label{eq:V6-separated-two-copy}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 C_\triangle
 =C_{\rm out}+\frac32A_GA_\xi.}
 \label{eq:V6-separated-area}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm out}^2+\frac23C_{\rm out}=A_MA_G,}
 \label{eq:V6-outer-heldout}
\end{equation}
and, whenever $A_F,A_G>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R(F\mid G)
 =\frac{A_\xi}{A_M+A_\xi}
  +\frac{2C_{\rm out}}
         {3(A_M+A_\xi)A_G}.}
 \label{eq:V6-full-from-separated}
\end{equation}
If $A_M>0$, put
\begin{equation}
 t_{\rm cf}:=\frac{A_\xi}{A_F}
 =\frac{\|\xi\|_2^2}{\operatorname{Var}(F)}.
 \label{eq:V6-centre-fraction}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R(F\mid G)
 =t_{\rm cf}+(1-t_{\rm cf})\mathbb R(M\mid G).}
 \label{eq:V6-convex-residual}
\end{equation}
Thus the centre and outer positive defects form a convex, not additive,
normalized ledger after the common fine variance is imposed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The orthogonal decomposition $F^\circ=M^\circ+\xi$ gives
$\operatorname{Var}(F)=\operatorname{Var}(M)+\|\xi\|_2^2$ and
$\operatorname{Cov}(F,G)=\operatorname{Cov}(M,G)$.  The two-copy identities
of Version~V5 therefore give
\eqref{eq:V6-separated-two-copy}.  Multiplying the exact covariance-
determinant decomposition \eqref{eq:V5-Schur-split} by six gives
\[
 C_\triangle-C_{\rm out}
 =6\operatorname{Var}(G)\|\xi\|_2^2
 =\frac32A_GA_\xi,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V6-separated-area}.  Applying the Version~V5 held-out
identity directly to the pair $(M,G)$ gives
\eqref{eq:V6-outer-heldout}.  Finally substitute
$A_F=A_M+A_\xi$ in the exact Version~V5 residual formula.  Rewriting its
outer term as
$(A_M/A_F)\mathbb R(M\mid G)$ gives
\eqref{eq:V6-convex-residual}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized native line converges to its centre-orbit
conditional line when visibility survives]
\label{cor:V6-normalized-line}
Assume $\operatorname{Var}(F)>0$ and $\operatorname{Var}(M)>0$.  With centered
unit vectors
\begin{equation}
 \widehat F=\frac{F-\mathbb EF}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(F)}},
 \qquad
 \widehat M=\frac{M-\mathbb EM}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(M)}},
 \label{eq:V6-normalized-FM}
\end{equation}
one has the exact identity
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\widehat F-\widehat M\|_2^2
 =2\left(1-\sqrt{1-t_{\rm cf}}\right)
 \le2t_{\rm cf}.}
 \label{eq:V6-normalized-FM-distance}
\end{equation}
Consequently, on an escaping selected-root subsequence with
$\operatorname{Var}(F_r)\ge v_*>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 t_{{\rm cf},r}\le\frac{\mathfrak e_{\rm cf}(\beta_r)}{v_*}\to0,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat F_r-\widehat M_r\|_2\to0.}
 \label{eq:V6-visible-outer-reduction}
\end{equation}
The native fine line becomes asymptotically centre-orbit measurable, but no
claim of blocked-old measurability is made.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Orthogonality gives
$\langle F^\circ,M^\circ\rangle=\|M^\circ\|_2^2$.  Hence
\[
 \langle\widehat F,\widehat M\rangle
 =\sqrt{\frac{\operatorname{Var}(M)}{\operatorname{Var}(F)}}
 =\sqrt{1-t_{\rm cf}}.
\]
Expanding the squared distance proves the equality.  Since
$1-\sqrt{1-t}\le t$ for $0\le t\le1$, the inequality follows.  The selected
statement uses \Cref{cor:V6-centre-extinction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Outward interval reduction from a plaquette and visibility
card]
\label{thm:V6-outer-interval}
Suppose a selected card supplies certified bounds
\begin{equation}
 \beta\ge b_->0,
 \qquad
 \bar p_{N,\mathscr D}(\beta)\le p_+,
 \qquad
 A_F\ge a_->0.
 \label{eq:V6-card-inputs}
\end{equation}
Set
\begin{equation}
 e_{\rm cf}^+
 :=K_{\rm fan}^2
   \left(10p_++8e^{-\delta_*b_-}\right),
 \qquad
 t_+:=\min\left\{1,\frac{2e_{\rm cf}^+}{a_-}\right\}.
 \label{eq:V6-card-centre-upper}
\end{equation}
Then $0\le t_{\rm cf}\le t_+$.  If the positive outer replica card gives
\begin{equation}
 r_-\le\mathbb R(M\mid G)\le r_+,
 \qquad 0\le r_-\le r_+\le1,
 \label{eq:V6-outer-residual-interval}
\end{equation}
then the full native residual obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_-
 \le\mathbb R(F\mid G)
 \le r_++t_+(1-r_+)\le1.}
 \label{eq:V6-full-residual-interval}
\end{equation}
Thus an escaping-root card needs no separately fitted centre phase.  It needs
one plaquette-defect upper bound, one native visibility floor, and the three
positive outer moments $A_M,A_G,C_{\rm out}$; $D_{\rm out}$ is required only
for orientation and checks \eqref{eq:V6-outer-heldout}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first two inputs and
\Cref{thm:V6-centre-stock-upper} give
$A_\xi=2\|\xi\|_2^2\le2e_{\rm cf}^+$.  Division by $A_F\ge a_-$ gives the
bound on $t_{\rm cf}$.  Equation \eqref{eq:V6-convex-residual} reads
$R=R_{\rm out}+t(1-R_{\rm out})$.  This expression is increasing in both
variables on the unit square.  Its minimum over the displayed intervals is
$r_-$ and its maximum is $r_++t_+(1-r_+)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Escaping-root visibility-or-outer-alignment alternative]
\label{cor:V6-escaping-subsequence}
Assume $\beta_r\to\infty$.  Since $|F_r|\le K_{\rm fan}$, every cofinal
sequence has a further cofinal subsequence on which
$A_{F,r}$ converges to some $a_\infty\in[0,2K_{\rm fan}^2]$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E6.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.7em]
\item If $a_\infty=0$, the native cutoff writer loses absolute source
      visibility.  Whitening it does not create a noncollapsed physical
      source.
\item If $a_\infty>0$, then $t_{{\rm cf},r}\to0$, the normalized native and
      centre-orbit conditional lines coalesce by
      \eqref{eq:V6-normalized-FM-distance}, and
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \left|\mathbb R(F_r\mid G_r)
             -\mathbb R(M_r\mid G_r)\right|
       \le t_{{\rm cf},r}\longrightarrow0}
       \label{eq:V6-residual-coalescence}
      \end{equation}
      for every normalized old column $G_r$ for which the outer residual is
      defined.
\end{enumerate}
Thus every noncollapsed escaping-root mixed obstruction is asymptotically an
outer old/fine obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The pair-difference stock is bounded by
$A_{F,r}=2\operatorname{Var}(F_r)\le2K_{\rm fan}^2$, so subsequential
compactness is elementary.  The first branch is the definition of visibility
collapse.  On the second branch, the fine variance has a positive lower
bound and \Cref{cor:V6-centre-extinction} gives $t_{{\rm cf},r}\to0$.
Equation \eqref{eq:V6-convex-residual} gives
\[
 \mathbb R(F_r\mid G_r)-\mathbb R(M_r\mid G_r)
 =t_{{\rm cf},r}\bigl(1-\mathbb R(M_r\mid G_r)\bigr),
\]
whose absolute value is at most $t_{{\rm cf},r}$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cutoff and radial source coefficients are independent}
\label{sec:V6-no-substitution}
% =============================================================================

The old/fine fan card compares two cutoff realizations.  The radial card
instead follows one already occurring Creutz source through nested spatial
shells.  The following finite model proves that no numerical implication
between their coefficients is available from Hilbert-space geometry alone.

\begin{theorem}[No universal substitution of a cutoff Schur residual for a
radial source coefficient]
\label{thm:V6-cutoff-radial-independent}
For every prescribed pair
\begin{equation}
 R_{\rm cut}\in[0,1],
 \qquad q_{\rm rad}\in[0,1],
 \label{eq:V6-arbitrary-pair}
\end{equation}
and every source scale $s>0$, there is a finite product probability model in
which:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N6.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.7em]
\item two unit-variance cutoff writers $F,G$ have normalized Schur residual
      exactly $R_{\rm cut}$;
\item an independent selected radial source has entrance stock $s^2$ and
      one-step coefficient exactly $q_{\rm rad}$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently neither a positive, zero, nor near-unit old/fine fan residual
bounds the radial coefficient, and the radial coefficient does not determine
native cutoff visibility.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $G,X,U$ be independent symmetric Rademacher variables.  Put
\[
 F=\sqrt{1-R_{\rm cut}}\,G+\sqrt{R_{\rm cut}}\,X.
\]
Then
$\operatorname{Var}(F)=\operatorname{Var}(G)=1$ and
$\operatorname{Cov}(F,G)=\sqrt{1-R_{\rm cut}}$, so
\[
 \mathbb R(F\mid G)
 =1-\operatorname{Cov}(F,G)^2=R_{\rm cut}.
\]
Independently, let $E$ be a Rademacher variable with
$\mathbb EE=q_{\rm rad}$ and put $V=UE$.  The pair $(U,V)$ is a binary
symmetric channel with
\[
 \mathbb E[U\mid V]=q_{\rm rad}V.
\]
Taking the inner radial message to be $U^-=sU$ and the outer shell record to
be $V$ gives
\[
 \|U^-\|_2^2=s^2,
 \qquad
 \|\mathbb E[U^-\mid V]\|_2^2=s^2q_{\rm rad}^2.
\]
Hence the selected radial norm ratio is $q_{\rm rad}$.  The two constructions
are independent factors, so the prescribed values coexist without
constraint.
\end{proof}

\begin{importedresult}[Exact positive four-leaf radial Read]
\label{imp:V6-four-leaf}
The earlier boundary programme
\begin{center}
\path{Renewal_Yang_Mills_Wilson_Boundary_Information_and_}\\[-0.25em]
\path{Cofinal_Contraction_Programme_V11(9).tex}
\end{center}
already constructs, for each selected card $(N,\beta,R)$, one four-leaf
conditional-replica tree with scalar leaves $A^-_{N,R},A^+_{N,R}$ and
$D_{N,R}^{\square}=A^-_{N,R}-A^+_{N,R}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb EA^-_{N,R}&=I_{N,R}^{\square},\\
 \mathbb EA^+_{N,R}&=I_{N,R+1}^{\square},\\
 \mathbb ED_{N,R}^{\square}
 &=I_{N,R}^{\square}-I_{N,R+1}^{\square}\ge0.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V6-imported-four-leaf}
\end{equation}
Whenever $I_{N,R}^{\square}>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (q_{N,R}^{\square})^2
 =\frac{I_{N,R+1}^{\square}}{I_{N,R}^{\square}}
 =1-\frac{\mathbb ED_{N,R}^{\square}}
          {\mathbb EA^-_{N,R}}.}
 \label{eq:V6-radial-positive-card}
\end{equation}
This exact source-specific Read, together with retained stock and physical
radius, is the radial acquisition.  It is imported rather than rederived.
\end{importedresult}

\begin{corollary}[The first remaining physical card on the escaping branch]
\label{cor:V6-first-remaining-card}
On an escaping weak-facing sequence, the centre-fibre row is controlled by
\eqref{eq:V6-extinction-rate}.  The first remaining cutoff data are therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_M,\quad A_G,\quad C_{\rm out},
 \quad\text{and optionally }D_{\rm out},}
 \label{eq:V6-next-cutoff-card}
\end{equation}
with a native visibility floor.  Independently, the first remaining radial
data are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb EA^-_{N,R},\quad
 \mathbb EA^+_{N,R},\quad
 \mathbb ED_{N,R}^{\square},\quad
 a_NR.}
 \label{eq:V6-next-radial-card}
\end{equation}
No entry in \eqref{eq:V6-next-cutoff-card} may replace an entry in
\eqref{eq:V6-next-radial-card}.  If the cutoff target is only the normalized
Schur residual, the signed entry $D_{\rm out}$ is not required.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The cutoff reduction is
\Cref{thm:V6-separated-replica,thm:V6-outer-interval,cor:V6-centre-extinction}.
The radial identities are \Cref{imp:V6-four-leaf}.  Independence of the two
quantities is \Cref{thm:V6-cutoff-radial-independent}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The $A_1,A_2,A_3$ germ is not the escaping-root radial card]
\label{fire:V6-germ-not-root-card}
The exact coefficients
\[
 A_1=5^{16}18^{-97},\qquad
 A_2=5^8 18^{-121},\qquad
 A_3=64\,18^{-131}
\]
are the first Taylor stocks at the Haar endpoint of one frozen finite card.
They certify nonzero source occurrence and the first two formal radial
transmissions near $\beta=0$.  The weak-facing ultraviolet-admissible branch
has $\beta_r\to\infty$.  No finite list of Taylor coefficients at zero fixes
the positive moments in \eqref{eq:V6-radial-positive-card} at those selected
roots.  Using $A_2/A_1$ or $A_3/A_2$ as a selected-root coefficient would
therefore be a change of physical card.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Complete weak-facing branch alternative and YM--A interface}
\label{sec:V6-branch-export}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Version V6 weak-facing branch completion]
\label{thm:V6-branch-completion}
For the predeclared weak-facing selected-root sequence, exactly one of the
following branches holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B6.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.7em]
\item \textbf{Bounded cofinal branch.}  There are $r_j\to\infty$ and
      $B<\infty$ with $\beta_{r_j}\le B$.  The native writer carries the
      noncollapsed old-record-orthogonal contact source
      \eqref{eq:V6-bounded-contact-source}, while every fixed raw local bank
      on that subsequence lands cylindrical Haar/contact-only.  The branch
      returns the typed \emph{rough-Haar/contact trajectory obstruction} and
      is terminal for a unique smooth raw local-vacuum interpretation.
\item \textbf{Escaping branch.}  One has $\beta_r\to\infty$ and
      \begin{equation}
       \|\xi_r\|_2^2\le\mathfrak e_{\rm cf}(\beta_r)\longrightarrow0.
       \label{eq:V6-branch-extinction}
      \end{equation}
      Along every further cofinal subsequence, either the native variance
      collapses, or a positive native visibility floor reduces the normalized
      cutoff problem to the outer card
      \eqref{eq:V6-next-cutoff-card} with vanishing error.  The radial
      trichotomy remains at the independent positive four-leaf card
      \eqref{eq:V6-next-radial-card}.
\end{enumerate}
No third branch exists.  In neither branch does the centre-fibre source
populate the reduced-fibre Wilson symbol margin or an Osterwalder--Schrader
mass.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The weak-facing selector either tends to infinity or does not.  In the latter
case, item~\textup{(I6.1)} supplies a bounded cofinal subsequence and
\Cref{cor:V6-bounded-terminal} gives branch~\textup{(B6.1)}.  In the former
case, \Cref{cor:V6-centre-extinction,cor:V6-escaping-subsequence} give the
absolute extinction and the visibility-or-outer-alignment alternative.
\Cref{thm:V6-cutoff-radial-independent,imp:V6-four-leaf} retain the radial
card.  The alternatives are exhaustive and disjoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gauge-compatible but still unpopulated mode-card landing]
\label{cor:V6-mode-interface}
On the bounded branch, the contact source remains gauge invariant and its
same-law score incidence annihilates every coarse gauge direction by the
Version~V5 Ward identity.  On the escaping visible branch, the normalized
native line and the centre-orbit conditional line $\widehat M_r$ coalesce as
vectors in the same occurring source Hilbert space once
\eqref{eq:V6-visible-outer-reduction} is certified.  Replacing one by the
other inside a mode functional additionally requires a uniform bound on the
corresponding score norm, or a direct mixed estimate; line convergence alone
does not supply that row.  In both cases the actual mode functional
\begin{equation}
 h\longmapsto\langle\xi_r,s_{r,h}\rangle
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 h\longmapsto\langle M_r^\circ,s_{r,h}\rangle
 \label{eq:V6-mode-functionals}
\end{equation}
must be read on the rooted transverse momentum--colour carrier.  Neither the
centre-stock bounds nor the outer covariance determinant evaluates the
signed reduced-fibre card
$\mathbb EK-\operatorname{Cov}(j)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Gauge annihilation of the first functional is
\Cref{thm:V5-Ward-landing}.  The source-Hilbert-space convergence of
normalized lines on the escaping visible branch is
\Cref{cor:V6-normalized-line}.  Cauchy--Schwarz transfers it to score
pairings only when the relevant score norms are uniformly bounded; otherwise

source writer and the mode score requires the mode score on the same
probability space, and none of the scalar source-stock identities constructs
that writer.  The signed Hessian-minus-covariance card is therefore unchanged.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The one-dimensional boundary source and its routed current ancestry}
\label{sec:V7-source-current}
% =============================================================================

Let \((\Omega,\mu)\) be one finite selected-root same-history probability
space.  Let
\[
 M,G\in L^2(\mu;\R)
\]
be respectively the centred outer boundary-source column and the centred
law-aligned old column.  Let
\[
 \mathbf J=(J_1,\ldots,J_d)^{\mathsf T}
 \in L^2(\mu;\C^d)
\]
be a centred finite current-coordinate bank obtained only after the physical
current-to-boundary route and the common supported gauge reduction have been
fixed.  The first axial YM--A card has \(d=3\) per retained colour after the
coarse gauge direction is removed, but the finite theorem is independent of
that dimension.

Put
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 v_M:=\mathbb E M^2,
 \qquad v_G:=\mathbb E G^2,
 \qquad c_{MG}:=\mathbb E(MG),\\
 K_J:=\mathbb E(\mathbf J\mathbf J^*),
 \qquad x_{MJ}:=\mathbb E(\mathbf J M)\in\C^d.
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:V7-basic-moments}
\end{equation}
For \(h\in\C^d\), define the current synthesis
\begin{equation}
 (\mathcal J h)(\omega):=h^*\mathbf J(\omega),
 \qquad
 \mathcal J:\C^d\longrightarrow L^2_0(\mu).
 \label{eq:V7-current-synthesis}
\end{equation}
Then \(K_J=\mathcal J^*\mathcal J\) and
\(x_{MJ}=\mathcal J^*M\).  When \(v_M>0\), let
\begin{equation}
 P_M:=\frac{\lvert M\rangle\langle M\rvert}{v_M}
 \label{eq:V7-source-projection}
\end{equation}
be the orthogonal projection onto the occurring outer source line.

\begin{theorem}[Exact one-line source/current Gram and ancestry short]
\label{thm:V7-source-current-short}
The common-history source/current Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{M/J}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
    v_M&x_{MJ}^*\\
    x_{MJ}&K_J
  \end{pmatrix}\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:V7-source-current-Gram}
\end{equation}
If \(v_M>0\), its current-over-source Schur residual is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{J\mid M}
 :=K_J-\frac{x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*}{v_M}
 =\mathcal J^*(I-P_M)\mathcal J\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:V7-current-ancestry}
\end{equation}
It vanishes exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J h
 =M\,\frac{x_{MJ}^*h}{v_M}
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\C^d,}
 \label{eq:V7-current-follower}
\end{equation}
that is, when every routed current coordinate is a deterministic linear
follower of the occurring outer source.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathbb I_{J\mid M}
 =\dim\Ran\bigl((I-P_M)\mathcal J\bigr),}
 \label{eq:V7-current-birth-rank}
\end{equation}
so its rank is the minimum number of orthogonal additional response-source
directions required by this finite joint panel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The block in \eqref{eq:V7-source-current-Gram} is the Gram of the family
consisting of \(M\) and the coordinate functions of \(\mathbf J\).  It is
therefore positive.  Since
\[
 \mathcal J^*P_M\mathcal J
 =\frac{\mathcal J^*M\,M^*\mathcal J}{v_M}
 =\frac{x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*}{v_M},
\]
its orthogonal source short is exactly
\eqref{eq:V7-current-ancestry}.  A positive Gram \(T^*T\) vanishes precisely
when \(T=0\); hence \(\mathbb I_{J\mid M}=0\) if and only if
\((I-P_M)\mathcal J=0\).  In that case
\[
 \mathcal J=P_M\mathcal J
 =M\,v_M^{-1}M^*\mathcal J,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V7-current-follower}; the converse is immediate.  Finally,
\(\rank(T^*T)=\rank T=\dim\Ran T\) in finite dimension, proving
\eqref{eq:V7-current-birth-rank}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Whitened form of the cofinal-programme incidence residual]
\label{cor:V7-whitened-incidence}
For the unit outer source \(\widehat M=M/\sqrt{v_M}\), put
\[
 X_{MJ}:=\mathbb E(\mathbf J\widehat M)=x_{MJ}/\sqrt{v_M}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{pmatrix}1&X_{MJ}^*\\X_{MJ}&K_J\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb I_{J\mid M}=K_J-X_{MJ}X_{MJ}^*.}
 \label{eq:V7-whitened-block}
\end{equation}
Thus, for the one-dimensional fan-source range, the missing mixed block in the
cofinal source/current theorem is exactly the vector \(X_{MJ}\), and its
ancestry residual is \eqref{eq:V7-current-ancestry}.  No explicit choice of an
ambient source-faithful isometry is needed once the physical current
coordinates and \(M\) occur on the same history; the common \(L^2(\mu)\)
realization supplies the incidence.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Divide the first row and column of
\eqref{eq:V7-source-current-Gram} by \(\sqrt{v_M}\).  The final statement is
only a coordinate economy: it presupposes the physical same-history current
Read and does not construct it.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[A positive ancestry residual is not a negative symbol]
\label{fire:V7-ancestry-not-symbol}
A positive \(\mathbb I_{J\mid M}\) proves that the routed current contains a

birth or survivor only after its current metric, physical radius, and cutoff

card.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{One positive three-replica panel reconstructs both missing mixed rows}
\label{sec:V7-three-replica}
% =============================================================================

Take three independent copies
\[
 (M_a,G_a,\mathbf J_a),\qquad a=1,2,3,
\]
of the same joint law.  Define the pair-difference stocks
\begin{align}
 A_M&:=\mathbb E(M_1-M_2)^2,
 &A_G&:=\mathbb E(G_1-G_2)^2,
 \label{eq:V7-pair-scalars}\\
 \mathbb A_J&:=\mathbb E\bigl[(\mathbf J_1-\mathbf J_2)
                         (\mathbf J_1-\mathbf J_2)^*\bigr].
 \label{eq:V7-pair-current}
\end{align}
The optional signed orientation checks are
\begin{align}
 D_{MG}&:=\mathbb E[(M_1-M_2)(G_1-G_2)],
 \label{eq:V7-cross-MG}\\
 \mathbf D_{MJ}&:=\mathbb E[(\mathbf J_1-\mathbf J_2)(M_1-M_2)].
 \label{eq:V7-cross-MJ}
\end{align}
Now define the scalar old/fine area and the vector source/current area by
\begin{align}
 \Delta^{MG}_{123}
 &:=(M_1-M_3)(G_2-G_3)-(M_2-M_3)(G_1-G_3),
 \label{eq:V7-area-MG}\\
 \boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123}
 &:=(M_1-M_3)(\mathbf J_2-\mathbf J_3)
   -(M_2-M_3)(\mathbf J_1-\mathbf J_3),
 \label{eq:V7-area-MJ}
\end{align}
and their positive expectations
\begin{equation}
 C_{\rm out}:=\mathbb E\abs{\Delta^{MG}_{123}}^2,
 \qquad
 \mathbb C_{\rm cur}:=
 \mathbb E\bigl[
 \boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123}
 (\boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123})^*
 \bigr]\succeq0.
 \label{eq:V7-area-positive}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Scalar and matrix three-replica area identities]
\label{thm:V7-matrix-area}
The pair-difference quantities are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_M=2v_M,
 \quad A_G=2v_G,
 \quad \mathbb A_J=2K_J,
 \quad D_{MG}=2c_{MG},
 \quad \mathbf D_{MJ}=2x_{MJ}.}
 \label{eq:V7-pair-identities}
\end{equation}
The positive area expectations are
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 C_{\rm out}=6(v_Mv_G-c_{MG}^2),}
 \label{eq:V7-scalar-area-identity}\\
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\rm cur}
 =6(v_MK_J-x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*).}
 \label{eq:V7-matrix-area-identity}
\end{align}
Consequently, whenever \(A_M,A_G>0\),
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{\rm out}(M\mid G)
 =1-\frac{c_{MG}^2}{v_Mv_G}
 =\frac{2C_{\rm out}}{3A_MA_G},}
 \label{eq:V7-outer-from-area}\\
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{J\mid M}
 =\frac{\mathbb C_{\rm cur}}{3A_M}.}
 \label{eq:V7-ancestry-from-area}
\end{align}
The same three replicas therefore reconstruct the outer cutoff residual and
the current-ancestry residual on one common history.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The pair-difference formulas are the ordinary two-copy covariance identities.
For the matrix area, write the alternating expansion
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123}
 =M_1\mathbf J_2+M_2\mathbf J_3+M_3\mathbf J_1
  -M_1\mathbf J_3-M_2\mathbf J_1-M_3\mathbf J_2.
 \label{eq:V7-six-term-area}
\end{equation}
The variables may be centred without changing differences.  In the expansion
of
\(\mathbb E[\boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123}
(\boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123})^*]\), a term survives only in either of two
ways.  First, an ordered pair \((i,j)\), \(i\ne j\), is paired with itself;
there are six such terms and each equals \(v_MK_J\).  Second, \((i,j)\) is
paired with its reverse \((j,i)\); the alternating signs are opposite, there
are six such terms, and each contributes \(-x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*\).  Every other
term contains a centred replica index appearing only once and vanishes by
independence.  This proves \eqref{eq:V7-matrix-area-identity}.  Taking
\(d=1\) and \(\mathbf J=G\) proves
\eqref{eq:V7-scalar-area-identity}.  Substitution of
\eqref{eq:V7-pair-identities} gives
\eqref{eq:V7-outer-from-area} and
\eqref{eq:V7-ancestry-from-area}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two held-out common-cylinder identities]
\label{cor:V7-heldout-identities}
The optional signed reads obey
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 D_{MG}^2+\frac23C_{\rm out}=A_MA_G,}
 \label{eq:V7-heldout-outer}\\
 \boxed{
 \mathbf D_{MJ}\mathbf D_{MJ}^*
 +\frac23\mathbb C_{\rm cur}
 =A_M\mathbb A_J.}
 \label{eq:V7-heldout-current}
\end{align}
Thus a positive five-object packet
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_M,
 \quad A_G,
 \quad C_{\rm out},
 \quad \mathbb A_J,
 \quad \mathbb C_{\rm cur}}
 \label{eq:V7-five-object-packet}
\end{equation}
reconstructs both unsigned targets.  The scalar \(D_{MG}\) and vector
\(\mathbf D_{MJ}\) are needed only for oriented transport, and otherwise
serve as held-out tests that all columns were acquired on one common law.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Insert \eqref{eq:V7-pair-identities} and
\eqref{eq:V7-scalar-area-identity}--
\eqref{eq:V7-matrix-area-identity}.  For example,
\[
 \mathbf D_{MJ}\mathbf D_{MJ}^*
 +\frac23\mathbb C_{\rm cur}
 =4x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*+4(v_MK_J-x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*)
 =4v_MK_J=A_M\mathbb A_J.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Outward intervals and typed executable outcomes]
\label{thm:V7-area-intervals}
Suppose outward intervals satisfy
\begin{equation}
 0<a_-\le A_M\le a_+,
 \qquad
 0<g_-\le A_G\le g_+,
 \qquad
 0\le c_-\le C_{\rm out}\le c_+,
 \label{eq:V7-scalar-interval-input}
\end{equation}
and Hermitian matrix bounds satisfy
\begin{equation}
 0\preceq C_-\preceq\mathbb C_{\rm cur}\preceq C_+.
 \label{eq:V7-matrix-interval-input}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{2c_-}{3a_+g_+}
 \le \mathbb R_{\rm out}(M\mid G)
 \le \frac{2c_+}{3a_-g_-},}
 \label{eq:V7-outer-interval}
\end{equation}
with the endpoints intersected with \([0,1]\), and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{C_-}{3a_+}
 \preceq\mathbb I_{J\mid M}
 \preceq\frac{C_+}{3a_-}.}
 \label{eq:V7-current-interval}
\end{equation}
The corresponding finite audit returns exactly one of the following.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E7.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.8em]
\item \(\mathsf{FOLLOWER}\): the upper matrix endpoint in
      \eqref{eq:V7-current-interval} is zero, proving
      \eqref{eq:V7-current-follower}.
\item \(\mathsf{CURRENT\mbox{-}BIRTH}\): a declared vector \(h\) has
      \(h^*C_-h>0\), giving a positive ancestry direction.
\item \(\mathsf{UNRESOLVED}\): the enclosure is positive but does not
      separate zero on the required bank.
\item \(\mathsf{ERROR}\): a denominator interval meets zero, a submitted
      support is inconsistent, or either held-out identity is excluded by the
      reported intervals.
\end{enumerate}
Only the first three are mathematical outcomes; \(\mathsf{ERROR}\) rejects an
ill-typed or non-common-cylinder packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All denominators are positive.  Monotonicity of multiplication and reciprocal
on positive scalar intervals gives \eqref{eq:V7-outer-interval}.  From
\(C_-\preceq\mathbb C_{\rm cur}\preceq C_+\) and
\(a_-\le A_M\le a_+\),
\[
 \frac{C_-}{3a_+}
 \preceq\frac{\mathbb C_{\rm cur}}{3A_M}
 \preceq\frac{C_+}{3a_-},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V7-current-interval}.  The first two outcomes follow from
\Cref{thm:V7-source-current-short}; the remaining two record failure to prove
a strict mathematical branch versus failure of the theorem domain.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Independent replicas are not the radial reverse-kernel tree]
\label{fire:V7-iid-not-radial}
The replicas in \Cref{thm:V7-matrix-area} are independent copies of one joint
same-history law.  The radial four-leaf card of Version~V6 has a different
conditional structure: two old shells are sampled conditionally independently
given a common outer shell, and two interiors are then sampled conditionally
independently over each old shell.  Replacing that tree by independent copies
of \((M,G,\mathbf J)\) destroys the tower identity which reconstructs
\(I_{N,R+1}^{\square}\).  The positive cards are complementary, not
interchangeable.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Ultraviolet extinction of centre-current ancestry}
\label{sec:V7-centre-current}
% =============================================================================

On the escaping branch of Version~V6, retain the exact orthogonal source split
\begin{equation}
 F=M+\xi,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(M\xi)=0,
 \qquad
 e:=\norm{\xi}_2^2.
 \label{eq:V7-F-M-xi}
\end{equation}
For the same current bank \(\mathbf J\), put
\begin{equation}
 x_{FJ}:=\mathbb E(\mathbf JF),
 \qquad
 x_{\xi J}:=\mathbb E(\mathbf J\xi),
 \qquad
 x_{FJ}=x_{MJ}+x_{\xi J}.
 \label{eq:V7-cross-split}
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Source/current Cauchy--Schwarz domination]
\label{lem:V7-cross-domination}
For every centred scalar \(\xi\in L^2(\mu)\) and centred current bank
\(\mathbf J\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 x_{\xi J}x_{\xi J}^*\preceq eK_J.}
 \label{eq:V7-cross-domination}
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every coefficient projection \(P\) and every
\(d_+<\infty\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 PK_JP\preceq d_+P,
 \label{eq:V7-current-window}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{Px_{\xi J}}^2\le d_+e.}
 \label{eq:V7-cross-window}
\end{equation}
Conversely, if a unit \(h\in\Ran P\) obeys
\(\abs{h^*x_{\xi J}}\ge b>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{h^*K_Jh\ge b^2/e.}
 \label{eq:V7-cross-blowup}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For every \(h\in\C^d\), scalar Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 h^*x_{\xi J}x_{\xi J}^*h
 =\abs{\mathbb E[\xi\,h^*\mathbf J]}^2
 \le e\,\mathbb E\abs{h^*\mathbf J}^2
 =e\,h^*K_Jh.
\]
This is the Loewner inequality \eqref{eq:V7-cross-domination}.  Compressing by
\(P\) and using \eqref{eq:V7-current-window} gives
\(Px_{\xi J}x_{\xi J}^*P\preceq ed_+P\); the norm of the rank-one left side
is \(\norm{Px_{\xi J}}^2\).  The last assertion is the same scalar inequality
rearranged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Extinction-or-current-blowup alternative]
\label{cor:V7-extinction-current}
Along every escaping weak-facing sequence, Version~V6 gives
\(e_r=\norm{\xi_r}_2^2\to0\).  Hence on any coefficient island with a uniform
current window
\begin{equation}
 P_rK_{J,r}P_r\preceq d_+P_r,
 \qquad d_+<\infty,
 \label{eq:V7-uniform-current-window}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\norm{P_rx_{\xi J,r}}\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V7-centre-current-extinction}
\end{equation}
If instead a centre-current pairing stays bounded below on unit vectors in
that island, the corresponding current Gram diverges at least as
\(e_r^{-1}\).  This is a typed current-properness obstruction, not a revival
of the extinct centre source.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \eqref{eq:V7-cross-window} and
\eqref{eq:V7-cross-blowup} at every cutoff.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Application to the cofinal low-island direct window]
\label{cor:V7-low-island-centre}
On the separated Yang--Mills low island of the supplied cofinal-survivor
programme, the direct window implies
\begin{equation}
 P_rK_{J,r}P_r\preceq d_+P_r
 \label{eq:V7-imported-low-island-window}
\end{equation}
for the source-whitened current Gram.  Therefore the centre-fibre component
cannot carry a nonzero current incidence on any escaping low-island family
satisfying that uniform direct window.  Every proper noncollapsed current
incidence must come from the outer line \(M_r\) or from the positive ancestry
residual \(\mathbb I_{J\mid M,r}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The imported low-island identity is
\(K_{J,r}=D_r-A_r\) compressed to the separated island; its displayed direct
window gives the upper bound in
\eqref{eq:V7-imported-low-island-window}.  Now use
\Cref{cor:V7-extinction-current}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative replacement of native ancestry by outer ancestry]
\label{thm:V7-ancestry-stability}
Retain \eqref{eq:V7-F-M-xi}, put
\begin{equation}
 v_F:=\norm{F}_2^2,
 \qquad
 v_M=v_F-e>0,
 \label{eq:V7-variance-split}
\end{equation}
and define
\begin{align}
 \mathbb I_{J\mid F}
 &:=K_J-\frac{x_{FJ}x_{FJ}^*}{v_F},
 \label{eq:V7-native-ancestry}\\
 \mathbb I_{J\mid M}
 &:=K_J-\frac{x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*}{v_M}.
 \label{eq:V7-outer-ancestry-again}
\end{align}
If
\begin{equation}
 v_F\ge v_*>0,
 \qquad
 \norm{K_J}_{\rm op}\le k_*<\infty,
 \label{eq:V7-stability-window}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathbb I_{J\mid F}-\mathbb I_{J\mid M}}_{\rm op}
 \le
 2k_*\sqrt{\frac{e}{v_*}}
 +k_*\frac{e}{v_*}.}
 \label{eq:V7-ancestry-stability-bound}
\end{equation}
In particular, on the escaping visible branch with a uniform current window,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{J\mid F,r}-\mathbb I_{J\mid M,r}
 \longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{in operator norm}.}
 \label{eq:V7-ancestry-coalescence}
\end{equation}
Thus the outer source/current card is not merely a convenient approximation:
it is the unique noncollapsed ancestry card left after centre-fibre extinction
under the stated properness window.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:V7-cross-domination},
\begin{equation}
 \norm{x_{FJ}}\le\sqrt{v_Fk_*},
 \qquad
 \norm{x_{MJ}}\le\sqrt{v_Mk_*},
 \qquad
 \norm{x_{\xi J}}\le\sqrt{ek_*}.
 \label{eq:V7-cross-norms}
\end{equation}
Since \(x_{FJ}=x_{MJ}+x_{\xi J}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\norm{
   x_{FJ}x_{FJ}^*/v_F-x_{MJ}x_{MJ}^*/v_M}\\
 &\quad\le
 \frac{(\norm{x_{FJ}}+\norm{x_{MJ}})\norm{x_{\xi J}}}{v_F}
 +\norm{x_{MJ}}^2\abs{v_F^{-1}-v_M^{-1}}\\
 &\quad\le
 2k_*\sqrt{e/v_F}+k_*e/v_F
 \le2k_*\sqrt{e/v_*}+k_*e/v_*.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The two ancestry residuals differ by the negative of the displayed matrix,
which proves \eqref{eq:V7-ancestry-stability-bound}.  Version~V6 supplies
\(e_r\to0\), giving \eqref{eq:V7-ancestry-coalescence}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Whitening cannot hide current blowup]
\label{fire:V7-whitening-blowup}
If \(v_F\to0\), the native source has absolute visibility collapse and no
normalized source/current angle is promoted.  If \(v_F\) stays positive but
\(K_J\) diverges quickly enough to defeat
\eqref{eq:V7-centre-current-extinction}, the first obstruction is the current
properness or relative-moment row.  Dividing by \(\sqrt{v_F}\) or
\(\sqrt e\) does not convert that divergence into a finite physical source
incidence.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Common-gauge covariance and the physical axial card}
\label{sec:V7-gauge-covariance}
% =============================================================================

The reduced-fibre Version~V6 proves that the comparison head and the positive
return share one gauge row and must be reduced with one common supported
pseudoinverse before their difference is scalarized.  The replica incidence
must respect that same order.

\begin{proposition}[Covariance of the replica card under a fixed coefficient map]
\label{prop:V7-linear-covariance}
Let \(T:\C^d\to\C^m\) be a deterministic linear map fixed before the readings,
and put \(\mathbf J'=T\mathbf J\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 K_{J'}&=TK_JT^*,
 &x_{MJ'}&=Tx_{MJ},\\
 \mathbb A_{J'}&=T\mathbb A_JT^*,
 &\mathbf D_{MJ'}&=T\mathbf D_{MJ},\\
 \mathbb C_{{\rm cur},J'}&=T\mathbb C_{{\rm cur},J}T^*,
 &\mathbb I_{J'\mid M}&=T\mathbb I_{J\mid M}T^*.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V7-linear-covariance}
\end{equation}
Hence the same positive three-replica packet may be acquired directly on the
already reduced three-dimensional axial bank, or compressed by the frozen
physical quotient map afterward.  It may not be compressed by a map fitted to
the observed residual.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Every identity follows by inserting \(\mathbf J'=T\mathbf J\) into the
definitions.  In particular,
\(\boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ'}_{123}=T\boldsymbol\Delta^{MJ}_{123}\), so its Gram
transforms by congruence.  Substitution in
\eqref{eq:V7-current-ancestry} proves the last formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Rooted transverse source/current card]
\label{cor:V7-transverse-card}
On the frozen nonzero axial momentum, let
\(T_q\) be the predeclared isometry from the common-gauge physical quotient to
\(E_{\perp,q}\cong\C^3\).  Apply
\Cref{prop:V7-linear-covariance} with \(T=T_q\) only after the YM--A Ward row
and common supported gauge reduction have passed.  The matrix
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I^{\perp}_{J\mid M}
 =\frac{T_q\mathbb C_{\rm cur}T_q^*}{3A_M}}
 \label{eq:V7-transverse-ancestry}
\end{equation}
is then the source-current ancestry residual on the same rooted transverse
carrier as the return-renormalized axial symbol.  It is normalized by the
actual source pair stock \(A_M\), not by the identity link metric or by the
flat fibre gap.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use \eqref{eq:V7-ancestry-from-area} and
\eqref{eq:V7-linear-covariance}.  The order qualification is inherited from
the exact common-gauge head/return identity: separate gauge shorts can lose
the shared correction and are not the physical axial card.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[How the YM--A weighted return theorem enters]
\label{ass:V7-YMA-weighted-return}
The weighted defect-channel condition in the supplied YM--A Version~V6 gives
an explicit physical-radius tail for the routed curvature-defect return.  It
can therefore provide the current properness and finite-head control needed
after \(\mathbb I^{\perp}_{J\mid M}\) is populated.  It does not set
\(\mathbb C_{\rm cur}\), because the latter also requires the boundary source
and current on one common history.  Conversely, a positive ancestry matrix
does not prove the weighted channel edge below one.  The incidence and radius
rows must both pass before a cofinal current survivor is promoted.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The cutoff, current-ancestry, and radial gates are independent}
\label{sec:V7-three-gates}
% =============================================================================

For a scalar current coordinate with \(K_J>0\), define its normalized ancestry
fraction
\begin{equation}
 r_{\rm anc}:=\frac{\mathbb I_{J\mid M}}{K_J}\in[0,1].
 \label{eq:V7-normalized-ancestry}
\end{equation}
Retain the normalized outer cutoff residual
\(r_{\rm cut}=\mathbb R_{\rm out}(M\mid G)\) and the selected radial source
coefficient \(q_{\rm rad}\in[0,1]\).

\begin{theorem}[Exact three-gate independence]
\label{thm:V7-three-gate-independence}
For every prescribed triple
\begin{equation}
 (r_{\rm cut},r_{\rm anc},q_{\rm rad})\in[0,1]^3,
 \label{eq:V7-arbitrary-gates}
\end{equation}
there is one finite product probability model in which the cutoff and ancestry
cards use the same outer source and which realizes all three values
simultaneously.  Therefore no function of either two gates determines the
third.  In particular:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G7.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.8em]
\item an exact old/fine attachment does not imply that the routed current is a
      follower of the boundary source;
\item a zero current-ancestry residual does not determine outward radial
      attenuation;
\item a near-unit radial channel does not determine the old/fine Schur angle
      or the current ancestry rank.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let \(M,U\) be independent symmetric Rademacher variables.  Let
\(H_{\rm cut},H_{\rm anc},H_{\rm rad}\in\{-1,1\}\) be mutually independent,
independent of \((M,U)\), and chosen with
\[
 \mathbb EH_{\rm cut}=\sqrt{1-r_{\rm cut}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb EH_{\rm anc}=\sqrt{1-r_{\rm anc}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb EH_{\rm rad}=q_{\rm rad}.
\]
Put
\[
 G=MH_{\rm cut},
 \qquad
 J=MH_{\rm anc}.
\]
Thus the cutoff and ancestry cards use the same outer source \(M\).  The
variables \(M,G,J\) are centred and have unit variance, while
\[
 \mathbb E(MG)=\sqrt{1-r_{\rm cut}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(MJ)=\sqrt{1-r_{\rm anc}}.
\]
Hence
\(
 \mathbb R_{\rm out}(M\mid G)=r_{\rm cut}
\)
and
\(
 K_J^{-1}\mathbb I_{J\mid M}=r_{\rm anc}
\).
Finally set \(V=UH_{\rm rad}\).  The variable \(V\) is symmetric and
independent of \(H_{\rm rad}\), so
\[
 \mathbb E[U\mid V]
 =V\mathbb E[H_{\rm rad}\mid V]
 =q_{\rm rad}V.
\]
Thus the radial norm ratio is \(q_{\rm rad}\).  Taking the product of these
finite sign spaces proves simultaneous realization.  The three freely chosen
means alter the three gates independently while retaining the common source
\(M\) in the first two cards.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[No combined scalar verdict before all three gates]
\label{fire:V7-no-combined-scalar}
The three-gate theorem is a non-substitution result.  It does not require all
three physical Reads to be performed by one instrument.  The outer and
current rows may share the common iid replica panel
\eqref{eq:V7-five-object-packet}; the radial row requires its reverse-kernel
four-leaf tree.  A weighted sum of their scalar residuals has no invariant
physical meaning and is not used as a contraction margin.
\end{firewall}
