\section{Target-minimal selected-root acquisition after Version V7}
\label{sec:V7-acquisition}
% =============================================================================

The first executable escaping-root packet is now finite and ordered.

\begin{definition}[Outer/current common-history acquisition packet]
\label{def:V7-common-history-packet}
At the first predeclared escaping selected root, freeze:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P7.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.8em]
\item the selected-root interval and the native/outer source type;
\item the law-aligned old column \(G\), the outer source \(M\), and the routed
      current bank \(\mathbf J\) on one same-history cylinder;
\item the common Ward-compatible axial quotient and its physical radius tags;
\item three independent copies of that complete joint cylinder.
\end{enumerate}
The positive output is the five-object packet
\eqref{eq:V7-five-object-packet}.  The optional signed outputs
\(D_{MG},\mathbf D_{MJ}\) are held out until orientation is required.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite decision order]
\label{thm:V7-decision-order}
A well-typed selected-root continuation proceeds in the following order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(D7.\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.8em]
\item If the weak-facing sequence has a bounded cofinal subsequence, return the
      already proved rough-Haar/contact trajectory obstruction; do not open the
      escaping card.
\item On an escaping branch, first certify an outer/native visibility floor.
      If \(A_M\) tends to zero, return source visibility collapse.
\item Acquire \eqref{eq:V7-five-object-packet}.  Use
      \eqref{eq:V7-outer-from-area} for old/fine alignment and
      \eqref{eq:V7-ancestry-from-area} for current ancestry.  Reject a packet
      which fails either held-out identity.
\item If \(\mathbb I_{J\mid M}=0\), route the current as a follower of the
      outer source and charge no second source birth.  If it is positive,
      retain its polar residual bank and apply the already supplied low-island
      relative-moment and transport tests before calling it a cofinal current
      survivor.
\item Independently run the Version~V6 conditional four-leaf tree to obtain
      \(I_{N,R}^{\square}\), \(I_{N,R+1}^{\square}\), and the radial loss.
      Continue only while the selected source stock remains visible and attach
      the physical radius \(a_NR\).
\item Export to YM--A only after the source/current residual has landed on the
      common-gauge transverse carrier.  A near-unit current return is a typed
      return survivor unless the complete head-minus-return interval is
      negative on the same physical vector.
\end{enumerate}
This order uses the same outer source stock \(A_M\) in both mixed cards and
therefore introduces no duplicated source normalization.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Item~\textup{(D7.1)} is the Version~V6 weak-facing alternative.  Items
\textup{(D7.2)--(D7.4)} are
\Cref{thm:V7-matrix-area,cor:V7-heldout-identities,thm:V7-source-current-short}.
Item~\textup{(D7.5)} is the independent four-leaf Read retained in Version~V6
and the non-substitution theorem
\Cref{thm:V7-three-gate-independence}.  The final item is the common-gauge
landing of \Cref{cor:V7-transverse-card} together with the sign firewall in
\Cref{fire:V7-ancestry-not-symbol}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Physical status after auditing the supplied files]
\label{ass:V7-physical-status}
None of the supplied files contains a joint selected-root sample of
\((M,G,\mathbf J)\), a current-to-boundary occurrence map, or the conditional
four-leaf radial moments.  Hence the mathematical identities in
\Cref{thm:V7-decision-order} are executable, but the present physical verdict
is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathsf{STOP}\\[-0.15em]
 \text{at the first common-history outer/current expectation row}\\[-0.1em]
 \text{and the independent radial four-leaf row}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V7-physical-stop}
\end{equation}
This is not evidence that either row vanishes or fails.  It is the exact
finite acquisition boundary after the new notes are incorporated.
\end{assessment}

\section*{Version V8: upstream source audit, complete native collapse, and the colour-selection obstruction}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Version V8: upstream source audit, complete native collapse, and the colour-selection obstruction}
\label{sec:V8-start}
\begin{center}
{\Large\bfseries Version V8}\\[0.35em]
{\large A forty-four-plaquette bound for the complete native fan,\\
its exact thirty-three-cycle quadratic tensor, and return to the physical source}
\end{center}

\paragraph{The upstream question.}
Versions~V5--V7 repeatedly isolated a mixed expectation conditional on a
noncollapsing native source.  Before another expectation is acquired, that
source-visibility premise must itself be tested against the literal Wilson
law.  The native fan is a fixed lattice-size combination of contractible
loops, whereas the original source \(Y_N^\square\) is built from rectangles
of fixed \emph{physical} size.  They agree neither as writers nor as cofinal
source families.  A leading coefficient at \(N=32\) does not identify them.
The present continuation therefore goes upstream of the replica panels and
returns to the pointwise native writer.

Two concrete obstructions are proved.  First, on every escaping periodic
Wilson sequence the \emph{whole} native variance tends to zero, not just the
centre-fibre part.  Thus the visible escaping-native branch retained in
Versions~V6--V7 is empty in its frozen normalization.  Second, on a
central-vacuum law, a scalar colour singlet has exactly zero overlap with an
equivariant adjoint current bank.  The scalar fan cannot be substituted for
the adjoint-valued reflected half-score synthesis in the shared programme.
These are respectively an absolute source-collapse statement and a
representation-selection statement; their law hypotheses are kept separate.

No surface coefficient \(A_1,A_2,A_3\), general Schur identity, replica-area
identity, or cofinal compactness theorem is recomputed.  The new finite
calculation is a positive plaquette envelope and the exact quadratic tensor
of the already fixed native fan.

\begin{assessment}[Earlier branches]
\label{ass:V8-correction}
The conditional probability identities of Versions~V5--V7 remain valid under
their stated hypotheses.  Their suggested \emph{application} through a
uniformly visible unrescaled native fan is superseded by
\Cref{thm:V8-native-collapse}.  The scalar/current identities in Version~V7
do not establish that its one-dimensional scalar source is the reflected
curvature-source bank: on the symmetry-preserving central-vacuum branch,
\Cref{thm:V8-colour-selection} proves that this identification fails whenever
the adjoint current is nonzero.  Neither correction changes a previously
frozen Wilson parameter, block map, writer, or coefficient normalization.
\end{assessment}

\section{The native writer and a forty-four-plaquette envelope}
\label{sec:V8-envelope}

Translate the existing native stencil so that its even centre is the origin.
Let \(C_4\) be the positively oriented square with corners
\((\pm2,\pm2,0,0)\).  There are eight middle edges, two on each side, in
cyclic order.  At middle position \(i\), let \(e_i:u_i\to v_i\) be the
original edge and let
\[
 P_{i,a}:u_i\to u_i+n_{i,a}\to v_i+n_{i,a}\to v_i,
 \qquad a\in\mathcal N:=\{0,2,-2,3,-3\}.
\]
Here \(n_{i,0}\) is the inward planar normal and the other four normals are
the two signed transverse coordinate directions.  The four two-edge corner
paths are unchanged from Version~V3.  Concatenating those corners and the
eight chosen staples gives the existing word \(\Gamma_\eta\),
\(\eta\in\mathcal N^8\).  Cancellation of consecutive inverse links is
performed in the word, not in a commutative trace approximation.

With \(\mathcal O_C=\frac13\operatorname{Re}\Tr U(C)\), define
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 n_{\rm fan}&=5^8,\\
 K_{\rm fan}&=\sqrt{18}\,5^4,\\
 f_N&=\frac{K_{\rm fan}}{n_{\rm fan}}
             \sum_{\eta\in\mathcal N^8}\mathcal O_{\Gamma_\eta},\\
 D_N&:=1-\frac{f_N}{K_{\rm fan}}.
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:V8-native-definition}
\end{equation}
This is exactly the Haar-unit writer of \eqref{eq:unit-fan}; it is not
renormalized again at nonzero coupling.  The established \(\SU(3)\) trace
range gives
\begin{equation}
 -\frac12K_{\rm fan}\le f_N\le K_{\rm fan},
 \qquad 0\le D_N\le\frac32.
 \label{eq:V8-native-range}
\end{equation}

Let \(\mathcal P_c\) be the four plaquettes of the central \(2\times2\)
square.  Let \(p_{i,0}\) be the inward plaquette between \(e_i\) and
\(P_{i,0}\), and let \(p_{i,a}\), \(a\ne0\), be the corresponding
transverse plaquette.  The sets
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal P_0=\{p_{i,0}:1\le i\le8\},\qquad
 \mathcal P_t=\{p_{i,a}:1\le i\le8,\ a\ne0\}
 \label{eq:V8-face-classes}
\end{equation}
are disjoint from one another and from \(\mathcal P_c\), and their
cardinalities are \(8\) and \(32\).  Write
\(d_p=1-\frac13\operatorname{Re}\Tr U_p\).

\begin{lemma}[Two-face replacement, with a nonabelian word certificate]
\label{lem:V8-two-face}
If \(t(\eta)=\#\{i:\eta_i\ne0\}\), then \(U(\Gamma_\eta)\) is a
product of
\begin{equation}
 m_\eta=4+2t(\eta)
 \label{eq:V8-filling-budget}
\end{equation}
conjugated plaquette holonomies or their inverses.  The plaquette occurrences
are the four members of \(\mathcal P_c\) and, for every \(\eta_i\ne0\),
one occurrence each of \(p_{i,0}\) and \(p_{i,\eta_i}\).  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 d\bigl(U(\Gamma_\eta)\bigr)
 \le m_\eta\left(
   \sum_{p\in\mathcal P_c}d_p
   +\sum_{i:\eta_i\ne0}(d_{p_{i,0}}+d_{p_{i,\eta_i}})\right).
 \label{eq:V8-word-bound}
\end{equation}
The integer \(m_\eta\) is a certified word-filling budget, not a claim that
this filling is minimal.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The all-planar concatenation reduces to the positively oriented \(C_2\)
square.  Its four-face nonabelian peeling is the already proved planar
peeling identity of the dedicated trajectory programme
(\texttt{lem:V5-planar-peeling}).  One replacement has the exact free-word
identity
\begin{equation}
 P_{i,a}P_{i,0}^{-1}
 =(P_{i,a}e_i^{-1})(e_iP_{i,0}^{-1}).
 \label{eq:V8-free-word}
\end{equation}
Both parenthesized words are oriented unit plaquette boundaries.  Replacing
a subpath in a based closed path conjugates this two-face product by the
preceding path holonomy.  Iterating over the nonplanar choices gives precisely
\eqref{eq:V8-filling-budget}.  This argument is at the group-word level and
is unaffected by subsequent backtrack cancellations or intersections of
plaquette supports.

For unitaries, \(\|I-AB\|_{\rm HS}\le\|I-A\|_{\rm HS}+\|I-B\|_{\rm HS}\)
and \(\|I-U\|_{\rm HS}^2=6d(U)\).  Unitary conjugation and inversion
preserve these norms.  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the \(m_\eta\) factors
gives \eqref{eq:V8-word-bound}.  The thirty-two replacements and the
disjointness of their canonical face classes are checked by the exact
coordinate certificate below.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise positive envelope of the complete native fan]
\label{thm:V8-envelope}
On every configuration of a nonwrapping native stencil,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad
 0\le D_N\le\min\left\{\frac32,\mathcal E_N\right\},\quad}
 \label{eq:V8-envelope}
\end{equation}
where the fixed positive writer uses only forty-four plaquettes:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_N=
 \frac{84}{5}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_c}d_p
 +\frac{344}{25}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_0}d_p
 +\frac{86}{25}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_t}d_p.}
 \label{eq:V8-explicit-envelope}
\end{equation}
The sum of its coefficients is exactly \(7184/25\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Average \eqref{eq:V8-word-bound} over the fixed uniform label set; this is a
finite combinatorial average, not a change to the Wilson law.  If
\(T=t(\eta)\), then \(T\) has the counting distribution
\(\Pr(T=t)=\binom8t4^t/5^8\).  Thus
\[
 \mathbb E_\eta m_\eta=4+2\cdot8\cdot\frac45=\frac{84}{5}.
\]
At one specified nonplanar label,
\[
 \mathbb E_\eta[m_\eta\mid\eta_i=a\ne0]
 =6+2\cdot7\cdot\frac45=\frac{86}{5}.
\]
Multiplication respectively by \(4/5\) and \(1/5\) gives the inward and
transverse coefficients in \eqref{eq:V8-explicit-envelope}.  Their sum is
\[
 4\frac{84}{5}+8\frac{344}{25}+32\frac{86}{25}
 =\frac{7184}{25}
 =\mathbb E_\eta m_\eta^2.
\]
The trace range gives the independent cap \(D_N\le3/2\).
\end{proof}

\section{The complete native source collapses on the escaping Wilson branch}
\label{sec:V8-collapse}

\begin{theorem}[Law-relative variance bound and periodic Wilson extinction]
\label{thm:V8-native-collapse}
For any probability law \(\nu\) on the same configurations,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E_\nu(K_{\rm fan}-f_N)
 &\le K_{\rm fan}\mathbb E_\nu\mathcal E_N,
 \label{eq:V8-mean-bound}\\
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(f_N)
 &\le K_{\rm fan}^2
       \mathbb E_\nu\min\{3/2,\mathcal E_N\}^{\,2}
 \le\frac32K_{\rm fan}^2\mathbb E_\nu\mathcal E_N.
 \label{eq:V8-law-variance}
\end{align}
In particular, for the periodic pure Wilson law \(\mu_{N,\beta}\), let
\(p_N(\beta)=\mathbb E_{\mu_{N,\beta}}d_p\) be the common elementary
plaquette defect.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mu_{N,\beta}}(f_N)
 \le \frac{10776}{25}K_{\rm fan}^2p_N(\beta)
 =3030750000\,p_N(\beta).}
 \label{eq:V8-variance-p}
\end{equation}
Consequently, uniformly over the nonwrapping native cards,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta\longrightarrow\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|f_N-K_{\rm fan}\|_{L^2(\mu_{N,\beta})}\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V8-full-extinction}
\end{equation}
In particular \(\operatorname{Var}(f_{N_r})\to0\) on every escaping
weak-facing root sequence, whether or not its escape rate is known.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Set \(D=D_N\).  The first bound is immediate from
\Cref{thm:V8-envelope}.  Since variance is the minimum squared distance to a
constant,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(f_N)
 \le\mathbb E_\nu(f_N-K_{\rm fan})^2
 =K_{\rm fan}^2\mathbb E_\nu D^2.
\]
Use \(D\le\min\{3/2,\mathcal E_N\}\) and
\(D^2\le(3/2)D\) to obtain \eqref{eq:V8-law-variance}.
Periodic hypercubic symmetry makes every expectation in the three face
classes equal to \(p_N(\beta)\).  Hence
\(\mathbb E\mathcal E_N=(7184/25)p_N(\beta)\), giving
\eqref{eq:V8-variance-p}.  The same upper bound applies to
\(\mathbb E(f_N-K_{\rm fan})^2\).

The imported volume-uniform plaquette estimate
\eqref{eq:V6-imported-plaquette} is
\[
 p_N(\beta)\le C_{\rm pl}\frac{1+\log\beta}{\beta}
\]
for sufficiently large \(\beta\), with a constant independent of \(N\).
Inserting it proves \eqref{eq:V8-full-extinction} and the claimed cofinal
consequence.  No root is computed or retuned in this argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[A coarse but decisive bound]
\label{rem:V8-constant-scope}
The coefficient \(3030750000\) is explicit and intentionally conservative.
It is not a sharp variance asymptotic and need not be useful at a moderate
selected coupling.  Its role is to settle the previously open cofinal
visibility premise.  A better constant cannot restore a positive limiting
variance in the same normalization.  For a nonperiodic or generated law,
\eqref{eq:V8-law-variance} remains pointwise-law valid, but its forty-four
plaquette expectations must be controlled in that law; the periodic value
\(p_N(\beta)\) is not substituted silently.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[The earlier visible escaping-native branch is empty]
\label{cor:V8-no-visible-branch}
In the notation of Versions~V6--V7, put
\[
 F_N=f_N-\mathbb E f_N,\qquad
 M_N=\mathbb E[F_N\mid\mathscr Q_N],\qquad
 \xi_N=F_N-M_N.
\]
On every escaping periodic Wilson sequence,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|F_N\|_2^2=\|M_N\|_2^2+\|\xi_N\|_2^2\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V8-all-stocks-collapse}
\end{equation}
Thus \(A_{F,N},A_{M,N},A_{\xi,N}\to0\).  For any possibly
cutoff-dependent record \(\mathscr A_N\), including a shell at a growing
physical radius,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathbb E[F_N\mid\mathscr A_N]\|_2^2
 \le\operatorname{Var}(f_N)\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V8-all-projections-collapse}
\end{equation}
No unrescaled descendant of this native source has a positive absolute
limiting stock.  In particular the uniform native variance floor in
\Cref{thm:V7-ancestry-stability} cannot hold on this escaping branch.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation is an orthogonal projection and hence a contraction.
Apply \Cref{thm:V8-native-collapse} and the existing Pythagoras identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Necessary cost of a renewed source calibration]
\label{cor:V8-renormalization-cost}
If a deterministic scale \(b_N\) is introduced and
\(\operatorname{Var}(b_Nf_N)\ge v_*>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 b_N^2p_N(\beta_N)\ge\frac{v_*}{3030750000}.
 \label{eq:V8-necessary-rescaling}
\end{equation}
For \(\beta_N\to\infty\), the imported plaquette upper bound further
forces
\[
 b_N^2\ge
 \frac{v_*\beta_N}{3030750000\,C_{\rm pl}(1+\log\beta_N)}.
\]
This is a necessary lower growth bound, not a sufficient renormalization,
not an exact scaling exponent, and not a prescription to change the frozen
physical source.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Multiply \eqref{eq:V8-variance-p} by \(b_N^2\) and rearrange.  A lower
bound on the normalization needed for noncollapse supplies no limiting law
or uniform integrability for the rescaled field.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The pure central reduced fibre has the same local extinction}

This paragraph is a separate law calculation.  It does not condition a
periodic expectation on an event of probability zero.  Use the literal
parity-tree fibre at \(W=I\), with \(45M^4\) free \(\SU(3)\) links,
\(96M^4\) plaquettes, and pure Wilson density
\[
 \nu_{\beta,M}(\dd z)=Z_{\beta,M}^{-1}
                   e^{-\beta V_M(z,I)}\dd m_{\rm red}(z).
\]
These are the reduced-fibre definitions of the supplied YM--A series; no
\(\Psi\ne0\) generated action is discarded by this notation.

\begin{proposition}[Pure central-fibre plaquette control without a Witten gap]
\label{prop:V8-fibre-plaquette}
There is a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(M\), such that for
large \(\beta\), every plaquette of the pure central fibre obeys
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{\nu_{\beta,M}}d_p
 \le C\frac{1+\log\beta}{\beta}.
 \label{eq:V8-fibre-plaquette}
\end{equation}
Therefore \(f_N\), evaluated in this section, also tends in \(L^2\) to
\(K_{\rm fan}\).  This assertion does not cover an arbitrary noncentral
background or an uncontrolled generated action.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
A neighbourhood of the identity in \(\SU(3)\) has exponential coordinates
in eight real dimensions with positive continuous Haar Jacobian.  Hence there
are \(c_0,r_0>0\) such that the Haar probability of
\(\|U-I\|_F\le r\) is at least \(c_0r^8\) for \(0<r\le r_0\).
Restrict every free link to radius \(\beta^{-1/2}\).  Tree and retained
links equal the identity.  The four-link telescoping estimate gives
\(d_p\le 8/(3\beta)\) on this product neighbourhood.  Writing
\(E=45M^4\), \(P=96M^4\), we obtain
\[
 Z_{\beta,M}\ge e^{-8P/3}(c_0\beta^{-4})^E,
 \qquad
 -\frac{\log Z_{\beta,M}}{P}
 \le\frac83+\frac{15}{32}(4\log\beta-\log c_0).
\]
The mean energy \(\mathbb E_{\nu_{t,M}}V_M\) decreases in \(t\), because
its derivative is \(-\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{t,M}}V_M\).  Since
\(Z_{0,M}=1\),
\[
 \beta\mathbb E_{\nu_{\beta,M}}V_M
 \le\int_0^\beta\mathbb E_{\nu_{t,M}}V_M\,\dd t
 =-\log Z_{\beta,M}.
\]
Thus the average plaquette defect is \(O((1+\log\beta)/\beta)\), uniformly
in \(M\).  Coarse-cell translation invariance gives at most ninety-six
plaquette types per cell.  Each individual mean is bounded by ninety-six
times the average, since all defects are nonnegative.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V8-fibre-plaquette}; \eqref{eq:V8-law-variance} then gives the
native extinction.  No spectral gap of the interacting Witten operator has
been assumed.
\end{proof}

\section{What the native fan actually measures: all thirty-three graph cycles}
\label{sec:V8-graph}

Let \(\mathcal G_F\) be the graph formed by the union of the forty staple
paths and four corner paths.  It has \(100\) edges and \(68\) vertices.
Let \(\partial:\R^{100}\to\R^{68}\) be its oriented incidence matrix.
For a word \(w\), write \(\ell(w)\) for its signed edge-occurrence vector.
Set
\[
 \ell_0=\ell(\Gamma_{(0,\ldots,0)}),\qquad
 d_{i,a}=\ell(P_{i,a})-\ell(P_{i,0}),\quad a\ne0,
\]
and assemble the \(100\times33\) integer matrix
\begin{equation}
 V=[\ell_0\mid(d_{i,a})_{i,a\ne0}].
 \label{eq:V8-cycle-basis}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[A complete cycle basis and an exact maximizer set]
\label{prop:V8-graph-maximizers}
The graph \(\mathcal G_F\) is connected, \(V\) has rank \(33\), and
\begin{equation}
 \Ran V=\Ker\partial,\qquad
 \dim\Ker\partial=100-68+1=33.
 \label{eq:V8-full-cycle-space}
\end{equation}
Moreover, for link configurations on this graph,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 f_N=K_{\rm fan}
 \iff
 U_{xy}=g_xg_y^{-1}\ \text{for some vertex family }(g_x).}
 \label{eq:V8-maximizer}
\end{equation}
Thus the maximum is exactly the graph pure-gauge orbit, not a larger
unobserved curvature family.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Each column of \(V\) is closed.  Every nonplanar staple has one transverse
parallel middle link which occurs in no other such staple and in no planar
staple or corner.  On these thirty-two private rows, the last thirty-two
columns of \(V\) form a signed identity matrix and the first column is
zero.  The remaining nonzero \(C_2\) column makes the rank \(33\).
Connectedness and the displayed counts are direct finite coordinate
calculations.  The cycle-dimension formula proves
\eqref{eq:V8-full-cycle-space}.

For the nonlinear statement, remove those thirty-two private links and one
edge \(e_*\) of \(C_2\), for example the positive direction-zero edge
based at \((-1,-1,0,0)\).  The remaining sixty-seven edges form a spanning
tree; this connectivity assertion is also replayed in the certificate.
Gauge every tree link to the identity.  The all-planar loop then contains
only the chord \(e_*\), with multiplicity one.  For each private chord,
the loop with that single nonplanar choice contains this chord exactly once,
no other private chord, and possibly \(e_*\).

Every term in the positive average \(f_N/K_{\rm fan}\) is at most one.
Equality of the average to one forces equality for the all-planar and the
thirty-two single-change loops.  A unitary has real trace three only when it
is the identity.  The base loop therefore fixes \(e_*\) to the identity,
and the single-change loops then fix every private chord to the identity.
All graph links are now the identity in tree gauge, proving the forward
implication.  The converse follows because all closed holonomies of a
pure-gauge connection are the identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact local marginal limit on escaping periodic Wilson cards]
\label{cor:V8-local-law}
Identify each translated native graph with the same fixed graph
\(\mathcal G_F\).  If \(\beta_N\to\infty\), its periodic Wilson link
marginal converges weakly to the measure
\begin{equation}
 \nu_F^{\rm flat}
 =\operatorname{Law}\{g_xg_y^{-1}:(x,y)\in E(\mathcal G_F)\},
 \label{eq:V8-flat-orbit-law}
\end{equation}
where the vertex variables are independent Haar variables.  In particular,
for every continuous gauge-invariant writer \(H\) on this fixed graph,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E H\to H(I),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(H)\to0.
 \label{eq:V8-all-native-observables}
\end{equation}
Individual gauge-dependent link variables do not have to converge to the
identity: the limit is the Haar measure on a pure-gauge orbit.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The graph configuration space is compact.  Any cluster measure has
\(D_N=0\) almost surely by \Cref{thm:V8-native-collapse} and continuity.
By \Cref{prop:V8-graph-maximizers}, its support is the pure-gauge orbit.
Every marginal is invariant under arbitrary gauge transformations at the
sixty-eight vertices, and this invariance passes to a weak limit.  That
compact group acts transitively on the pure-gauge orbit.  Its invariant
probability is unique: averaging any continuous test function over the group
gives one constant on the orbit, which every invariant probability must
integrate to that same value.  The pushforward in
\eqref{eq:V8-flat-orbit-law} has this invariance, so it is the unique cluster
measure.  Gauge-invariant \(H\) is constant on the orbit, and applying weak
convergence to \(H\) and \(|H|^2\) proves
\eqref{eq:V8-all-native-observables}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact first nonzero native jet}

Equip \(\mathfrak{su}(3)\) with \(\langle X,Y\rangle=-\Tr(XY)\).
For \(a=(a_e)_{e\in E(\mathcal G_F)}\), evaluate the native fan at
\(U_e(t)=e^{t a_e}\).  Define the real symmetric \(100\times100\) matrix
\begin{equation}
 Q_F:=\frac1{5^8}\sum_{\eta}\ell(\Gamma_\eta)\ell(\Gamma_\eta)^{\mathsf T}.
 \label{eq:V8-Q-definition}
\end{equation}
This finite tensor is a deterministic local Taylor coefficient, not a
covariance evaluated in a Gaussian replacement law.

\begin{theorem}[Complete native quadratic tensor and exact spectrum]
\label{thm:V8-quadratic-spectrum}
Let \(z_i\in\{0,e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4\}\subset\R^4\) encode the five choices
at position \(i\), independently and uniformly in the combinatorial label
average.  Put \(y=(1,z_1,\ldots,z_8)\), \(W=\mathbb E_\eta yy^{\mathsf T}\).
Then
\begin{equation}
 Q_F=VWV^{\mathsf T},\qquad W\succ0,
 \label{eq:V8-Q-factor}
\end{equation}
where \(25W\) has entries
\begin{equation}
 (25W)_{00}=25,\quad (25W)_{0j}=(25W)_{j0}=5,
 \quad
 (25W)_{ij}=
 \begin{cases}
 5,&i=j>0,\\
 0,&i\ne j\text{ in the same menu},\\
 1,&i,j\text{ in different menus}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:V8-W-entries}
\end{equation}
The complete spectrum, including multiplicities, is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{spec}(Q_F)=
 \left\{
 0^{[67]},\ (2/5)^{[15]},\ (4/5)^{[16]},\
 \frac{21-\sqrt{393}}5,\ \frac{21+\sqrt{393}}5
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V8-spectrum}
\end{equation}
If \(P_{\rm cyc}\) is the orthogonal cycle projection, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{21-\sqrt{393}}5P_{\rm cyc}
 \preceq Q_F\preceq
 \frac{21+\sqrt{393}}5P_{\rm cyc},\qquad
 \Ker Q_F=\Ran\partial^{\mathsf T}.}
 \label{eq:V8-cycle-frame}
\end{equation}
Finally,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 f_N(e^{t a})=K_{\rm fan}
 -\frac{K_{\rm fan}t^2}{6}
       \sum_{e,e'}(Q_F)_{ee'}\langle a_e,a_{e'}\rangle
 +O_a(t^3).}
 \label{eq:V8-native-jet}
\end{equation}
Thus \(Df_N(I)=0\), and the Hessian of \(K_{\rm fan}-f_N\) has rank
\(33\cdot8=264\), exactly all graph cycle directions in all eight colours.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The loop incidence satisfies \(\ell(\Gamma_\eta)=Vy\).  The moments of the
independent five-point choices give \eqref{eq:V8-W-entries}.  If
\(c^{\mathsf T}Wc=0\), then \(c^{\mathsf T}y=0\) for all choices.
The all-zero choice first kills \(c_0\), and each single nonzero choice
kills its corresponding coefficient.  Hence \(W\succ0\).  Together with
\Cref{prop:V8-graph-maximizers}, this proves the rank and kernel assertions.

The nonzero spectrum of \(25Q_F\) is the spectrum of the integer matrix
\(H=(25W)V^{\mathsf T}V\).  It is similar to the positive symmetric matrix
\((25W)^{1/2}V^{\mathsf T}V(25W)^{1/2}\).  Exact integer multiplication of
the displayed geometric matrix gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 H^4-240H^3+7700H^2-78000H+240000I=0,\\
 \Tr H=680,\qquad \Tr H^2=49600.
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:V8-polynomial-certificate}
\end{equation}
These three identities are the finite spectral certificate; the complete
matrices and a standard-library integer replay accompany this source.  The
annihilating polynomial factors as
\[
 (x-10)(x-20)(x^2-210x+1200).
\]
Its four real roots are distinct.  Rationality of \(H\) gives equal
multiplicity \(c\) to the two irrational conjugates.  If the other
multiplicities are \(a,b\), dimension and the two traces give
\[
 a+b+2c=33,\quad10a+20b+210c=680,\quad
 100a+400b+41700c=49600.
\]
The unique solution is \((a,b,c)=(15,16,1)\).  Dividing the roots by
\(25\) proves \eqref{eq:V8-spectrum}.  Positivity of the least root follows
from \(393<21^2\); it is smaller than \(2/5\) because \(393>19^2\).
This proves \eqref{eq:V8-cycle-frame} without a sampled eigenvalue.

For one loop, the first-order holonomy is
\(I+t\sum_e\ell_e a_e+O(t^2)\).  The trace of the first derivative is
zero.  Cyclicity of trace in the second derivative gives
\[
 \left.\frac{\dd^2}{\dd t^2}\mathcal O_\Gamma(e^{t a})\right|_{t=0}
 =-\frac13\left\|\sum_e\ell_e a_e\right\|^2.
\]
Average over the fixed dictionary to obtain \eqref{eq:V8-native-jet}.
The tensor is \((K_{\rm fan}/3)Q_F\otimes I_8\) for the deficit Hessian,
so its rank is \(264\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What the quadratic tensor does not say]
\label{rem:V8-jet-scope}
The constant in \eqref{eq:V8-cycle-frame} is a local graph-frame constant.
It is not the reduced-fibre \(\lambda_*\), a Wilson expectation, a
Witten spectral gap, a radial SDPI coefficient, or a Yang--Mills mass.
The exact jet shows that the surviving native observable is a quadratic
colour-singlet curvature composite.  It does not prove a fluctuation scale
\(a_e=O(\beta^{-1/2})\) uniformly in the cutoff or that multiplication of
\(f_N-\mathbb E f_N\) by \(\beta\) has a nontrivial limiting law.
\end{remark}

\section{The scalar-to-adjoint bridge is forbidden by the central colour symmetry}
\label{sec:V8-colour}

The following statement concerns a law that is invariant under constant
\(\SU(3)\) conjugation.  It applies to the pure central reduced fibre and
to any submitted generated action preserving that symmetry.  A noncentral
toron background generally has a smaller stabilizer and must be tested with
that stabilizer instead.

\begin{lemma}[A nine-element exact adjoint annihilator]
\label{lem:V8-colour-twirl}
Let \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}\),
\(C=\operatorname{diag}(1,\zeta,\zeta^2)\), and
\(Se_j=e_{j+1\pmod3}\).  These matrices lie in \(\SU(3)\), and for every
complex \(3\times3\) matrix \(X\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac19\sum_{a,b=0}^2 C^aS^bX S^{-b}C^{-a}
 =\frac{\Tr X}{3}I.
 \label{eq:V8-colour-twirl}
\end{equation}
In particular this average vanishes for every adjoint colour vector.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Averaging conjugation by \(C\) kills every off-diagonal matrix unit.
Averaging the three cyclic permutations then replaces the diagonal by its
mean.  Both determinants are one.  The exact replay checks the identity on
all nine matrix units in the ring \(\Z[\zeta]\), with
\(\zeta^2+\zeta+1=0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact singlet--adjoint selection rule]
\label{thm:V8-colour-selection}
Let \(\nu\) be an invariant law, let \(M\in L^2(\nu;\R)\) be a colour
singlet, and let
\(\mathcal J:E_{\rm dir}\otimes\mathfrak{sl}_3(\C)\to L^2(\nu)\)
be a complex-linear equivariant synthesis.  Thus, for the unitary action
\(\mathcal U_g\) on scalar functions,
\[
 \mathcal U_gM=M,\qquad
 \mathcal U_g\mathcal J(h\otimes X)
 =\mathcal J(h\otimes gXg^{-1}).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle M,\mathcal J(h\otimes X)\rangle=0
 \quad\text{for every }h,X.}
 \label{eq:V8-exact-cross-zero}
\end{equation}
In the covariance conventions of Version~V7, for a full equivariant adjoint
bank this means
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 x_{MJ}=0,\qquad
 \mathbb I_{J\mid M}=K_J,\qquad
 \mathbb C_{\rm cur}=6v_MK_J.}
 \label{eq:V8-ancestry-colour}
\end{equation}
The last two identities are read when \(v_M>0\); the cross-block vanishing
holds even when \(M=0\).  A zero ancestry residual is therefore possible
only for a zero current bank, not through improved scalar/current alignment.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Unitarity and invariance of \(M\) make
\(\langle M,\mathcal J(h\otimes X)\rangle\) unchanged by conjugating
\(X\).  Average over the nine conjugations in
\Cref{lem:V8-colour-twirl}.  Linearity and \(\Tr X=0\) give zero.
This proves the entire coefficient cross block, not just one preferred
colour polarization.  The remaining identities follow by substitution in
the already established covariance and replica formulas; those formulas are
not reproved here.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Application to the actual central-fibre score and Witten family]
\label{prop:V8-Witten-colour}
Suppose the literal reduced action \(\Phi(z,W)\) is invariant under
simultaneous global conjugation and the retained background is \(W=I\).
Its centred coarse score bank, its score gradient, and its minimum Witten
current family are equivariant in the adjoint coarse colour index.  Any
\emph{equivariant} physical route from that current family to scalar
boundary functions therefore satisfies \eqref{eq:V8-exact-cross-zero}
against the native fan, its centred outer conditional expectation, or any
bank of colour-singlet Wilson traces.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Differentiate
\(\Phi(gzg^{-1},gWg^{-1})=\Phi(z,W)\) at \(W=I\).  For the score
\(j_h=-D_h\Phi\) this gives
\(\mathcal U_gj_h=j_{\operatorname{Ad}_g h}\); centring preserves this
identity.  The exterior derivative is equivariant.  The fibre product metric
and law are invariant, so the weighted adjoint and the Witten operator
commute with the induced unitary action on forms.  Its supported inverse and
inverse square root consequently commute as well.  Hence the score gradient
and the current family transform by the same coarse adjoint index.
Composition with an equivariant route preserves this property.

The native fan is a sum of traces, so is a singlet.  The centre rotation
commutes with global conjugation; conditional expectation onto its invariant
record commutes with that conjugation whenever the law is invariant.  The
outer conditional writer is therefore also a singlet.  Apply
\Cref{thm:V8-colour-selection}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The source identification which must not be made]
\label{ass:V8-source-type}
The shared cofinal programme starts from a reflected \emph{half-score
synthesis} indexed by curvature-source coefficients.  It is not the scalar
Wilson-loop observable \(f_N\).  Version~V7's statement that its scalar
outer/current panel provides precisely that missing bridge was too strong
without an additional source identification.  On a symmetry-preserving
central-vacuum route, \eqref{eq:V8-exact-cross-zero} shows that the scalar
identification cannot work for a nonzero adjoint bank.  A positive
\(\mathbb I_{J\mid M}=K_J\) here is forced by source type; it is not
by itself a newly discovered physical current occurrence or a failing
Yang--Mills Hessian.

Fixing a test colour \(X\) does not remove the selection rule, since the
entire linear functional on \(X\) vanishes.  A field-dependent colour frame,
a symmetry-breaking conditioning, or an insertion carrying another adjoint
index is a different physical packet.  None is inserted retrospectively.
The existing adjoint-valued reflected source is the appropriate starting
point for the YM--A current-ancestry row.
\end{assessment}

\begin{remark}[Complex coefficient convention]
\label{rem:V8-complex-convention}
For a random column \(\mathbf J\), the map
\(h\mapsto h^*\mathbf J\) written in Version~V7 is conjugate-linear in
ordinary complex coordinates.  Its Hilbert-space synthesis interpretation
uses the conjugate coefficient space, or equivalently one first uses real
coefficients and then complexifies the corresponding linear synthesis.
The displayed covariance matrices and positive replica identities are
unchanged.  The selection rule above is stated directly for a linear
intertwiner, avoiding any adjoint ambiguity in that interpretation.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Why the native-collapse bound does not erase the physical source]
\label{prop:V8-growing-budget}
A contractible loop with an explicit \(m_N\)-plaquette word filling obeys
\[
 \mathbb E d(U_C)\le m_N^2 p_N(\beta_N)
\]
on a periodic Wilson law.  Hence this argument forces collapse for a growing
family only if its squared filling budget times \(p_N\) tends to zero.
For the frozen response rectangles this condition is not available.  In
fact, at every root of the same response \(\chi_N(\beta_N)=u_*>0\),
\begin{equation}
 p_N(\beta_N)\ge
 \frac{4096(1-e^{-u_*/2})}{81N^4},\qquad
 (A_N^{\max})^2p_N(\beta_N)\ge1-e^{-u_*/2},
 \label{eq:V8-physical-scale-obstruction}
\end{equation}
where \(A_N^{\max}=(3N/8)^2\).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The first inequality is the same nonabelian telescoping bound applied to the
specified filling; no fixed-size assumption enters it.  The root lower bound
and the maximal rectangle area in
\eqref{eq:V8-physical-scale-obstruction} are the imported
\texttt{thm:V5-response-plaquette-lower} of the dedicated trajectory
programme, recalled in the V8 source audit.  Their product is the second
inequality.  Thus the bound which closes the native branch does not supply a
vanishing bound for the physical rectangle family.  This is a statement about
the applicability of the estimate, not a proof of a positive variance for the
Creutz contrast.
\end{proof}

\label{thm:V8-export}
For the unaltered programme the following conclusions now hold.

\item The bounded-root contact result of Version~V5 and the conditional

\end{enumerate}
No assertion here decides weak-facing-root escape, the original radial

Combine \Cref{thm:V8-envelope,thm:V8-native-collapse,cor:V8-no-visible-branch,prop:V8-graph-maximizers,thm:V8-quadratic-spectrum,thm:V8-colour-selection,prop:V8-Witten-colour,prop:V8-growing-budget}.  The final limitations identify
objects not equated with the native writer by any of those results.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The first unclosed YM--B row]
\label{ass:V9-first-row}

      kernels;

      \(U_{N,R}^\square\), its conditional-expectation recursion, and Fisher

      are not selected-root radial values.
\end{enumerate}
The first unclosed row is the one named in \Cref{op:V8-next}: a direct,
source-relative finite-physical-width ratio with a certified nonzero
infinitesimal denominator.  The present continuation constructs a positive
finite-displacement card which converges to exactly that ratio and supplies a
rigorous denominator interval.  It does not assign the missing Wilson
expectation a value.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[Two distinct upstream scalars]
\label{fire:V9-two-scalars}
The unnormalized partition curvature of the reduced-fibre coarse-field
experiment and the normalized source Fisher transmission of this boundary
experiment are distinct targets.  A fibre-independent coarse action factor is
invisible to the normalized source likelihoods below, while it changes the
reduced-fibre physical Hessian.  Conversely, the radial likelihood card below
contains no direct second-action row and cannot close the YM--A first axial
symbol.  The two programmes remain complementary rather than mutually
substitutable.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The odd shell-likelihood source secant}
\label{sec:V9-odd-likelihood}
% =============================================================================

Fix one finite selected-root card \((N,\beta)\), and center the frozen physical
source \(Y_N^\square\) under \(\mu_{N,\beta}\).  Put
\begin{equation}
 K_N^\square:=\norm{Y_N^\square}_{L^\infty(\mu_{N,\beta})}<\infty.
 \label{eq:V9-source-bound}
\end{equation}
For every shell enclosing the source, retain the inherited source tilt
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\dd\mu_{N,\beta}^{\vartheta}}{\dd\mu_{N,\beta}}
 =\exp\!\left(\vartheta Y_N^\square-\psi_N(\vartheta)\right),
 \qquad
 \psi_N(\vartheta)=\log\mathbb E e^{\vartheta Y_N^\square}.
 \label{eq:V9-source-tilt}
\end{equation}
Let \(m_{N,R}^{\vartheta}\) be its shell marginal and define the likelihood
with respect to the untilted shell law by
\begin{equation}
 \ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta}(b)
 :=\frac{\dd m_{N,R}^{\vartheta}}{\dd m_{N,R}}(b)
 =\frac{\mathbb E[e^{\vartheta Y_N^\square}\mid B_{N,R}=b]}
        {\mathbb E e^{\vartheta Y_N^\square}}.
 \label{eq:V9-shell-likelihood}
\end{equation}
All these functions are strictly positive and bounded on a finite card.

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite-displacement likelihood tower]
\label{thm:V9-likelihood-tower}
For every \(R<S\) whose shells enclose the source,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \ell_{N,S}^{\vartheta}(B_{N,S})
 =\mathbb E\!\left[
   \ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta}(B_{N,R})\mid B_{N,S}
  \right].}
 \label{eq:V9-likelihood-tower}
\end{equation}
For adjacent shells this is
\begin{equation}
 \ell_{N,R+1}^{\vartheta}
 =\mathcal T_{N,R}\ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta},
 \label{eq:V9-likelihood-adjacent}
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal T_{N,R}\) is the already frozen reverse conditional
operator.  Differentiation at the origin gives
\begin{equation}
 \left.\partial_\vartheta\ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta}\right|_{\vartheta=0}
 =U_{N,R}^\square.
 \label{eq:V9-likelihood-derivative}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The inherited source-tilt theorem states that the forward annular kernel is
independent of \(\vartheta\).  Hence
\(m_{N,R}^{\vartheta}K_{N;R\to S}^{\to}=m_{N,S}^{\vartheta}\), while the
same identity at \(\vartheta=0\) transports \(m_{N,R}\) to \(m_{N,S}\).
Bayes disintegration gives, for every bounded test \(g\) on the outer shell,
\[
 \int g\ell_{N,S}^{\vartheta}\,\dd m_{N,S}
 =\int g(B_{N,S})\ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta}(B_{N,R})\,\dd\lambda_{N;R,S},
\]
which is exactly \eqref{eq:V9-likelihood-tower}.  The adjacent statement is
the definition of the Bayes-adjoint operator.  Differentiating
\eqref{eq:V9-shell-likelihood} at zero and using
\(\mathbb E Y_N^\square=0\) gives
\(\mathbb E[Y_N^\square\mid B_{N,R}]=U_{N,R}^\square\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Odd source-likelihood secant and its positive stock]
\label{def:V9-odd-secant}
For \(\vartheta\ne0\), put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}
 :=\frac{\ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta}-\ell_{N,R}^{-\vartheta}}
         {2\vartheta},
 \qquad
 J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}
 :=\norm{\mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}_{L^2(m_{N,R})}^{2}.}
 \label{eq:V9-odd-secant-stock}
\end{equation}
The secant is centered because both likelihoods integrate to one.  Its stock
is the expectation of the nonnegative shell writer
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr W_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}(b)
 :=\frac1{4\vartheta^2}
   \left(
    \frac{\mathbb E[e^{\vartheta Y_N^\square}\mid B_{N,R}=b]}
         {\mathbb E e^{\vartheta Y_N^\square}}
   -\frac{\mathbb E[e^{-\vartheta Y_N^\square}\mid B_{N,R}=b]}
         {\mathbb E e^{-\vartheta Y_N^\square}}
   \right)^2,}
 \label{eq:V9-positive-stock-writer}
\end{equation}
namely \(J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}=\mathbb E\mathscr W_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}\).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite-secant information Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V9-secant-Pythagoras}
For \(R<S\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr U_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}(B_{N,S})
 =\mathbb E\!\left[
   \mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}(B_{N,R})\mid B_{N,S}
  \right],}
 \label{eq:V9-secant-tower}
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}-J_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}
 &={}\norm{
       \mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}(B_{N,R})
       -\mathscr U_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}(B_{N,S})
      }_2^2\\
 &=\mathbb E\!\left[
   \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
    \mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}(B_{N,R})\mid B_{N,S}
   \right)
  \right]\ge0.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V9-secant-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
For consecutive shells the nonnegative loss writer is
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr D_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}(b,b')
 :=\left(
    \mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}(b)
    -\mathscr U_{N,R+1}^{[\vartheta]}(b')
   \right)^2.
 \label{eq:V9-loss-writer}
\end{equation}
For any \(R<S\), the consecutive martingale differences are pairwise
orthogonal and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}-J_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}
 =\sum_{q=R}^{S-1}\mathbb E\mathscr D_{N,q}^{[\vartheta]}.}
 \label{eq:V9-finite-width-loss-sum}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Subtract the \(-\vartheta\) instance of
\eqref{eq:V9-likelihood-tower} from the \(+\vartheta\) instance and divide by
\(2\vartheta\).  Conditional expectation is the orthogonal projection from
the old shell sigma-field onto the new one, so Pythagoras and the
conditional-variance identity give \eqref{eq:V9-secant-Pythagoras}.  Along a
nested shell filtration the reverse-martingale differences
\(\mathscr U_q^{[\vartheta]}-\mathscr U_{q+1}^{[\vartheta]}\) are mutually
orthogonal.  Telescoping the vector and taking its squared norm proves
\eqref{eq:V9-finite-width-loss-sum}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Direct finite-width secant transmission]
\label{cor:V9-direct-secant-ratio}
On the branch \(J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}>0\), define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Q_{N;R\to S}^{[\vartheta]}
 :=\frac{J_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}}
          {J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}
 =1-\frac{\sum_{q=R}^{S-1}
                 \mathbb E\mathscr D_{N,q}^{[\vartheta]}}
               {J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}
 \in[0,1].}
 \label{eq:V9-direct-secant-ratio}
\end{equation}
This is one finite-physical-width endpoint ratio.  It need not be evaluated by
multiplying separately rounded adjacent ratios.  If
\(J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}=0\), the secant is zero at every later shell, but no
claim about the infinitesimal source score is made until the finite-
 displacement error is controlled.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Divide \eqref{eq:V9-finite-width-loss-sum} by the positive old stock.  If the
old stock is zero, \eqref{eq:V9-secant-tower} and contractivity force every
later secant stock to vanish.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{A universal finite-displacement error and a certified denominator}
\label{sec:V9-error}
% =============================================================================

The next estimate is deliberately finite-card and source relative.  It
requires only the actual bound \(K_N^\square\), not a spectral gap, a
minorization coefficient, or a Taylor coefficient from the native fan.

\begin{lemma}[Third derivative of a bounded shell likelihood]
\label{lem:V9-third-derivative}
Let \(Y\) be centered and \(\abs{Y}\le K\), let \(\mathscr G\) be any
sub-sigma-field, and put
\begin{equation}
 \ell_t=\frac{\mathbb E[e^{tY}\mid\mathscr G]}{\mathbb E e^{tY}}.
 \label{eq:V9-abstract-likelihood}
\end{equation}
For every \(\tau\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{\abs t\le\tau}\norm{\partial_t^3\ell_t}_{\infty}
 \le16K^3e^{2K\tau}.}
 \label{eq:V9-third-derivative-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write
\[
 a_t=\mathbb E[e^{tY}\mid\mathscr G],
 \qquad
 \psi(t)=\log\mathbb E e^{tY},
 \qquad
 h_t=e^{-\psi(t)},
 \qquad
 \ell_t=a_th_t.
\]
For \(j=0,1,2,3\),
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\partial_t^ja_t}_\infty\le K^je^{K\tau}
 \qquad(\abs t\le\tau).
 \label{eq:V9-a-derivatives}
\end{equation}
Under the exponentially tilted law,
\[
 \psi'(t)=\mathbb E_tY,
 \qquad
 \psi''(t)=\operatorname{Var}_t(Y),
 \qquad
 \psi'''(t)=\mathbb E_t[(Y-\mathbb E_tY)^3].
\]
Thus
\begin{equation}
 \abs{\psi'}\le K,
 \qquad
 0\le\psi''\le K^2,
 \qquad
 \abs{\psi'''}\le2K^3.
 \label{eq:V9-psi-bounds}
\end{equation}
The last inequality follows from
\(\abs{Y-\mathbb E_tY}\le2K\) and
\(\mathbb E_t(Y-\mathbb E_tY)^2\le K^2\).  Also
\(h_t\le e^{K\tau}\), and differentiation gives
\[
 h_t'=-\psi'h_t,
 \quad
 h_t''=((\psi')^2-\psi'')h_t,
 \quad
 h_t'''=(-\psi'''+3\psi'\psi''-(\psi')^3)h_t.
\]
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \abs{h_t'}\le Ke^{K\tau},\qquad
 \abs{h_t''}\le2K^2e^{K\tau},\qquad
 \abs{h_t'''}\le6K^3e^{K\tau}.
 \label{eq:V9-h-derivatives}
\end{equation}
Leibniz' rule now yields
\[
 \partial_t^3(a_th_t)
 =a_t'''h_t+3a_t''h_t'+3a_t'h_t''+a_th_t'''.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:V9-a-derivatives} and
\eqref{eq:V9-h-derivatives}, the four coefficients are respectively bounded
by \(1,3,6,6\) times \(K^3e^{2K\tau}\).  Their sum proves
\eqref{eq:V9-third-derivative-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-secant approximation of the physical source score]
\label{thm:V9-secant-error}
For every nonzero real \(\vartheta\), put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_N(\vartheta)
 :=\frac83(K_N^\square)^3
     e^{2K_N^\square\abs\vartheta}\vartheta^2.}
 \label{eq:V9-epsilon}
\end{equation}
Then, simultaneously for every shell enclosing the source,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathscr U_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}-U_{N,R}^\square}_\infty
 \le\varepsilon_N(\vartheta),
 \qquad
 \abs{
  \sqrt{J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}
  -\sqrt{I_{N,R}^\square}
 }
 \le\varepsilon_N(\vartheta).}
 \label{eq:V9-score-stock-error}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left(\max\{0,\sqrt{J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}
                    -\varepsilon_N(\vartheta)\}\right)^2
 \le I_{N,R}^\square
 \le
 \left(\sqrt{J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}
                    +\varepsilon_N(\vartheta)\right)^2.}
 \label{eq:V9-stock-interval}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{lem:V9-third-derivative} to
\(Y=Y_N^\square\), \(\mathscr G=\sigma(B_{N,R})\), and
\(\tau=\abs\vartheta\).  The symmetric first-difference remainder gives
\[
 \left\|
  \frac{\ell_{\vartheta}-\ell_{-\vartheta}}{2\vartheta}
  -\ell_0'
 \right\|_\infty
 \le\frac{\vartheta^2}{6}
     \sup_{\abs t\le\abs\vartheta}\norm{\ell_t'''}_\infty,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V9-epsilon}.  By
\eqref{eq:V9-likelihood-derivative}, \(\ell_0'=U_{N,R}^\square\).
The \(L^2\) error is at most the same \(L^\infty\) error because the shell
law is a probability.  The reverse triangle inequality for norms gives the
second estimate in \eqref{eq:V9-score-stock-error}; squaring its two sides
gives \eqref{eq:V9-stock-interval}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Denominator-safe finite-width Fisher ratio]
\label{cor:V9-ratio-interval}
Let \(R<S\), abbreviate
\(\varepsilon=\varepsilon_N(\vartheta)\), and suppose
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt{J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}>\varepsilon.
 \label{eq:V9-denominator-pass}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left(
   \frac{\max\{0,\sqrt{J_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}}-\varepsilon\}}
        {\sqrt{J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}+\varepsilon}
  \right)^2
 \le\frac{I_{N,S}^\square}{I_{N,R}^\square}\\
 &\hspace{4em}\le
 \min\!\left\{1,
  \left(
   \frac{\sqrt{J_{N,S}^{[\vartheta]}}+\varepsilon}
        {\sqrt{J_{N,R}^{[\vartheta]}}-\varepsilon}
  \right)^2\right\}.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V9-ratio-interval}
\end{equation}
The lower denominator in \eqref{eq:V9-denominator-pass} is an actual source-
visibility certificate.  If it fails, the correct output is unresolved source
visibility at the chosen displacement, not contraction and not survival.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the lower and upper norm bounds in
\eqref{eq:V9-score-stock-error} at the two endpoint shells and divide by the
strictly positive old lower bound.  The extra upper cap one is the exact
conditional-expectation contraction
\(I_{N,S}^\square\le I_{N,R}^\square\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Outward interval inputs]
\label{cor:V9-outward-inputs}
Suppose a validated physical computation returns
\begin{equation}
 0\le\underline J_T\le J_{N,T}^{[\vartheta]}
 \le\overline J_T
 \qquad(T=R,S)
 \label{eq:V9-J-input-intervals}
\end{equation}
and an upper bound \(K_N^\square\le\overline K_N\).  Put
\begin{equation}
 \overline\varepsilon_N(\vartheta)
 =\frac83\overline K_N^3e^{2\overline K_N\abs\vartheta}\vartheta^2,
 \label{eq:V9-epsilon-outward}
\end{equation}
\begin{align}
 L_T&:=\left(
       \max\{0,\sqrt{\underline J_T}
                    -\overline\varepsilon_N(\vartheta)\}
      \right)^2,
 &
 U_T&:=\left(
       \sqrt{\overline J_T}
                    +\overline\varepsilon_N(\vartheta)
      \right)^2.
 \label{eq:V9-stock-outward}
\end{align}
Then \(I_{N,T}^\square\in[L_T,U_T]\).  If \(L_R>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{L_S}{U_R}
 \le\frac{I_{N,S}^\square}{I_{N,R}^\square}
 \le\min\left\{1,\frac{U_S}{L_R}\right\}.}
 \label{eq:V9-ratio-outward}
\end{equation}
Thus the physical ratio can be certified from positive endpoint stocks and a
source bound without subtracting two nearly equal infinitesimal Fisher
estimates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Monotonicity of square root and
\eqref{eq:V9-stock-interval} give the endpoint intervals.  Division of
positive intervals gives \eqref{eq:V9-ratio-outward}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A directly available bound for the Creutz source]
\label{prop:V9-Creutz-bound}
Let \(W_{\alpha,N}>0\) be the four frozen normalized loop means and let
\(\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}=\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}U_{C_{\alpha,N}}\).
The previously established cancellation of the four centering constants gives
\begin{equation}
 Y_N^\square
 =\sum_{\alpha\in\{11,00,10,01\}}
   \epsilon_\alpha\frac{\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}}{W_{\alpha,N}},
 \qquad
 (\epsilon_{11},\epsilon_{00},\epsilon_{10},\epsilon_{01})=(1,1,-1,-1).
 \label{eq:V9-Creutz-normalized}
\end{equation}
Since \(\abs{\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}}\le1\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_N^\square\le\sum_\alpha W_{\alpha,N}^{-1}.}
 \label{eq:V9-Creutz-K-bound}
\end{equation}
If a selected-root card supplies positive lower intervals
\(W_{\alpha,N}\ge\underline W_{\alpha,N}>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 \overline K_N:=\sum_\alpha\underline W_{\alpha,N}^{-1}
 \label{eq:V9-Creutz-K-outward}
\end{equation}
is an admissible input to \Cref{cor:V9-outward-inputs}.  A sharper direct
bound for \(Y_N^\square\) may replace this triangle estimate without changing
the theorem.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V9-Creutz-normalized} is the inherited normalized
four-loop definition after the signed constants cancel.  The normalized real
trace lies in \([-1/2,1]\), hence has absolute value at most one.  The triangle
inequality proves \eqref{eq:V9-Creutz-K-bound}; replacing each denominator by
a positive lower endpoint gives \eqref{eq:V9-Creutz-K-outward}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Target-native scope, fixed-card completeness, and cofinal use}
\label{sec:V9-scope-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-card completeness of the secant compiler]
\label{thm:V9-fixed-card-complete}
Fix a finite card and shells \(R<S\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item As \(\vartheta\to0\),
      \begin{equation}
       \mathscr U_{N,T}^{[\vartheta]}
       \longrightarrow U_{N,T}^\square
       \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty,
       \qquad
       J_{N,T}^{[\vartheta]}\longrightarrow I_{N,T}^\square
       \quad(T=R,S).
       \label{eq:V9-fixed-limit}
      \end{equation}
\item If \(I_{N,R}^\square>0\), then for every \(\delta>0\) there is a
      nonzero rational \(\vartheta\), chosen before the endpoint integrals are
      evaluated, for which the denominator condition
      \eqref{eq:V9-denominator-pass} holds and the interval in
      \eqref{eq:V9-ratio-interval} has width smaller than \(\delta\).
\item If \(I_{N,R}^\square=0\), the compiler does not manufacture a ratio.
      A nonzero finite secant at an isolated displacement may represent a
      higher odd source response and is not an infinitesimal visibility
      certificate by itself.
\end{enumerate}
Thus every finite nonzero physical source ratio is, in principle, decidable by
the positive secant card.  Uniform cofinal conditioning is a separate
quantitative row.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The estimate \eqref{eq:V9-score-stock-error} tends to zero as
\(\vartheta\to0\), proving item~\textup{(F1)}.  If the limiting old norm is
positive, continuity makes the lower denominator positive for all sufficiently
small displacements.  Both endpoint norm intervals then converge to their
exact values, and division is continuous at a positive denominator; rational
numbers are dense, proving item~\textup{(F2)}.  Item~\textup{(F3)} is the
logical boundary of the same estimate: when the derivative vanishes, a finite
central difference need not vanish identically.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Cofinal secant schedule and direct physical-width handoff]
\label{thm:V9-cofinal-handoff}
Let \((N_n,\beta_n,R_n,S_n)\) be selected physical cards with
\begin{equation}
 r_n:=a_{N_n}(S_n-R_n)
 \label{eq:V9-physical-width}
\end{equation}
and let \(\vartheta_n\ne0\) be predeclared displacements.  Suppose outward
endpoint intervals as in \Cref{cor:V9-outward-inputs} give \(L_{R,n}>0\), and
put
\begin{equation}
 \underline Q_n:=\frac{L_{S,n}}{U_{R,n}},
 \qquad
 \overline Q_n:=\min\left\{1,\frac{U_{S,n}}{L_{R,n}}\right\}.
 \label{eq:V9-Q-interval}
\end{equation}
Then the inherited radial source ratio satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \underline Q_n
 \le\frac{I_{N_n,S_n}^\square}{I_{N_n,R_n}^\square}
 \le\overline Q_n.}
 \label{eq:V9-physical-ratio-handoff}
\end{equation}
Accordingly:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item any uniform physical-width contraction inequality proved from
      \(\overline Q_n\) is a valid input to the already established cofinal
      contraction branch;
\item a uniform positive lower bound on \(\underline Q_n\) with
      \(r_n\to0\) is a contact-scale retained-source packet;
\item a uniform positive lower bound on \(\underline Q_n\) with
      \(\liminf r_n>0\) is a positive-range retained-source packet;
\item failure of \(L_{R,n}>0\) is returned as source-visibility failure of the
      present card and is not silently identified with radial contraction.
\end{enumerate}
These statements perform only the quantitative handoff; the gauge quotient,
minorization-collapse branch, boundary-score branch, and physical survivor
classification remain those of the inherited theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V9-physical-ratio-handoff} is
\eqref{eq:V9-ratio-outward} on each selected card.  The four conclusions are
exactly the inputs distinguished by the inherited physical-radius theorem:
an upper attenuation estimate, a retained fraction on shrinking width, a
retained fraction on positive width, or a missing entrance denominator.  No
new trichotomy is proved or substituted.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Relative-error criterion for asymptotic exactness]
\label{cor:V9-relative-error}
If exact secant stocks are available and
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\varepsilon_{N_n}(\vartheta_n)}
      {\sqrt{J_{N_n,R_n}^{[\vartheta_n]}}}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\varepsilon_{N_n}(\vartheta_n)}
      {\sqrt{J_{N_n,S_n}^{[\vartheta_n]}}}\longrightarrow0,
 \label{eq:V9-relative-error-condition}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N_n,S_n}^\square}{I_{N_n,R_n}^\square}
 =\frac{J_{N_n,S_n}^{[\vartheta_n]}}
        {J_{N_n,R_n}^{[\vartheta_n]}}
  (1+o(1)).}
 \label{eq:V9-ratio-asymptotic}
\end{equation}
The condition is not automatic when the normalized rectangle means become
small; the displacement schedule must resolve the growing source bound or a
sharper derivative enclosure must be supplied.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The reverse triangle inequality in
\eqref{eq:V9-score-stock-error} gives
\(
 \sqrt{I_{N_n,T_n}^\square}/
 \sqrt{J_{N_n,T_n}^{[\vartheta_n]}}=1+o(1)
\)
at both endpoints.  Squaring and dividing proves
\eqref{eq:V9-ratio-asymptotic}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Normalized radial invariance under scalar cylinder gains]
\label{prop:V9-gain-invariance}
Replace the unnormalized source-deformed cylinder at parameter \(\vartheta\)
by \(e^{-c(\vartheta)}\) times itself, where \(c\) is any real scalar
function independent of the Wilson configuration.  Then every normalized
law \(\mu_{N,\beta}^{\vartheta}\), shell likelihood
\(\ell_{N,R}^{\vartheta}\), odd secant, stock, loss, and ratio in this
continuation is unchanged.  The same transformation changes the unnormalized
log partition by \(c(\vartheta)\).  Hence the present card is complete for its
normalized radial target but cannot determine an unnormalized action
curvature.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The scalar gain cancels when the deformed cylinder is normalized.  Every
listed radial object is constructed from the resulting normalized laws and
the fixed shell projection.  The unnormalized log partition acquires the
additive term \(c\), so its second derivative need not be invariant.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What the attachments do and do not populate]
\label{ass:V9-attachment-status}
The new YM--A note supplies the partition-curvature nonidentifiability theorem

\section{Version V10 entry: move upstream of the composite source tilt}
\label{sec:V10-entry}
% =============================================================================

Version~V9 constructed a valid scalar positive card by placing the complete
Creutz source in an exponential deformation and taking a symmetric likelihood
secant.  That card remains useful whenever the composite source deformation is
itself an occurring and calibrated experiment.  Its finite-displacement error
and denominator test are not altered here.

The new audit identifies an earlier choice which must be made before that
experiment is charged.  The original selected source is already assembled
from four physically declared Wilson-loop writers on the base selected-root
law.  The radial target is only the norm ratio of their conditional source
messages.  It can therefore be reconstructed exactly from a four-dimensional
base-law message Gram, without introducing a neighboring source-deformed law,
a displacement schedule, or the growing sup-norm bound
\(K_N^\square\).  This is the target-native route when conditional replicas of
the original Wilson cylinder occur but a composite exponential source tilt has
not been independently loaded.

There is also an upstream stopping fact.  The attached dedicated trajectory
programme proves that positivity, analyticity, the strong-end area exponents,
the weak endpoint, and finiteness of the stable-root set do not determine
whether the weak-facing roots stay bounded or escape.  Thus no continuation of
the scalar response axioms can discharge the first item of
\Cref{op:V9-next}.  Root escape requires an actual Wilson correlation, force--
memory, area-cone, or direct response-envelope estimate.  The radial card below
is consequently formulated at an arbitrary already selected finite root and
is branch covariant.

\label{fire:V10-V9-valid}

Neither route populates the unnormalized partition curvature required by the
first axial YM--A card.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The four-loop source factorization on the original Wilson law}
\label{sec:V10-source-frame}
% =============================================================================

Use the fixed label order
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak I_\square=(11,00,10,01),
 \qquad
 \epsilon=(1,1,-1,-1)^{\mathsf T}.
 \label{eq:V10-labels-signs}
\end{equation}
Let
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal O
 =\bigl(\mathcal O_{11},\mathcal O_{00},
         \mathcal O_{10},\mathcal O_{01}\bigr)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 W=\mathbb E\mathcal O
 =\bigl(W_{11},W_{00},W_{10},W_{01}\bigr)^{\mathsf T},
 \label{eq:V10-loop-vector}
\end{equation}
where every \(W_\alpha>0\) on the finite selected card.  Put
\begin{equation}
 D_W=\operatorname{diag}(W_\alpha),
 \qquad
 X=\mathcal O-W,
 \qquad
 c=D_W^{-1}\epsilon.
 \label{eq:V10-centered-primitive-frame}
\end{equation}
The entries of \(X\) are bounded by two in absolute value, independently of
how small an individual loop mean is.

\begin{theorem}[Exact primitive-loop factorization of the Creutz source]
\label{thm:V10-source-factorization}
Let
\begin{equation}
 Y_\alpha=\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{W_\alpha}-1
 \label{eq:V10-normalized-loop-score}
\end{equation}
be the four already frozen centered loop writers.  Then the physical source is
exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Y_N^\square
 =\epsilon^{\mathsf T}(Y_\alpha)_\alpha
 =c^{\mathsf T}X.}
 \label{eq:V10-source-factorization}
\end{equation}
In particular, the large coefficients \(W_\alpha^{-1}\) belong to the final
contrast vector \(c\); they need not be inserted into a neighboring action in
order to evaluate the base-law radial stock.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By definition,
\[
 \epsilon^{\mathsf T}(Y_\alpha)_\alpha
 =\epsilon^{\mathsf T}D_W^{-1}\mathcal O
  -\epsilon^{\mathsf T}\one.
\]
The last term vanishes because the entries of \(\epsilon\) sum to zero.
Moreover
\(
 c^{\mathsf T}W=\epsilon^{\mathsf T}\one=0
\), so
\(
 \epsilon^{\mathsf T}D_W^{-1}\mathcal O
 =c^{\mathsf T}(\mathcal O-W)
\).  This is \eqref{eq:V10-source-factorization}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Relation with the previously known global contrast frame]
\label{ass:V10-global-frame}
The dedicated trajectory notes already show that four loop means and ten
ordinary second moments determine the complete equal-time contrast frame.
The new object below is different: it is the same four-dimensional source
frame after conditional expectation onto each physical boundary shell.  Its
nested Gram difference is the exact radial information loss.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Nested primitive message Grams and the exact radial quotient}
\label{sec:V10-message-Gram}
% =============================================================================

For every shell radius \(T\) enclosing the source, define the primitive
four-loop message and its Gram by
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf m_{N,T}
 :=\mathbb E[X\mid B_{N,T}]\in L^2(\mu_{N,\beta};\R^4),
 \qquad
 C_{N,T}:=\mathbb E[\mathbf m_{N,T}\mathbf m_{N,T}^{\mathsf T}].
 \label{eq:V10-primitive-message-Gram}
\end{equation}
Throughout this continuation, all expectations are taken in the already
selected base Wilson law unless a different law is displayed explicitly.

\begin{theorem}[Matrix conditional-expectation Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V10-matrix-Pythagoras}
Let \(R<S\).  Then
\begin{align}
 \mathbf m_{N,S}
 &=\mathbb E[\mathbf m_{N,R}\mid B_{N,S}],
 \label{eq:V10-vector-tower}\\
 C_{N,R}-C_{N,S}
 &=\boxed{
   \mathbb E\!
   \left[
    (\mathbf m_{N,R}-\mathbf m_{N,S})(\mathbf m_{N,R}-\mathbf m_{N,S})^{\mathsf T}
   \right]\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:V10-matrix-loss}
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 U_{N,T}^\square=c^{\mathsf T}\mathbf m_{N,T},
 \qquad
 I_{N,T}^\square=c^{\mathsf T}C_{N,T}c,}
 \label{eq:V10-source-stock-from-frame}
\end{equation}
and, whenever \(I_{N,R}^\square>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,S}^\square}{I_{N,R}^\square}
 =\frac{c^{\mathsf T}C_{N,S}c}
        {c^{\mathsf T}C_{N,R}c},
 \qquad
 I_{N,R}^\square-I_{N,S}^\square
 =c^{\mathsf T}(C_{N,R}-C_{N,S})c.}
 \label{eq:V10-exact-radial-ratio}
\end{equation}
The kernel inclusion
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\Ker C_{N,R}\subseteq\Ker C_{N,S}}
 \label{eq:V10-kernel-nesting}
\end{equation}
holds automatically.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The ordinary conditional-expectation tower applied componentwise to
\(X\) gives \eqref{eq:V10-vector-tower}.  Put
\(
 d=\mathbf m_{N,R}-\mathbf m_{N,S}
\).  Since
\(
 \mathbb E[d\mid B_{N,S}]=0
\), both cross matrices
\(
 \mathbb E[d \mathbf m_{N,S}^{\mathsf T}]
\) and their transposes vanish.  Expanding
\(
 \mathbf m_{N,R}=\mathbf m_{N,S}+d
\) therefore gives
\eqref{eq:V10-matrix-loss}.

By \Cref{thm:V10-source-factorization},
\[
 \mathbb E[Y_N^\square\mid B_{N,T}]
 =c^{\mathsf T}\mathbb E[X\mid B_{N,T}],
\]
which is the first identity in \eqref{eq:V10-source-stock-from-frame}.
Taking its squared norm gives the second.  Subtraction and division give
\eqref{eq:V10-exact-radial-ratio}.  Finally, if \(C_{N,R}v=0\), positivity
implies
\(v^{\mathsf T}C_{N,R}v=0\).  Since
\(0\preceq C_{N,S}\preceq C_{N,R}\), one also has
\(v^{\mathsf T}C_{N,S}v=0\), hence \(C_{N,S}v=0\).
\end{proof}

For a coordinate-free normalized loss, let
\begin{equation}
 P_{N,R}=C_{N,R}C_{N,R}^{\dagger},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{N;S\mid R}
 =C_{N,R}^{\dagger/2}
  (C_{N,R}-C_{N,S})
  C_{N,R}^{\dagger/2}.
 \label{eq:V10-normalized-loss}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Exact source-frame Rayleigh card]
\label{cor:V10-Rayleigh-card}
One has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{0\preceq\Lambda_{N;S\mid R}\preceq P_{N,R}.}
 \label{eq:V10-loss-window}
\end{equation}
If \(I_{N,R}^\square>0\), put
\begin{equation}
 z_{N,R}
 =\frac{C_{N,R}^{1/2}c}{\sqrt{I_{N,R}^\square}}.
 \label{eq:V10-normalized-source-coordinate}
\end{equation}
Then \(z_{N,R}\in\Ran P_{N,R}\), \(\|z_{N,R}\|=1\), and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,S}^\square}{I_{N,R}^\square}
 =1-\ip{z_{N,R}}{\Lambda_{N;S\mid R}z_{N,R}}.}
 \label{eq:V10-Rayleigh-ratio}
\end{equation}
Thus failure of radial contraction on the physical Creutz source is a
near-kernel statement in the four-dimensional primitive loop-message frame,
not an unspecified ambient shell mode.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Congruence of
\(
 0\preceq C_{N,R}-C_{N,S}\preceq C_{N,R}
\)
by \(C_{N,R}^{\dagger/2}\) gives
\eqref{eq:V10-loss-window}.  The norm of \(z_{N,R}\) is
\[
 \frac{c^{\mathsf T}C_{N,R}c}{I_{N,R}^\square}=1.
\]
The support nesting in \eqref{eq:V10-kernel-nesting} implies that the loss
matrix is supported on \(\Ran P_{N,R}\).  Therefore
\[
 \ip{z_{N,R}}{\Lambda_{N;S\mid R}z_{N,R}}
 =\frac{c^{\mathsf T}(C_{N,R}-C_{N,S})c}
       {I_{N,R}^\square},
\]
and \eqref{eq:V10-Rayleigh-ratio} follows from
\eqref{eq:V10-exact-radial-ratio}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact acquisition on the undeformed selected-root cylinder}
\label{sec:V10-base-law-acquisition}
% =============================================================================

Fix one shell \(T\).  Draw \(B_{N,T}\) from its actual marginal and,
conditionally on that shell, draw two independent source interiors
\(u_1,u_2\).  Write
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal O^{(j)}=\mathcal O(u_j),
 \qquad
 X^{(j)}=\mathcal O^{(j)}-W,
 \qquad j=1,2.
 \label{eq:V10-two-interior-replicas}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact endpoint replica reconstruction]
\label{thm:V10-replica-reconstruction}
The primitive shell-message Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 C_{N,T}
 =\mathbb E[X^{(1)}(X^{(2)})^{\mathsf T}]
 =G_{N,T}-WW^{\mathsf T},}
 \label{eq:V10-replica-Gram}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 G_{N,T}
 :=\mathbb E[\mathcal O^{(1)}(\mathcal O^{(2)})^{\mathsf T}].
 \label{eq:V10-raw-replica-Gram}
\end{equation}
The matrix is symmetric, so four loop means and ten real cross-replica
moments at each endpoint determine the exact radial card
\eqref{eq:V10-exact-radial-ratio}.  The four means are already part of the
selected Creutz response; the genuinely new boundary data are therefore ten
moments per endpoint.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditionally on \(B_{N,T}\), independence gives
\[
 \mathbb E[X^{(1)}(X^{(2)})^{\mathsf T}\mid B_{N,T}]
 =\mathbf m_{N,T}\mathbf m_{N,T}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Averaging gives the first identity.  Expanding
\(
 X^{(j)}=\mathcal O^{(j)}-W
\)
and using
\(
 \mathbb E\mathcal O^{(j)}=W
\)
gives the second.  Symmetry follows because the conditional value is an outer
product of one real vector with itself.
\end{proof}

The signed cross moments in \eqref{eq:V10-raw-replica-Gram} can themselves be
obtained from positive outcome probabilities.  For every replica and loop
label, append an independent calibrated sign bit
\(S_{j,\alpha}\in\{-1,+1\}\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P(S_{j,\alpha}=+1\mid\mathcal O_\alpha^{(j)}=o)
 =\frac{1+o}{2}.
 \label{eq:V10-threshold-bit}
\end{equation}
This is admissible because
\(-1\le\mathcal O_\alpha\le1\).

\begin{corollary}[Positive two-bit implementation]
\label{cor:V10-positive-bit}
For every \(\alpha,\gamma\),
\begin{align}
 W_\alpha
 &=\mathbb E S_{j,\alpha},
 \label{eq:V10-bit-mean}\\
 (G_{N,T})_{\alpha\gamma}
 &=\mathbb E[S_{1,\alpha}S_{2,\gamma}]
 =2\mathbb P(S_{1,\alpha}=S_{2,\gamma})-1.
 \label{eq:V10-bit-cross}
\end{align}
Hence the entire exact base-law frame may be reconstructed from ordinary
nonnegative two-bit outcome frequencies.  A direct deterministic loop Read is
an equivalent and simpler implementation when the link configuration is
already available.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the conditional mean of
\eqref{eq:V10-threshold-bit}.  Given the two loop values and the two independent
randomizers,
\[
 \mathbb E[S_{1,\alpha}S_{2,\gamma}
           \mid\mathcal O^{(1)},\mathcal O^{(2)}]
 =\mathcal O_\alpha^{(1)}\mathcal O_\gamma^{(2)}.
\]
Averaging gives the first equality in \eqref{eq:V10-bit-cross}; the second is
the elementary identity for a product of two sign bits.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Comparator occurrence and calibration]
\label{fire:V10-bit-occurrence}
The sign-bit realization is an acquisition option, not an automatically
occurring Wilson variable.  Its randomizer, threshold rule, and common-shell
replica incidence must be fixed before the outcomes are read.  If the loop
values are integrated directly, no auxiliary bit is needed.  Algebraically
compatible bit tables acquired on different shell populations do not populate
\eqref{eq:V10-replica-Gram}.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Why response roots and global loop moments do not determine radial transport}
\label{sec:V10-nonidentifiability}
% =============================================================================

\begin{proposition}[Base response data do not determine a shell coefficient]
\label{prop:V10-marginals-no-radial}
There are two finite cards with the same base law of
\((\mathcal O_{11},\mathcal O_{00},\mathcal O_{10},\mathcal O_{01})\), the
same four means, every same-law loop moment, the same Creutz response, and the
same inner record, but with radial source ratios one and zero.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Take any centered nonzero Creutz source \(Y\) on a finite probability space
and let the inner record reveal \(Y\).  In the first card take the outer record
to be the same record.  Then
\(
 \mathbb E[Y\mid B_S]=\mathbb E[Y\mid B_R]=Y
\), so the ratio is one.  In the second card take the outer record to be
trivial.  Then
\(
 \mathbb E[Y\mid B_S]=\mathbb EY=0
\), so the ratio is zero.  The base law and all of its loop moments are
unchanged.  Only the physical record map differs.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Upstream consequence for the weak-facing problem]
\label{ass:V10-root-consequence}
The weak-facing root determines which base Wilson law is selected; it does not
determine how much of the Creutz source is visible at a later physical shell.
Conversely, the exact frame card can be populated at any selected finite root
without first proving a cofinal root theorem.  Root escape and radial
transmission are independent physical rows and must not be used to infer one
another.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{A validated denominator-safe compiler for the exact frame}
\label{sec:V10-interval-compiler}
% =============================================================================

Suppose a validated computation provides positive mean intervals
\begin{equation}
 0<\underline W_\alpha
 \le W_\alpha
 \le\overline W_\alpha\le1
 \label{eq:V10-mean-intervals}
\end{equation}
and symmetric approximants \(\widehat C_T\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \norm{C_{N,T}-\widehat C_T}_{\rm op}\le\delta_T,
 \qquad T\in\{R,S\}.
 \label{eq:V10-C-error}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{align}
 \widehat c_\alpha
 &:=\frac{\epsilon_\alpha}{2}
    \left(
     \frac1{\underline W_\alpha}
     +\frac1{\overline W_\alpha}
    \right),
 \label{eq:V10-c-mid}\\
 h_\alpha
 &:=\frac12
    \left(
     \frac1{\underline W_\alpha}
     -\frac1{\overline W_\alpha}
    \right),
 \qquad
 \eta_c:=\left(\sum_\alpha h_\alpha^2\right)^{1/2}.
 \label{eq:V10-c-radius}
\end{align}
Then \(\|c-\widehat c\|\le\eta_c\).

\begin{lemma}[Uniform primitive-message Gram bound]
\label{lem:V10-C-bound}
For every shell and every finite Wilson card,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\norm{C_{N,T}}_{\rm op}\le16.}
 \label{eq:V10-C-uniform-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Each component of \(X=\mathcal O-W\) has absolute value at most two, so
\(\|X\|_{\mathbb R^4}\le4\).  Conditional Jensen gives
\(\|\mathbf m_{N,T}\|\le4\).  Hence, for every unit vector \(v\),
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}C_{N,T}v
 =\mathbb E|v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf m_{N,T}|^2
 \le\mathbb E\|\mathbf m_{N,T}\|^2
 \le16.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Outward exact-frame stock intervals]
\label{thm:V10-stock-interval}
Put
\begin{align}
 \widehat I_T
 &:=\widehat c^{\mathsf T}\widehat C_T\widehat c,
 \label{eq:V10-I-hat}\\
 E_T
 &:=16\eta_c(2\|\widehat c\|+\eta_c)
    +\delta_T\|\widehat c\|^2,
 \label{eq:V10-I-error}\\
 L_T&:=\max\{0,\widehat I_T-E_T\},
 \qquad
 U_T:=\widehat I_T+E_T.
 \label{eq:V10-I-interval}
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{I_{N,T}^\square\in[L_T,U_T].}
 \label{eq:V10-stock-outward}
\end{equation}
If \(L_R>0\), the exact radial ratio obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{L_S}{U_R}
 \le\frac{I_{N,S}^\square}{I_{N,R}^\square}
 \le\min\left\{1,\frac{U_S}{L_R}\right\}.}
 \label{eq:V10-ratio-outward}
\end{equation}
If \(L_R=0\), the card is source-visibility \(\mathsf{STOP}\), not a
contraction verdict.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(e=c-\widehat c\).  Using the true positive Gram in the coefficient
error terms gives
\begin{align*}
 &\left|
 c^{\mathsf T}C_{N,T}c
 -\widehat c^{\mathsf T}\widehat C_T\widehat c
 \right|\notag\\
 &\quad\le
 |e^{\mathsf T}C_{N,T}c|
 +|\widehat c^{\mathsf T}C_{N,T}e|
 +|\widehat c^{\mathsf T}(C_{N,T}-\widehat C_T)
                      \widehat c|\\
 &\quad\le
 16\eta_c(\|c\|+\|\widehat c\|)
 +\delta_T\|\widehat c\|^2\\
 &\quad\le E_T,
\end{align*}
where \Cref{lem:V10-C-bound} and
\(\|c\|\le\|\widehat c\|+\eta_c\) were used.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V10-stock-outward}.  Division of two positive intervals gives the
first two bounds in \eqref{eq:V10-ratio-outward}; the exact matrix
Pythagoras supplies the additional upper bound one.
\end{proof}

The matrix error in \eqref{eq:V10-C-error} may be obtained directly from the
raw replica matrix.  If
\begin{equation}
 \norm{G_{N,T}-\widehat G_T}_{\rm op}\le\delta_T^G,
 \qquad
 \norm{W-\widehat W}\le\eta_W,
 \label{eq:V10-raw-errors}
\end{equation}
then \(\|W\|\le2\) and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{C_{N,T}-(\widehat G_T-\widehat W\widehat W^{\mathsf T})}_{\rm op}
 \le
 \delta_T^G+\eta_W(4+\eta_W).}
 \label{eq:V10-raw-to-centered-error}
\end{equation}
Indeed,
\[
 WW^{\mathsf T}-\widehat W\widehat W^{\mathsf T}
 =(W-\widehat W)W^{\mathsf T}
  +\widehat W(W-\widehat W)^{\mathsf T},
\]
and
\(\|\widehat W\|\le2+\eta_W\).

\begin{corollary}[Entrywise quadrature errors]
\label{cor:V10-entrywise-errors}
If a symmetric matrix approximant has certified entry errors
\(
 |(C_{N,T}-\widehat C_T)_{\alpha\gamma}|
 \le e_{\alpha\gamma}
\), then one may take
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \delta_T
 =\left(
   \sum_\alpha e_{\alpha\alpha}^2
   +2\sum_{\alpha<\gamma}e_{\alpha\gamma}^2
  \right)^{1/2}.}
 \label{eq:V10-entry-Frobenius}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, whose square is exactly
the displayed symmetric entry count.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Support and status semantics]
\label{fire:V10-status}
The exact inputs satisfy
\(
 C_{N,R}\succeq C_{N,S}\succeq0
\).  A submitted interval packet which is
provably incompatible with those cone constraints is ill typed and is
reported as \(\mathsf{ERROR}\), not as a Yang--Mills obstruction.  Failure of
the lower source-stock endpoint is \(\mathsf{UNRESOLVED}\) or
\(\mathsf{STOP}\) at source visibility.  A contraction or survivor verdict is
returned only from a strict ratio interval on a physically occurring card.
\end{firewall}
