\section{The exact four-dimensional failure object}
\label{sec:V10-extremizer}
% =============================================================================

The finite source frame also identifies the only possible noncircular failure
object when a sequence of radial ratios tends to one.  For a positive
semidefinite matrix \(C\), let
\(
 \lambda_{\min}^+(C)
\) denote its least positive eigenvalue.

\begin{theorem}[Frame-softening or a primitive-loop no-loss survivor]
\label{thm:V10-frame-survivor}
Consider a sequence of selected cards and physical widths
\((R_n,S_n)\), with
\begin{equation}
 I_{n,R_n}^\square\ge i_*>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{I_{n,S_n}^\square}{I_{n,R_n}^\square}\longrightarrow1.
 \label{eq:V10-near-unit-hyp}
\end{equation}
After passage to a subsequence, at least one of the following occurs.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item \textbf{Primitive-frame softening:}
      \begin{equation}
       \lambda_{\min}^+(C_{n,R_n})\longrightarrow0.
       \label{eq:V10-frame-softening}
      \end{equation}
      This is a loss of conditioning or a support transition in the four-loop
      message frame.
\item \textbf{Stable-frame no-loss survivor:} the ranks of \(C_{n,R_n}\)
      are constant, their least positive eigenvalues are bounded below, and,
      after identifying the four loop labels, there are limits
      \begin{equation}
       C_{n,R_n}\to C_R^\infty,
       \qquad
       C_{n,S_n}\to C_S^\infty,
       \qquad
       z_{n,R_n}\to z_\infty,
       \label{eq:V10-frame-limits}
      \end{equation}
      with \(\|z_\infty\|=1\) and
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \Lambda_\infty z_\infty=0,
       \qquad
       \Lambda_\infty
       =(C_R^\infty)^{\dagger/2}
        (C_R^\infty-C_S^\infty)
        (C_R^\infty)^{\dagger/2}.}
       \label{eq:V10-limit-no-loss}
      \end{equation}
      The corresponding normalized physical source messages are the images
      of \(z_{n,R_n}\) under the source-minimal four-loop frame synthesis.
\end{enumerate}
Thus a near-unit physical-source channel cannot remain an unnamed shell
singular vector: it either exposes collapse of the actual four-loop source
metric or produces a normalized no-loss contrast in that metric.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The matrices \(C_{n,T}\) have norm at most sixteen by
\Cref{lem:V10-C-bound}, so they have convergent subsequences.  If
\eqref{eq:V10-frame-softening} occurs, take the first branch.  Otherwise pass
to a subsequence on which the rank is constant and the positive spectrum is
bounded below by some \(\mu>0\).  Spectral projections and Moore--Penrose
inverse square roots are then continuous, so the normalized loss matrices
\(
 \Lambda_{n;S_n\mid R_n}
\)
converge to \(\Lambda_\infty\).

Every \(z_{n,R_n}\) is a unit vector in a fixed four-dimensional space; take a
further convergent subsequence.  By \Cref{cor:V10-Rayleigh-card},
\[
 \ip{z_{n,R_n}}
     {\Lambda_{n;S_n\mid R_n}z_{n,R_n}}
 =1-\frac{I_{n,S_n}^\square}{I_{n,R_n}^\square}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Passing to the limit gives
\(
 \ip{z_\infty}{\Lambda_\infty z_\infty}=0
\).  Positivity of \(\Lambda_\infty\) implies
\(\Lambda_\infty z_\infty=0\).

For the final interpretation, let
\(
 \mathscr M_{n,R}a=a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf m_{n,R}
\).  Its Gram is \(C_{n,R}\), so
\(
 \mathscr V_{n,R}=\mathscr M_{n,R}C_{n,R}^{\dagger/2}
\)
is an isometry on the supported coefficient space.  Direct substitution gives
\[
 \mathscr V_{n,R}z_{n,R}
 =\frac{U_{n,R}^\square}{\sqrt{I_{n,R}^\square}}.
\]
Thus the limiting coefficient is attached to the actual normalized physical
source message.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Physical-radius typing of the frame survivor]
\label{cor:V10-radius-typing}
Let
\(
 r_n=a_{N_n}(S_n-R_n)
\) be the selected physical width.  On the stable-frame branch of
\Cref{thm:V10-frame-survivor}, a subsequence with \(r_n\to0\) is a
contact-scale retained-source packet, whereas
\(\liminf r_n>0\) is a positive-range retained-source packet.  If a strict
uniform upper ratio below one is instead certified, the inherited contraction
branch applies.  This corollary identifies the finite source coefficient; it
does not convert the spatial shell channel into an Osterwalder--Schrader time
semigroup.
\end{corollary}

\section{Version V11 entry: remove target inflation before another acquisition}
\label{sec:V11-entry}
% =============================================================================

Version~V10 reconstructed the complete four-dimensional message Gram of the
four primitive Wilson loops.  That packet is exact and remains necessary when
the requested output includes the primitive loss direction, support rank, or
frame-softening witness.  The immediate YM--B target is weaker: it is the
single selected-source ratio
\[
 \frac{I_{N,S}^{\square}}{I_{N,R}^{\square}}
\]
on one already frozen physical shell pair.  Acquiring twenty primitive-loop
cross moments merely to obtain this scalar is therefore not target minimal.

The correct upstream reduction has two parts.  First, the radial information
loss is exactly the Fisher information of the \emph{Bayes-reverse shell
kernel} under the already declared source tilt.  Thus the primary card is one
old source stock and one reverse-posterior loss.  Second, if a positive
bounded-output Read is desired, the entire source may be compressed before
replication to one calibrated sign bit.  One equality-event probability at
each endpoint then determines the exact radial ratio.  The four-loop matrix
card is reopened only after a near-unit ratio when the direction of failure is
itself part of the output.

\begin{assessment}[Earlier root information retained but not repeated]
\label{ass:V11-root-retained}
The dedicated trajectory programme already proves that the weak-facing roots
leave the complete pinned-sheet strong-coupling corridor and supplies the
static-force/returning-memory and finite-depth area-cone routes for extending
that exclusion.  It also proves that the scalar endpoint axioms alone do not
decide escape.  Version~V11 neither repeats those results nor fits a new root.
All statements below are branch covariant at an arbitrary selected finite
root.  The unresolved intermediate-coupling root row remains logically
separate from the radial Read.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[Target-native correction, not deletion of V10]
\label{fire:V11-target-native}
The scalar card below does not reconstruct the primitive four-loop message
matrix, its kernel, or the polarization of a surviving no-loss direction.
Version~V10 remains the correct diagnostic packet for those stronger targets.
Conversely, no full matrix packet is charged merely to decide one selected
source ratio.  This distinction is an information reduction after the source,
shells, and physical width have already been fixed; it is not a change of
source or geometry.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The source tilt changes only the Bayes-reverse shell kernel}
\label{sec:V11-Bayes-reverse}
% =============================================================================

Fix one finite selected-root Wilson card and two shell radii $R<S$ enclosing
the complete physical source.  Write
\[
 m_R=m_{N,R},\qquad m_S=m_{N,S},\qquad
 \lambda_{R,S}=m_RK_{R\to S}^{\to}=m_SK_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}
\]
for the shell marginals, their joint law, and the composed forward and reverse
kernels.  The superscripts $N,\beta$ are suppressed in this section.  Retain
the centered source tilt
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\dd\mu^{\vartheta}}{\dd\mu}
 =e^{\vartheta Y^{\square}-\psi(\vartheta)},
 \qquad
 \ell_T^{\vartheta}
 =\frac{\dd m_T^{\vartheta}}{\dd m_T}
 =\frac{\mathbb E[e^{\vartheta Y^{\square}}\mid B_T]}
        {\mathbb E e^{\vartheta Y^{\square}}},
 \quad T\in\{R,S\}.
 \label{eq:V11-shell-likelihoods}
\end{equation}
The inherited local-source theorem gives
\begin{equation}
 K_{R\to S}^{\to,\vartheta}=K_{R\to S}^{\to},
 \qquad
 \ell_S^{\vartheta}(B_S)
 =\mathbb E[\ell_R^{\vartheta}(B_R)\mid B_S].
 \label{eq:V11-fixed-forward-tower}
\end{equation}
Strict positivity of the exponential tilt implies
$\ell_R^{\vartheta},\ell_S^{\vartheta}>0$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact Bayes-reverse likelihood and source-loss score]
\label{thm:V11-Bayes-reverse}
The tilted reverse kernel is absolutely continuous with respect to the base
reverse kernel and obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow,\vartheta}(b_S,\cdot)}
      {\dd K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}(b_S,\cdot)}(b_R)
 =\frac{\ell_R^{\vartheta}(b_R)}
        {\ell_S^{\vartheta}(b_S)}.}
 \label{eq:V11-reverse-likelihood}
\end{equation}
Its score at the base law is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left.\partial_{\vartheta}\right|_{0}
 \log\frac{\dd K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow,\vartheta}}
          {\dd K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}}
 =U_R^{\square}(B_R)-U_S^{\square}(B_S).}
 \label{eq:V11-reverse-score}
\end{equation}
It is centered conditionally on $B_S$, and its Fisher information is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{R\mid S}^{\leftarrow,\square}
 :=\int\left|U_R^{\square}(b_R)-U_S^{\square}(b_S)\right|^2
       \dd\lambda_{R,S}
 =I_R^{\square}-I_S^{\square}.}
 \label{eq:V11-reverse-Fisher-loss}
\end{equation}
Thus the outward source-information loss is not a deformation of the forward
Wilson kernel.  It is the amount by which the posterior law of the old shell
changes when the source tilt is inferred from the outer shell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Under the source tilt the joint shell law may be factored in the forward
orientation as
\[
 \dd\lambda_{R,S}^{\vartheta}(b_R,b_S)
 =\ell_R^{\vartheta}(b_R)\,
   \dd m_R(b_R)K_{R\to S}^{\to}(b_R,\dd b_S),
\]
because the forward kernel is unchanged.  Its outer marginal is
$\ell_S^{\vartheta}m_S$.  Factoring the same joint law in the reverse
orientation and dividing by
$m_S^{\vartheta}K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}$ gives
\eqref{eq:V11-reverse-likelihood}.  Differentiating the logarithm at zero and
using
$\partial_{\vartheta}\ell_T^{\vartheta}|_0=U_T^{\square}$ proves
\eqref{eq:V11-reverse-score}.  The likelihood ratio in
\eqref{eq:V11-reverse-likelihood} integrates to one in $b_R$ for every
$b_S$, so its score is conditionally centered.  Finally, the inherited
conditional-expectation Pythagoras gives
\[
 \|U_R^{\square}-U_S^{\square}\|_{L^2(\lambda_{R,S})}^2
 =\|U_R^{\square}\|_2^2-\|U_S^{\square}\|_2^2,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V11-reverse-Fisher-loss}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Irreducible two-scalar radial card]
\label{cor:V11-two-scalar-card}
On the visible branch $I_R^{\square}>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_S^{\square}}{I_R^{\square}}
 =1-
 \frac{\mathcal J_{R\mid S}^{\leftarrow,\square}}
      {I_R^{\square}}.}
 \label{eq:V11-two-scalar-ratio}
\end{equation}
Hence the selected-source radial verdict requires only the two nonnegative
scalars
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 I_R^{\square},\qquad
 \mathcal J_{R\mid S}^{\leftarrow,\square}.}
 \label{eq:V11-two-positive-scalars}
\end{equation}
Equivalently one may use the two endpoint stocks $I_R^{\square},I_S^{\square}$.
If $I_R^{\square}=0$, then $I_S^{\square}=0$ and the card returns source
invisibility rather than contraction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Substitute \eqref{eq:V11-reverse-Fisher-loss}.  Monotonicity gives
$0\le I_S^{\square}\le I_R^{\square}$.  The zero-denominator statement is
the same monotonicity.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact finite-displacement posterior information chains}
\label{sec:V11-information-chains}
% =============================================================================

For probability measures $\nu\ll\rho$, write
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(\nu\Vert\rho)
 =\int\log\frac{\dd\nu}{\dd\rho}\,\dd\nu,
 \qquad
 \chi^2(\nu\Vert\rho)
 =\int\left(\frac{\dd\nu}{\dd\rho}-1\right)^2\dd\rho.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact reverse-posterior KL and $\chi^2$ chains]
\label{thm:V11-posterior-chains}
For every finite source displacement $\vartheta$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm KL}(m_R^{\vartheta}\Vert m_R)
 =D_{\rm KL}(m_S^{\vartheta}\Vert m_S)
 +\int
 D_{\rm KL}\!\left(
 K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow,\vartheta}(b_S,\cdot)
 \Vert
 K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}(b_S,\cdot)
 \right)\dd m_S^{\vartheta}(b_S).}
 \label{eq:V11-KL-chain}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{align}
 &\boxed{
 \chi^2(m_R^{\vartheta}\Vert m_R)
 -\chi^2(m_S^{\vartheta}\Vert m_S)
 =\int|\ell_R^{\vartheta}(b_R)-\ell_S^{\vartheta}(b_S)|^2
       \dd\lambda_{R,S}}
 \label{eq:V11-chi2-Pythagoras}\\
 &=\boxed{
 \int (\ell_S^{\vartheta}(b_S))^2
 \chi^2\!\left(
 K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow,\vartheta}(b_S,\cdot)
 \Vert
 K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}(b_S,\cdot)
 \right)\dd m_S(b_S).}
 \label{eq:V11-reverse-chi2}
\end{align}
Both remainder terms are nonnegative.  Their infinitesimal limit is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lim_{\vartheta\to0}\frac{1}{\vartheta^2}
 \int|\ell_R^{\vartheta}-\ell_S^{\vartheta}|^2\dd\lambda_{R,S}
 =I_R^{\square}-I_S^{\square}.}
 \label{eq:V11-chi2-Fisher-limit}
\end{equation}
A zero conditional KL remainder at one nonzero displacement is equivalent to
$K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow,\vartheta}=K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}$ almost surely,
and hence to $\ell_R^{\vartheta}(B_R)=\ell_S^{\vartheta}(B_S)$ on the joint
shell law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward factorizations
\[
 \lambda_{R,S}^{\vartheta}=m_R^{\vartheta}K_{R\to S}^{\to},
 \qquad
 \lambda_{R,S}=m_RK_{R\to S}^{\to}
\]
have the same conditional kernel.  Therefore
$D_{\rm KL}(\lambda_{R,S}^{\vartheta}\Vert\lambda_{R,S})
 =D_{\rm KL}(m_R^{\vartheta}\Vert m_R)$.  Applying the ordinary relative-
entropy chain rule to the reverse factorizations gives
\eqref{eq:V11-KL-chain}.

For the $\chi^2$ identity, the likelihood tower gives
$\ell_S^{\vartheta}=\mathbb E[\ell_R^{\vartheta}\mid B_S]$.
Conditional-expectation Pythagoras therefore yields
\[
 \mathbb E[(\ell_R^{\vartheta}-1)^2]
 -\mathbb E[(\ell_S^{\vartheta}-1)^2]
 =\mathbb E[(\ell_R^{\vartheta}-\ell_S^{\vartheta})^2],
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V11-chi2-Pythagoras}.  With
$r^{\vartheta}=\ell_R^{\vartheta}/\ell_S^{\vartheta}$,
\eqref{eq:V11-reverse-likelihood} gives
$\mathbb E[r^{\vartheta}\mid B_S]=1$ under the base reverse kernel.  Since
$\ell_R^{\vartheta}-\ell_S^{\vartheta}
 =\ell_S^{\vartheta}(r^{\vartheta}-1)$, conditioning on $B_S$ proves
\eqref{eq:V11-reverse-chi2}.  Boundedness of the finite-card source makes the
likelihood differentiable in $L^{\infty}$, with derivative
$U_T^{\square}$; division by $\vartheta^2$ and dominated convergence prove
\eqref{eq:V11-chi2-Fisher-limit}.  Relative entropy vanishes exactly when the
two conditional probabilities agree, and
\eqref{eq:V11-reverse-likelihood} gives the last equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Relation to Version V9]
\label{ass:V11-V9-relation}
The one-sided $\chi^2$ chain gives a direct positive finite-displacement
posterior loss.  Version~V9's odd symmetric likelihood secant remains the
better route when an $O(\vartheta^2)$ Fisher approximation is required.  The
present theorem supplies the missing Bayes-reverse interpretation and shows
that the exact infinitesimal loss is a conditional posterior information, not
an independently priced annular source.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The scalar card does not reconstruct the primitive loss direction}
\label{sec:V11-diagnostic-hierarchy}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Nonidentifiability: one radial ratio does not determine the V10 loss kernel]
\label{cth:V11-scalar-not-frame}
Let $c=e_1\in\R^2$, let
\[
 C_R=I_2,
 \qquad
 C_S^{(a)}=\begin{pmatrix}q&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 C_S^{(b)}=\begin{pmatrix}q&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad 0<q<1.
\]
Both cards satisfy
$0\preceq C_S\preceq C_R$ and have the same visible selected-source ratio
\begin{equation}
 \frac{c^{\mathsf T}C_S^{(a)}c}{c^{\mathsf T}C_Rc}
 =\frac{c^{\mathsf T}C_S^{(b)}c}{c^{\mathsf T}C_Rc}=q.
 \label{eq:V11-same-scalar-ratio}
\end{equation}
Nevertheless
\[
 \rank(C_R-C_S^{(a)})=2,
 \qquad
 \rank(C_R-C_S^{(b)})=1,
\]
and their no-loss kernels are different.  Hence a target-minimal scalar Read
cannot identify the primitive-loop failure direction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All matrices are diagonal.  The selected coefficient $c=e_1$ sees only their
first entry, proving \eqref{eq:V11-same-scalar-ratio}.  Their loss matrices are
$\operatorname{diag}(1-q,1)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(1-q,0)$, which have the
stated ranks and kernels.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact acquisition hierarchy]
\label{cor:V11-acquisition-hierarchy}
The correct order is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item acquire the two-scalar card \eqref{eq:V11-two-positive-scalars} when the
      target is only contraction versus retained-source transmission;
\item attach the physical width and return the inherited trichotomy;
\item acquire the V10 four-loop message matrices only when a near-unit branch
      requires the primitive softening or no-loss polarization itself.
\end{enumerate}
Reversing this order is target inflation, while using the scalar card to claim
a matrix witness is target overstatement.
\end{corollary}

% =============================================================================
\section{A certified source range from the four Wilson rectangles}
\label{sec:V11-source-range}
% =============================================================================

\begin{lemma}[Exact real-trace interval for $\SU(3)$]
\label{lem:V11-SU3-trace-range}
For every $U\in\SU(3)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{-\frac12\le\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}U\le1.}
 \label{eq:V11-SU3-trace-range}
\end{equation}
Both endpoints are attained.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write the eigenvalues as
$e^{\mathrm i\alpha},e^{\mathrm i\beta},e^{-\mathrm i(\alpha+\beta)}$.
With
$u=(\alpha+\beta)/2$ and $v=(\alpha-\beta)/2$,
\[
 \operatorname{ReTr}U
 =2\cos u\cos v+\cos(2u).
\]
For fixed $u$, the minimum over $v$ is
$-2|\cos u|+2\cos^2u-1$.  Putting $x=|\cos u|$ gives
\[
 2x^2-2x-1=2(x-\tfrac12)^2-\tfrac32\ge-\tfrac32.
\]
The upper bound three is immediate.  Equality below occurs at the nontrivial
centre elements and equality above at the identity.  Divide by three.
\end{proof}

Retain the four positive selected-root loop means and write
\begin{equation}
 A_N^{+}:=W_{11,N}^{-1}+W_{00,N}^{-1},
 \qquad
 A_N^{-}:=W_{10,N}^{-1}+W_{01,N}^{-1}.
 \label{eq:V11-reciprocal-arms}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Rectangle-box range of the complete Creutz source]
\label{prop:V11-source-box}
The centered physical source obeys
\begin{equation}
 -\frac12A_N^{+}-A_N^{-}
 \le Y_N^{\square}
 \le A_N^{+}+\frac12A_N^{-}.
 \label{eq:V11-source-box}
\end{equation}
Consequently the symmetric bound
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_N^{\rm bit}
 :=\max\left
 \{A_N^{+}+\tfrac12A_N^{-},
   \tfrac12A_N^{+}+A_N^{-}\right\}
 =\frac34(A_N^{+}+A_N^{-})
  +\frac14|A_N^{+}-A_N^{-}|}
 \label{eq:V11-bit-scale}
\end{equation}
satisfies $|Y_N^{\square}|\le K_N^{\rm bit}$.  If only positive lower
intervals $W_{\alpha,N}\ge\underline W_{\alpha,N}$ are available, replacing
each reciprocal by $\underline W_{\alpha,N}^{-1}$ gives an outward valid
value of $K_N^{\rm bit}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Because the Creutz signs sum to zero,
\[
 Y_N^{\square}
 =\frac{\mathcal O_{11}}{W_{11}}
  +\frac{\mathcal O_{00}}{W_{00}}
  -\frac{\mathcal O_{10}}{W_{10}}
  -\frac{\mathcal O_{01}}{W_{01}}.
\]
Apply \eqref{eq:V11-SU3-trace-range} separately to each term.  The maximum
uses value one on the positive arms and value $-1/2$ on the negative arms;
the minimum uses the opposite endpoints.  Taking the larger absolute endpoint
gives \eqref{eq:V11-bit-scale}.  Reciprocal monotonicity proves the interval
statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Actual support bounds may be sharper]
The four loop holonomies are correlated, so the rectangle-box value need not
be the exact essential supremum of their assembled contrast.  Any independently
certified smaller common scale $K_N\ge\|Y_N^{\square}\|_{\infty}$ may replace
$K_N^{\rm bit}$ in the binary card below.  The radial ratio is independent of
which valid common scale is used.
\end{remark}

% =============================================================================
\section{One calibrated sign bit gives the exact radial ratio}
\label{sec:V11-binary-card}
% =============================================================================

\begin{construction}[Same-event source comparator]
\label{con:V11-source-bit}
Fix a number $K_N\ge\|Y_N^{\square}\|_{\infty}$.  On each independently drawn
source interior attach a fresh randomizer and export a sign
$S_N\in\{-1,+1\}$ with conditional law
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb P(S_N=+1\mid\mathscr F_{\rm src})
 =\frac12\left(1+\frac{Y_N^{\square}}{K_N}\right).}
 \label{eq:V11-ideal-bit}
\end{equation}
Thus
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[S_N\mid\mathscr F_{\rm src}]
 =\frac{Y_N^{\square}}{K_N},
 \qquad
 \mathbb ES_N=0.
 \label{eq:V11-bit-mean}
\end{equation}
The randomizers used on distinct replica leaves are independent conditional on
the physical histories.  This construction is a Read of the already occurring
source; it is not a new Yang--Mills source deformation.
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[One equality probability per endpoint]
\label{thm:V11-binary-endpoint}
At shell $T$, draw two conditionally independent source interiors over the same
record $B_T$ and apply \Cref{con:V11-source-bit} independently to obtain
$S_{T,1},S_{T,2}$.  Put
\begin{equation}
 p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}:=
 \mathbb P(S_{T,1}=S_{T,2}).
 \label{eq:V11-equality-probability}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 2p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}-1
 =\mathbb E[S_{T,1}S_{T,2}]
 =\frac{I_{N,T}^{\square}}{K_N^2}.}
 \label{eq:V11-bit-stock}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac12\le p_{N,S}^{\rm eq}
 \le p_{N,R}^{\rm eq}\le1,}
 \label{eq:V11-bit-monotonicity}
\end{equation}
and, whenever $p_{N,R}^{\rm eq}>1/2$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,S}^{\square}}{I_{N,R}^{\square}}
 =\frac{2p_{N,S}^{\rm eq}-1}
        {2p_{N,R}^{\rm eq}-1},
 \qquad
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}-I_{N,S}^{\square}}
      {I_{N,R}^{\square}}
 =\frac{2(p_{N,R}^{\rm eq}-p_{N,S}^{\rm eq})}
        {2p_{N,R}^{\rm eq}-1}.}
 \label{eq:V11-bit-ratio}
\end{equation}
The common scale $K_N$ cancels exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditionally on $B_T$, the two complete leaf experiments are independent and
both have mean
\[
 \mathbb E[S_{T,j}\mid B_T]
 =K_N^{-1}\mathbb E[Y_N^{\square}\mid B_T]
 =K_N^{-1}U_{N,T}^{\square}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E[S_{T,1}S_{T,2}\mid B_T]
 =K_N^{-2}(U_{N,T}^{\square})^2.
\]
Average and use
$\one_{\{S_1=S_2\}}=(1+S_1S_2)/2$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:V11-bit-stock}.  The source-stock monotonicity gives
\eqref{eq:V11-bit-monotonicity}, and division proves
\eqref{eq:V11-bit-ratio}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two positive marks on the inherited four-leaf tree]
\label{cor:V11-four-leaf-bits}
On the already imported four-leaf radial tree, attach independent bits
$S_{j\ell}$ to the four source leaves.  Define
\begin{align}
 p_R^{\rm tree}
 &:=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^{2}
       \mathbb P(S_{j1}=S_{j2}),
 \label{eq:V11-tree-inner-equality}\\
 p_S^{\rm tree}
 &:=\frac14\sum_{\ell,k=1}^{2}
       \mathbb P(S_{1\ell}=S_{2k}).
 \label{eq:V11-tree-outer-equality}
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 2p_R^{\rm tree}-1=\frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}}{K_N^2},
 \qquad
 2p_S^{\rm tree}-1=\frac{I_{N,S}^{\square}}{K_N^2}.}
 \label{eq:V11-tree-bit-card}
\end{equation}
Thus one occurrence of the existing tree needs only two equality-type output
frequencies for the scalar radial target.  It need not expose the complete
four-loop matrix unless the diagnostic target of \Cref{cor:V11-acquisition-hierarchy}
is invoked.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Within one old-shell branch, conditional independence of the two source leaves
gives the first identity exactly as in \Cref{thm:V11-binary-endpoint}.  Across
the two old-shell branches, conditional independence over $B_S$ and the tower
property make every cross product have conditional mean
$(U_{N,S}^{\square}/K_N)^2$.  Averaging the two and four equality events gives
\eqref{eq:V11-tree-bit-card}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Comparator occurrence and calibration]
\label{fire:V11-comparator-occurrence}
Equation \eqref{eq:V11-ideal-bit} is licensed only when the source value,
randomizer, threshold comparison, and bit belong to the same source-leaf
event, with fresh randomizers on different leaves.  Matching marginal bit
frequencies or separately calibrated randomizers do not establish this joint
word.  When no such comparator occurs, the direct analog four-leaf products
remain the target-minimal route; the missing instrument is not inferred from
the algebraic existence of its ideal conditional law.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Calibration-safe intervals and comparator conditioning}
\label{sec:V11-calibration}
% =============================================================================

Let $\widetilde S_N$ be an actual sign output on one source leaf and put
\begin{equation}
 d_N
 :=\mathbb E[\widetilde S_N\mid\mathscr F_{\rm src}]
   -\frac{Y_N^{\square}}{K_N}.
 \label{eq:V11-comparator-bias}
\end{equation}
For a target shell $T$, define only the calibration component visible to that
use class,
\begin{equation}
 \delta_{N,T}^{\rm cal}
 :=\left\|
   \mathbb E[d_N\mid B_{N,T}]
  \right\|_2.
 \label{eq:V11-shell-calibration-error}
\end{equation}
The stronger bound $\|d_N\|_2\le\delta$ implies
$\delta_{N,T}^{\rm cal}\le\delta$ for every shell.

\begin{theorem}[Calibration-safe stock and ratio interval]
\label{thm:V11-calibration-interval}
Suppose two actual comparator leaves are conditionally independent over
$B_{N,T}$ and let
\(
 \widetilde p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}
 =\mathbb P(\widetilde S_{T,1}=\widetilde S_{T,2})
\).
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \sqrt{2\widetilde p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}-1}
  -\frac{\sqrt{I_{N,T}^{\square}}}{K_N}
 \right|
 \le\delta_{N,T}^{\rm cal}.}
 \label{eq:V11-calibration-root-bound}
\end{equation}
Let validated probability intervals satisfy
\[
 0\le\underline p_T\le\widetilde p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}
 \le\overline p_T\le1,
 \qquad T\in\{R,S\},
\]
with $\overline p_T\ge1/2$, and let
$\delta_T\ge\delta_{N,T}^{\rm cal}$.  Put
\begin{align}
 \underline q_T&:=\max\{0,2\underline p_T-1\},
 &\overline q_T&:=\max\{0,2\overline p_T-1\},
 \label{eq:V11-q-interval}\\
 L_T&:=K_N^2
 \left(\max\{0,\sqrt{\underline q_T}-\delta_T\}\right)^2,
 &U_T&:=K_N^2
 \left(\sqrt{\overline q_T}+\delta_T\right)^2.
 \label{eq:V11-calibrated-stock-interval}
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{I_{N,T}^{\square}\in[L_T,U_T].}
 \label{eq:V11-stock-interval}
\end{equation}
If $L_R>0$, the denominator-safe radial interval is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{L_S}{U_R}
 \le\frac{I_{N,S}^{\square}}{I_{N,R}^{\square}}
 \le\min\left\{1,\frac{U_S}{L_R}\right\}.}
 \label{eq:V11-calibrated-ratio-interval}
\end{equation}
An interval with $\overline p_T<1/2$ is inconsistent with the declared
conditional-iid comparator and is an input error, not a physical obstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put
$\kappa_N=\mathbb E[\widetilde S_N\mid\mathscr F_{\rm src}]$.
The conditional mean of one actual endpoint bit is
\[
 \widetilde u_T
 =\mathbb E[\kappa_N\mid B_T]
 =K_N^{-1}U_T^{\square}+\mathbb E[d_N\mid B_T].
\]
Conditional independence gives
$2\widetilde p_T^{\rm eq}-1=\|\widetilde u_T\|_2^2\ge0$.
The reverse triangle inequality and
\eqref{eq:V11-shell-calibration-error} prove
\eqref{eq:V11-calibration-root-bound}.  Insert the probability and calibration
intervals, square the nonnegative endpoints, and multiply by $K_N^2$ to get
\eqref{eq:V11-stock-interval}.  Division of two positive stock intervals and
the exact data-processing upper bound one give
\eqref{eq:V11-calibrated-ratio-interval}.  The error statement follows from
the proved nonnegativity of every equality excess.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Optimal symmetric one-bit scale and the conditioning stop]
\label{prop:V11-bit-conditioning}
Suppose a sign output $S\in\{-1,+1\}$ satisfies the exact symmetric decoder
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[S\mid\mathscr F_{\rm src}]=Y_N^{\square}/\kappa_N.
 \label{eq:V11-general-bit-decoder}
\end{equation}
Then necessarily
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\kappa_N\ge\|Y_N^{\square}\|_{\infty}.}
 \label{eq:V11-minimum-bit-scale}
\end{equation}
For every shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}-\frac12
 =\frac{I_{N,T}^{\square}}{2\kappa_N^2}.}
 \label{eq:V11-bit-excess}
\end{equation}
Thus even a probability interval centered at the exact value and having
half-width $h_T$ can certify a positive source denominator only if
\begin{equation}
 h_T<p_{N,T}^{\rm eq}-\frac12
 =\frac{I_{N,T}^{\square}}{2\kappa_N^2}.
 \label{eq:V11-resolution-condition}
\end{equation}
If $\kappa_N^2/I_{N,R}^{\square}\to\infty$, the exact bit card becomes
asymptotically fair and hence ill conditioned.  This is a comparator-Read
conditioning obstruction.  It does not imply
$I_{N,R}^{\square}\to0$ and must not be reported as physical source
invisibility.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The conditional expectation of a sign lies in $[-1,1]$, so
\eqref{eq:V11-general-bit-decoder} implies
$|Y_N^{\square}|\le\kappa_N$ almost surely.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V11-bit-excess} is \Cref{thm:V11-binary-endpoint} with $K_N$ replaced
by $\kappa_N$.  A lower endpoint above one half requires the displayed
resolution.  The last conclusion distinguishes vanishing of a normalized
instrument signal from vanishing of the unscaled source stock.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Which route to use]
\label{ass:V11-route-choice}
The exact binary card is the smallest positive-outcome packet when its
same-event comparator is available and sufficiently conditioned.  If the bit
excess is too small, one should not append a larger hierarchy of bits.  The
correct fallback is the already occurring analog source product in the
four-leaf tree, or the V10 primitive matrix if the failure direction is
required.  The route is selected by physical occurrence and conditioning,
not by which representation gives the preferred numerical verdict.
\end{assessment}

For a selected cofinal sequence, write

 \qquad
 p_{S,n}=p_{N_n,S_n}^{\rm eq},
 \qquad
 \ell_n=a_{N_n}(S_n-R_n).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Target-native equality-event trichotomy]
\label{thm:V11-bit-trichotomy}
Assume the inherited cofinal shell-incidence, physical-radius, and
compactness hypotheses of the existing trichotomy, exact comparator occurrence,
$p_{R,n}>1/2$, and a retained source-visibility floor
$I_{N_n,R_n}^{\square}\ge i_*>0$.  Put
\begin{equation}
 Q_n^{\rm bit}
 :=\frac{2p_{S,n}-1}{2p_{R,n}-1}
 =\frac{I_{N_n,S_n}^{\square}}{I_{N_n,R_n}^{\square}}.
 \label{eq:V11-bit-Q}
\end{equation}
Then the existing YM--B trichotomy is read exactly as follows.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T11.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5em]
\item If $\sup_nQ_n^{\rm bit}\le1-\delta$ for some $\delta>0$ on the
      predeclared physical-width family, the selected source has uniform
      radial contraction on that family.
\item If $Q_n^{\rm bit}\to1$ and $\ell_n\to0$, the normalized source packet is
      retained only at contact scale.
\item If $Q_n^{\rm bit}\to1$ and $\liminf_n\ell_n>0$, the normalized source
      packet is retained at positive physical range.
\item If the lower interval for $p_{R,n}-1/2$ vanishes, the output is source-
      visibility or comparator-conditioning $\mathsf{STOP}$ according to
      whether an analog lower stock is also absent.  It is not a contraction
      verdict.
\end{enumerate}
When a near-unit branch requires a primitive witness, one then acquires the
V10 matrix packet and applies its frame-softening/no-loss alternative.  The
scalar equality card alone is not promoted to that stronger witness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V11-bit-Q} is
\eqref{eq:V11-bit-ratio}.  The first three items are exactly the inherited
selected-source trichotomy after substituting this identity and retaining the
physical-width tag.  The fourth is the denominator discipline of
\Cref{thm:V11-calibration-interval,prop:V11-bit-conditioning}.  The final
qualification is \Cref{cth:V11-scalar-not-frame}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Spatial posterior loss is not a Yang--Mills mass]

The Bayes-reverse score is a source-parameter posterior on two spatial shell

centre-neutral vacuum-sector transfer.  No temporal gap or continuum

\end{firewall}

\section{Version V12 direction: move from an unpopulated scalar Read to the force which selects it}
\label{sec:V12-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V11 reduced the selected radial target to the two scalars
\(I_R^{\square}\) and
\(\mathcal J_{R\mid S}^{\leftarrow,\square}\), or to an equivalent calibrated
binary packet.  No supplied cylinder populated those values.  Replacing that
stop by a still larger replica or comparator hierarchy would therefore be
circular.  The present continuation moves one arrow upstream and uses the
already occurring Wilson coupling deformation itself.

Fix one finite Wilson card, one coupling \(\beta_*\), and one predeclared
physical shell pair \(R<S\).  The selected Creutz writer is frozen at the base
coupling before the coupling tangent is taken:
\begin{equation}
 Y:=Y_{N,\beta_*}^{\square},
 \qquad \mathbb E_{\beta_*}Y=0.
 \label{eq:V12-frozen-source}
\end{equation}
This order is essential.  The four normalizing loop means used in \(Y\) may
vary with \(\beta\), but their variation belongs to the already established
response derivative.  It is not silently reinserted by changing the source
writer while differentiating the base law.

Let \(A=A_N\) be the Wilson action and put
\begin{equation}
 V:=-(A-\mathbb E_{\beta_*}A).
 \label{eq:V12-full-coupling-score}
\end{equation}
Thus \(V\) is the score of the physical coupling curve
\(\beta_*+t\) at \(t=0\).  The inherited exact response identity gives
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 C_*:=\langle Y,V\rangle
      =-\chi_N'(\beta_*).}
 \label{eq:V12-response-force}
\end{equation}
At a regular stable down-crossing, \(C_*>0\).

The new question is not whether another representation of
\(I_S^{\square}/I_R^{\square}\) exists.  It is where the actual response force
\(C_*\) is carried relative to the shell pair.  The answer is an exact
three-level matrix Pythagoras.

\begin{firewall}[Distinct target from the YM--A partition curvature]
\label{fire:V12-not-YMA-curvature}
The coupling score and the normalized shell likelihoods determine the
positive Fisher geometry below.  They do not determine the unnormalized
coarse action-curvature gauge isolated in YM--A Version~V8.  Conversely, the
YM--A partition secant does not determine the Bayes-reverse radial source

\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The two-parameter physical score card on one shell pair}
\label{sec:V12-score-card}
% =============================================================================

Let \(B_R,B_S\) be the inherited inner and outer shell records on their common
base cylinder.  Write
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr G_{RS}=\sigma(B_R,B_S),
 \qquad
 \mathscr G_S=\sigma(B_S).
 \label{eq:V12-shell-sigma-fields}
\end{equation}
The physical source lies inside the inner shell, so the inherited source
Markov property is
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[Y\mid\mathscr G_{RS}]
 =\mathbb E[Y\mid B_R].
 \label{eq:V12-source-Markov}
\end{equation}
Define the source messages
\begin{equation}
 U_R=\mathbb E[Y\mid B_R],
 \qquad
 U_S=\mathbb E[Y\mid B_S],
 \label{eq:V12-source-messages}
\end{equation}
and the coupling scores
\begin{equation}
 V_R=\mathbb E[V\mid B_R],
 \qquad
 V_{RS}=\mathbb E[V\mid B_R,B_S],
 \qquad
 V_S=\mathbb E[V\mid B_S].
 \label{eq:V12-coupling-scores}
\end{equation}
The score of the physical forward shell kernel is
\begin{equation}
 S_{R\to S}^{\beta}:=V_{RS}-V_R.
 \label{eq:V12-forward-score}
\end{equation}
It is centered conditionally on \(B_R\).

Use the scalar stocks
\begin{align}
 G&=\|Y\|_2^2,
 &I_R&=\|U_R\|_2^2,
 &I_S&=\|U_S\|_2^2
 \label{eq:V12-source-stocks}\\
 J_*&=\|V\|_2^2,
 &J_R&=\|V_R\|_2^2,
 &J_{RS}&=\|V_{RS}\|_2^2,
 &J_S&=\|V_S\|_2^2
 \label{eq:V12-coupling-stocks}\\
 J_{R\to S}&=\|S_{R\to S}^{\beta}\|_2^2,
 &C_R&=\langle U_R,V_R\rangle,
 &C_S&=\langle U_S,V_S\rangle
 \label{eq:V12-cross-stocks}
\end{align}
All inner products in this continuation are taken in the base Wilson law or
its displayed shell marginal.

\begin{lemma}[Score projection and physical forward-score decomposition]
\label{lem:V12-score-projection}
The shell scores in \eqref{eq:V12-coupling-scores} are the logarithmic scores
of the corresponding pushforward laws.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 V_{RS}=V_R+S_{R\to S}^{\beta},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[S_{R\to S}^{\beta}\mid B_R]=0,
 \qquad
 J_{RS}=J_R+J_{R\to S}.}
 \label{eq:V12-forward-score-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
The source and score towers obey
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 U_S=\mathbb E[U_R\mid B_S],
 \qquad
 V_S=\mathbb E[V_{RS}\mid B_S].}
 \label{eq:V12-two-towers}
\end{equation}
Finally,
\begin{equation}
 \langle U_R,V_{RS}\rangle=C_R.
 \label{eq:V12-CR-joint}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For any finite differentiable probability family with score \(W\), the score
of a pushforward to a record \(\mathscr G\) is
\(\mathbb E[W\mid\mathscr G]\).  Indeed, for every bounded
\(\mathscr G\)-measurable test \(f\), differentiation gives
\[
 \left.\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\right|_{0}\mathbb E_t f
 =\mathbb E(fW)
 =\mathbb E\bigl(f\,\mathbb E[W\mid\mathscr G]\bigr).
\]
Apply this to \(V\) and to the three shell records.  Factorization of the
joint shell law as the inner marginal times the physical forward kernel gives
\(V_{RS}=V_R+S_{R\to S}^{\beta}\).  Integrating a kernel score over its target
variable gives zero, hence the conditional centering.  Orthogonality to every
\(B_R\)-measurable function gives the norm identity in
\eqref{eq:V12-forward-score-Pythagoras}.

The first tower identity in \eqref{eq:V12-two-towers} is the inherited source
Markov recursion.  The second is ordinary conditional-expectation
composition through
\(\mathscr G_S\subseteq\mathscr G_{RS}\).  Finally, \(U_R\) is
\(B_R\)-measurable and the forward score is conditionally centered, so
\[
 \langle U_R,V_{RS}\rangle
 =\langle U_R,V_R\rangle
  +\langle U_R,S_{R\to S}^{\beta}\rangle
 =C_R.
\]
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact three-level source--force Fisher Pythagoras}
\label{sec:V12-Fisher-Pythagoras}
% =============================================================================

Define the source martingale differences
\begin{equation}
 Y_0=Y-U_R,
 \qquad
 Y_1=U_R-U_S,
 \qquad
 Y_2=U_S,
 \label{eq:V12-source-levels}
\end{equation}
and the coupling-score differences
\begin{equation}
 V_0=V-V_{RS},
 \qquad
 V_1=V_{RS}-V_S,
 \qquad
 V_2=V_S.
 \label{eq:V12-score-levels}
\end{equation}
For \(i=0,1,2\), put
\begin{equation}
 G_i=\|Y_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 H_i=\|V_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 h_i=\langle Y_i,V_i\rangle.
 \label{eq:V12-level-stocks}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Joint source--coupling Fisher Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V12-joint-Fisher-Pythagoras}
The three matrix-valued level Grams
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb M_i
 :=\begin{pmatrix}G_i&h_i\\h_i&H_i\end{pmatrix}
 \succeq0,
 \qquad i=0,1,2,
 \label{eq:V12-level-Grams}
\end{equation}
are explicitly
\begin{align}
 \mathbb M_0
 &=\begin{pmatrix}
     G-I_R&C_*-C_R\\
     C_*-C_R&J_*-J_{RS}
    \end{pmatrix}
 \label{eq:V12-hidden-Gram}\\
 \mathbb M_1
 &=\begin{pmatrix}
     I_R-I_S&C_R-C_S\\
     C_R-C_S&J_{RS}-J_S
    \end{pmatrix}
  =\begin{pmatrix}
     I_R-I_S&C_R-C_S\\
     C_R-C_S&J_R+J_{R\to S}-J_S
    \end{pmatrix}
 \label{eq:V12-reverse-Gram}\\
 \mathbb M_2
 &=\begin{pmatrix}
     I_S&C_S\\
     C_S&J_S
    \end{pmatrix}.
 \label{eq:V12-outer-Gram}
\end{align}
They satisfy the exact matrix identity
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{pmatrix}G&C_*\\C_*&J_*\end{pmatrix}
 =\mathbb M_0+\mathbb M_1+\mathbb M_2.}
 \label{eq:V12-full-matrix-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 C_*=(C_*-C_R)+(C_R-C_S)+C_S.}
 \label{eq:V12-force-telescope}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Consider the nested sigma-algebras
\[
 \mathscr F_{\rm full}
 \supseteq\mathscr G_{RS}
 \supseteq\mathscr G_S
 \supseteq\{\varnothing,\Omega\}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:V12-source-Markov}, the conditional expectations of the source
along this chain are \(Y,U_R,U_S,0\).  The corresponding conditional
expectations of the coupling score are \(V,V_{RS},V_S,0\).  Hence the two
vector-valued martingale-difference sequences are precisely
\((Y_i)_{i=0}^2\) and \((V_i)_{i=0}^2\).

Conditional-expectation orthogonality gives, for \(i\ne j\),
\[
 \langle Y_i,Y_j\rangle
 =\langle V_i,V_j\rangle
 =\langle Y_i,V_j\rangle=0.
\]
Therefore the Gram of \((Y,V)\) is the sum of the three level Grams, proving
\eqref{eq:V12-full-matrix-Pythagoras}.  Each level Gram is positive because it
is the Gram of the pair \((Y_i,V_i)\).

The diagonal source identities are the ordinary information Pythagoras:
\[
 G_0=G-I_R,
 \qquad G_1=I_R-I_S,
 \qquad G_2=I_S.
\]
The score identities are
\[
 H_0=J_*-J_{RS},
 \qquad H_1=J_{RS}-J_S,
 \qquad H_2=J_S,
\]
and \eqref{eq:V12-forward-score-Pythagoras} gives the second expression for
\(H_1\).  For the cross terms, orthogonality and
\eqref{eq:V12-CR-joint} give
\[
 h_0=C_*-C_R,
 \qquad h_1=C_R-C_S,
 \qquad h_2=C_S.
\]
This proves all displayed formulas and the force telescope.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact joint Bayes-reverse Fisher matrix]
\label{cor:V12-reverse-Fisher}
Under the two-parameter deformation obtained by combining the frozen source
tilt with the Wilson coupling curve, the two scores of the Bayes-reverse
kernel \(K_{S\to R}^{\leftarrow}\) are
\begin{equation}
 D_Y=U_R-U_S,
 \qquad
 D_\beta=V_R+S_{R\to S}^{\beta}-V_S=V_{RS}-V_S.
 \label{eq:V12-reverse-scores}
\end{equation}
Their complete Fisher matrix is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E
 \begin{pmatrix}D_Y\\D_\beta\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}D_Y&D_\beta\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
   I_R-I_S&C_R-C_S\\
   C_R-C_S&J_R+J_{R\to S}-J_S
  \end{pmatrix}\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:V12-joint-reverse-Fisher}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (C_R-C_S)^2
 \le
 (I_R-I_S)(J_R+J_{R\to S}-J_S).}
 \label{eq:V12-force-memory-determinant}
\end{equation}
If \(I_R>0\), this yields the source-specific contraction estimate
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_S}{I_R}
 \le
 1-\frac{(C_R-C_S)^2}
          {I_R(J_R+J_{R\to S}-J_S)} }
 \label{eq:V12-force-memory-contraction}
\end{equation}
whenever the denominator on the right is positive.  A zero coupling-memory
denominator forces \(C_R-C_S=0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The source score is the Version~V11 Bayes-reverse score.  For the coupling
parameter, differentiate the identity
\(K^{\leftarrow}=m_RK^{\to}/m_S\): its score is the inner marginal score plus
the forward-kernel score minus the outer marginal score.  This is
\(D_\beta\).  The displayed matrix is therefore the Gram of the two reverse
scores and equals \(\mathbb M_1\) by
\Cref{thm:V12-joint-Fisher-Pythagoras}.  Its determinant is nonnegative,
which gives \eqref{eq:V12-force-memory-determinant}.  Divide by \(I_R\) and
the coupling-memory stock to obtain
\eqref{eq:V12-force-memory-contraction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What the new mixed entry measures]
\label{ass:V12-mixed-entry}
The cross term \(C_R-C_S\) is not a new source birth.  It is the part of the
physical response force lost when the old shell is reconstructed from the
outer shell.  The second diagonal is the coupling-score memory in the same
Bayes-reverse posterior.  Their determinant is therefore a literal
force--memory inequality on the already occurring source route.  No radial
loss is inferred from a separately sampled action variance or from a fitted
correlation coefficient.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Regular selected roots give a force--memory radius alternative}
\label{sec:V12-regular-root}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Regular-root source--force correlation]
\label{def:V12-root-correlation}
Suppose \(\beta_*\) is a simple stable down-crossing of
\(\chi_N(\beta)=u_*\).  Put
\begin{equation}
 s_*=-\chi_N'(\beta_*)=C_*>0,
 \qquad
 \gamma_*^2
 :=\frac{s_*^2}{GJ_*}\in(0,1].
 \label{eq:V12-gamma}
\end{equation}
The number \(\gamma_*\) is the absolute correlation of the frozen physical
Creutz source with the Wilson coupling score.  It is invariant under common
positive rescaling of either score.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Regular-root force--memory radius alternative]
\label{thm:V12-regular-root-alternative}
At every regular selected root and for every predeclared physical shell pair
\(R<S\), at least one of the following three alternatives holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item \textbf{Inner/contact source loss.}
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \frac{G-I_R}{G}\ge\frac{\gamma_*^2}{9}.}
       \label{eq:V12-inner-loss}
      \end{equation}
\item \textbf{Annular radial contraction.}
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \frac{I_R-I_S}{I_R}\ge\frac{\gamma_*^2}{9},
       \qquad
       \frac{I_S}{I_R}\le1-\frac{\gamma_*^2}{9}.}
       \label{eq:V12-annular-loss}
      \end{equation}
\item \textbf{Outer source visibility.}
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \frac{I_S}{G}\ge\frac{\gamma_*^2}{9}.}
       \label{eq:V12-outer-visibility}
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The branch is attained by one of the three level Grams in
\eqref{eq:V12-level-Grams}; no data-dependent shell decomposition is chosen.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:V12-force-telescope},
\[
 h_0+h_1+h_2=s_*>0.
\]
Hence one index \(i\) satisfies \(h_i\ge s_*/3\).  Positivity of
\(\mathbb M_i\) gives
\[
 h_i^2\le G_iH_i.
\]
Since \(H_i\le H_0+H_1+H_2=J_*\),
\[
 G_i\ge\frac{s_*^2}{9J_*}
      =\frac{\gamma_*^2}{9}G.
\]
For \(i=0\) and \(i=2\), this is exactly
\eqref{eq:V12-inner-loss} and \eqref{eq:V12-outer-visibility}.  For \(i=1\),
use \(I_R\le G\) to obtain
\[
 \frac{I_R-I_S}{I_R}
 \ge\frac{I_R-I_S}{G}
 \ge\frac{\gamma_*^2}{9},
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V12-annular-loss}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal regular-root handoff]
\label{cor:V12-cofinal-regular}
Let \(\beta_n^{\rm wf}\) be a cofinal sequence of simple weak-facing roots and
suppose
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\ge\gamma_0>0.
 \label{eq:V12-gamma-floor}
\end{equation}
For any predeclared sequence of shell pairs, pass to a subsequence on which the
same branch of \Cref{thm:V12-regular-root-alternative} occurs.  Then,
respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C12.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5em]
\item the source-to-inner-shell stock loses at least the fixed fraction
      \(\gamma_0^2/9\);
\item the selected radial coefficient obeys
      \begin{equation}
       q_{N_n;R_n\to S_n}^{\square}
       \le\sqrt{1-\gamma_0^2/9}<1;
       \label{eq:V12-q-contraction}
      \end{equation}
\item the outer shell retains at least the fixed fraction
      \(\gamma_0^2/9\) of the complete physical source stock.
\end{enumerate}
If \(a_{N_n}R_n\to0\), item~\textup{(C12.1)} is a contact-scale source loss.
If \(\liminf a_{N_n}S_n>0\), item~\textup{(C12.3)} is an absolute
positive-range visibility packet.  The latter still requires a near-unit
adjacent channel before it is called the positive-range survivor of the
terminal trichotomy.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
There are only three branches.  Pass to a subsequence on which one occurs and
apply the uniform lower bound in \eqref{eq:V12-gamma-floor}.  In the annular
branch, the squared radial coefficient is \(I_S/I_R\), which gives
\eqref{eq:V12-q-contraction}.  The physical interpretations use the already
frozen radius tags and do not alter the source or shell pair.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Root ramification or normalized force softening]
\label{thm:V12-root-softening}
For every stable down-crossing of the analytic function
\(f_N(\beta)=\chi_N(\beta)-u_*\), its zero multiplicity is odd.  Exactly one of
the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.8em]
\item the root is simple, \(f_N'(\beta_*)<0\), and
      \Cref{thm:V12-regular-root-alternative} applies;
\item the root has odd multiplicity \(m\ge3\), in which case
      \(f_N'(\beta_*)=0\) and, for some \(a_N>0\),
      \begin{equation}
       \frac{f_N(\beta_*-h)-f_N(\beta_*+h)}{2h}
       =a_Nh^{m-1}+O(h^m);
       \label{eq:V12-ramified-secant}
      \end{equation}
\item along a sequence of simple roots, the normalized correlations
      \(\gamma_n\) tend to zero.
\end{enumerate}
The last two branches are typed selector/force-softening outputs.  They do not
prove radial contraction or source invisibility.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A stable down-crossing changes sign from positive to negative.  The first
nonzero Taylor coefficient therefore has odd order \(m\) and negative sign:
\[
 f_N(\beta_*+t)=-a_Nt^m+O(t^{m+1}),
 \qquad a_N>0.
\]
For \(m=1\), the derivative is negative.  For \(m\ge3\), it vanishes and the
symmetric secant is \eqref{eq:V12-ramified-secant}.  On any cofinal sequence
of simple roots, compactness of \([0,1]\) for \(\gamma_n\) gives, after a
subsequence, either a positive lower limit or convergence to zero.  The first
case is \Cref{cor:V12-cofinal-regular}; the second is item~\textup{(R3)}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Failure of the second point test loads a noncollapsed physical source}
\label{sec:V12-corridor-source}
% =============================================================================

The dedicated physical-trajectory programme has already proved the following
Wilson-specific corridor statement.  It is imported here and not recomputed.

\begin{importedresult}[Frozen strong corridor and response-erosion alternative]
\label{imp:V12-corridor}
There are fixed numbers
\begin{equation}
 B_-=B_1,
 \qquad B_+=2B_1,
 \qquad \Delta B=B_+-B_->0,
 \label{eq:V12-corridor}
\end{equation}
and constants \(\mu_1>0\), \(C_\angle<\infty\), independent of \(N\), such
that, with \(d=N/8\),
\begin{equation}
 \chi_N(B_-)\ge\mu_1d^2-C_\angle.
 \label{eq:V12-Bminus-floor}
\end{equation}
If \(\chi_N(B_+)>u_*\), the weak-facing root lies beyond \(B_+\).  If this
point test fails along a cofinal subsequence, then the response loses order
\(d^2\) somewhere in \((B_-,B_+)\).  The exact derivative is
\begin{equation}
 \chi_N'(\beta)
 =\operatorname{Cov}_{\beta}
   (Y_{N,\beta}^{\square},A_N).
 \label{eq:V12-imported-derivative}
\end{equation}
\end{importedresult}

The imported result gives a slope witness.  The next theorem extracts a
cutoff-uniform physical source stock from it without assuming a pointwise
bound for the action variance.

\begin{theorem}[Advance-or-noncollapsed-corridor-source theorem]
\label{thm:V12-corridor-source}
For every cofinal cutoff sequence, after passing to a subsequence, one of the
following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.8em]
\item \(\chi_N(B_+)>u_*\) eventually, hence the weak-facing root is beyond
      \(B_+\);
\item there are couplings \(\beta_N^{\rm src}\in(B_-,B_+)\) with
      \(\chi_N'(\beta_N^{\rm src})<0\) and
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \bigl\|Y_{N,\beta_N^{\rm src}}^{\square}\bigr\|_2^2
       \ge
       g_*:=\frac{\mu_1^2}{294912\,\Delta B}>0.}
       \label{eq:V12-corridor-source-floor}
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Thus failure to advance the second point test cannot be represented only by a
large negative derivative.  It also loads a noncollapsed physical Creutz
source somewhere in the same fixed coupling corridor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Assume the first branch fails along a subsequence, so
\(\chi_N(B_+)\le u_*\).  For all sufficiently large \(N\),
\eqref{eq:V12-Bminus-floor} gives
\begin{equation}
 D_N:=\chi_N(B_-)-\chi_N(B_+)
 \ge\frac{\mu_1}{2}d^2
 =\frac{\mu_1N^2}{128}.
 \label{eq:V12-response-drop}
\end{equation}
Let
\begin{equation}
 E_N=\{\beta\in(B_-,B_+):\chi_N'(\beta)<0\},
 \quad
 G_N(\beta)=\|Y_{N,\beta}^{\square}\|_2^2,
 \quad
 J_N(\beta)=\operatorname{Var}_{\beta}(A_N).
 \label{eq:V12-corridor-GJ}
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:V12-imported-derivative} and Cauchy--Schwarz,
\begin{equation}
 [-\chi_N'(\beta)]_+^2
 \le G_N(\beta)J_N(\beta).
 \label{eq:V12-pointwise-force-bound}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\[
 D_N\le\int_{E_N}[-\chi_N'(\beta)]\,\dd\beta.
\]
The four-dimensional periodic lattice has \(6N^4\) plaquettes, and the sharp
\(\SU(3)\) plaquette action lies in \([0,3/2]\).  Hence
\(0\le A_N\le9N^4\).  Differentiating the mean action gives
\begin{equation}
 \int_{B_-}^{B_+}J_N(\beta)\,\dd\beta
 =\mathbb E_{B_-}A_N-\mathbb E_{B_+}A_N
 \le9N^4.
 \label{eq:V12-integrated-action-variance}
\end{equation}
Applying Cauchy--Schwarz to the integral over \(E_N\) yields
\begin{align}
 D_N^2
 &\le
 \left(\int_{E_N}G_N(\beta)\,\dd\beta\right)
 \left(\int_{E_N}J_N(\beta)\,\dd\beta\right)
 \notag\\
 &\le
 \Delta B\,
 \sup_{\beta\in E_N}G_N(\beta)\,
 9N^4.
 \label{eq:V12-integrated-force-bound}
\end{align}
Insert \eqref{eq:V12-response-drop} to obtain
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\beta\in E_N}G_N(\beta)
 \ge\frac{\mu_1^2}{147456\,\Delta B}.
 \label{eq:V12-corridor-sup-floor}
\end{equation}
Choose \(\beta_N^{\rm src}\in E_N\) within one half of this supremum.  This
gives \eqref{eq:V12-corridor-source-floor} and preserves the strict negative
slope.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The corridor source is not silently declared to be the selected root]
\label{fire:V12-corridor-not-root}
The coupling \(\beta_N^{\rm src}\) is an attained point in the fixed corridor.
It is not asserted to equal the last stable weak-facing crossing.  The theorem
populates a noncollapsed physical source card on the failure branch; it does
not retune the selector or infer root escape.  Transport from this corridor
card to a selected root is an additional physical row.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Half-stock radius and extraction of a positive-range near-unit card}
\label{sec:V12-half-radius}
% =============================================================================

Let a source-loaded sequence be supplied either by
\Cref{thm:V12-corridor-source} or by a selected-root lower stock.  On each
card, augment the shell chain by the source level
\begin{equation}
 I_{N,0}^{\square}:=G_N.
 \label{eq:V12-source-level-zero}
\end{equation}
Let the predeclared nonwrapping physical shell grid have radii
\begin{equation}
 0=r_{N,0}<r_{N,1}<\cdots<r_{N,L_N},
 \qquad r_{N,j}=a_NR_{N,j},
 \label{eq:V12-physical-shell-grid}
\end{equation}
with mesh tending to zero and with every fixed compact physical interval
covered eventually.  The source stocks are nonincreasing in \(j\).

\begin{definition}[Half-stock radius]
\label{def:V12-half-radius}
Put
\begin{equation}
 r_{1/2,N}
 :=\inf\{r_{N,j}:I_{N,j}^{\square}\le G_N/2\},
 \qquad \inf\varnothing:=+\infty.
 \label{eq:V12-half-radius}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Half-stock radius alternative]
\label{thm:V12-half-radius}
Assume \(G_N\ge g_*>0\) and the shell-grid hypotheses above.  After passing to
a subsequence, \(r_{1/2,N}\to r_*\in[0,\infty]\).  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.8em]
\item If \(r_*=0\), every shell card with relative source visibility strictly
      above \(1/2\) lies at contact scale.  For those visible adjacent cards,
      either their supremal radial coefficient is eventually bounded below one,
      or there is a sequence with coefficient tending to one; these are,
      respectively, uniform contraction and a contact-scale survivor at the
      relative threshold \(1/2\).
\item If \(r_*>0\), there exist adjacent shell cards \(c_N\) with
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \liminf r(c_N)>0,
       \qquad
       I_{N,R(c_N)}^{\square}\ge\frac{g_*}{2},
       \qquad
       q(c_N)\longrightarrow1.}
       \label{eq:V12-positive-range-extraction}
      \end{equation}
      Hence the source-loaded sequence contains a positive-range near-unit
      physical-source card.
\end{enumerate}
The theorem uses only the actual conditional source stocks and their physical
radii.  It does not use the coupling score as a clock.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Sequential compactness of \([0,\infty]\) gives a convergent subsequence.
Suppose first that \(r_*=0\).  By monotonicity, once the stock crosses below
\(G_N/2\), it never rises above that threshold.  Therefore every card with
relative visibility greater than \(1/2\) has radius at most
\(r_{1/2,N}\) plus one mesh step, which tends to zero.  No positive-range
near-unit card exists at this threshold.  Let \(Q_N\) be the supremum of the
adjacent coefficients over these visible cards.  After a subsequence, either
\(\limsup Q_N<1\), which is uniform contraction, or \(Q_N\to1\); choosing a
card within \(1/N\) of the supremum gives a near-unit card whose radius tends
to zero, which is the contact branch.

Now assume \(r_*>0\).  If \(r_*<\infty\), choose a fixed interval
\([a,b]\subset(0,r_*)\), for example
\(a=r_*/4\), \(b=r_*/2\).  If \(r_*=\infty\), choose any fixed
\(0<a<b<\infty\).  For all large \(N\), every grid stock in \([a,b]\) is
larger than \(G_N/2\).  Let \(j_N<k_N\) be the first and last grid indices in
that interval.  The number \(m_N=k_N-j_N\) tends to infinity because the mesh
tends to zero, and
\begin{equation}
 \prod_{j=j_N}^{k_N-1}q_{N,j}^2
 =\frac{I_{N,k_N}^{\square}}{I_{N,j_N}^{\square}}
 \ge\frac{G_N/2}{G_N}
 =\frac12.
 \label{eq:V12-half-product}
\end{equation}
Hence at least one adjacent coefficient in the product satisfies
\begin{equation}
 q(c_N)^2\ge2^{-1/m_N}\longrightarrow1.
 \label{eq:V12-near-unit-extraction}
\end{equation}
Its inner radius lies in \([a,b]\), and its source stock is at least
\(G_N/2\ge g_*/2\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:V12-positive-range-extraction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[First noncircular physical route after V11]
\label{ass:V12-noncircular-route}
Version~V11 stopped because its irreducible two-scalar Read was unpopulated.
Version~V12 supplies two upstream alternatives which do not manufacture that
Read:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.8em]
\item at a regular selected root, the joint source--coupling reverse Fisher
      matrix forces contact loss, annular contraction, or outer visibility;
\item if the frozen second point test fails, the actual Wilson response erosion
      loads a noncollapsed physical source in the fixed corridor, whose
      half-stock radius gives a terminating contact-versus-positive-range
      audit.
\end{enumerate}
The remaining physical values are now the root regularity/correlation and the
actual shell stocks of one loaded source, rather than another representation
of an unknown scalar.
\end{assessment}

\label{thm:V12-export}

 \begin{pmatrix}G&C_*\\C_*&J_*\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}G-I_R&C_*-C_R\\C_*-C_R&J_*-J_{RS}\end{pmatrix}
  +\begin{pmatrix}I_R-I_S&C_R-C_S\\C_R-C_S&J_{RS}-J_S\end{pmatrix}

 (C_R-C_S)^2

 r_{1/2,N}\to r_*>0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad

 \label{eq:V12-export}

This is a force--memory and physical-radius export.  It does not assign the

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V13 direction: use the literal rectangle geometry before another shell Read}
\label{sec:V13-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V12 moved upstream from an unpopulated radial ratio to the Wilson
coupling force which selects the response root.  Its remaining alternatives
still allowed the complete Creutz source stock to collapse on the selected
sequence.  Another representation of the same endpoint ratio would not decide
that earlier source-visibility row.

The present continuation therefore returns to the literal four-rectangle
geometry.  Three rectangles contain a boundary edge traversed by no other
selected loop.  The smallest rectangle has no private edge, but one of its
corners contains a private two-link interaction: the smallest loop uses both
corner links, the two one-sided larger rectangles use one link each, and the
largest rectangle uses neither.  Conditional finite energy and the exact
fundamental Haar moment then force a nonzero part of the complete Creutz
source to remain hidden from every separating shell.

The estimate is Wilson specific, dimension free, and requires no new source
deformation, comparator, Witten current, or auxiliary shell bank.  It closes
the source-invisibility loophole on every bounded weak-facing subsequence and
returns a precise normalization-escape alternative on an escaping subsequence.

\begin{firewall}[The new gap is a source-entry gap]
\label{fire:V13-entry-not-adjacent}
The estimate below compares the complete physical source with a separating
boundary record.  It is a source-specific strict contraction from source level
to shell level.  It does not assert that every later adjacent shell channel is
uniformly contractive.  A residual message may still have a contact-scale or
positive-range near-unit follower, and that distinction is made by the
inherited physical-radius trichotomy.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Private edge and corner coordinates of the four physical rectangles}
\label{sec:V13-private-geometry}
% =============================================================================

Work in the nonwrapping coordinate chart of the selected $(x_0,x_1)$ plane.
For $N\in16\mathbb N$, put
\begin{equation}
 r_0=t_0=\frac N8,
 \qquad
 r_1=t_1=\frac{3N}{16}.
 \label{eq:V13-half-lengths}
\end{equation}
Thus $C_{\epsilon\eta}$ is the oriented boundary of
$[-r_\epsilon,r_\epsilon]\times[-t_\eta,t_\eta]$, with the remaining two
coordinates fixed.  An unoriented unit edge is denoted by $[x,x+\widehat\mu]$;
its orientation inside a loop is irrelevant for the incidence statements.

\begin{lemma}[Exact private-coordinate incidence]
\label{lem:V13-private-incidence}
The following three edges are traversed by exactly the displayed rectangle:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 e_{11}
 &=[(r_1,t_0,0,0),(r_1,t_0+1,0,0)]
 &&\subset C_{11},\\
 e_{10}
 &=[(r_0,t_0,0,0),(r_0+1,t_0,0,0)]
 &&\subset C_{10},\\
 e_{01}
 &=[(r_0,t_0,0,0),(r_0,t_0+1,0,0)]
 &&\subset C_{01}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:V13-private-edges}
\end{equation}
None belongs to another selected contour.

At the upper-right corner of $C_{00}$, put
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{00}
 &:=[(r_0-1,t_0,0,0),(r_0,t_0,0,0)],\\
 v_{00}
 &:=[(r_0,t_0-1,0,0),(r_0,t_0,0,0)].
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:V13-C00-corner-pair}
\end{equation}
Then $C_{00}$ traverses both links, $C_{10}$ traverses $h_{00}$ but not
$v_{00}$, $C_{01}$ traverses $v_{00}$ but not $h_{00}$, and $C_{11}$
traverses neither.  Each single link belongs to six plaquettes, the two corner
links share exactly one plaquette, and their union is incident to exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{6+6-1=11}
 \label{eq:V13-eleven-plaquettes}
\end{equation}
plaquettes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The side $x_0=r_1$ of $C_{11}$ extends from $-t_1$ to $t_1$, whereas the
corresponding side of $C_{10}$ stops at $t_0$; this proves the privacy of
$e_{11}$.  The side $x_1=t_0$ of $C_{10}$ extends from $-r_1$ to $r_1$,
whereas the side of $C_{00}$ stops at $r_0$; this proves the privacy of
$e_{10}$.  The analogous comparison of the sides $x_0=r_0$ of $C_{01}$ and
$C_{00}$ proves the privacy of $e_{01}$.

The edge $h_{00}$ lies on the common $x_1=t_0$ side of $C_{00}$ and $C_{10}$,
while $v_{00}$ lies on the common $x_0=r_0$ side of $C_{00}$ and $C_{01}$.
The larger contour $C_{11}$ uses the displaced sides $x_0=r_1$ and
$x_1=t_1$.  In four dimensions an edge in direction $\mu$ belongs to the two
$(\mu,\nu)$ plaquettes on either side for each of the three directions
$\nu\ne\mu$, hence to six plaquettes.  The perpendicular corner links share
only the $(0,1)$ plaquette immediately inside $C_{00}$, proving the count.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The smallest rectangle is isolated at interaction order two]
\label{rem:V13-C00-interaction}
No edge of $C_{00}$ is private: every horizontal side edge is also used by
$C_{01}$ and every vertical side edge by $C_{10}$.  The pair
$(h_{00},v_{00})$ is nevertheless private after removing one-link functions.
This is why the complete source estimate uses a two-link Haar interaction for
the $00$ arm rather than pretending that a private edge exists.
\end{remark}

% =============================================================================
\section{Sharp conditional finite-energy comparison on one and two links}
\label{sec:V13-finite-energy}
% =============================================================================

For a finite link set $E$, let $\mathscr F_E$ be the sigma-algebra generated
by all links outside $E$, and let $n(E)$ be the number of plaquettes incident
to at least one link of $E$.

\begin{lemma}[Sharp trace-range conditional ellipticity]
\label{lem:V13-conditional-ellipticity}
Conditionally on $\mathscr F_E$, the links in $E$ have a density
$\rho_{E,\beta}^{\eta}$ with respect to product Haar measure $h_E$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 e^{-\frac32n(E)\beta}
 \le \rho_{E,\beta}^{\eta}
 \le e^{\frac32n(E)\beta}}
 \label{eq:V13-general-ellipticity}
\end{equation}
uniformly in the exterior configuration.  Hence every real square-integrable
function $F$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Var}_{\rho_{E,\beta}^{\eta}}(F)
 \ge
 e^{-\frac32n(E)\beta}
 \operatorname{Var}_{h_E}(F).}
 \label{eq:V13-variance-comparison}
\end{equation}
In particular, the one-link exponent is $9\beta$, while the corner-pair
exponent is $33\beta/2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Only plaquettes incident to $E$ enter the conditional density.  By
\Cref{lem:V11-SU3-trace-range}, the range of $\operatorname{ReTr}U$ on
$\SU(3)$ has length $9/2$.  The oscillation of the conditional logarithmic
weight is therefore at most
\[
 \frac\beta3\,n(E)\,\frac92
 =\frac32n(E)\beta.
\]
A normalized positive density whose logarithm has oscillation at most $D$ lies
between $e^{-D}$ and $e^D$, proving
\eqref{eq:V13-general-ellipticity}.  Finally,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(F)
 =\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\int(F-a)^2\rho\,\dd h_E
 \ge e^{-D}
      \inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\int(F-a)^2\,\dd h_E,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V13-variance-comparison}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One-link and corner-interaction Haar floors]
\label{lem:V13-Haar-floors}
Let $f_A(U)=\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}(UA)$ for $A\in\SU(3)$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \int f_A\,\dd U=0,
 \qquad
 \int f_A^2\,\dd U=\frac1{18}.
 \label{eq:V13-one-link-Haar}
\end{equation}
Moreover, for fixed matrices and signs, a two-link word
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(U,V)
 =\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}
  (A_0U^{\sigma}A_1V^{\tau}A_2),
 \qquad \sigma,\tau\in\{1,-1\},
 \label{eq:V13-two-link-word}
\end{equation}
has product-Haar norm squared $1/18$ and is orthogonal to the closed additive
space
\begin{equation}
 \{a(U)+b(V)+c:a\in L^2(\dd U),\ b\in L^2(\dd V),\ c\in\mathbb R\}.
 \label{eq:V13-additive-space}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the same fundamental character orthogonality used in
\Cref{lem:fan-orthogonality}.  Inversion and left or right multiplication by a
fixed group element preserve Haar measure.  For the two-link word, integration
in $V$ gives zero for every fixed $U$, and integration in $U$ gives zero for
every fixed $V$.  Hence $\Phi$ is orthogonal to constants and every one-variable
function.  For fixed $U$, the product in \eqref{eq:V13-two-link-word} is Haar
distributed as $V$ varies, so a second application of
\eqref{eq:V13-one-link-Haar} gives $\|\Phi\|_2^2=1/18$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{A private-coordinate lower bound for the complete Creutz source}
\label{sec:V13-source-loss}
% =============================================================================

Fix a finite card $(N,\beta)$ and abbreviate
\begin{equation}
 G_N(\beta)=\|Y_N^\square\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 I_{N,R}^\square
 =\left\|\mathbb E[Y_N^\square\mid B_{N,R}]\right\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V13-G-I}
\end{equation}
Every selected loop mean $W_{\alpha,N}(\beta)$ is strictly positive.

\begin{theorem}[Complete private-coordinate source-loss floor]
\label{thm:V13-private-source-loss}
For every admissible separating shell $B_{N,R}$,
\begin{equation}
 G_N-I_{N,R}^\square
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18W_{\alpha,N}^2},
 \qquad \alpha\in\{11,10,01\}.
 \label{eq:V13-private-one-link-loss}
\end{equation}
Also,
\begin{equation}
 G_N-I_{N,R}^\square
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{18W_{00,N}^2}.
 \label{eq:V13-private-corner-loss}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_N-I_{N,R}^\square
 \ge
 \max\left\{
 \frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18W_{11,N}^2},
 \frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18W_{10,N}^2},
 \frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18W_{01,N}^2},
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{18W_{00,N}^2}
 \right\}>0.}
 \label{eq:V13-complete-source-loss}
\end{equation}
The missing source component is gauge invariant because it is a conditional
variance of the gauge-invariant Creutz writer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Consider a private edge $e_\alpha$ from
\Cref{lem:V13-private-incidence} and condition on every other link.  Only the
loop $C_\alpha$ depends on $U_{e_\alpha}$, so for fixed exterior links
\[
 Y_N^\square
 =\epsilon_\alpha W_{\alpha,N}^{-1}
   f_A(U_{e_\alpha}^{\sigma})+c
\]
for some exterior-dependent $A\in\SU(3)$, sign $\sigma$, and scalar $c$.
By \Cref{lem:V13-conditional-ellipticity,lem:V13-Haar-floors},
\[
 \operatorname{Var}
  (Y_N^\square\mid\mathscr F_{e_\alpha})
 \ge\frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18W_{\alpha,N}^2}.
\]

For the $00$ arm, condition on all links except $(h_{00},v_{00})$.  By the
incidence statement, the four-loop contrast has the form
\[
 Y_N^\square(U,V)
 =W_{00,N}^{-1}\Phi(U,V)+a(U)+b(V)+c,
\]
where $\Phi$ is a two-link word of the form
\eqref{eq:V13-two-link-word}.  Under product Haar measure, the interaction
$\Phi$ is orthogonal to the remaining additive terms.  Its product-Haar
variance therefore contributes at least $1/(18W_{00,N}^2)$.  The
11-plaquette density comparison gives \eqref{eq:V13-private-corner-loss}.

The chosen source edges lie strictly inside every separating collar, so
$\sigma(B_{N,R})\subseteq\mathscr F_E$.  For nested sigma-algebras
$\mathscr G\subseteq\mathscr H$, conditional Pythagoras gives
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid\mathscr G)
 =\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid\mathscr H)
  +\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}
    (\mathbb E[Y\mid\mathscr H]\mid\mathscr G).
\]
Taking $\mathscr G=\sigma(B_{N,R})$ and $\mathscr H=\mathscr F_E$ proves that
each local conditional floor is also a lower bound for
$G_N-I_{N,R}^\square$.  Taking the maximum proves
\eqref{eq:V13-complete-source-loss}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dimension-free source-entry contraction]
\label{cor:V13-source-entry-gap}
Let
\begin{equation}
 W_{\min,N}=\min_{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square}W_{\alpha,N}.
 \label{eq:V13-Wmin}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 G_N-I_{N,R}^\square
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{18W_{\min,N}^2}.
 \label{eq:V13-min-source-loss}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{G_N-I_{N,R}^\square}{G_N}
 \ge\delta_{\rm ent}(\beta)
 :=\frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{162},
 \qquad
 \frac{I_{N,R}^\square}{G_N}
 \le1-\delta_{\rm ent}(\beta).}
 \label{eq:V13-relative-entry-gap}
\end{equation}
In particular, $G_N>0$ and no finite-coupling separating shell contains the
complete Creutz source as a deterministic function.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose an arm whose mean is $W_{\min,N}$.  If it is one of $11,10,01$, use
\eqref{eq:V13-private-one-link-loss} and weaken $e^{-9\beta}$ to
$e^{-33\beta/2}$.  If it is $00$, use
\eqref{eq:V13-private-corner-loss}.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V13-min-source-loss}.

By \Cref{thm:V10-source-factorization,lem:V11-SU3-trace-range}, the range width
of the complete contrast is at most
\[
 \frac32\sum_{\alpha}W_{\alpha,N}^{-1}
 \le\frac6{W_{\min,N}}.
\]
Popoviciu's variance inequality gives
$G_N\le9/W_{\min,N}^2$.  Dividing
\eqref{eq:V13-min-source-loss} by this upper bound proves
\eqref{eq:V13-relative-entry-gap}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Selected-root absolute contact-loss floor]
\label{cor:V13-root-contact-floor}
At any selected response root
\begin{equation}
 -\log\frac{W_{11,N}W_{00,N}}{W_{10,N}W_{01,N}}=u_*>0,
 \label{eq:V13-root-equation}
\end{equation}
one has, for every separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_N-I_{N,R}^\square
 \ge\frac1{18}
       \exp\left(u_*-\frac{33}{2}\beta_N^{\rm wf}\right).}
 \label{eq:V13-root-absolute-loss}
\end{equation}
Hence the complete source stock is strictly positive on every finite selected
root.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Put $a_\alpha=-\log W_{\alpha,N}\ge0$.  The root equation gives
$a_{11}+a_{00}\ge u_*$.  Hence either
$W_{11,N}\le e^{-u_*/2}$ or $W_{00,N}\le e^{-u_*/2}$.  In the first case,
\eqref{eq:V13-private-one-link-loss} gives
$e^{u_*-9\beta}/18$, which is at least the displayed lower bound.  In the
second case, \eqref{eq:V13-private-corner-loss} gives the common bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What has been removed from the acquisition list]
\label{ass:V13-denominator-removed}
At a finite selected root, the complete source denominator $G_N$ is no longer
an open zero-versus-nonzero row.  The remaining physical questions concern
its cofinal lower scale and the retained shell stocks.  A numerical routine
which reports $G_N=0$ at finite $\beta$ is inconsistent with the literal
four-rectangle Wilson card.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Bounded weak-facing roots now carry an absolute cofinal trichotomy}
\label{sec:V13-bounded-root}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Uniform bounded-root source-entry packet]
\label{thm:V13-bounded-root-entry}
Suppose a cofinal weak-facing subsequence satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0<\beta_n^{\rm wf}\le B<\infty.
 \label{eq:V13-bounded-roots}
\end{equation}
Then, uniformly in $n$ and every admissible separating radius,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_n-I_{n,R}^\square\ge g_B:=\frac{e^{-9B}}{18},
 \qquad
 G_n\ge g_B,}
 \label{eq:V13-bounded-absolute-floor}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{n,R}^\square}{G_n}
 \le1-\delta_B,
 \qquad
 \delta_B:=\frac{e^{-33B/2}}{162}>0.}
 \label{eq:V13-bounded-relative-gap}
\end{equation}
Thus the bounded-root branch has neither complete-source collapse nor exact
source-to-boundary transport.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the private $C_{11}$ edge in
\eqref{eq:V13-private-one-link-loss}.  Since
$W_{11,N}\le1$ and $\beta\le B$, it gives the first inequality in
\eqref{eq:V13-bounded-absolute-floor}; the second follows because
$I_{n,R}^\square\ge0$.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V13-bounded-relative-gap} is
\Cref{cor:V13-source-entry-gap} with $\beta\le B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Absolute bounded-root contraction/contact/positive-range alternative]
\label{cor:V13-bounded-root-trichotomy}
Assume in addition the vanishing-mesh physical shell grid of
\Cref{thm:V12-half-radius}.  After passing to a subsequence, exactly one of the
following occurs on cards with retained stock at least $G_n/2$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B13.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5em]
\item their adjacent source coefficients are eventually bounded above by
      $1-\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon>0$;
\item there are contact-scale cards $c_n$ with $q(c_n)\to1$ and
      \begin{equation}
       I_{n,R(c_n)}^\square\ge\frac{g_B}{2};
       \label{eq:V13-contact-absolute-stock}
      \end{equation}
\item there are positive-range cards $c_n$ with $q(c_n)\to1$,
      $\liminf r(c_n)>0$, and
      \begin{equation}
       I_{n,R(c_n)}^\square\ge\frac{g_B}{2}.
       \label{eq:V13-positive-absolute-stock}
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Every branch also carries the uniform source-entry loss
\eqref{eq:V13-bounded-relative-gap}.  Therefore the contact and positive-range
witnesses are absolute physical-source packets rather than normalized
zero-over-zero effects.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The source lower bound in \eqref{eq:V13-bounded-absolute-floor} supplies the
hypothesis $G_n\ge g_B$ of \Cref{thm:V12-half-radius}.  Its contact half-radius
branch gives either the first or second alternative, and its positive
half-radius branch gives the third.  On either survivor branch,
$I_{n,R(c_n)}^\square\ge G_n/2\ge g_B/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Bounded-root branch status]
\label{ass:V13-bounded-status}
The bounded weak-facing branch is now closed at theorem level: it has a
uniform absolute source stock, a uniform non-gauge source-entry gap, and the
exact contraction/contact/positive-range alternative with absolute survivor
stock.  Choosing which residual shell branch occurs on a numerical card still
requires the already minimal scalar shell Read; it does not require another
source representation.
\end{assessment}
