\section{Escaping roots: noncollapsed source or a typed normalization escape}
\label{sec:V13-escaping-root}
% =============================================================================

For a selected card define the four finite-energy conditioning scales
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \kappa_{11,N}&=e^{9\beta_N/2}W_{11,N},
 &\kappa_{10,N}&=e^{9\beta_N/2}W_{10,N},\\
 \kappa_{01,N}&=e^{9\beta_N/2}W_{01,N},
 &\kappa_{00,N}&=e^{33\beta_N/4}W_{00,N}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:V13-conditioning-scales}
\end{equation}
Then \Cref{thm:V13-private-source-loss} is equivalently
\begin{equation}
 G_N-I_{N,R}^\square
 \ge\frac1{18\kappa_{\alpha,N}^2}
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square.
 \label{eq:V13-kappa-loss}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Escaping-root source alternative]
\label{thm:V13-escaping-source-alternative}
Let $\beta_n^{\rm wf}\to\infty$.  After passing to a subsequence, exactly one
of the following occurs.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E13.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5em]
\item \textbf{Noncollapsed physical source.}  There is $g_*>0$ such that
      $G_n\ge g_*$.  The half-stock theorem gives the same absolute
      contraction/contact/positive-range alternative as in
      \Cref{cor:V13-bounded-root-trichotomy}, with $g_*$ in place of $g_B$.
\item \textbf{Absolute source collapse.}
      \begin{equation}
       G_n\longrightarrow0.
       \label{eq:V13-source-collapse}
      \end{equation}
      Then, for every shell sequence,
      \begin{equation}
       I_{n,R_n}^\square\longrightarrow0,
       \label{eq:V13-all-messages-collapse}
      \end{equation}
      and all four conditioning scales diverge:
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \kappa_{11,n},\kappa_{10,n},\kappa_{01,n},\kappa_{00,n}
       \longrightarrow\infty.}
       \label{eq:V13-all-kappa-diverge}
      \end{equation}
      At a selected response root they obey
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \kappa_{11,n}\kappa_{00,n}
       =e^{15\beta_n/4-u_*}
        \kappa_{10,n}\kappa_{01,n}.}
       \label{eq:V13-kappa-root-balance}
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The second branch is a source-normalization escape of the frozen physical
contrast.  A near-unit ratio of two vanishing shell stocks on that branch is
not an absolute survivor certificate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Pass to a subsequence on which either $G_n$ has a positive lower bound or tends
to zero.  In the first case, apply \Cref{thm:V12-half-radius}.  In the second,
$I_{n,R_n}^\square\le G_n\to0$.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V13-kappa-loss} and
$G_n-I_{n,R}^\square\le G_n$ imply
$1/(18\kappa_{\alpha,n}^2)\le G_n$, proving
\eqref{eq:V13-all-kappa-diverge}.

At a root,
$W_{11}W_{00}=e^{-u_*}W_{10}W_{01}$.  Substitute
\eqref{eq:V13-conditioning-scales}.  The positive-arm exponent is
$9/2+33/4=51/4$ and the negative-arm exponent is $9$, whose difference is
$15/4$.  This gives \eqref{eq:V13-kappa-root-balance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source collapse forces force softening or coupling-memory escape]
\label{cor:V13-force-or-memory}
At any simple selected root, let
\begin{equation}
 s_n=-\chi_{N_n}'(\beta_n^{\rm wf}),
 \qquad
 J_{*,n}=\operatorname{Var}_{\beta_n^{\rm wf}}(A_{N_n}).
 \label{eq:V13-slope-action-variance}
\end{equation}
On the source-collapse branch,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{|s_n|}{\sqrt{J_{*,n}}}
 \le\sqrt{G_n}\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V13-unit-score-force-softening}
\end{equation}
If $\liminf|s_n|>0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{J_{*,n}\ge\frac{s_n^2}{G_n}\longrightarrow\infty.}
 \label{eq:V13-coupling-memory-escape}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The Version~V12 response-force identity is
$s_n=\langle Y_n,V_n\rangle$, where
$\|Y_n\|_2^2=G_n$ and $\|V_n\|_2^2=J_{*,n}$.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives both
claims.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Renormalizing a collapsed source changes the programme]
\label{fire:V13-no-silent-rescaling}
On branch~\textup{(E13.2)}, the normalized vector
$Y_n/\sqrt{G_n}$ may still have nontrivial relative shell coefficients.  It is
not an absolute occurrence of the frozen source unless the diverging
renormalization is independently calibrated and transported.  Such a
renormalized composite is a new physical loading and is not created by a
zero-over-zero radial ratio.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V14 direction: the remaining upstream issue is source normalization}
\label{sec:V14-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V13 proved a strict private-coordinate loss for the one frozen Creutz
contrast.  It also left a bounded-root contraction/contact/positive-range
alternative on the residual shell messages.  Before that alternative can be
exported as a cofinal physical source packet, however, one must determine
whether the frozen normalization itself remains finite.  A ratio of two
positive stocks does not answer that question.

The present continuation combines two already literal pieces of Wilson
structure:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(U14.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item the private-edge and private-corner analysis of Version~V13, now applied
      to every coefficient vector in the complete four-arm normalized loop
      frame; and
\item the exact one-link conditional density floor, now iterated along one
      complete rectangle side at the actual coupling rather than weakened to
      a fixed bounded-coupling constant.
\end{enumerate}
The result is an exact four-dimensional source-frame coercivity theorem and a
source-overdrive lower bound which is valid at every finite coupling.  On a
bounded weak-facing branch the hidden source stock diverges exponentially in
$N$.  More generally, any cofinal branch on which the frozen physical source
has a uniform upper $L^2$ bound must satisfy a logarithmic lower bound on the
selected coupling.  Thus bounded roots and sublogarithmic escaping roots are
not candidates for an unrenormalized finite source landing.

No new radial estimator is introduced.  The Version~V11 two-scalar posterior
loss and the Version~V10 matrix card remain the correct downstream Reads once
source normalization has passed.

\begin{firewall}[Overdrive is not contraction]
\label{fire:V14-overdrive-not-contraction}
A divergent source stock is a failure of the frozen physical normalization,
not a proof that an outward conditional-expectation coefficient is small.
Conversely, a near-unit ratio of two divergent stocks is not a finite cofinal
source survivor.  The present theorem precedes the adjacent-shell radial
verdict and does not replace it.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The complete normalized four-arm source frame}
\label{sec:V14-four-arm-frame}
% =============================================================================

Retain the Version~V10 ordering
$\mathfrak I_\square=(11,00,10,01)$ and write
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf Y_N
 :=\bigl(Y_{11,N},Y_{00,N},Y_{10,N},Y_{01,N}\bigr)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 Y_{\alpha,N}=\frac{\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}}{W_{\alpha,N}}-1.
 \label{eq:V14-normalized-loop-vector}
\end{equation}
Its complete equal-time source metric, shell message, shell-message metric,
and hidden source metric are
\begin{align}
 \Gamma_N
 &:=\mathbb E[\mathbf Y_N\mathbf Y_N^{\mathsf T}],
 \label{eq:V14-full-source-metric}\\
 \mathbf U_{N,R}
 &:=\mathbb E[\mathbf Y_N\mid B_{N,R}],
 \qquad
 M_{N,R}:=\mathbb E[\mathbf U_{N,R}\mathbf U_{N,R}^{\mathsf T}],
 \label{eq:V14-message-metric}\\
 H_{N,R}
 &:=\Gamma_N-M_{N,R}
 =\mathbb E\!\left[
  (\mathbf Y_N-\mathbf U_{N,R})
  (\mathbf Y_N-\mathbf U_{N,R})^{\mathsf T}
 \right]\succeq0.
 \label{eq:V14-hidden-source-metric}
\end{align}
Let
\begin{equation}
 D_{W,N}=\operatorname{diag}
 (W_{11,N},W_{00,N},W_{10,N},W_{01,N}).
 \label{eq:V14-loop-mean-diagonal}
\end{equation}
All four diagonal entries are strictly positive on every finite selected
Wilson card.

\begin{theorem}[Complete four-arm private-coordinate coercivity]
\label{thm:V14-four-arm-coercivity}
For every finite coupling $\beta>0$ and every admissible separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 H_{N,R}
 \succeq
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{72}\,D_{W,N}^{-2}.}
 \label{eq:V14-absolute-matrix-floor}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_N\preceq\frac94D_{W,N}^{-2},}
 \label{eq:V14-source-metric-upper}
\end{equation}
so that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 H_{N,R}
 \succeq
 \delta_{\rm ent}(\beta)\Gamma_N,
 \qquad
 M_{N,R}
 \preceq
 \bigl(1-\delta_{\rm ent}(\beta)\bigr)\Gamma_N,}
 \label{eq:V14-relative-matrix-gap}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \delta_{\rm ent}(\beta)
 :=\frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{162}>0.}
 \label{eq:V14-entry-gap-constant}
\end{equation}
In particular, $\Gamma_N$ and $H_{N,R}$ are positive definite and the complete
normalized four-loop source frame has rank four.  No nonzero normalized
four-loop contrast is measurable with respect to a separating shell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $a=(a_{11},a_{00},a_{10},a_{01})^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^4$ and put
\[
 F_a=a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N.
\]
For $\alpha\in\{11,10,01\}$, condition on the private edge
$e_\alpha$ of \Cref{lem:V13-private-incidence}.  Every loop other than
$C_\alpha$ is then constant in that link, so
\[
 F_a
 =\frac{a_\alpha}{W_{\alpha,N}}f_A(U_{e_\alpha}^{\sigma})+c
\]
for an exterior-dependent $A\in\SU(3)$, orientation $\sigma$, and scalar $c$.
The one-link part of
\Cref{lem:V13-conditional-ellipticity,lem:V13-Haar-floors} gives
\begin{equation}
 a^{\mathsf T}H_{N,R}a
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18}
 \frac{a_\alpha^2}{W_{\alpha,N}^2},
 \qquad \alpha\in\{11,10,01\}.
 \label{eq:V14-three-private-directions}
\end{equation}
For the $00$ coefficient, condition on the private corner pair
$(h_{00},v_{00})$.  Exactly as in the proof of
\Cref{thm:V13-private-source-loss}, the $00$ term is the only two-variable
interaction and all other loop terms lie in the additive one-variable space.
Therefore
\begin{equation}
 a^{\mathsf T}H_{N,R}a
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{18}
 \frac{a_{00}^2}{W_{00,N}^2}.
 \label{eq:V14-private-corner-direction}
\end{equation}
The shell sigma-algebra is contained in each exterior sigma-algebra used
above, so conditional Pythagoras passes every local lower bound to
$H_{N,R}$.

Since $e^{-9\beta}\ge e^{-33\beta/2}$, the four inequalities imply
\[
 a^{\mathsf T}H_{N,R}a
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{18}
 \max_{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square}
 \frac{a_\alpha^2}{W_{\alpha,N}^2}
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{72}
 \sum_\alpha\frac{a_\alpha^2}{W_{\alpha,N}^2},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V14-absolute-matrix-floor}.

By \Cref{lem:V11-SU3-trace-range}, each real normalized loop trace
$\mathcal O_\alpha$ has range length $3/2$.  Constants do not affect range,
so
\[
 \operatorname{osc}(F_a)
 \le\frac32\sum_\alpha\frac{|a_\alpha|}{W_{\alpha,N}}
 \le3\left(\sum_\alpha\frac{a_\alpha^2}{W_{\alpha,N}^2}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Popoviciu's variance inequality gives
\[
 a^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_Na
 =\operatorname{Var}(F_a)
 \le\frac14\operatorname{osc}(F_a)^2
 \le\frac94a^{\mathsf T}D_{W,N}^{-2}a,
\]
proving \eqref{eq:V14-source-metric-upper}.  Thus
$D_{W,N}^{-2}\succeq(4/9)\Gamma_N$, and substitution into
\eqref{eq:V14-absolute-matrix-floor} gives
\eqref{eq:V14-relative-matrix-gap}.  Strict positivity follows from the
positive diagonal matrix on the right of
\eqref{eq:V14-absolute-matrix-floor}.  If a nonzero contrast were
$B_{N,R}$-measurable, its hidden conditional variance would vanish,
contradicting the same inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source-whitened entry singular-value bound]
\label{cor:V14-entry-singular-value}
Let $\mathscr S_N:\mathbb R^4\to L_0^2(\mu_{N,\beta})$ synthesize the four
normalized loop writers, and let $P_R$ be conditional expectation onto
$B_{N,R}$.  In the source metric $\Gamma_N$, the shell-visible synthesis
$P_R\mathscr S_N$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left\|
  P_R\mathscr S_N\Gamma_N^{-1/2}
 \right\|_{\rm op}^2
 \le1-\delta_{\rm ent}(\beta).}
 \label{eq:V14-entry-singular-value}
\end{equation}
Thus the source-to-first-shell channel is strictly contractive on the entire
four-arm source atlas at every finite coupling.  This is not a uniform bound
for every later adjacent shell.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The Gram of the source-whitened visible synthesis is
$\Gamma_N^{-1/2}M_{N,R}\Gamma_N^{-1/2}$.  Apply
\eqref{eq:V14-relative-matrix-gap} and take the largest eigenvalue.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Sharp all-coupling Haar refresh and physical-rectangle attenuation}
\label{sec:V14-sharp-refresh}
% =============================================================================

Version~V6 of the dedicated trajectory analysis used a fixed bounded-coupling
Haar-refresh mass.  Version~V13 supplies the sharper one-link conditional
ellipticity at the actual coupling.  The next statement records the resulting
all-coupling form directly in the present series.

\begin{lemma}[Actual-coupling one-link Haar refresh]
\label{lem:V14-actual-Haar-refresh}
Condition on every link except one.  The conditional density $h_{e,\beta}$ of
that link relative to normalized Haar measure has the decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 h_{e,\beta}(U)
 =c_\beta+(1-c_\beta)\widetilde h_{e,\beta}(U),
 \qquad
 c_\beta=e^{-9\beta},}
 \label{eq:V14-Haar-refresh}
\end{equation}
where $\widetilde h_{e,\beta}\ge0$ and
$\int\widetilde h_{e,\beta}\,\dd U=1$.

If $S$ is a finite link set such that no plaquette contains two links of $S$,
the joint conditional density of $(U_e)_{e\in S}$ factors into the product of
the one-link densities in \eqref{eq:V14-Haar-refresh}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For one link, \Cref{lem:V13-conditional-ellipticity} has $n(E)=6$ and gives
$h_{e,\beta}\ge e^{-9\beta}=c_\beta$.  Since $h_{e,\beta}$ integrates to one,
\[
 \widetilde h_{e,\beta}
 :=\frac{h_{e,\beta}-c_\beta}{1-c_\beta}
\]
is a probability density for $\beta>0$.  If no plaquette contains two
selected links, every conditional plaquette term depends on at most one of
them.  The exponent and product Haar measure therefore factorize.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[All-coupling attenuation along an isolated loop side]
\label{thm:V14-all-coupling-loop-attenuation}
Let $C$ be a simple loop and let $S$ be a set of $m$ edges of $C$, each
traversed once, such that no plaquette contains two selected edges.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \mathbb E_{\mu_{N,\beta}}
  \frac13\operatorname{ReTr}U(C)
 \right|
 \le(1-e^{-9\beta})^m.}
 \label{eq:V14-all-coupling-attenuation}
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds in a finite region with arbitrary fixed exterior
links.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Condition on all links outside $S$ and use the factorization in
\Cref{lem:V14-actual-Haar-refresh}.  Expand the product of the $m$ refresh
decompositions.  Every term containing at least one Haar factor vanishes after
integration in that edge, because the loop trace is a nontrivial fundamental
matrix coefficient of that link or its inverse.  Only the term selecting
$\widetilde h_{e,\beta}$ at every edge remains.  Its coefficient is
$(1-e^{-9\beta})^m$ and the real normalized trace is bounded in absolute value
by one.  Averaging the exterior proves the claim.
\end{proof}

For the selected rectangles, define the longest available side lengths
\begin{equation}
 \ell_{00,N}=\frac N4,
 \qquad
 \ell_{10,N}=\ell_{01,N}=\ell_{11,N}=\frac{3N}{8}.
 \label{eq:V14-long-side-lengths}
\end{equation}
Every edge on one straight side satisfies the no-common-plaquette condition.

\begin{corollary}[Sharp physical-rectangle attenuation]
\label{cor:V14-rectangle-attenuation}
For every finite selected Wilson card and every $\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0<W_{\alpha,N}(\beta)
 \le
 \bigl(1-e^{-9\beta}\bigr)^{\ell_{\alpha,N}}.}
 \label{eq:V14-rectangle-attenuation}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 W_{11,N}(\beta)^2
 \le
 \bigl(1-e^{-9\beta}\bigr)^{3N/4}.}
 \label{eq:V14-W11-square-upper}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose all elementary links on a longest straight side of the rectangle and
apply \Cref{thm:V14-all-coupling-loop-attenuation}.  The side counts follow
from \eqref{eq:V13-half-lengths}.  Strict positivity is part of the inherited
finite Wilson character layer.
\end{proof}

\section{Source overdrive and the exact logarithmic scale}
\label{sec:V14-overdrive}
% =============================================================================

Put
\begin{equation}
 x(\beta)=e^{-9\beta}\in(0,1).
 \label{eq:V14-x-beta}
\end{equation}
For a separating shell, write
\begin{equation}
 L_{N,R}^{\rm hid}(\beta)
 :=G_N(\beta)-I_{N,R}^{\square}(\beta).
 \label{eq:V14-hidden-Creutz-stock}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-overdrive lower envelope]
\label{thm:V14-source-overdrive-envelope}
For every finite coupling and every admissible separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 L_{N,R}^{\rm hid}(\beta)
 \ge
 \mathfrak L_N(\beta)
 :=\frac{x(\beta)}{18}
   \bigl(1-x(\beta)\bigr)^{-3N/4}.}
 \label{eq:V14-exact-overdrive-envelope}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 L_{N,R}^{\rm hid}(\beta)
 \ge
 \frac1{18}\exp\!\left(
  \frac{3N}{4}e^{-9\beta}-9\beta
 \right).}
 \label{eq:V14-exponential-overdrive-envelope}
\end{equation}
The complete hidden four-arm metric also obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lambda_{\min}(H_{N,R})
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{72}
 \bigl(1-e^{-9\beta}\bigr)^{-N/2}.}
 \label{eq:V14-full-frame-overdrive}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the $11$ private-edge term of
\eqref{eq:V13-private-one-link-loss} and then
\eqref{eq:V14-W11-square-upper}:
\[
 L_{N,R}^{\rm hid}
 \ge\frac{e^{-9\beta}}{18W_{11,N}^2}
 \ge\frac{x(\beta)}{18}
       (1-x(\beta))^{-3N/4}.
\]
Since $-\log(1-x)\ge x$ for $0<x<1$, this implies
\eqref{eq:V14-exponential-overdrive-envelope}.

For the matrix estimate, combine
\eqref{eq:V14-absolute-matrix-floor} with
\eqref{eq:V14-rectangle-attenuation}.  Every selected rectangle has a side of
length at least $N/4$, hence
\[
 D_{W,N}^{-2}
 \succeq(1-e^{-9\beta})^{-N/2}I_4.
\]
Substitution proves \eqref{eq:V14-full-frame-overdrive}.
\end{proof}

Define the source-normalization exponent
\begin{equation}
 \Theta_N(\beta)
 :=\frac{3N}{4}e^{-9\beta}-9\beta.
 \label{eq:V14-normalization-exponent}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal normalization trichotomy]
\label{cor:V14-normalization-trichotomy}
Along any selected sequence $(N_n,\beta_n)$, pass to a subsequence on which one
of the following occurs.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N14.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.2em]
\item $\Theta_{N_n}(\beta_n)\to+\infty$.  Then
      $L_{N_n,R_n}^{\rm hid}\to\infty$ for every separating shell sequence:
      the frozen source is overdriven.
\item $\Theta_{N_n}(\beta_n)\to\theta\in\mathbb R$.  Then the hidden source stock
      has a uniform positive lower bound.
\item $\Theta_{N_n}(\beta_n)\to-\infty$.  This is the only branch on which
      $G_{N_n}(\beta_n)\to0$ is possible.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, source collapse implies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{3N_n}{4}e^{-9\beta_n}-9\beta_n
 \longrightarrow-\infty.}
 \label{eq:V14-collapse-scale-necessary}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The extended real line is sequentially compact, so every real sequence has a
subsequence converging to $+\infty$, to a finite real number, or to
$-\infty$.  Apply
\eqref{eq:V14-exponential-overdrive-envelope}.  Since
$0\le L_{N,R}^{\rm hid}\le G_N$, source collapse forces the displayed lower
bound to tend to zero, which is exactly
\eqref{eq:V14-collapse-scale-necessary}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sublogarithmic escape is source overdrive]
\label{cor:V14-sublog-overdrive}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$.  If along a cofinal sequence
\begin{equation}
 \beta_n
 \le\left(\frac19-\varepsilon\right)\log N_n
 \label{eq:V14-sublog-hypothesis}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $n$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_{N_n}(\beta_n)-I_{N_n,R_n}^{\square}(\beta_n)
 \longrightarrow\infty}
 \label{eq:V14-sublog-conclusion}
\end{equation}
for every separating shell sequence.  Therefore a collapsed or uniformly
bounded frozen source requires
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \frac{\beta_n}{\log N_n}\ge\frac19.}
 \label{eq:V14-logarithmic-rate}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Under \eqref{eq:V14-sublog-hypothesis},
\[
 e^{-9\beta_n}\ge N_n^{-1+9\varepsilon}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \Theta_{N_n}(\beta_n)
 \ge\frac34N_n^{9\varepsilon}
    -(1-9\varepsilon)\log N_n
 \longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
Use \Cref{cor:V14-normalization-trichotomy}.  The last assertion is the
contrapositive along every subsequence.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{A finite source frame forces quantitative root escape}
\label{sec:V14-logarithmic-escape}
% =============================================================================

Let $\mathcal W_0:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ denote the principal Lambert
function, characterized by
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal W_0(z)e^{\mathcal W_0(z)}=z.
 \label{eq:V14-Lambert-definition}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic escape forced by a bounded frozen source]
\label{thm:V14-bounded-source-forces-escape}
Suppose on a sequence of selected cards that
\begin{equation}
 G_N(\beta_N)\le G^*<\infty.
 \label{eq:V14-source-upper-window}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 e^{-9\beta_N}
 \le
 \frac{4}{3N}
 \mathcal W_0\!\left(\frac{27}{2}G^*N\right),}
 \label{eq:V14-Lambert-x-bound}
\end{equation}
and hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta_N
 \ge
 \frac19\log\!\left[
  \frac{3N}
       {4\mathcal W_0((27/2)G^*N)}
 \right].}
 \label{eq:V14-Lambert-beta-bound}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta_N
 \ge
 \frac19\bigl(\log N-\log\log N-O_{G^*}(1)\bigr).}
 \label{eq:V14-loglog-asymptotic}
\end{equation}
Thus any direct cofinal landing of the frozen source in a source-faithful
Hilbert space, even only weakly, forces the weak-facing roots to escape at
least at this logarithmic rate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hidden stock is at most the complete stock.  By
\eqref{eq:V14-exponential-overdrive-envelope}, with
$x=e^{-9\beta_N}$,
\[
 x\exp\!\left(\frac{3N}{4}x\right)
 \le18G^*.
\]
Put $y=3Nx/4$.  Then
\[
 ye^y\le\frac{27}{2}G^*N.
\]
The function $y\mapsto ye^y$ is increasing on $[0,\infty)$, so
$y\le\mathcal W_0((27/2)G^*N)$, proving
\eqref{eq:V14-Lambert-x-bound}.  Taking $-\frac19\log$ gives
\eqref{eq:V14-Lambert-beta-bound}.  The standard elementary bounds
$\mathcal W_0(z)\le\log(1+z)$ and
$\mathcal W_0(z)=\log z-\log\log z+o(1)$ give
\eqref{eq:V14-loglog-asymptotic}.

A weakly convergent sequence in a Hilbert space is norm bounded.  Therefore a
source-faithful isometric landing of the frozen source implies
\eqref{eq:V14-source-upper-window}, and the same conclusion follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded weak-facing roots are a source-overdrive obstruction]
\label{cor:V14-bounded-root-overdrive}
Suppose a cofinal weak-facing subsequence satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0<\beta_n^{\rm wf}\le B<\infty.
 \label{eq:V14-bounded-root-hypothesis}
\end{equation}
Put $x_B=e^{-9B}$.  Then every separating shell obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_n-I_{n,R}^{\square}
 \ge
 \frac{x_B}{18}(1-x_B)^{-3N_n/4}
 \ge
 \frac1{18}\exp\!\left(
  \frac{3N_n}{4}x_B-9B
 \right)
 \longrightarrow\infty.}
 \label{eq:V14-bounded-root-overdrive}
\end{equation}
The complete hidden four-arm metric satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lambda_{\min}(H_{n,R})
 \ge
 \frac{e^{-33B/2}}{72}
 (1-x_B)^{-N_n/2}
 \longrightarrow\infty.}
 \label{eq:V14-bounded-root-frame-overdrive}
\end{equation}
At the same time the four raw rectangle means vanish by
\eqref{eq:V14-rectangle-attenuation}.  Hence the bounded branch is a
zero-over-zero response carried by an infinitely overdriven normalized source
frame.  Without an independently loaded cutoff-dependent renormalization it
is a typed rough-Haar/source-normalization obstruction, not a finite absolute
contact or positive-range source packet.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The function $x\mapsto x(1-x)^{-3N/4}$ is increasing on $(0,1)$.  Since
$\beta_n\le B$, one has $x(\beta_n)\ge x_B$, and
\eqref{eq:V14-exact-overdrive-envelope} gives the first inequality.  The
second is $-\log(1-x_B)\ge x_B$.  The matrix bound follows similarly from
\eqref{eq:V14-full-frame-overdrive}.  Finally, every side length in
\eqref{eq:V14-long-side-lengths} tends to infinity, so
\eqref{eq:V14-rectangle-attenuation} sends all four raw means to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Qualification of the Version V13 bounded branch]
\label{ass:V14-V13-bounded-qualification}
The normalized radial alternatives of \Cref{cor:V13-bounded-root-trichotomy}
remain valid as statements about conditional-expectation ratios.  Version~V14
adds the logically prior fact that the frozen source metric diverges on that
branch.  Therefore those ratios may be exported as a finite physical source
only after a cutoff-dependent normalization has been declared, calibrated,
and transported.  Without that new loading, the bounded branch terminates at
source overdrive.
\end{assessment}

\section{The unavoidable normalization tax}
\label{sec:V14-normalization-tax}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Minimum cutoff-dependent rescaling required by a finite source]
\label{thm:V14-normalization-tax}
Let $a_N\in\mathbb R$ and suppose the rescaled frozen source
$\widetilde Y_N=a_NY_N^\square$ has a uniform upper stock
\begin{equation}
 \|\widetilde Y_N\|_2^2\le M.
 \label{eq:V14-rescaled-upper-stock}
\end{equation}
Then, for every separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |a_N|^2
 \le
 18M e^{9\beta_N}
 \bigl(1-e^{-9\beta_N}\bigr)^{3N/4}.}
 \label{eq:V14-normalization-tax}
\end{equation}
On a bounded-root branch $\beta_N\le B$ this forces
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |a_N|
 \le
 \sqrt{18M}\,e^{9B/2}
 (1-e^{-9B})^{3N/8}
 \longrightarrow0}
 \label{eq:V14-bounded-normalization-tax}
\end{equation}
exponentially.  Therefore a finite replacement of the bounded-branch source
is necessarily a new cutoff-dependent physical loading; it cannot be an
unchanged occurrence of the frozen Creutz source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:V14-exact-overdrive-envelope},
\[
 \|a_NY_N^\square\|_2^2
 =|a_N|^2G_N
 \ge|a_N|^2\mathfrak L_N(\beta_N).
\]
Combine this with \eqref{eq:V14-rescaled-upper-stock} and invert
$\mathfrak L_N$.  The bounded-coupling statement follows by monotonicity.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Whitening does not occur by notation]
\label{fire:V14-no-automatic-whitening}
The unit vector $Y_N^\square/\sqrt{G_N}$ exists on every finite card, but its
appearance in a Rayleigh quotient does not establish a cutoff-compatible
physical source.  A cofinal normalized source requires an actual amplitude
calibration, source-faithful transport, and a nonvanishing target Read.  The
normalization tax above quantifies the missing amplitude on the bounded
branch.
\end{firewall}

\section{Revised cofinal route and termination boundary}
\label{sec:V14-cofinal-route}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Version V14 source-normalization alternative]
\label{thm:V14-cofinal-alternative}
For any cofinal sequence of finite weak-facing cards, after passage to a
subsequence exactly one of the following source-normalization branches is
available.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C14.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.2em]
\item \emph{Overdrive.}  The hidden stock, or the least hidden four-arm source
      eigenvalue, diverges.  The frozen source has no direct finite Hilbert
      landing.  A renormalized replacement must be declared as a new loading.
\item \emph{Finite noncollapsed source.}  There are constants
      $0<g_*\le G_N\le G^*<\infty$.  Then
      \eqref{eq:V14-Lambert-beta-bound} forces logarithmic root escape, and the
      only remaining radial acquisition is the Version~V11 two-scalar
      posterior-loss card with its physical-width tag.
\item \emph{Source collapse.}  $G_N\to0$.  Then
      \eqref{eq:V14-collapse-scale-necessary} and
      \eqref{eq:V14-logarithmic-rate} hold, every absolute shell message
      collapses, and no absolute survivor of the frozen source is reported.
\item \emph{Unbounded but non-overdrive-classified source.}  The stock is not
      uniformly bounded, while the explicit lower envelope does not itself
      tend to infinity.  The actual source stock is the first unresolved
      physical value; a radial ratio is not read before it.
\end{enumerate}
On branch~\textup{(C14.2)}, the existing contraction/contact/positive-range
trichotomy is complete once the two scalar shell stocks are populated.  On
branches~\textup{(C14.1)} and~\textup{(C14.3)}, continuation with a normalized
source requires a separately declared physical loading.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Pass to subsequences according to the lower-envelope behaviour and the upper
and lower behaviour of $G_N$.  The conclusions of the first and third branches
are \Cref{cor:V14-normalization-trichotomy}.  The second branch uses
\Cref{thm:V14-bounded-source-forces-escape} and the already proved Version~V11
radial identity.  The fourth branch records the only remaining possibility
without inferring an unmeasured stock.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The actual upstream advance]
\label{ass:V14-progress}
The first unresolved arrow is no longer merely ``bounded roots or escaping
roots.''  For the frozen physical source it is now:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{source overdrive}\\
 \text{or a logarithmically escaping finite source}\\
 \text{or source collapse/new loading}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V14-upstream-summary}
\end{equation}
The bounded-root branch has been decided conditionally: it is incompatible
with a finite unrenormalized source frame.  What remains on the admissible
finite-source branch is one actual source-stock interval and one actual
posterior shell-loss interval, not another representation theorem.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Version V14 export]
\label{thm:V14-export}
Versions~V1--V13 are retained.  Version~V14 additionally exports
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 H_{N,R}\succeq\frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{72}D_{W,N}^{-2}

 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 G_N-I_{N,R}^{\square}\to\infty,\\[0.35em]

 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V14-export}

This is a source-kernel and normalization export.  It neither populates the

\begin{proof}

\Cref{thm:V14-four-arm-coercivity,thm:V14-source-overdrive-envelope,thm:V14-bounded-source-forces-escape,cor:V14-sublog-overdrive,cor:V14-bounded-root-overdrive}.
\end{proof}

\begin{openproblem}[Version V15: populate the logarithmic-or-faster physical source branch or terminate]
\label{op:V14-next}
Preserve the complete present source.  No further equivalent radial estimator,
source encoding, or generic shell theorem is opened.  Proceed in this order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V15.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item If the selected weak-facing roots have a bounded subsequence, export the

\item Otherwise place the selected roots relative to the logarithmic threshold

\item On the logarithmic-or-faster branch, acquire one actual interval for the

      the primitive survivor polarization.  Its support is already certified
      by \Cref{thm:V14-four-arm-coercivity}.
\item Terminate YM--B after exporting the first selected-root radial packet or
      the source-normalization obstruction to YM--A.
\end{enumerate}
The first remaining datum is therefore an absolute selected source-stock
interval in the logarithmic-or-faster window.  A sixth representation of the
same radial ratio is circular.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of Version V14]
\label{fire:V14-scope}
The new results use the literal rectangle geometry, exact $SU(3)$ trace range,
finite-energy one-link law, Haar refresh, and the already established private
coordinates.  They prove full four-arm source-frame coercivity and quantify
the only coupling scale on which the frozen source can remain finite.  They do
not determine the actual weak-facing sequence, populate $G_N$ or a shell-loss
Read on that sequence, control the source-orthogonal Wilson-network core,
construct a temporal transfer, or prove a Yang--Mills mass gap.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V15 direction: absolute overdrive and relative transmission must be separated}
\label{sec:V15-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V14 proved that the frozen normalized Creutz source is exponentially
overdriven on every bounded-coupling cofinal branch.  That is an absolute
normalization obstruction.  It does not decide the scale-invariant radial
quantity
\[
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}}{G_N}
 =\frac{\|\mathbb E[Y_N^{\square}\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2}
       {\|Y_N^{\square}\|_2^2}.
\]
Continuing with a further representation of the Version~V11 two-scalar card
would therefore be circular.  The correct upstream question is whether the
same long-side Haar refresh which made the rectangle means small also makes
\emph{all second moments and cross moments} asymptotically Haar.  If it does,
the complete four-loop source metric is well conditioned in the bounded raw
loop coordinates while every boundary message is small.  The radial quotient
can then be decided even when the original normalized source norm diverges.

The present continuation proves exactly that.  Its principal output is a
Wilson-specific generalized contraction
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 M_{N,R}\preceq
 \kappa_N(\beta)^2\,\Gamma_N,
 \qquad
 \kappa_N(\beta)^2
 =\frac{288\,r_N(\beta)^2}{1-143\,r_N(\beta)},}
 \label{eq:V15-principal-contraction-preview}
\end{equation}
valid whenever $143r_N(\beta)<1$, where
\begin{equation}
 r_N(\beta):=\bigl(1-e^{-9\beta}\bigr)^{N/4}.
 \label{eq:V15-r-preview}
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform over every admissible separating shell.  In particular,
if $Ne^{-9\beta_N}\to\infty$, then $\kappa_N(\beta_N)\to0$.
This includes every bounded weak-facing branch and every refresh-dominant
escaping branch.

The same calculation supplies a canonical cutoff-dependent amplitude which
balances the four raw Wilson-loop coefficients before any shell value is read.
It pays the Version~V14 normalization tax without whitening by an unknown
source stock and leaves every radial ratio unchanged.

\begin{firewall}[No new radial estimator]
\label{fire:V15-no-new-estimator}
The proof below does not introduce a sixth estimator of
$I_{N,S}^{\square}/I_{N,R}^{\square}$.  It derives a direct upper bound for the
existing conditional expectation from the literal Wilson one-link law and the
literal four rectangle paths.  On the remaining logarithmic-or-faster window,
the Version~V11 posterior-loss Read remains the target-minimal physical
acquisition.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The bounded raw four-loop frame and its shell messages}
\label{sec:V15-raw-frame}
% =============================================================================

Retain the ordering
$\mathfrak I_\square=(11,00,10,01)$ and put
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf O_N
 :=(\mathcal O_{11,N},\mathcal O_{00,N},
    \mathcal O_{10,N},\mathcal O_{01,N})^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \mathbf W_N:=\mathbb E\mathbf O_N.
 \label{eq:V15-raw-loop-vector}
\end{equation}
The centered bounded raw-loop vector is
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf X_N:=\mathbf O_N-\mathbf W_N.
 \label{eq:V15-centered-raw-vector}
\end{equation}
Define its equal-time covariance, boundary message, and boundary-message
covariance by
\begin{align}
 \Sigma_N
 &:=\mathbb E[\mathbf X_N\mathbf X_N^{\mathsf T}],
 \label{eq:V15-raw-covariance}\\
 \mathbf m_{N,R}
 &:=\mathbb E[\mathbf X_N\mid B_{N,R}],
 \qquad
 K_{N,R}:=\mathbb E[\mathbf m_{N,R}\mathbf m_{N,R}^{\mathsf T}].
 \label{eq:V15-raw-message-covariance}
\end{align}
With $D_{W,N}$ from \eqref{eq:V14-loop-mean-diagonal}, the normalized frame of
Version~V14 satisfies the exact congruences
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbf Y_N=D_{W,N}^{-1}\mathbf X_N,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_N=D_{W,N}^{-1}\Sigma_ND_{W,N}^{-1},
 \qquad
 M_{N,R}=D_{W,N}^{-1}K_{N,R}D_{W,N}^{-1}.}
 \label{eq:V15-raw-normalized-congruence}
\end{equation}
Thus a generalized order $K_{N,R}\preceq q^2\Sigma_N$ in the bounded raw
coordinates is exactly the same order $M_{N,R}\preceq q^2\Gamma_N$ in the
possibly overdriven normalized source coordinates.

For the rest of the append put
\begin{equation}
 x(\beta):=e^{-9\beta},
 \qquad
 \rho(\beta):=1-x(\beta),
 \qquad
 r_N(\beta):=\rho(\beta)^{N/4}.
 \label{eq:V15-refresh-parameters}
\end{equation}

% =============================================================================
\section{A private straight side for every pair of physical rectangles}
\label{sec:V15-pair-private-geometry}
% =============================================================================

The second-moment argument needs not only a long side of one rectangle, but a
long side which is absent from any prescribed different rectangle.

\begin{lemma}[Pair-private straight-side geometry]
\label{lem:V15-pair-private-side}
For every ordered pair of distinct labels
$\alpha,\gamma\in\mathfrak I_\square$, the rectangle $C_\alpha$ contains a
straight side $S_{\alpha\mid\gamma}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |S_{\alpha\mid\gamma}|\ge\frac N4,
 \qquad
 S_{\alpha\mid\gamma}\cap E(C_\gamma)=\varnothing,}
 \label{eq:V15-pair-private-side}
\end{equation}
and no plaquette contains two edges of $S_{\alpha\mid\gamma}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $C_\alpha=C(r_i,t_j)$ and $C_\gamma=C(r_k,t_\ell)$ with
$r_0=t_0=N/8$ and $r_1=t_1=3N/16$.  If $r_i\ne r_k$, choose either vertical
side of $C_\alpha$.  It lies on the line $x=\pm r_i$, whereas the vertical
sides of $C_\gamma$ lie on $x=\pm r_k$; the horizontal sides of
$C_\gamma$ have the other edge orientation.  Hence no selected edge belongs
to $C_\gamma$.  Its length is $2t_j\ge N/4$.

If $r_i=r_k$, distinctness of the labels forces $t_j\ne t_\ell$.  Choose
either horizontal side of $C_\alpha$.  It lies on $y=\pm t_j$, distinct from
the horizontal sides of $C_\gamma$, and its edge orientation differs from the
vertical sides of $C_\gamma$.  Its length is $2r_i\ge N/4$.

Finally, a plaquette contains at most one edge from a fixed straight lattice
line in a fixed orientation.  Hence no plaquette contains two selected side
edges.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Long-side refresh controls means, second moments, and mixed moments}
\label{sec:V15-refresh-moments}
% =============================================================================

For a simple loop $C$, write
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal O_C(U):=\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}U(C).
 \label{eq:V15-loop-observable}
\end{equation}
The next theorem is the new moment consequence of the exact mixture
\eqref{eq:V14-Haar-refresh}.

\begin{theorem}[Conditional Haar thermalization from one isolated side]
\label{thm:V15-conditional-Haar-thermalization}
Let $S$ be a set of $m$ once-traversed edges of a simple loop $C$, with no
plaquette containing two selected edges.  Condition on all links outside $S$.
Then there are exterior-measurable quantities $q_C,q_{C^2}$ satisfying
$|q_C|\le1$ and $0\le q_{C^2}\le1$ such that
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 &=\rho(\beta)^m q_C,
 \label{eq:V15-conditional-first-moment}\\
 \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C^2\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 &=\frac{1-\rho(\beta)^m}{18}
   +\rho(\beta)^m q_{C^2}.
 \label{eq:V15-conditional-second-moment}
\end{align}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C^2\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]-\frac1{18}
 \right|
 \le\frac{17}{18}\rho(\beta)^m.}
 \label{eq:V15-second-moment-error}
\end{equation}

If $D$ is another loop which traverses no edge of $S$, there is an
exterior-measurable $q_{C,D}$ with $|q_{C,D}|\le1$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C\mathcal O_D\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 =\rho(\beta)^m q_{C,D}.}
 \label{eq:V15-conditional-cross-moment}
\end{equation}
All statements remain valid in a finite region with arbitrary fixed exterior
links.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:V14-actual-Haar-refresh}, the conditional law of the selected
links is the product of the mixtures
\[
 x(\beta)m_{\rm H}+\rho(\beta)\widetilde\mu_e,
\]
where $m_{\rm H}$ is normalized Haar measure.  Expand the product over subsets
of links chosen from the Haar component.

For the first moment, every term with a nonempty Haar subset vanishes after
integrating any one Haar edge, because $C$ traverses that edge once and the
fundamental matrix coefficient has zero Haar mean.  The sole all-residual term
has coefficient $\rho^m$ and absolute value at most one, proving
\eqref{eq:V15-conditional-first-moment}.

For the second moment, consider a term with at least one Haar edge and
integrate that edge first.  Left and right multiplication by the fixed
remaining holonomies preserve Haar measure, so the complete loop holonomy is
Haar.  The exact $\SU(3)$ moment is
\[
 \int_{\SU(3)}
 \left(\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}U\right)^2\dd U=\frac1{18}
\]
by \Cref{lem:V13-Haar-floors}.  Therefore every nonempty-Haar term contributes
exactly $1/18$.  Their total coefficient is $1-\rho^m$.  The all-residual term
has coefficient $\rho^m$ and a conditional squared trace between zero and one,
which proves \eqref{eq:V15-conditional-second-moment} and
\eqref{eq:V15-second-moment-error}.

For the mixed moment, $\mathcal O_D$ is independent of every selected edge.
Any nonempty-Haar term again vanishes when one selected Haar edge is
integrated.  The remaining all-residual term has coefficient $\rho^m$ and
absolute value at most one.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V15-conditional-cross-moment}.  Fixed exterior links merely enter the
exterior-measurable coefficients and do not change the argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What is new relative to Version V14]
\label{rem:V15-new-moment-content}
Version~V14 used only \eqref{eq:V15-conditional-first-moment}.  The exact
$1/18$ contribution in \eqref{eq:V15-conditional-second-moment} and the
pair-private mixed estimate \eqref{eq:V15-conditional-cross-moment} are the new
inputs.  They control the conditioning of the complete four-loop covariance,
which a collection of first-moment attenuation bounds does not determine.
\end{remark}

% =============================================================================
\section{Uniform raw covariance and boundary-message estimates}
\label{sec:V15-covariance-estimates}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Complete four-loop Haar covariance window]
\label{thm:V15-raw-covariance-window}
For every finite selected Wilson card and every $\beta>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left\|\Sigma_N-\frac1{18}I_4\right\|_{\rm op}
 \le\frac{143}{18}\,r_N(\beta).}
 \label{eq:V15-raw-covariance-window}
\end{equation}
For every admissible separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\preceq K_{N,R}\preceq16\,r_N(\beta)^2 I_4.}
 \label{eq:V15-raw-message-upper}
\end{equation}
Both estimates are uniform in the shell radius and in fixed exterior boundary
conditions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every selected rectangle has a straight side of length at least $N/4$.
Apply \Cref{thm:V15-conditional-Haar-thermalization} and average the exterior.
For each label $\alpha$,
\begin{equation}
 |W_{\alpha,N}|\le r_N,
 \qquad
 \left|\mathbb E\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}^2-\frac1{18}\right|
 \le\frac{17}{18}r_N.
 \label{eq:V15-diagonal-prebounds}
\end{equation}
Hence
\begin{equation}
 \left| (\Sigma_N)_{\alpha\alpha}-\frac1{18}\right|
 \le\frac{17}{18}r_N+r_N^2
 \le\frac{35}{18}r_N.
 \label{eq:V15-diagonal-covariance-error}
\end{equation}

For distinct $\alpha,\gamma$, use the pair-private side of
\Cref{lem:V15-pair-private-side}.  It has at least $N/4$ edges and is absent
from $C_\gamma$, so
\[
 |\mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mathcal O_{\gamma,N}]|
 \le r_N.
\]
After centering,
\begin{equation}
 |(\Sigma_N)_{\alpha\gamma}|
 \le r_N+r_N^2\le2r_N.
 \label{eq:V15-offdiagonal-covariance-error}
\end{equation}
The maximum absolute row sum of
$\Sigma_N-I_4/18$ is therefore at most
\[
 \frac{35}{18}r_N+3(2r_N)=\frac{143}{18}r_N.
\]
The symmetric Schur row bound proves
\eqref{eq:V15-raw-covariance-window}.

For the shell message, the fixed-exterior form of
\eqref{eq:V15-conditional-first-moment} and the tower property give
\[
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mid B_{N,R}]
 \right|\le r_N.
\]
Together with $|W_{\alpha,N}|\le r_N$, this yields the pointwise vector bound
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathbf m_{N,R}\|_2^2\le4(2r_N)^2=16r_N^2.
 \label{eq:V15-message-vector-bound}
\end{equation}
For every $v\in\mathbb R^4$,
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}K_{N,R}v
 =\mathbb E|v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf m_{N,R}|^2
 \le16r_N^2\|v\|_2^2,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V15-raw-message-upper}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Haar conditioning of the raw four-loop frame]
\label{cor:V15-raw-frame-conditioning}
If $143r_N(\beta)<1$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{1-143r_N(\beta)}{18}I_4
 \preceq\Sigma_N
 \preceq
 \frac{1+143r_N(\beta)}{18}I_4.}
 \label{eq:V15-raw-frame-two-sided}
\end{equation}
In particular, the raw four-loop frame is linearly independent and its
condition number is at most
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{cond}(\Sigma_N)
 \le\frac{1+143r_N}{1-143r_N}.}
 \label{eq:V15-raw-frame-condition-number}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply the spectral perturbation bound to
\eqref{eq:V15-raw-covariance-window}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Complete source-relative contraction to every separating shell}
\label{sec:V15-source-relative-contraction}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Wilson long-side source-to-shell contraction]
\label{thm:V15-source-to-shell-contraction}
Assume $143r_N(\beta)<1$ and define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_N(\beta)^2
 :=\frac{288\,r_N(\beta)^2}{1-143\,r_N(\beta)}.}
 \label{eq:V15-kappa-definition}
\end{equation}
Then, for every admissible separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_{N,R}\preceq\kappa_N(\beta)^2\Sigma_N,}
 \label{eq:V15-raw-generalized-contraction}
\end{equation}
and, equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 M_{N,R}\preceq\kappa_N(\beta)^2\Gamma_N.}
 \label{eq:V15-normalized-generalized-contraction}
\end{equation}
Thus every nonzero four-loop source contrast $a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N$ obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{
  \|\mathbb E[a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 }{
  \|a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\|_2^2
 }
 \le\kappa_N(\beta)^2.}
 \label{eq:V15-every-contrast-ratio}
\end{equation}
In particular, for the physical Creutz contrast,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}(\beta)}{G_N(\beta)}
 \le\kappa_N(\beta)^2.}
 \label{eq:V15-Creutz-entry-ratio}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{cor:V15-raw-frame-conditioning},
\[
 \Sigma_N\succeq\frac{1-143r_N}{18}I_4.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:V15-raw-message-upper},
\[
 K_{N,R}
 \preceq16r_N^2I_4
 \preceq
 \frac{288r_N^2}{1-143r_N}\Sigma_N,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V15-raw-generalized-contraction}.  Congruence by the
invertible diagonal $D_{W,N}^{-1}$ and
\eqref{eq:V15-raw-normalized-congruence} give
\eqref{eq:V15-normalized-generalized-contraction}.  Compressing that order by
$a$ gives \eqref{eq:V15-every-contrast-ratio}.  The Creutz source corresponds
to $a=(1,1,-1,-1)^{\mathsf T}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit finite-card strict-contraction threshold]
\label{cor:V15-explicit-strict-threshold}
Let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_{\rm c}
 :=\frac{\sqrt{21601}-143}{576}
 =0.006897198952609\ldots.}
 \label{eq:V15-critical-r}
\end{equation}
Then $\kappa_N(\beta)^2<1$ whenever $r_N(\beta)<r_{\rm c}$.  A sufficient
condition stated directly in the physical coupling is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Ne^{-9\beta}>\tau_{\rm c},
 \qquad
 \tau_{\rm c}:=4\log(r_{\rm c}^{-1})
 =19.9065595947\ldots.}
 \label{eq:V15-critical-tau}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The inequality $\kappa_N^2<1$ is equivalent to
\[
 288r_N^2+143r_N-1<0.
\]
Its positive root is \eqref{eq:V15-critical-r}; moreover
$r_{\rm c}<1/143$, so the denominator in
\eqref{eq:V15-kappa-definition} is positive.  Since
$1-x<e^{-x}$ for $x>0$,
\[
 r_N(\beta)
 =(1-e^{-9\beta})^{N/4}
 <\exp\left(-\frac N4e^{-9\beta}\right).
\]
Condition \eqref{eq:V15-critical-tau} therefore implies
$r_N<e^{-\tau_{\rm c}/4}=r_{\rm c}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Refresh-dominant cofinal extinction]
\label{thm:V15-refresh-dominant-extinction}
Let $(N_n,\beta_n)$ be any cofinal sequence with $N_n\to\infty$.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{N_ne^{-9\beta_n}\longrightarrow\infty,}
 \label{eq:V15-refresh-dominant-condition}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{R\ {\mathrm{separating}}}
 \frac{I_{N_n,R}^{\square}(\beta_n)}{G_{N_n}(\beta_n)}
 \le\kappa_{N_n}(\beta_n)^2
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V15-uniform-boundary-extinction}
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds simultaneously for every nonzero contrast in the
complete four-arm normalized source frame.

Conversely, if \eqref{eq:V15-refresh-dominant-condition} fails, there is a
cofinal subsequence on which
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 N_ne^{-9\beta_n}\le C<\infty,
 \qquad
 \beta_n\ge\frac19\log N_n-\frac19\log C.}
 \label{eq:V15-remaining-log-window}
\end{equation}
Thus the only branch not decided by long-side Haar thermalization is the
logarithmic-or-faster coupling window.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put $x_n=e^{-9\beta_n}$.  Under
\eqref{eq:V15-refresh-dominant-condition},
\[
 0\le r_{N_n}(\beta_n)
 \le e^{-N_nx_n/4}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The formula \eqref{eq:V15-kappa-definition} then gives
$\kappa_{N_n}^2\to0$, uniformly in the shell radius.  Apply
\Cref{thm:V15-source-to-shell-contraction}.

If $N_ne^{-9\beta_n}$ does not tend to infinity, choose a cofinal subsequence
on which it is bounded by $C$.  Taking logarithms gives
\eqref{eq:V15-remaining-log-window}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The bounded-root branch has no boundary source survivor]
\label{cor:V15-bounded-root-extinction}
If the selected weak-facing roots have a cofinal subsequence with
$0<\beta_n^{\rm wf}\le B<\infty$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{R\ {\mathrm{separating}}}
 \frac{I_{N_n,R}^{\square}(\beta_n^{\rm wf})}
      {G_{N_n}(\beta_n^{\rm wf})}
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V15-bounded-root-relative-extinction}
\end{equation}
This coexists with the Version~V14 divergence of the unrescaled source stock:
the source is absolutely overdriven but its entire source-relative boundary
message vanishes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
One has $N_ne^{-9\beta_n^{\rm wf}}\ge N_ne^{-9B}\to\infty$.  Apply
\Cref{thm:V15-refresh-dominant-extinction}.  The absolute overdrive statement
is \Cref{cor:V14-bounded-root-overdrive}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Branch-wise termination supplied by V15]
\label{ass:V15-branch-termination}
On every refresh-dominant branch, including every bounded-root branch, the
source-to-separating-shell channel is not merely separated from one: its
complete source-relative norm tends to zero.  Hence neither a contact-scale
nor a positive-range boundary survivor of the frozen Creutz direction can be
carried through the separating shell on that branch.  The remaining physical
question is confined to \eqref{eq:V15-remaining-log-window}; it is no longer a
question about bounded roots or sublogarithmic escape.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{A canonical balanced loading which pays the normalization tax}
\label{sec:V15-balanced-loading}
% =============================================================================

The preceding contraction is scale invariant and therefore already applies to
the original source.  For a finite absolute source packet, however, Version~V14
correctly requires an explicit cutoff-dependent amplitude.  The raw-loop frame
provides one without using $G_N$ or any shell value.

Let
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon_\square:=(1,1,-1,-1)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 b_N:=D_{W,N}^{-1}\varepsilon_\square.
 \label{eq:V15-Creutz-raw-coefficient}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_N^{\rm bal}
 :=\|b_N\|_2^{-1}
 =\left(\sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square}
          W_{\alpha,N}^{-2}\right)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 u_N:=a_N^{\rm bal}b_N.}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-amplitude}
\end{equation}
Then $\|u_N\|_2=1$.  The balanced Creutz source is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widehat Y_N^{\square}
 :=a_N^{\rm bal}Y_N^{\square}
 =u_N^{\mathsf T}\mathbf X_N.}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-source}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical raw-coefficient-balanced Creutz loading]
\label{thm:V15-balanced-source}
The amplitude in \eqref{eq:V15-balanced-amplitude} is the unique positive
scalar for which the raw-loop coefficient vector of
$aY_N^{\square}$ has Euclidean norm one.  It uses only the four loop means
already required to define the source and is fixed before any shell message is
read.

Put
\begin{equation}
 \widehat G_N:=\|\widehat Y_N^{\square}\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 \widehat I_{N,R}:=
 \|\mathbb E[\widehat Y_N^{\square}\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-stocks}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \left|\widehat G_N-\frac1{18}\right|
 \le\frac{143}{18}r_N(\beta),}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-total-window}\\
 \boxed{
 0\le\widehat I_{N,R}\le16r_N(\beta)^2,}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-message-window}\\
 \boxed{
 \frac{\widehat I_{N,R}}{\widehat G_N}
 =\frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}}{G_N}.}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-ratio-invariance}
\end{align}
If $W_{\min,N}:=\min_\alpha W_{\alpha,N}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac12W_{\min,N}
 \le a_N^{\rm bal}\le W_{\min,N}.}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-amplitude-window}
\end{equation}
At every weak-facing root, the unit coefficient vector satisfies the exact
projective relation
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 u_{11,N}u_{00,N}
 =e^{u_*}u_{10,N}u_{01,N},}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-root-relation}
\end{equation}
with signs
$u_{11,N},u_{00,N}>0$ and $u_{10,N},u_{01,N}<0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The raw coefficient vector of $aY_N^{\square}$ is $ab_N$, so the equation
$\|ab_N\|_2=1$ has the unique positive solution
$a=\|b_N\|_2^{-1}$.  Equation \eqref{eq:V15-balanced-source} follows from
$Y_N^{\square}=\varepsilon_\square^{\mathsf T}D_{W,N}^{-1}\mathbf X_N$.
Since $u_N$ is a unit vector,
\[
 \widehat G_N=u_N^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Nu_N,
 \qquad
 \widehat I_{N,R}=u_N^{\mathsf T}K_{N,R}u_N.
\]
The bounds \eqref{eq:V15-balanced-total-window} and
\eqref{eq:V15-balanced-message-window} are therefore
\Cref{thm:V15-raw-covariance-window}.  Both stocks are multiplied by the same
factor $(a_N^{\rm bal})^2$ relative to the original Creutz stocks, proving
\eqref{eq:V15-balanced-ratio-invariance}.

Because
\[
 W_{\min,N}^{-2}
 \le\sum_\alpha W_{\alpha,N}^{-2}
 \le4W_{\min,N}^{-2},
\]
reciprocal square roots give
\eqref{eq:V15-balanced-amplitude-window}.  Finally, the selected response
identity
$W_{11,N}W_{00,N}=e^{-u_*}W_{10,N}W_{01,N}$ gives
\[
 \frac{(a_N^{\rm bal})^2}{W_{11,N}W_{00,N}}
 =e^{u_*}\frac{(a_N^{\rm bal})^2}{W_{10,N}W_{01,N}},
\]
which is precisely \eqref{eq:V15-balanced-root-relation} with the declared
signs.
\end{proof}

\label{cor:V15-balanced-noncollapse}

\begin{proposition}[Exact scalar calibration cocycle]
\label{prop:V15-balanced-cocycle}
For adjacent cutoffs $X<Y$, put
\begin{equation}

 :=\frac{a_Y^{\rm bal}}{a_X^{\rm bal}}>0.}

Then
\begin{equation}

 \mathfrak a_{Z/Y}^{\rm bal}\mathfrak a_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}

For any independently declared linear physical source transport $T_{Y/X}$,

 -\mathfrak a_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}T_{Y/X}\widehat Y_X^{\square}

  \bigl(Y_Y^{\square}-T_{Y/X}Y_X^{\square}\bigr).}
 \label{eq:V15-balanced-transport-defect}
\end{equation}

unknown source-shape defect.  The old/fine mixed Gram is still required to
evaluate the parenthesized physical transport mismatch.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The cocycle law is cancellation of the intermediate positive amplitude.
Substitute
$\widehat Y_X^{\square}=a_X^{\rm bal}Y_X^{\square}$ on both sides of
\eqref{eq:V15-balanced-transport-defect}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Version V15 source-normalization and radial alternative]
\label{thm:V15-cofinal-alternative}
Along every cofinal weak-facing sequence, after passage to a subsequence, the
quantity
\[
 \tau_n:=N_ne^{-9\beta_n^{\rm wf}}
\]
has a limit $\tau_\infty\in[0,\infty]$, and exactly one of the following
three cases occurs.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V15.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item \emph{Refresh-dominant contraction.}
      $\tau_\infty=\infty$.  Then the complete normalized four-arm
      source-to-separating-shell norm tends to zero as in
      \eqref{eq:V15-uniform-boundary-extinction}.  The original source may be
      overdriven, but the balanced source has stock tending to $1/18$ and
      boundary stock tending to zero.
\item \emph{Finite strict refresh contraction.}
      $\tau_{\rm c}<\tau_\infty<\infty$.  Then the source-to-shell channel has
      a uniform strict edge
      $\sup_n\kappa_{N_n}(\beta_n^{\rm wf})<1$ after omission of finitely many
      cards.
\item \emph{Critical logarithmic-or-faster window.}
      $0\le\tau_\infty\le\tau_{\rm c}$.  Then
      \eqref{eq:V15-remaining-log-window} holds, but the present refresh bound
      does not force a strict shell ratio.  The first physical value is exactly
      the Version~V11 old source stock and reverse-posterior loss on one
      selected physical shell pair.
\end{enumerate}
No fourth branch is created by source overdrive: it is an absolute amplitude
issue which is either retained as an obstruction or paid by the explicit
balanced loading without changing the radial ratio.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The compactness of the extended half-line $[0,\infty]$ gives a subsequence on
which $\tau_n\to\tau_\infty$.  The infinite case is
\Cref{thm:V15-refresh-dominant-extinction,cor:V15-balanced-noncollapse}.
If $\tau_\infty<\infty$, then
$x_n=e^{-9\beta_n^{\rm wf}}=\tau_n/N_n\to0$ and
\[
 r_{N_n}(\beta_n^{\rm wf})
 =(1-x_n)^{N_n/4}\longrightarrow e^{-\tau_\infty/4}.
\]
When $\tau_\infty>\tau_{\rm c}$, the limit is strictly below $r_{\rm c}$,
so \Cref{cor:V15-explicit-strict-threshold} gives a uniform strict edge.
When $\tau_\infty\le\tau_{\rm c}$, that sufficient bound reaches or exceeds
one and supplies no strict verdict; the logarithmic lower bound is
\eqref{eq:V15-remaining-log-window}.  Scaling invariance is
\eqref{eq:V15-balanced-ratio-invariance}.
\end{proof}

\end{assessment}

\section{Version V16 direction: replace exponentially small refresh by a native circle fibre}
\label{sec:V16-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V15 closed the complete source-relative boundary channel whenever the
finite-energy Haar-refresh count
\(
 N e^{-9\beta}
\)
diverges.  Its remaining window was logarithmic or faster because the
Doeblin component \(e^{-9\beta}\) is exponentially small in the coupling.
Repeating the Version~V11 posterior-loss representation inside that window
would be circular: the target-minimal scalar Read is already known, and the
missing issue is whether the exact one-link Wilson heat bath has a stronger
native contraction than its worst-point minorization.

It does.  Every one-link heat bath contains a canonical right circle adapted
to any tested input vector of the defining representation.  Along that circle
the logarithm of the conditional density has derivative at most \(6\beta\).
A one-dimensional concentration lemma then bounds the first Fourier
coefficient away from one by order \((1+\beta)^{-2}\).  Since a physical
rectangle has a plaquette-disjoint straight side of length at least \(N/4\),
these polynomial one-link deficits accumulate exponentially in
\(N/(1+\beta)^2\).

The new argument is upstream of the endpoint posterior card and uses no new
source deformation, replica hierarchy, or primitive shell basis.  It keeps
the four physical rectangles, their normalization, the selected Wilson law,
and every shell record fixed.

\begin{firewall}[The circle fibre is a proof device, not a new gauge orbit]
\label{fire:V16-circle-not-source}
The right circle below is used only to disintegrate the already occurring
