\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{A logarithmic-Lipschitz circle density has a polynomial Fourier deficit}
\label{sec:V16-circle-lemma}
% =============================================================================

Write
\(
 \mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)
\)
with normalized Haar measure \(\dd t/(2\pi)\), and let
\(
 d_{\mathbb T}
\)
be its geodesic distance in \([0,\pi]\).

\begin{lemma}[Peak bound for a logarithmic-Lipschitz circle density]
\label{lem:V16-circle-peak}
Let \(p>0\) be a continuously differentiable probability density on
\(\mathbb T\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\log p(t)\right|\le K.
 \label{eq:V16-log-Lipschitz}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|p\|_{\infty}\le \pi(1+K).}
 \label{eq:V16-circle-peak}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(t_0\) be a maximizer and put \(M=p(t_0)\).  The logarithmic Lipschitz
bound gives
\[
 p(t)\ge M e^{-K d_{\mathbb T}(t,t_0)}.
\]
For \(K>0\), integration yields
\[
 1\ge \frac{M}{\pi}\int_0^\pi e^{-Ks}\,\dd s
   =M\frac{1-e^{-\pi K}}{\pi K}.
\]
The elementary inequality
\(
 1-e^{-x}\ge x/(1+x)
\)
gives
\[
 M\le 1+\pi K\le\pi(1+K).
\]
For \(K=0\), the density is constant and the same conclusion is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[First circle Fourier coefficient deficit]
\label{thm:V16-circle-Fourier-deficit}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{lem:V16-circle-peak},
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \int_{\mathbb T}e^{it}p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}
 \right|
 \le
 1-\frac{1}{4\pi^2(1+K)^2}.}
 \label{eq:V16-circle-Fourier-deficit}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If the displayed Fourier coefficient vanishes there is nothing to prove.
Otherwise choose \(\theta\) so that multiplication by \(e^{-i\theta}\)
makes it nonnegative real.  Put
\[
 r_K=\frac{1}{2(1+K)},
 \qquad
 A_\theta=\{t:d_{\mathbb T}(t,\theta)<r_K\}.
\]
By \Cref{lem:V16-circle-peak},
\[
 \int_{A_\theta}p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}
 \le \pi(1+K)\frac{2r_K}{2\pi}=\frac12.
\]
Thus the complement has probability at least one half.  Since
\(
 1-\cos s\ge2s^2/\pi^2
\)
for \(0\le s\le\pi\),
\begin{align*}
 1-
 \left|
  \int e^{it}p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}
 \right|
 &=\int_{\mathbb T}
   \bigl(1-\cos(t-\theta)\bigr)
   p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}\\
 &\ge \frac12\frac{2r_K^2}{\pi^2}
 =\frac{1}{4\pi^2(1+K)^2}.
\end{align*}
This is \eqref{eq:V16-circle-Fourier-deficit}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why a polynomial deficit is enough]
\label{rem:V16-polynomial-enough}
The constant in \eqref{eq:V16-circle-Fourier-deficit} is deliberately
unoptimized.  Its significance is the power \((1+K)^{-2}\).  Repeating this
deficit over \(O(N)\) independent link fibres produces an exponential of
\(-cN/(1+\beta)^2\), which is much stronger in the logarithmic window than
the finite-energy Doeblin exponent \(-cNe^{-9\beta}\).
\end{remark}

% =============================================================================
\section{Polynomial contraction of every one-link Wilson mean matrix}
\label{sec:V16-one-link}
% =============================================================================

Condition on all links except one oriented link \(e\).  Up to an additive
constant independent of \(U_e\), its Wilson conditional law has density
\begin{equation}
 \dd\nu_{e,\beta}(U)
 =Z_e^{-1}e^{\beta\Phi_e(U)}\,\dd U,
 \qquad
 \Phi_e(U)=\frac13\sum_{j=1}^{m_e}
             \operatorname{ReTr}(UB_j),
 \qquad m_e\le6,
 \label{eq:V16-one-link-law}
\end{equation}
for exterior-measurable matrices \(B_j\in\SU(3)\).  A plaquette in which the
link originally occurs with inverse orientation is put in this form by
complex conjugation of its trace.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform circle derivative of the one-link potential]
\label{lem:V16-circle-derivative}
Let \(w,w'\in\mathbb C^3\) be orthonormal and define
\begin{equation}
 R_t
 :=\exp\!\left(it(P_w-P_{w'})\right)\in\SU(3).
 \label{eq:V16-right-circle}
\end{equation}
Then \(R_tw=e^{it}w\), and for every \(U\in\SU(3)\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Phi_e(UR_t)\right|\le6.}
 \label{eq:V16-potential-circle-Lipschitz}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The generator
\(
 X=i(P_w-P_{w'})
\)
is traceless skew Hermitian and has operator norm one.  For each summand,
\[
 \left|
  \frac{\dd}{\dd t}
  \frac13\operatorname{ReTr}(UR_tB_j)
 \right|
 =\frac13\left|\operatorname{ReTr}(UR_tXB_j)\right|
 \le\frac13\cdot3\|X\|_{\rm op}=1.
\]
There are at most six plaquettes incident with one four-dimensional lattice
link, so summation proves the claim.
\end{proof}

Define the conditional defining-representation mean matrix
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf M_{e,\beta}
 :=\int_{\SU(3)}U\,\dd\nu_{e,\beta}(U).
 \label{eq:V16-link-mean-matrix}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Native one-link circle contraction]
\label{thm:V16-one-link-circle-contraction}
For every exterior configuration, every finite Wilson coupling \(\beta\ge0\),
and every lattice link,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathsf M_{e,\beta}\|_{\rm op}
 \le1-\delta_{\rm circ}(\beta),
 \qquad
 \delta_{\rm circ}(\beta)
 :=\frac{1}{4\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2}.}
 \label{eq:V16-one-link-contraction}
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds for
\(
 \int U^{-1}\,\dd\nu_{e,\beta}(U)
\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix unit vectors \(v,w\in\mathbb C^3\), choose an orthogonal unit vector
\(w'\), and use the circle \(H_w=\{R_t\}\) of
\eqref{eq:V16-right-circle}.  Weil integration for the compact quotient
\(\SU(3)/H_w\) gives a normalized quotient measure and, after choosing any
Borel section \(s\), the disintegration
\[
 \int_{\SU(3)}F(U)\,\dd U
 =\int_{\SU(3)/H_w}\int_{\mathbb T}
  F(s(q)R_t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}\,\dd\bar m(q).
\]
After insertion of the Gibbs weight in \eqref{eq:V16-one-link-law}, this
becomes a quotient probability \(\eta\) and conditional circle densities
\[
 p_q(t)
 =\frac{e^{\beta\Phi_e(s(q)R_t)}}
        {\int_{\mathbb T}e^{\beta\Phi_e(s(q)R_u)}\,\dd u/(2\pi)}.
\]
By \Cref{lem:V16-circle-derivative},
\[
 |\partial_t\log p_q(t)|\le6\beta.
\]
Hence \Cref{thm:V16-circle-Fourier-deficit} gives
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathbb T}e^{it}p_q(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}\right|
 \le1-\delta_{\rm circ}(\beta)
\]
for every quotient fibre.  Since
\(
 s(q)R_tw=e^{it}s(q)w
\),
\begin{align*}
 |v^*\mathsf M_{e,\beta}w|
 &=\left|
   \int_{\SU(3)/H_w}
   v^*s(q)w
   \left(\int e^{it}p_q(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}\right)
   \dd\eta(q)
  \right|\\
 &\le1-\delta_{\rm circ}(\beta).
\end{align*}
Taking the supremum over unit \(v,w\) proves the operator-norm estimate.
Finally, \(U^{-1}=U^*\), so the inverse-orientation mean is
\(\mathsf M_{e,\beta}^*\) and has the same norm.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Comparison with finite-energy minorization]
\label{ass:V16-two-one-link-mechanisms}
The Haar-refresh mass \(e^{-9\beta}\) of Version~V14 is a pointwise density
minorant and is essentially forced by the full one-link action oscillation.
The new number \(\delta_{\rm circ}(\beta)\) is not a density minorant.  It is
a first-representation contraction obtained after integrating along an
actual compact subgroup fibre.  The two estimates answer different
questions and may be combined, but neither is substituted for the other.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Long-side matrix damping on the physical rectangle card}
\label{sec:V16-long-side}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial long-side Wilson attenuation]
\label{thm:V16-long-side-attenuation}
Let \(C\) be a simple Wilson loop and let \(S\) be a set of \(m\) edges of
\(C\), each traversed once, such that no plaquette contains two selected
edges.  Then, conditionally on every link outside \(S\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 \right|
 \le
 \bigl(1-\delta_{\rm circ}(\beta)\bigr)^m.}
 \label{eq:V16-long-side-conditional}
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds after conditioning only on any sub-sigma-algebra of
\(\mathscr F_{S^c}\), including every admissible separating shell record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because no plaquette contains two selected links, their joint conditional law
factorizes exactly, as in \Cref{lem:V14-actual-Haar-refresh}.  After the
complement is fixed, the ordered loop holonomy is a product of fixed unitary
matrices and the selected link matrices or their inverses.  Integrating the
selected links one at a time replaces each by
\(
 \mathsf M_{e,\beta}
\)
or its adjoint.  The normalized trace is bounded by the product of their
operator norms.  Apply \Cref{thm:V16-one-link-circle-contraction}.  The last
statement is the tower property.
\end{proof}

For the four selected rectangles put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 s_N(\beta)
 :=\bigl(1-\delta_{\rm circ}(\beta)\bigr)^{N/4}.}
 \label{eq:V16-polynomial-side-factor}
\end{equation}
Every rectangle has a straight side of length at least \(N/4\), and
\Cref{lem:V15-pair-private-side} verifies the required plaquette separation.
Therefore, for every label \(\alpha\) and every separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |W_{\alpha,N}|\le s_N(\beta),
 \qquad
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mid B_{N,R}]
 \right|
 \le s_N(\beta).}
 \label{eq:V16-loop-and-message-bound}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Raw four-loop boundary-message bound]
\label{cor:V16-raw-message-bound}
With the raw message covariance \(K_{N,R}\) of
\eqref{eq:V15-raw-message-covariance},
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\preceq K_{N,R}\preceq16s_N(\beta)^2I_4.}
 \label{eq:V16-raw-message-bound}
\end{equation}
The estimate is uniform over every admissible separating shell and every fixed
exterior boundary condition.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V16-loop-and-message-bound} gives
\[
 |(\mathbf m_{N,R})_\alpha|
 =\left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mid B_{N,R}]-W_{\alpha,N}
 \right|
 \le2s_N.
\]
Hence \(\|\mathbf m_{N,R}\|_2^2\le16s_N^2\), and compression against an
arbitrary vector proves the matrix order.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Complete source-relative contraction without a Haar-covariance window}
\label{sec:V16-source-contraction}
% =============================================================================

The Version~V15 generalized bound used asymptotic Haar conditioning of the raw
four-loop covariance.  In the present window that covariance theorem need not
be available.  The complete private-coordinate floor of Version~V14 supplies
the missing denominator directly.

\begin{theorem}[Circle-fibre source-to-shell contraction]
\label{thm:V16-source-to-shell-contraction}
For every finite selected Wilson card and every admissible separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 M_{N,R}
 \preceq
 \kappa_{N,\rm circ}(\beta)^2\Gamma_N,}
 \label{eq:V16-normalized-source-contraction}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{N,\rm circ}(\beta)^2
 :=\min\left\{
  1,
  1152e^{33\beta/2}s_N(\beta)^2
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V16-circle-kappa}
\end{equation}
Consequently every nonzero normalized four-loop contrast obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{
  \|\mathbb E[a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 }{
  \|a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\|_2^2
 }
 \le\kappa_{N,\rm circ}(\beta)^2,}
 \label{eq:V16-every-source-ratio}
\end{equation}
and in particular
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}(\beta)}{G_N(\beta)}
 \le\kappa_{N,\rm circ}(\beta)^2.}
 \label{eq:V16-Creutz-ratio}
\end{equation}
No condition of the form \(143r_N<1\) is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The congruences in \eqref{eq:V15-raw-normalized-congruence} and
\Cref{cor:V16-raw-message-bound} give
\[
 M_{N,R}
 \preceq16s_N^2D_{W,N}^{-2}.
\]
On the other hand,
\(
 \Gamma_N\succeq H_{N,R}
\), and the complete private-coordinate coercivity
\eqref{eq:V14-absolute-matrix-floor} gives
\[
 \Gamma_N
 \succeq\frac{e^{-33\beta/2}}{72}D_{W,N}^{-2}.
\]
Thus
\[
 D_{W,N}^{-2}\preceq72e^{33\beta/2}\Gamma_N
\]
and hence
\[
 M_{N,R}
 \preceq1152e^{33\beta/2}s_N^2\Gamma_N.
\]
Conditional expectation also gives the universal order
\(M_{N,R}\preceq\Gamma_N\).  Taking the better of the two bounds proves
\eqref{eq:V16-normalized-source-contraction}.  Scalar compression gives the
remaining statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hybrid executable contraction card]
\label{cor:V16-hybrid-card}
Let \(r_N(\beta)=(1-e^{-9\beta})^{N/4}\) be the Version~V15 refresh factor and
use the convention
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_{N,\rm Haar}^2
 :=\begin{cases}
 \dfrac{288r_N(\beta)^2}{1-143r_N(\beta)},&143r_N(\beta)<1,\\[0.8em]
 +\infty,&143r_N(\beta)\ge1.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:V16-Haar-kappa-convention}
\end{equation}
Then the finite card may use
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{N,\rm hyb}^2
 :=\min\{1,\kappa_{N,\rm Haar}^2,
              1152e^{33\beta/2}s_N(\beta)^2\},}
 \label{eq:V16-hybrid-kappa}
\end{equation}
and
\(
 M_{N,R}\preceq\kappa_{N,\rm hyb}^2\Gamma_N
\)
for every separating shell.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Combine \Cref{thm:V15-source-to-shell-contraction} with
\Cref{thm:V16-source-to-shell-contraction} and the universal conditional-
expectation order.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Finite threshold and sub-cubic-root cofinal extinction}
\label{sec:V16-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

Since \(1-x\le e^{-x}\),
\begin{equation}
 s_N(\beta)^2
 \le
 \exp\!\left[
  -\frac{N}{8\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2}
 \right].
 \label{eq:V16-side-exponential}
\end{equation}
Define the circle-fibre contraction exponent
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_N^{\rm circ}(\beta)
 :=\frac{N}{8\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2}
   -\frac{33}{2}\beta
   -\log1152.}
 \label{eq:V16-contraction-exponent}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit finite-card circle threshold]
\label{cor:V16-finite-threshold}
For every finite card,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}}{G_N}
 \le\min\{1,e^{-\Delta_N^{\rm circ}(\beta)}\}.}
 \label{eq:V16-explicit-ratio}
\end{equation}
In particular, strict source-to-shell contraction is certified whenever
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 N>
 8\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2
 \left(\log1152+\frac{33}{2}\beta\right).}
 \label{eq:V16-finite-strict-threshold}
\end{equation}
More generally, the right side of \eqref{eq:V16-explicit-ratio} is at most
\(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) whenever
\begin{equation}
 N\ge
 8\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2
 \left(\log\frac{1152}{\varepsilon}+\frac{33}{2}\beta\right).
 \label{eq:V16-finite-epsilon-threshold}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Insert \eqref{eq:V16-side-exponential} into
\eqref{eq:V16-circle-kappa}.  The two threshold statements are the conditions
\(\Delta_N^{\rm circ}>0\) and
\(\Delta_N^{\rm circ}\ge\log(1/\varepsilon)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sub-cubic-root weak-coupling closure]
\label{thm:V16-subcubic-closure}
Let \(N_n\to\infty\) and let \(\beta_n\ge0\) be any coupling sequence.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta_n=o(N_n^{1/3}),}
 \label{eq:V16-subcubic-hypothesis}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{N_n}^{\rm circ}(\beta_n)\longrightarrow+\infty,
 \qquad
 \sup_{R\ {\rm separating}}
 \frac{I_{N_n,R}^{\square}}{G_{N_n}}
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V16-subcubic-extinction}
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for every scalar rescaling of the source, including
the balanced loading of Version~V15.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If \((\beta_n)\) has a bounded subsequence, the first term in
\eqref{eq:V16-contraction-exponent} grows linearly in \(N_n\) there.  On an
unbounded subsequence, eventually \(\beta_n\ge1\) and
\[
 (1+6\beta_n)^2\le49\beta_n^2.
\]
Hence
\[
 \frac{1}{\beta_n}
 \frac{N_n}{8\pi^2(1+6\beta_n)^2}
 \ge
 \frac{N_n}{392\pi^2\beta_n^3}
 \longrightarrow\infty
\]
by \eqref{eq:V16-subcubic-hypothesis}.  This dominates the linear debit
\(33\beta_n/2\) and the fixed logarithm in
\eqref{eq:V16-contraction-exponent}.  The ratio conclusion follows from
\eqref{eq:V16-explicit-ratio}, uniformly in \(R\).  Multiplying the source by
a nonzero scalar changes numerator and denominator by the same factor.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The entire logarithmic window is closed]
\label{cor:V16-log-window-closed}
If, along selected weak-facing roots,
\begin{equation}
 \beta_N^{\rm wf}=O((\log N)^a)
 \qquad\text{for any fixed }a<\infty,
 \label{eq:V16-polylog-root}
\end{equation}
then the complete physical Creutz source is source-relatively extinguished at
every separating shell:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_R
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}(\beta_N^{\rm wf})}
      {G_N(\beta_N^{\rm wf})}
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V16-polylog-extinction}
\end{equation}
In particular, the critical logarithmic-or-faster window left by Version~V15
no longer requires the Version~V11 posterior Read on any polylogarithmic root
branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every fixed power of \(\log N\) is \(o(N^{1/3})\), so apply
\Cref{thm:V16-subcubic-closure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Any branch not closed by the circle exponent is cubic-root fast]
\label{prop:V16-unresolved-cubic-root}
Suppose a cofinal subsequence satisfies
\(
 \Delta_{N_n}^{\rm circ}(\beta_n)\le C
\)
for some finite \(C\).  Then eventually \(\beta_n\ge1\) and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta_n
 \ge
 c_C N_n^{1/3},
 \qquad
 c_C:=
 \left[
 392\pi^2
 \left(\frac{33}{2}+\log1152+\max\{C,0\}\right)
 \right]^{-1/3}.}
 \label{eq:V16-cubic-root-lower}
\end{equation}
Thus every cofinal branch not already extinguished by
\Cref{thm:V16-subcubic-closure} contains a cubic-root-or-faster weak-coupling
subbranch.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The assumed upper bound and \eqref{eq:V16-contraction-exponent} imply
\[
 N_n
 \le
 8\pi^2(1+6\beta_n)^2
 \left(
  \frac{33}{2}\beta_n+
  \log1152+C
 \right).
\]
A bounded \(\beta_n\) would make the right side bounded while \(N_n\to\infty\),
so eventually \(\beta_n\ge1\).  Then
\[
 (1+6\beta_n)^2\le49\beta_n^2
\]
and
\[
 \frac{33}{2}\beta_n+
 \log1152+C
 \le
 \left(
  \frac{33}{2}+\log1152+\max\{C,0\}
 \right)\beta_n.
\]
Rearrangement gives \eqref{eq:V16-cubic-root-lower}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Physical interpretation and the revised terminating branch map}
\label{sec:V16-interpretation}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Version V16 weak-facing branch classification]
\label{thm:V16-branch-classification}
Let \((N_n,\beta_n^{\rm wf})\) be the frozen weak-facing selected-root sequence.
After passage to a subsequence, one of the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.2em]
\item \(\Delta_{N_n}^{\rm circ}(\beta_n^{\rm wf})\to+\infty\).  Then the
      complete four-arm source-to-separating-shell channel converges to zero
      in the physical source metric, uniformly in the shell radius.
\item The circle exponent stays bounded above.  Then the selected roots have
      a cubic-root-or-faster subbranch in the explicit sense of
      \eqref{eq:V16-cubic-root-lower}.  Only on this branch does the
      Version~V11 posterior-loss pair remain a necessary physical Read.
\end{enumerate}
Every bounded, logarithmic, polylogarithmic, and more generally
sub-cubic-root root sequence lies in the first branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Either the exponent has a subsequence tending to infinity or it has a
subsequence bounded above.  In the first case use
\eqref{eq:V16-explicit-ratio}; in the second use
\Cref{prop:V16-unresolved-cubic-root}.  The final sentence is
\Cref{thm:V16-subcubic-closure,cor:V16-log-window-closed}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced source handoff]
\label{cor:V16-balanced-handoff}
Let \(\widehat Y_N^{\square}=a_N^{\rm bal}Y_N^{\square}\) be the balanced
source of Version~V15.  On every branch with
\(
 \Delta_N^{\rm circ}(\beta_N)\to+\infty
\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_R
 \frac{
  \|\mathbb E[\widehat Y_N^{\square}\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 }{
  \|\widehat Y_N^{\square}\|_2^2
 }
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V16-balanced-relative-extinction}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_R
 \|\mathbb E[\widehat Y_N^{\square}\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V16-balanced-absolute-extinction}
\end{equation}
This absolute conclusion uses only the bounded raw-loop normalization; it
does not assert that the balanced total stock has a positive limiting lower
bound outside the Version~V15 refresh-dominant branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The ratio is invariant under nonzero scalar source rescaling.  In the raw
coordinates of Version~V15 the balanced coefficient vector has Euclidean norm
one.  Each component \(\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\) has range length \(3/2\), so
Popoviciu gives diagonal variance at most \(9/16\).  Hence
\[
 \|\widehat Y_N^{\square}\|_2^2
 \le\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_N\le\frac94.
\]
Multiplying this uniform upper bound by
\eqref{eq:V16-balanced-relative-extinction} proves
\eqref{eq:V16-balanced-absolute-extinction}.  No lower source-stock limit is
inferred.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What has and has not been exported to YM--A]
\label{ass:V16-YMA-export}
On every sub-cubic-root weak-facing branch, YM--B now exports a complete
source-metric spatial extinction certificate.  Hence no contact-scale or
positive-range survivor of the selected Creutz source can cross a separating
shell on that branch.  This does not determine YM--A's unnormalized partition
curvature, signed reduced-fibre Hessian, source-orthogonal centre-neutral
network sector, or Osterwalder--Schrader time transfer.  The spatial certificate
is one boundary input and is not renamed as a mass gap.
\end{assessment}

\label{cert:V16-verifier}

\item It exhibits a card with

\item It checks the finite threshold, the hybrid minimum, the sub-cubic-root

      plaquette count, side exponent, and source comparison factor.
\end{enumerate}
The replay does not generate a selected Wilson root, a cubic-root-fast
posterior loss, an OS transfer, or a continuum mass.
\end{certificate}

\begin{theorem}[Version V16 export]
\label{thm:V16-export}
Versions~V1--V15 are retained.  Version~V16 additionally exports
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \|\mathsf M_{e,\beta}\|_{\rm op}
 \le1-\frac{1}{4\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2},\\[0.35em]
 s_N(\beta)
 =\left(1-\frac{1}{4\pi^2(1+6\beta)^2}\right)^{N/4},\\[0.35em]
 M_{N,R}\preceq
 \min\{1,1152e^{33\beta/2}s_N(\beta)^2\}\Gamma_N,\\[0.35em]
 \beta_N=o(N^{1/3})
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sup_R\frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}}{G_N}\longrightarrow0.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V16-export}
\end{equation}
Thus the complete logarithmic and polylogarithmic selected-root windows are
closed without a posterior-shell Read.  The only remaining root branch is
cubic-root fast or faster, on which the already isolated Version~V11
posterior card remains the first physical value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use
\Cref{thm:V16-one-link-circle-contraction,thm:V16-long-side-attenuation,thm:V16-source-to-shell-contraction,thm:V16-subcubic-closure}.

\section{Version V17 direction: thermalize the source metric before reading another posterior}
\label{sec:V17-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V16 proved a polynomial defining-representation contraction and used
it to control the boundary-message numerator.  Its denominator was still the
Version~V14 private-coordinate floor
\(
 e^{-33\beta/2}D_{W,N}^{-2}/72
\), so the resulting exponent compared
\(N/(1+\beta)^2\) with \(\beta\) and stopped at the cubic-root scale.
Opening another posterior estimator at that point would be premature.  The
source denominator is itself a degree-two Wilson-loop moment, and the same
one-link circle disintegration can be applied to the finite Peter--Weyl bank
which occurs in that moment.

The present continuation therefore moves one arrow upstream.  It proves a
native one-link contraction simultaneously on
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak R_2
 =\{\mathbf3,\overline{\mathbf3},\mathbf6,
       \overline{\mathbf6},\mathbf8\},}
 \label{eq:V17-degree-two-bank}
\end{equation}
uses the exact character decomposition of the squared real fundamental trace,
and reconstructs the complete raw four-loop source metric near its Haar value.
The exponentially small private-coordinate denominator then disappears from
the source-relative ratio.  No new boundary record, source deformation,
replica hierarchy, or fitted source normalization is introduced.

\begin{firewall}[Why this is not another equivalent circle estimator]
\label{fire:V17-not-equivalent-circle}
Version~V16 controlled only the first fundamental moment and therefore still
needed an unrelated exponential lower bound for the total source metric.
Version~V17 controls every irreducible summand of the actual quadratic source
moment.  It closes a previously missing denominator row rather than
re-encoding the already isolated posterior loss.  The Version~V11 scalar
posterior card remains untouched and is used only on the trajectory branch
which survives the new source-metric estimate.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{A second-derivative circle bound controls every nonzero Fourier mode}
\label{sec:V17-circle-second-order}
% =============================================================================

Retain the normalized circle Haar measure \(\dd t/(2\pi)\).  The first
improvement is that the one-link Wilson potential has a bounded second circle
derivative.  This gives a square-root peak bound and hence a Fourier deficit of
order \((1+\beta)^{-1}\), rather than the order
\((1+\beta)^{-2}\) consequence of a first-derivative estimate alone.

\begin{lemma}[Second-order peak bound]
\label{lem:V17-second-order-peak}
Let \(p>0\) be a twice continuously differentiable probability density on
\(\mathbb T\), and suppose
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{\dd^2}{\dd t^2}\log p(t)\right|\le K.
 \label{eq:V17-log-second-bound}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|p\|_\infty
 \le \pi\sqrt{\mathrm e(1+K)}.}
 \label{eq:V17-second-order-peak}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(t_0\) maximize \(q=\log p\), so \(q'(t_0)=0\).  Taylor's theorem and
\eqref{eq:V17-log-second-bound} give
\[
 q(t_0+s)\ge q(t_0)-\frac K2s^2.
\]
Put \(a=(1+K)^{-1/2}\le1<\pi\).  For \(|s|\le a\), the right-hand side is at
least \(q(t_0)-1/2\).  If \(M=p(t_0)\), normalization therefore gives
\[
 1\ge \frac1{2\pi}\int_{-a}^{a}p(t_0+s)\,\dd s
 \ge \frac{Ma}{\pi\sqrt{\mathrm e}}.
\]
Rearrangement proves \eqref{eq:V17-second-order-peak}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform deficit for all nonzero circle Fourier modes]
\label{thm:V17-all-Fourier-deficit}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{lem:V17-second-order-peak}, for every
\(n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \int_{\mathbb T}e^{int}p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}
 \right|
 \le1-\delta_2(K),
 \qquad
 \delta_2(K):=\frac1{4\pi^2\mathrm e(1+K)}.}
 \label{eq:V17-all-Fourier-deficit}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let \(M=\|p\|_\infty\).  Since the circle average of \(p\) is one, \(M\ge1\).
If the Fourier coefficient is nonzero, choose \(\theta\) so that its rotation
by \(e^{-i\theta}\) is nonnegative real.  For
\(
 r=\pi/(2M)\le\pi/2
\), let
\[
 E_{n,\theta,r}
 =\{t:d_{\mathbb T}(nt,\theta)<r\}.
\]
The map \(t\mapsto nt\) preserves normalized Haar measure, so
\(
 |E_{n,\theta,r}|/(2\pi)=r/\pi
\).  Hence
\[
 \int_{E_{n,\theta,r}}p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}
 \le M\frac r\pi=\frac12.
\]
On the complementary set,
\(
 1-\cos(nt-\theta)\ge2r^2/\pi^2
\).  Therefore
\[
 1-\left|\int e^{int}p(t)\frac{\dd t}{2\pi}\right|
 \ge\frac12\frac{2r^2}{\pi^2}
 =\frac1{4M^2}.
\]
Insert \eqref{eq:V17-second-order-peak}.  The zero-coefficient case is
immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The role of higher Fourier modes]
\label{rem:V17-higher-modes}
The degree-two Wilson moment contains circle weights up to four.  A first-mode
estimate alone does not control the zero-weight and higher-weight pieces of
\(\mathbf6\) or \(\mathbf8\).  The uniform statement
\eqref{eq:V17-all-Fourier-deficit} is exactly what permits one common
finite-representation contraction.
\end{remark}

% =============================================================================
\section{An exact eight-circle frame for the degree-two \texorpdfstring{\(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)}{SU(3)} bank}
\label{sec:V17-representation-frame}
% =============================================================================

Let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_8\) be the standard Hermitian Gell--Mann
matrices normalized by
\(
 \operatorname{Tr}(\lambda_a\lambda_b)=2\delta_{ab}
\).  Define the eight integral circle generators
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 H_a=\lambda_a\quad(1\le a\le7),
 \qquad
 H_8=\sqrt3\lambda_8=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-2).}
 \label{eq:V17-eight-circles}
\end{equation}
Every \(e^{itH_a}\) has period \(2\pi\).  For a unitary representation
\(\rho\), write \(\mathrm d\rho(H_a)\) for the Hermitian generator determined by
\(
 \rho(e^{itH_a})=e^{itd\rho(H_a)}
\).

\begin{lemma}[Exact representation frame and weight bounds]
\label{lem:V17-representation-frame}
For the representations in \eqref{eq:V17-degree-two-bank}, the following
statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item In the defining basis of \(\mathbf3\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a=1}^{8}\mathrm d\rho_{\mathbf3}(H_a)^2
 =\operatorname{diag}(6,6,8)\succeq6I_3.
 \label{eq:V17-frame-3}
\end{equation}
\item In the symmetric basis
\(
 e_1^2,e_2^2,e_3^2,
 (e_1e_2+e_2e_1)/\sqrt2,
 (e_1e_3+e_3e_1)/\sqrt2,
 (e_2e_3+e_3e_2)/\sqrt2
\)
of \(\mathbf6=\operatorname{Sym}^2\mathbf3\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a=1}^{8}\mathrm d\rho_{\mathbf6}(H_a)^2
 =\operatorname{diag}(16,16,24,16,14,14)
 \succeq14I_6.
 \label{eq:V17-frame-6}
\end{equation}
\item In the normalized Gell--Mann basis of the adjoint representation,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a=1}^{8}\mathrm d\rho_{\mathbf8}(H_a)^2
 =\operatorname{diag}(12,12,12,18,18,18,18,12)
 \succeq12I_8.
 \label{eq:V17-frame-8}
\end{equation}
\item The maximum absolute weights of any one \(H_a\) are respectively
\begin{equation}
 L_{\mathbf3}=L_{\overline{\mathbf3}}=2,
 \qquad
 L_{\mathbf6}=L_{\overline{\mathbf6}}=4,
 \qquad
 L_{\mathbf8}=3.
 \label{eq:V17-weight-maxima}
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every unit vector \(b\) in any representation
\(\rho\in\mathfrak R_2\), at least one generator \(H_a\) has nonzero-weight
projection \(P_{a,\ne0}b\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|P_{a,\ne0}b\|^2\ge a_{\rm PW},
 \qquad a_{\rm PW}:=\frac7{64}.}
 \label{eq:V17-nonzero-weight-fraction}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For \(\mathbf3\), direct multiplication of the matrices in
\eqref{eq:V17-eight-circles} gives \eqref{eq:V17-frame-3}.  On
\(\operatorname{Sym}^2\mathbf3\), the generator is
\(
 H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_a
\); compression to the displayed orthonormal symmetric basis gives
\eqref{eq:V17-frame-6}.  On the adjoint representation the generator is
\(
 X\mapsto[H_a,X]
\); its matrix in the basis \(\lambda_j/\sqrt2\) gives
\eqref{eq:V17-frame-8}.  These are finite exact matrix multiplications.
The conjugate representations have the same squared frame.

For \(a\le7\), \(H_a\) is conjugate to
\(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,0)\), while \(H_8\) has eigenvalues
\(1,1,-2\).  The weights in \(\mathbf6\) are pairwise sums of defining
weights, and those in \(\mathbf8\subset\mathbf3\otimes\overline{\mathbf3}\)
are their differences.  This proves \eqref{eq:V17-weight-maxima}.

Now fix a unit vector \(b\).  One of the eight frame summands has squared norm
at least one eighth of the corresponding lower frame eigenvalue.  If
\(b=\sum_m b_m\) is its weight decomposition, then
\[
 \|\mathrm d\rho(H_a)b\|^2
 =\sum_m m^2\|b_m\|^2
 \le L_\rho^2\sum_{m\ne0}\|b_m\|^2.
\]
The resulting nonzero-weight fractions are
\[
 \frac6{8\cdot2^2}=\frac3{16},
 \qquad
 \frac{14}{8\cdot4^2}=\frac7{64},
 \qquad
 \frac{12}{8\cdot3^2}=\frac16.
\]
Their minimum is \(7/64\), proving
\eqref{eq:V17-nonzero-weight-fraction}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Native one-link contraction on the finite Peter--Weyl bank}
\label{sec:V17-one-link-bank}
% =============================================================================

Retain the exact one-link Wilson law of
\eqref{eq:V16-one-link-law}.  Along any circle in
\eqref{eq:V17-eight-circles}, a single plaquette term obeys
\begin{equation}
 \left|
 \frac{\dd^2}{\dd t^2}
 \frac13\operatorname{ReTr}(UR_tB)
 \right|
 \le\frac13\operatorname{Tr}|H_a^2|
 \le2.
 \label{eq:V17-one-plaquette-second-derivative}
\end{equation}
Since at most six plaquettes meet one link, every conditional circle density
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\partial_t^2\log p_q(t)\right|\le12\beta.}
 \label{eq:V17-one-link-log-second}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \delta_{\rm PW}(\beta)
 :=\frac1{4\pi^2\mathrm e(1+12\beta)},
 \qquad
 \eta_{\rm PW}(\beta)
 :=\frac7{64}
   \left(2\delta_{\rm PW}-\delta_{\rm PW}^2\right),
 \qquad
 q_{\rm PW}(\beta):=\sqrt{1-\eta_{\rm PW}(\beta)}.}
 \label{eq:V17-PW-constants}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Peter--Weyl one-link contraction]
\label{thm:V17-one-link-PW-contraction}
For every exterior configuration, every \(\beta\ge0\), every
\(\rho\in\mathfrak R_2\), and every lattice link,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left\|
  \int_{\SU(3)}\rho(U)\,\dd\nu_{e,\beta}(U)
 \right\|_{\rm op}
 \le q_{\rm PW}(\beta)<1.}
 \label{eq:V17-one-link-PW-contraction}
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds for inverse link orientation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix a unit vector \(b\) in the representation space.  By
\Cref{lem:V17-representation-frame}, choose \(H_a\) such that the nonzero
weight component has squared norm at least \(7/64\).  Disintegrate the
one-link law over the right cosets of \(\{e^{itH_a}\}\), exactly as in
\Cref{thm:V16-one-link-circle-contraction}.  On every quotient fibre, the
conditional circle density satisfies \eqref{eq:V17-one-link-log-second}.

Write \(b=\sum_m b_m\) for the orthogonal weight decomposition.  The circle
average on one quotient fibre is
\[
 \sum_m \widehat p_q(-m)b_m.
\]
The zero-weight coefficient is one, while every nonzero coefficient has
modulus at most \(1-\delta_{\rm PW}\) by
\Cref{thm:V17-all-Fourier-deficit}.  Hence its squared norm is at most
\begin{align*}
 \|b_0\|^2+(1-\delta_{\rm PW})^2
       \sum_{m\ne0}\|b_m\|^2
 &\le1-\frac7{64}
      \left(2\delta_{\rm PW}-\delta_{\rm PW}^2\right)\\
 &=1-\eta_{\rm PW}.
\end{align*}
The left coset representative acts unitarily.  Averaging the fibre estimates
and using the triangle inequality gives
\(
 \|A_\rho b\|\le q_{\rm PW}
\), where
\(
 A_\rho=\int\rho(U)\,\dd\nu_{e,\beta}(U)
\).  Taking the supremum over \(b\) proves
\eqref{eq:V17-one-link-PW-contraction}.  Inverse orientation replaces the
mean by its adjoint and leaves the norm unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What the finite bank adds]
\label{ass:V17-bank-adds}
The defining representation controls a loop mean.  The bank
\(\mathfrak R_2\) additionally controls the adjoint and symmetric-square
components of a loop square.  This is the minimum Peter--Weyl enlargement
needed by the actual source covariance; no dense Wilson-network algebra is
used.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact quadratic character thermalization on a physical long side}
\label{sec:V17-quadratic-thermalization}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Long-side character attenuation]
\label{thm:V17-character-attenuation}
Let \(C\) be a simple loop and let \(S\) contain \(m\) once-traversed edges of
\(C\), with no plaquette containing two selected edges.  For every
\(\rho\in\mathfrak R_2\), conditionally on all links outside \(S\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\chi_\rho(U(C))\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 \right|
 \le (\dim\rho)q_{\rm PW}(\beta)^m.}
 \label{eq:V17-character-attenuation}
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds after conditioning on any smaller sigma-algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The selected links have a conditionally factorized Wilson law.  In the
representation \(\rho\), integration replaces every selected link or inverse
link by an operator of norm at most \(q_{\rm PW}\), by
\Cref{thm:V17-one-link-PW-contraction}.  All interspersed fixed matrices are
unitary.  The absolute trace is at most \(\dim\rho\) times the resulting
operator norm, proving the first claim.  The second is the tower property.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact square of the normalized real fundamental trace]
\label{lem:V17-character-square}
For \(U\in\SU(3)\), put
\(
 \mathcal O(U)=\frac13\operatorname{ReTr}U
\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O(U)^2
 =\frac1{18}
  +\frac1{36}
   \left(
    \chi_{\mathbf3}(U)+\chi_{\overline{\mathbf3}}(U)
    +\chi_{\mathbf6}(U)+\chi_{\overline{\mathbf6}}(U)
    +2\chi_{\mathbf8}(U)
   \right).}
 \label{eq:V17-character-square}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(z=\operatorname{Tr}U\).  The tensor decompositions
\[
 \mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3=\mathbf6\oplus\overline{\mathbf3},
 \qquad
 \mathbf3\otimes\overline{\mathbf3}=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf8
\]
give
\[
 z^2=\chi_{\mathbf6}+\chi_{\overline{\mathbf3}},
 \qquad
 |z|^2=1+\chi_{\mathbf8},
\]
and their conjugates.  Expanding
\(
 \mathcal O^2=(z+\overline z)^2/36
\)
proves \eqref{eq:V17-character-square}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional first, second, and mixed loop moments]
\label{thm:V17-loop-moment-thermalization}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:V17-character-attenuation},
\begin{align}
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 \right|
 &\le q_{\rm PW}^m,
 \label{eq:V17-first-moment}\\
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C^2\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
  -\frac1{18}
 \right|
 &\le\frac{17}{18}q_{\rm PW}^m.
 \label{eq:V17-second-moment}
\end{align}
If a second normalized real fundamental loop \(D\) traverses none of the
selected links, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_C\mathcal O_D
             \mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 \right|
 \le q_{\rm PW}^m.}
 \label{eq:V17-mixed-moment}
\end{equation}
All three inequalities persist under further conditioning onto a smaller
record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first inequality is \Cref{thm:V17-character-attenuation} in the defining
representation, divided by three and combined with its conjugate.  For the
second, insert \eqref{eq:V17-character-square}.  The sum of the dimensions of
the nontrivial character terms, with the adjoint counted twice, is
\[
 3+3+6+6+2\cdot8=34.
\]
Division by \(36\) gives the coefficient \(17/18\).  For the mixed moment,
condition on the complement of \(S\).  The loop \(D\) is then independent of
every selected link and has absolute value at most one; integrate the
fundamental coefficient of \(C\) as in
\eqref{eq:V17-first-moment}.  The tower property gives the final statement.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Haar conditioning of the complete four-loop source metric}
\label{sec:V17-source-metric}
% =============================================================================

For the four physical rectangles define the native Peter--Weyl side factor
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta)
 :=q_{\rm PW}(\beta)^{N/4}
 =\left(1-\eta_{\rm PW}(\beta)\right)^{N/8}.}
 \label{eq:V17-side-factor}
\end{equation}
Every rectangle has an admissible straight side of length at least \(N/4\),
and every ordered pair of distinct rectangles has a pair-private such side by
\Cref{lem:V15-pair-private-side}.

\begin{theorem}[Complete raw four-loop covariance window]
\label{thm:V17-raw-covariance-window}
Let \(\Sigma_N\) and \(K_{N,R}\) be the raw four-loop covariance and its
shell-visible message covariance from
\eqref{eq:V15-raw-covariance}--\eqref{eq:V15-raw-message-covariance}.  Then
for every finite Wilson card and every separating shell,
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \left\|\Sigma_N-\frac1{18}I_4\right\|_{\rm op}
 \le\frac{143}{18}r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta),}
 \label{eq:V17-raw-covariance-window}\\
 \boxed{
 0\preceq K_{N,R}
 \preceq16\bigl(r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta)\bigr)^2I_4.}
 \label{eq:V17-raw-message-window}
\end{align}
The bounds are uniform over separating shell radii and fixed exterior boundary
conditions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:V17-loop-moment-thermalization} to one long side of each
rectangle and to the pair-private side for every ordered pair.  It gives
\[
 |W_{\alpha,N}|\le r_N^{\rm PW},
 \qquad
 \left|
  \mathbb E\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}^2-\frac1{18}
 \right|
 \le\frac{17}{18}r_N^{\rm PW},
\]
and, for \(\alpha\ne\gamma\),
\[
 |\mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mathcal O_{\gamma,N}]|
 \le r_N^{\rm PW}.
\]
Since \(0\le r_N^{\rm PW}\le1\), centering gives
\begin{align*}
 \left| (\Sigma_N)_{\alpha\alpha}-\frac1{18}\right|
 &\le\frac{17}{18}r_N^{\rm PW}+(r_N^{\rm PW})^2
 \le\frac{35}{18}r_N^{\rm PW},\\
 |(\Sigma_N)_{\alpha\gamma}|
 &\le r_N^{\rm PW}+(r_N^{\rm PW})^2
 \le2r_N^{\rm PW}.
\end{align*}
The maximum absolute row sum is
\(
 35r/18+3(2r)=143r/18
\), proving \eqref{eq:V17-raw-covariance-window}.

The conditional first-moment bound gives, pointwise in the shell record,
\[
 \left|
  \mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mid B_{N,R}]-W_{\alpha,N}
 \right|
 \le2r_N^{\rm PW}.
\]
The squared Euclidean norm of the four-component message is therefore at most
\(16(r_N^{\rm PW})^2\), which proves the matrix order
\eqref{eq:V17-raw-message-window}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform raw-frame conditioning]
\label{cor:V17-raw-frame-conditioning}
If
\(
 143r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta)<1
\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{1-143r_N^{\rm PW}}{18}I_4
 \preceq\Sigma_N
 \preceq
 \frac{1+143r_N^{\rm PW}}{18}I_4.}
 \label{eq:V17-raw-frame-two-sided}
\end{equation}
In particular, the raw four-loop frame has rank four and condition number at
most
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{cond}(\Sigma_N)
 \le\frac{1+143r_N^{\rm PW}}
          {1-143r_N^{\rm PW}}.}
 \label{eq:V17-raw-frame-condition-number}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is the spectral consequence of
\eqref{eq:V17-raw-covariance-window}.
\end{proof}

\section{Complete source-relative contraction without a private-coordinate debit}
\label{sec:V17-source-contraction}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Peter--Weyl source-to-shell contraction]
\label{thm:V17-source-to-shell-contraction}
Put
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2
 :=\begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \frac{288(r_N^{\rm PW})^2}{1-143r_N^{\rm PW}},
 &143r_N^{\rm PW}<1,\\[0.9em]
 1,&143r_N^{\rm PW}\ge1,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \widehat\kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2:=\min\{1,\kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2\}.
 \label{eq:V17-PW-kappa}
\end{equation}
Then, for every separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 M_{N,R}
 \preceq\widehat\kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2\Gamma_N.}
 \label{eq:V17-normalized-source-contraction}
\end{equation}
Consequently every nonzero normalized four-loop contrast obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{
  \|\mathbb E[a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 }{
  \|a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\|_2^2
 }
 \le\widehat\kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2,}
 \label{eq:V17-every-source-ratio}
\end{equation}
and the physical Creutz source satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}(\beta)}{G_N(\beta)}
 \le\widehat\kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2.}
 \label{eq:V17-Creutz-ratio}
\end{equation}
No factor exponential in \(\beta\) occurs in this ratio.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the branch \(143r_N^{\rm PW}<1\),
\Cref{thm:V17-raw-covariance-window,cor:V17-raw-frame-conditioning} give
\[
 K_{N,R}\preceq16(r_N^{\rm PW})^2I_4
 \preceq
 \frac{288(r_N^{\rm PW})^2}{1-143r_N^{\rm PW}}\Sigma_N.
\]
Congruence by \(D_{W,N}^{-1}\) and
\eqref{eq:V15-raw-normalized-congruence} yield
\eqref{eq:V17-normalized-source-contraction}.  On the complementary branch,
conditional expectation gives the universal order
\(
 M_{N,R}\preceq\Gamma_N
\).  Scalar compression proves the remaining statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact finite-card threshold]
\label{cor:V17-finite-threshold}
Let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_{\rm c}
 =\frac{\sqrt{21601}-143}{576}
 =0.006897198952609\ldots}
 \label{eq:V17-critical-r}
\end{equation}
be the positive root of \(288r^2+143r-1=0\).  If
\begin{equation}
 r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta)<r_{\rm c},
 \label{eq:V17-finite-strict-condition}
\end{equation}
then \(\widehat\kappa_{N,\rm PW}<1\), uniformly for every separating shell.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Under \eqref{eq:V17-finite-strict-condition}, one has
\(143r_N^{\rm PW}<1\), and
\(
 288r^2/(1-143r)<1
\)
is equivalent to \(288r^2+143r-1<0\).
\end{proof}

\section{Sublinear-coupling extinction and the remaining linear branch}
\label{sec:V17-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

Since \(0<\delta_{\rm PW}<1\),
\(
 2\delta_{\rm PW}-\delta_{\rm PW}^2\ge\delta_{\rm PW}
\).  Therefore
\begin{equation}
 \eta_{\rm PW}(\beta)
 \ge\frac7{256\pi^2\mathrm e(1+12\beta)},
 \label{eq:V17-eta-lower}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta)
 \le
 \exp\left[
  -\frac{7N}{2048\pi^2\mathrm e(1+12\beta)}
 \right].}
 \label{eq:V17-side-exponential}
\end{equation}

Define the native Peter--Weyl accumulation parameter
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Xi_N^{\rm PW}(\beta):=\frac{N}{1+12\beta}.}
 \label{eq:V17-Xi}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Sublinear-coupling source-relative extinction]
\label{thm:V17-sublinear-extinction}
For every cofinal sequence satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \beta_N=o(N),
 \label{eq:V17-sublinear-coupling}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{R\ {\rm separating}}
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\square}(\beta_N)}{G_N(\beta_N)}
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V17-sublinear-extinction}
\end{equation}
More generally, the same conclusion holds whenever
\(
 \Xi_N^{\rm PW}(\beta_N)\to\infty
\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Condition \eqref{eq:V17-sublinear-coupling} is equivalent to
\(
 N/(1+12\beta_N)\to\infty
\).  Equation \eqref{eq:V17-side-exponential} then gives
\(
 r_N^{\rm PW}\to0
\).  The explicit expression
\eqref{eq:V17-PW-kappa} implies
\(
 \widehat\kappa_{N,\rm PW}^2\to0
\), and \eqref{eq:V17-Creutz-ratio} is uniform in the shell radius.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced source landing on the sublinear branch]
\label{cor:V17-balanced-landing}
For the canonical balanced source of Version~V15,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\widehat Y_N^{\square}\|_2^2\longrightarrow\frac1{18},
 \qquad
 \sup_R
 \|\mathbb E[\widehat Y_N^{\square}\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 \longrightarrow0}
 \label{eq:V17-balanced-landing}
\end{equation}
whenever \(\beta_N=o(N)\).  Thus this branch carries a finite noncollapsed
balanced source and a completely vanishing separating-shell message.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The balanced raw coefficient vector has Euclidean norm one.  Apply
\eqref{eq:V17-raw-covariance-window} and
\eqref{eq:V17-raw-message-window}, then use
\(r_N^{\rm PW}\to0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit sufficient linear-scale threshold]
\label{cor:V17-linear-threshold}
Put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \tau_{\rm PW}
 :=\frac{2048\pi^2\mathrm e}{7}
   \log\frac1{r_{\rm c}}
 =39062.7088481\ldots.}
 \label{eq:V17-tau-PW}
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}
 \frac{N}{1+12\beta}>\tau_{\rm PW},
 \label{eq:V17-Xi-threshold}
\end{equation}
then every separating-shell source channel is strictly contractive.  If the
left-hand side tends to infinity, its source-relative norm tends to zero.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V17-side-exponential} and
\eqref{eq:V17-Xi-threshold} give
\(
 r_N^{\rm PW}<r_{\rm c}
\).  Apply \Cref{cor:V17-finite-threshold}.  The second statement is
\Cref{thm:V17-sublinear-extinction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Revised weak-facing trajectory alternative]
\label{thm:V17-trajectory-alternative}
For every selected weak-facing sequence, pass to a subsequence on which
\(
 \Xi_N^{\rm PW}(\beta_N^{\rm wf})
\)
converges in \([0,\infty]\).  Exactly one of the following occurs.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item \(\Xi_N^{\rm PW}\to\infty\).  Then the complete source-relative shell
      message vanishes uniformly over every separating shell, and the balanced
      source has the landing \eqref{eq:V17-balanced-landing}.
\item \(\Xi_N^{\rm PW}\to\xi\in(\tau_{\rm PW},\infty)\).  Then all sufficiently
      large cards have one uniform strict source-to-shell contraction.
\item \(\Xi_N^{\rm PW}\to\xi\in[0,\tau_{\rm PW}]\).  If \(\xi>0\), then
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \frac{\beta_N^{\rm wf}}{N}
       \longrightarrow\frac1{12\xi};}
       \label{eq:V17-linear-root-limit}
      \end{equation}
      if \(\xi=0\), then
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \frac{\beta_N^{\rm wf}}{N}\longrightarrow\infty.}
       \label{eq:V17-superlinear-root-limit}
      \end{equation}
      This is the only branch on which the Version~V11 posterior pair remains
      an unresolved physical acquisition.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, every bounded, logarithmic, polylogarithmic, power-law
\(N^a\) with \(a<1\), and more generally every sublinear selected-root
sequence lies in item~\textup{(P1)}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Subsequence convergence in the one-point compactification is elementary.
Items~\textup{(P1)} and \textup{(P2)} follow from
\Cref{thm:V17-sublinear-extinction,cor:V17-linear-threshold}.  If
\(
 N/(1+12\beta_N)\to\xi>0
\), inversion gives
\(
 (1+12\beta_N)/N\to1/\xi
\), hence \eqref{eq:V17-linear-root-limit}.  If the quotient tends to zero,
its reciprocal diverges, proving \eqref{eq:V17-superlinear-root-limit}.  The
final sentence is immediate from \(\beta_N=o(N)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The actual V17 advance]
\label{ass:V17-progress}
The unpopulated trajectory is no longer cubic-root fast.  Every selected-root
sequence below linear scale has complete source-relative boundary extinction,
and a finite-limit range of sufficiently small linear coefficients has strict
contraction as well.  The only surviving branch is linear or superlinear in
\(N\), with the explicit conservative threshold of
\eqref{eq:V17-tau-PW}.  On that branch the next datum is not another circle
bound: it is the already isolated selected-root posterior loss or a
Wilson-specific root upper bound.
\end{assessment}

\begin{assessment}[Export boundary toward YM--A]
\label{ass:V17-YMA-export}
Version~V17 exports a noncollapsed balanced source together with complete
spatial boundary extinction throughout the sublinear weak-facing regime.  It
does not determine the unnormalized axial partition curvature, the signed
reduced-fibre Hessian, the source-orthogonal centre-neutral network sector, or
the Osterwalder--Schrader semigroup.  The spatial Peter--Weyl estimate is not
renamed as a temporal mass gap.
\end{assessment}

\section{Version V18 direction: stop improving the local constant and move to the actual cutoff incidence}
\label{sec:V18-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V17 closes every selected-root branch with
$\beta_N=o(N)$ by a uniform one-link Peter--Weyl thermalization estimate.
Its remaining branch is linear or faster in the lattice side length.  A
further enlargement of the finite representation bank would be circular
unless it changed this scaling barrier.

The first result below proves that the barrier is intrinsic to every
worst-exterior one-link method.  When all six staples adjacent to one link are
flat, the defining-representation conditional mean has deficit
$2/(3\beta)+o(\beta^{-1})$.  Therefore no uniform one-link contraction can
have a larger-order weak-coupling deficit, and a product over $O(N)$ links
cannot force extinction when $\beta$ is of order $N$ or larger.

The continuation then moves to the actual upstream cutoff incidence.  For one
dyadic pair, each of the four fine physical rectangles is exactly the ordered
two-edge lift of the corresponding coarse rectangle.  Hence there is no
physical writer-shape defect.  The complete adjacent-cutoff source problem is
reduced to two genuinely independent rows:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{natural coarse law versus induced blocked fine law}\\
 {}+\ \text{motion of the normalized four-loop coefficient direction}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V18-two-rows}
\end{equation}
A quantitative Hellinger theorem below converts these two rows into an
outward old/fine Schur interval.  The selected Creutz response relation alone
does not control the second row.

\begin{firewall}[No new local thermalization hierarchy]
\label{fire:V18-no-local-hierarchy}
The identity-staple lower example proves optimality only for uniform
one-link, worst-exterior product estimates.  It is not a lower bound on the
actual physical Wilson-loop expectation, because the flat exterior need not
have appreciable probability.  Its role is methodological: another local
circle, larger finite representation bank, or sharper universal constant
cannot by itself remove the linear-scale branch.  The remaining progress must
come from selected-root information, blocked-law comparison, or the already
isolated posterior shell Read.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The linear scaling barrier is optimal for every uniform one-link method}
\label{sec:V18-local-optimality}
% =============================================================================

We first record the elementary Laplace statement needed for the actual
$\SU(3)$ conditional law.

\begin{lemma}[Ratio form of the compact Laplace principle]
\label{lem:V18-Laplace}
Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension $d$, let $m$ have a smooth
strictly positive density, and let $\varphi\ge0$ be smooth with a unique
minimum $x_0$, $\varphi(x_0)=0$, and positive-definite Hessian at $x_0$.
For
\[
 \dd\pi_\lambda
 =Z_\lambda^{-1}e^{-\lambda\varphi}\,\dd m,
 \qquad \lambda\to\infty,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_{\pi_\lambda}\varphi
 =\frac{d}{2\lambda}+O(\lambda^{-3/2}).}
 \label{eq:V18-Laplace-ratio}
\end{equation}
The error constant depends only on a fixed local chart and on finitely many
local derivatives of $\varphi$ and the density of $m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose local coordinates $x\in\mathbb R^d$ centered at $x_0$.  For some
positive matrix $H$ and smooth positive density $a$,
\[
 \varphi(x)=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+O(|x|^3),
 \qquad
 \dd m=a(x)\,\dd x,
 \qquad a(0)>0.
\]
After shrinking the chart, $\varphi(x)\ge c|x|^2$ there, while compactness and
uniqueness of the minimum give $\varphi\ge c_0>0$ off the chart.  Set
$x=\lambda^{-1/2}z$.  Gaussian domination, followed by Taylor expansion of
$\varphi$ and $a$, gives
\begin{align*}
 Z_\lambda
 &=\lambda^{-d/2}a(0)
   \int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-z^{\mathsf T}Hz/2}\,\dd z
   \bigl(1+O(\lambda^{-1/2})\bigr),\\
 \int_M\varphi e^{-\lambda\varphi}\,\dd m
 &=\lambda^{-d/2-1}a(0)
   \int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz
        e^{-z^{\mathsf T}Hz/2}\,\dd z
   \bigl(1+O(\lambda^{-1/2})\bigr).
\end{align*}
For completeness, the Taylor expansion may be restricted first to
$|z|\le\lambda^{1/10}$; the complement inside the chart is
$O(e^{-c\lambda^{1/5}})$, and the complement of the chart is
$O(e^{-c_0\lambda})$.  The Gaussian identity
\[
 \int\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz\,e^{-z^{\mathsf T}Hz/2}\,\dd z
 =\frac d2\int e^{-z^{\mathsf T}Hz/2}\,\dd z
\]
then proves \eqref{eq:V18-Laplace-ratio} after division.
\end{proof}

Set
\begin{equation}
 d(U):=1-\frac13\operatorname{Re}\Tr U,
 \qquad U\in\SU(3).
 \label{eq:V18-Wilson-defect}
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Flat-point Hessian of the normalized Wilson defect]
\label{lem:V18-flat-Hessian}
With the invariant inner product
$\langle X,Y\rangle=-\Tr(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(3)$,
\begin{equation}
 d(e^X)=\frac16\|X\|^2+O(\|X\|^4).
 \label{eq:V18-defect-expansion}
\end{equation}
Thus the identity is the unique minimum of $d$, its Hessian is
$\frac13I_8$, and it is nondegenerate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For anti-Hermitian traceless $X$,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\Tr e^X
 =3+\frac12\Tr X^2+O(\|X\|^4)
 =3-\frac12\|X\|^2+O(\|X\|^4),
\]
because the traces of odd powers are purely imaginary.  This gives
\eqref{eq:V18-defect-expansion}.  The bound
$\operatorname{Re}\Tr U\le3$ is saturated only when all three unit-modulus
eigenvalues equal one, hence only at $U=I$.
\end{proof}

Condition one lattice link and set every exterior link equal to the identity.
All six staples are then the identity, and the actual one-link Wilson law is
\begin{equation}
 \dd\nu_\beta^{\rm id}(U)
 =\frac{e^{2\beta\operatorname{Re}\Tr U}}{
        \int_{\SU(3)}e^{2\beta\operatorname{Re}\Tr V}\,\dd V}
   \,\dd U
 =\frac{e^{-6\beta d(U)}}{
        \int_{\SU(3)}e^{-6\beta d(V)}\,\dd V}
   \,\dd U.
 \label{eq:V18-identity-staple-law}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp scaling obstruction for uniform one-link contraction]
\label{thm:V18-one-link-optimality}
Let
\[
 \mathsf M_\beta^{\eta}
 =\int_{\SU(3)}U\,\dd\nu_{e,\beta}^{\eta}(U)
\]
be the defining-representation conditional mean for exterior configuration
$\eta$, and let
\[
 q_3(\beta):=\sup_\eta\|\mathsf M_\beta^{\eta}\|_{\rm op}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 q_3(\beta)
 \ge
 1-\frac{2}{3\beta}+O(\beta^{-3/2})
 \qquad(\beta\to\infty).}
 \label{eq:V18-q-lower}
\end{equation}
Consequently every exterior-uniform one-link estimate
$\|\mathsf M_\beta^{\eta}\|_{\rm op}\le1-\delta(\beta)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \delta(\beta)
 \le\frac{2}{3\beta}+O(\beta^{-3/2}).}
 \label{eq:V18-delta-upper}
\end{equation}
The same restriction applies to every finite Peter--Weyl bank containing the
defining representation.

More generally, suppose a long-side argument uses $m_N$ links and only a
uniform one-link coefficient $q(\beta)\ge q_3(\beta)$.  If
$m_N/N\to\ell>0$ and $\beta_N/N\to c\in(0,\infty)$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}q(\beta_N)^{m_N}
 \ge e^{-2\ell/(3c)}>0.}
 \label{eq:V18-linear-barrier}
\end{equation}
If $\beta_N/N\to\infty$, the lower limit is one.  For the physical side
$m_N=N/4$, the finite linear-scale floor is $e^{-1/(6c)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The law \eqref{eq:V18-identity-staple-law} is conjugation invariant, so its
matrix mean is $m_\beta I_3$.  It is also invariant under inversion, hence
$m_\beta$ is real.  Taking the trace gives
\[
 m_\beta
 =\mathbb E_{\nu_\beta^{\rm id}}
   \frac13\operatorname{Re}\Tr U
 =1-\mathbb E_{\nu_\beta^{\rm id}}d(U).
\]
Apply \Cref{lem:V18-Laplace} with $d=8$ and $\lambda=6\beta$:
\[
 1-m_\beta
 =\frac8{12\beta}+O(\beta^{-3/2})
 =\frac{2}{3\beta}+O(\beta^{-3/2}).
\]
The identity exterior is included in the supremum defining $q_3$, proving
\eqref{eq:V18-q-lower} and \eqref{eq:V18-delta-upper}.  If
$\beta_N/N\to c$, then
\[
 \log q(\beta_N)
 \ge-\frac{2}{3\beta_N}+O(\beta_N^{-3/2}),
\]
and multiplication by $m_N$ gives
$-2\ell/(3c)+o(1)$.  The superlinear case is identical with limiting exponent
zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The V17 scaling boundary is method-optimal]
\label{ass:V18-method-optimal}
Version~V17 proves extinction whenever $N/\beta_N\to\infty$.  The identity-
staple law shows that this is the best possible scaling conclusion obtainable
from an exterior-uniform product of one-link representation means.  Improving
constants remains useful on a fixed linear-slope branch, but cannot turn a
linear or superlinear sequence into automatic extinction.  The remaining
arrow programme must therefore read the selected trajectory or its actual
cutoff incidence.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The four physical rectangles have exact dyadic writer incidence}
\label{sec:V18-dyadic-geometry}
% =============================================================================

Let $M\in16\mathbb N$ and put $N=2M$.  Denote the inherited block map by
\begin{equation}
 (B_{N\to M}U)_{x,\mu}
 =U_{2x,\mu}U_{2x+\widehat\mu,\mu}.
 \label{eq:V18-block-map}
\end{equation}
For an oriented coarse path $\gamma$, let $\mathsf L\gamma$ be the fine path
obtained by replacing each positive coarse edge by its two ordered fine edges,
and each negative edge by the reversed inverse pair.

\begin{lemma}[Path-word covariance of the dyadic block]
\label{lem:V18-path-lift}
For every coarse path $\gamma$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 U_{\mathsf L\gamma}
 =(B_{N\to M}U)_\gamma.}
 \label{eq:V18-path-holonomy}
\end{equation}
If $C_{\epsilon\eta}^{(M)}$ is one of the four physical rectangles at cutoff
$M$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathsf L C_{\epsilon\eta}^{(M)}
 =C_{\epsilon\eta}^{(N)}.}
 \label{eq:V18-rectangle-lift}
\end{equation}
Consequently, pointwise on the fine link cylinder,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{\epsilon\eta,N}
 =\mathcal O_{\epsilon\eta,M}\circ B_{N\to M}}
 \label{eq:V18-loop-pullback}
\end{equation}
for all four labels.  If $a_N=a_M/2$, the two contours have exactly the same
physical side lengths and physical support radius.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V18-path-holonomy} follows by substituting
\eqref{eq:V18-block-map} into the ordered product along $\gamma$; the negative
orientation is the inverse of the same ordered pair.  At cutoff $M$, the two
half-length choices are $M/8$ and $3M/16$.  Their fine counterparts are
$N/8=2(M/8)$ and $3N/16=2(3M/16)$.  Hence doubling every vertex and replacing
every edge by two edges produces the literal fine rectangle, proving
\eqref{eq:V18-rectangle-lift}.  Taking the normalized real trace proves
\eqref{eq:V18-loop-pullback}.  Multiplication by the lattice spacings proves
the physical-length statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No adjacent-cutoff rectangle-shape birth]
\label{cor:V18-no-shape-birth}
Let
\[
 \mathbf O_M
 =(
  \mathcal O_{11,M},\mathcal O_{00,M},
  \mathcal O_{10,M},\mathcal O_{01,M})^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then the complete fine raw rectangle vector is exactly
$\mathbf O_M\circ B_{N\to M}$.  Thus the old/fine physical-source comparison
has no unaccounted path, orientation, support, or loop-word defect.  Any
remaining mixed residual is produced by the two rows in
\eqref{eq:V18-two-rows}, not by a new fine rectangle source.
\end{corollary}

% =============================================================================
\section{Canonical law-aligned old/fine source Gram}
\label{sec:V18-law-aligned-card}
% =============================================================================

Let
\begin{equation}
 \mu:=\mu_{M,\beta_M}^{\rm nat},
 \qquad
 \nu:=(B_{N\to M})_*\mu_{N,\beta_N}^{\rm nat}
 \label{eq:V18-two-laws}
\end{equation}
be, respectively, the natural coarse Wilson law and the coarse trace law
induced from the fine selected card.  Both have strictly positive bounded
densities with respect to coarse product Haar measure $m_M$.  Write
$p=\dd\mu/\dd m_M$ and $q=\dd\nu/\dd m_M$.  Hence they are
mutually absolutely continuous.  Put
\begin{equation}
 r:=\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}=\frac pq,
 \qquad h:=\sqrt r,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak h_{Y/X}:=\|h-1\|_{L^2(\nu)}.
 \label{eq:V18-Hellinger}
\end{equation}
The corresponding Hellinger affinity is
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal A_{Y/X}:=\int h\,\dd\nu,
 \qquad
 \boxed{\mathfrak h_{Y/X}^2=2(1-\mathcal A_{Y/X}).}
 \label{eq:V18-affinity}
\end{equation}

\begin{importedresult}[Canonical same-observable law incidence]
\label{imp:V18-law-incidence}
The attached Grand Tensor manuscript proves that multiplication
$U_hf=hf$ is a unitary map $L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\nu)$ and transports the natural
coarse null vector $1$ to $h$.  With $P_h=I-|h\rangle\langle h|$ and
$\mathcal C_h=P_hM_h$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C_h f=h(f-\mu(f)).
 \label{eq:V18-imported-incidence}
\end{equation}
Thus a naturally centered coarse observable is transported as the same
physical observable multiplied by $h$; the density square root is not a new
source direction.  This general theorem is imported and is not reproved here.
\end{importedresult}

For $\lambda\in\{\mu,\nu\}$, define the four means and the balanced Creutz
coefficient direction by
\begin{equation}
 W^\lambda:=\mathbb E_\lambda\mathbf O_M,
 \qquad
 b^\lambda:=D_{W^\lambda}^{-1}\varepsilon_\square,
 \qquad
 u^\lambda:=\frac{b^\lambda}{\|b^\lambda\|_2},
 \label{eq:V18-balanced-directions}
\end{equation}
where
$\varepsilon_\square=(1,1,-1,-1)^{\mathsf T}$.
The balanced source functions on the common coarse configuration space are
\begin{equation}
 F_\lambda
 :=(u^\lambda)^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_M-W^\lambda),
 \qquad
 \sigma_\lambda^2:=\|F_\lambda\|_{L^2(\lambda)}^2.
 \label{eq:V18-balanced-sources}
\end{equation}
By \Cref{lem:V18-path-lift}, $F_\nu\circ B_{N\to M}$ is precisely the fine
balanced physical source.  The aligned old column on the induced-law Hilbert
space is
\begin{equation}
 G_{X\uparrow Y}:=U_hF_\mu=hF_\mu
 =\mathcal C_h\bigl((u^\mu)^{\mathsf T}\mathbf O_M\bigr).
 \label{eq:V18-aligned-old-column}
\end{equation}
It satisfies $\|G_{X\uparrow Y}\|_{L^2(\nu)}=\sigma_\mu$.

\begin{definition}[Exact physical old/fine balanced Gram]
\label{def:V18-old-fine-Gram}
The law-aligned adjacent-cutoff Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
   \sigma_\nu^2&c_{Y/X}\\
   c_{Y/X}&\sigma_\mu^2
  \end{pmatrix}\succeq0,}
 \qquad
 c_{Y/X}:=\int F_\nu F_\mu\sqrt{pq}\,\dd m_M.
 \label{eq:V18-old-fine-Gram}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
$c_{Y/X}=\langle F_\nu,hF_\mu\rangle_{L^2(\nu)}$.
When both stocks are nonzero, put
\begin{equation}
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 :=\frac{c_{Y/X}}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu},
 \qquad
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 :=1-|\alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}|^2.
 \label{eq:V18-alpha-residual}
\end{equation}
Separate positive rescaling of the old and fine source columns does not change
$\alpha$ or $\mathbb R$.  Hence this is also the normalized mixed residual of
the original unbalanced Creutz sources.
\end{definition}

\begin{proof}[Proof of the assertions in the definition]
The two columns $F_\nu$ and $hF_\mu$ belong to one real Hilbert space
$L^2(\nu)$, so \eqref{eq:V18-old-fine-Gram} is their Gram.  The diagonal old
entry equals $\int h^2F_\mu^2\,\dd\nu=\int F_\mu^2\,\dd\mu$.  Multiplying the
two columns by arbitrary positive scalars cancels from their normalized inner
product.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What exact dyadic incidence has removed]
\label{ass:V18-removed-rows}
The pointwise identity \eqref{eq:V18-loop-pullback} removes the physical path
and source-support row completely.  The density $h$ accounts for the
natural-versus-induced law mismatch; $u^\mu$ and $u^\nu$ account for the
motion of the normalized Creutz direction.  The scalar $c_{Y/X}$ is therefore
the exact remaining mixed value.  A comparison of separately centered source
vectors without $h$, or a comparison using the constant rather than the
transported null $h$, is not the physical law-aligned card.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{A quantitative Hellinger--coefficient transport theorem}
\label{sec:V18-quantitative-transport}
% =============================================================================

The normalized real trace obeys
$-1/2\le\mathcal O_{\alpha,M}\le1$.  Hence
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathbf O_M-W^\lambda\|_2\le3
 \quad\text{pointwise},
 \qquad
 \|F_\lambda\|_\infty\le3.
 \label{eq:V18-uniform-source-bound}
\end{equation}
Put
\begin{equation}
 \delta_u:=\|u^\nu-u^\mu\|_2,
 \qquad
 \delta_W:=\|W^\nu-W^\mu\|_2.
 \label{eq:V18-two-drifts}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Outward old/fine Schur bound from one law row and four means]
\label{thm:V18-Hellinger-transport}
For the exact physical pair above,
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \|F_\nu-hF_\mu\|_{L^2(\nu)}
 \le
 \mathcal E_{Y/X}
 :=3\delta_u+\delta_W+3\mathfrak h_{Y/X},}
 \label{eq:V18-detailed-E}\\
 \boxed{
 \delta_W\le4\mathfrak h_{Y/X},
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_{Y/X}\le3\delta_u+7\mathfrak h_{Y/X}.}
 \label{eq:V18-compressed-E}
\end{align}
If $\sigma_\nu>0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \le
 \min\left\{1,
 \frac{\mathcal E_{Y/X}^2}{\sigma_\nu^2}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V18-Schur-upper}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \ge
 \frac{\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2-
       \mathcal E_{Y/X}^2}
      {2\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}}
 \label{eq:V18-oriented-alpha-lower}
\end{equation}
whenever the right side is used as a real oriented lower bound.

If
\begin{equation}
 \delta_{\log W}
 :=\max_\alpha
   \left|\log\frac{W_\alpha^\nu}{W_\alpha^\mu}\right|,
 \label{eq:V18-log-mean-drift}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \delta_u\le2(e^{\delta_{\log W}}-1),
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_{Y/X}
 \le6(e^{\delta_{\log W}}-1)+7\mathfrak h_{Y/X}.}
 \label{eq:V18-log-transport-bound}
\end{equation}
Thus four old/fine loop means, one Hellinger affinity, and a fine-source stock
lower endpoint give a complete sufficient interval for the mixed Schur row.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Using \eqref{eq:V18-balanced-sources},
\[
 F_\nu-F_\mu
 =(u^\nu-u^\mu)^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_M-W^\nu)
 +(u^\mu)^{\mathsf T}(W^\mu-W^\nu).
\]
Equation \eqref{eq:V18-uniform-source-bound} gives
\[
 \|F_\nu-F_\mu\|_{L^2(\nu)}
 \le3\delta_u+\delta_W.
\]
Also
\[
 \|(1-h)F_\mu\|_{L^2(\nu)}
 \le3\|h-1\|_{L^2(\nu)}.
\]
The triangle inequality proves \eqref{eq:V18-detailed-E}.

For each component, $|\mathcal O_\alpha|\le1$ and
\[
 \left|\mu(\mathcal O_\alpha)-\nu(\mathcal O_\alpha)\right|
 =\left|\int\mathcal O_\alpha(h-1)(h+1)\,\dd\nu\right|
 \le\mathfrak h_{Y/X}\|h+1\|_2.
\]
Since $\|h\|_2=\|1\|_2=1$, one has $\|h+1\|_2\le2$.
Taking the Euclidean norm of four components gives
$\delta_W\le4\mathfrak h_{Y/X}$, proving
\eqref{eq:V18-compressed-E}.

The squared distance from $F_\nu$ to the line spanned by $hF_\mu$ is
$\sigma_\nu^2\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}$.  The particular point $hF_\mu$ on
that line gives
\[
 \sigma_\nu^2\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \le\|F_\nu-hF_\mu\|_2^2,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V18-Schur-upper}.  Expanding the same squared distance
gives
\[
 2c_{Y/X}
 =\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2
  -\|F_\nu-hF_\mu\|_2^2,
\]
and proves \eqref{eq:V18-oriented-alpha-lower}.

Finally, let $b^\lambda=D_{W^\lambda}^{-1}\varepsilon_\square$.  The logarithmic
bound implies componentwise
$|b_\alpha^\nu-b_\alpha^\mu|
 \le(e^{\delta_{\log W}}-1)|b_\alpha^\mu|$.
The standard normalization inequality
\[
 \left\|\frac{x}{\|x\|}-\frac{y}{\|y\|}\right\|
 \le\frac{2\|x-y\|}{\|y\|}
\]
then gives the first bound in \eqref{eq:V18-log-transport-bound}; substitution
in \eqref{eq:V18-compressed-E} gives the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Relative-entropy input]
\label{cor:V18-KL-input}
The Hellinger row satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak h_{Y/X}^2
 \le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|\nu).}
 \label{eq:V18-Hellinger-KL}
\end{equation}
Hence the right side of \eqref{eq:V18-log-transport-bound} remains valid with
$\mathfrak h_{Y/X}$ replaced by
$\sqrt{D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|\nu)}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Jensen's inequality applied under $\mu$,
\[
 \log\mathcal A_{Y/X}
 =\log\mathbb E_\mu\sqrt{\frac{\dd\nu}{\dd\mu}}
 \ge-\frac12D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|\nu).
\]
Thus $D_{\rm KL}\ge-2\log\mathcal A_{Y/X}
\ge2(1-\mathcal A_{Y/X})=\mathfrak h_{Y/X}^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal adjacent-cutoff pass]
\label{cor:V18-cofinal-old-fine}
Consider adjacent dyadic physical cards for which
\begin{equation}
 \inf_n\sigma_{\nu_n}^2\ge g_*>0,
 \qquad
 \delta_{\log W,n}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 D_{\rm KL}(\mu_n\|\nu_n)\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:V18-cofinal-assumptions}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y_n/X_n}^{\rm bal}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \alpha_{Y_n/X_n}^{\rm bal}\longrightarrow1.}
 \label{eq:V18-cofinal-alpha}
\end{equation}
The source support remains at the fixed physical rectangle radius.  Thus this
is a positive-range adjacent-cutoff alignment pass.  If, in addition, the
physical incidences compose on one declared common-screen system and
$\sum_n\mathcal E_{Y_n/X_n}<\infty$, then the transported sources are
strongly Cauchy there.  A positive-range \emph{boundary} survivor still
requires the independent radial posterior channel to have a near-unit
positive-range packet.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Under \eqref{eq:V18-cofinal-assumptions}, the upper bound in
\eqref{eq:V18-log-transport-bound} tends to zero.  Apply
\eqref{eq:V18-Schur-upper}.  The norm difference also tends to zero, so
$|\sigma_{\mu_n}-\sigma_{\nu_n}|\to0$; then
\eqref{eq:V18-oriented-alpha-lower} gives the oriented limit.  The physical
support statement is \Cref{lem:V18-path-lift}.  Under the additional
summability and composition hypotheses, the triangle inequality gives
\[
 \|F_m-J_{m\leftarrow n}F_n\|
 \le\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}\mathcal E_{Y_k/X_k}\longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the asserted strong Cauchy statement.  The final qualification is the
already proved independence of cutoff attachment and radial shell
transmission.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The selected response relation does not transport the source direction}
\label{sec:V18-projective-no-go}
% =============================================================================

At every selected root, the balanced coefficient vector satisfies
\[
 u_{11}u_{00}=e^{u_*}u_{10}u_{01}
\]
with sign pattern $(+,+,-,-)$.  This is only one projective equation.

\begin{theorem}[Projective Creutz data do not determine adjacent coefficient transport]
\label{thm:V18-projective-no-go}
Let $\Lambda=e^{u_*}>0$.  For $t>0$, define
\begin{equation}
 v(t):=(\sqrt\Lambda\,t,\sqrt\Lambda/t,-1,-1)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 u(t):=\frac{v(t)}{\|v(t)\|_2}.
 \label{eq:V18-projective-family}
\end{equation}
Then every $u(t)$ has the selected sign pattern and obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 u_{11}(t)u_{00}(t)
 =\Lambda u_{10}(t)u_{01}(t).}
 \label{eq:V18-projective-same-root}
\end{equation}
Nevertheless,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lim_{t\to\infty}
 \|u(t)-u(t^{-1})\|_2=\sqrt2.}
 \label{eq:V18-projective-separation}
\end{equation}
Each direction is compatible with a positive scalar mean vector
$W_\alpha=k/|u_\alpha(t)|$ after choosing $k>0$ sufficiently small.  Hence the
selected response equation and positivity of the four means, by themselves,
do not imply $\delta_u\to0$ across cutoffs.  No claim is made that every such
scalar vector is realized by a Wilson law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Both products in \eqref{eq:V18-projective-same-root} are divided by the same
normalization $\|v(t)\|_2^2$, while the corresponding products of the raw
entries are $\Lambda$ and $1$.  As $t\to\infty$, $u(t)$ tends to the first
coordinate vector and $u(t^{-1})$ tends to the second.  Their distance is
$\sqrt2$.  Finally, with $W_\alpha=k/|u_\alpha|$, the balanced vector
$D_W^{-1}\varepsilon_\square$ is a positive multiple of $u$; a small common
$k$ places all means in $(0,1]$ and preserves the product relation.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact first adjacent-cutoff acquisition]
\label{ass:V18-first-acquisition}
The response root selects each cutoff law but does not align its balanced
source direction with the neighboring cutoff.  The first exact adjacent-
cutoff packet is therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (W^\mu,W^\nu)
 \quad+\quad
 \mathcal A_{Y/X}
 \quad+\quad
 \sigma_\nu^2,}
 \label{eq:V18-minimum-sufficient-packet}
\end{equation}
for the sufficient Hellinger route, or the single direct mixed scalar
$c_{Y/X}$ together with the two diagonal stocks for the exact route.  The
four means are already part of the selected Creutz response.  The genuinely
new sufficient datum is the natural/induced Hellinger affinity.  If the bound
is inconclusive, the exact mixed scalar remains the target; another source
encoding is not introduced.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Revised cofinal decision and the remaining linear branch}
\label{sec:V18-cofinal-decision}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Version V18 noncircular Yang--Mills boundary alternative]
\label{thm:V18-alternative}
For a cofinal dyadic selected sequence, retain the exact physical rectangle
incidence of \Cref{lem:V18-path-lift}.  Then the YM--B decision is ordered as
follows.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T18.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.2em]
\item If $\beta_N=o(N)$, Version~V17 already gives complete source-relative
      extinction at every separating shell.  No old/fine near-unit result can
      turn that radial contraction into a boundary survivor.
\item On a linear-or-faster branch, the one-link method is exhausted by
      \Cref{thm:V18-one-link-optimality}.  Evaluate the adjacent law/direction
      packet \eqref{eq:V18-minimum-sufficient-packet}, or acquire the exact
      scalar \eqref{eq:V18-old-fine-Gram}.
\item If \eqref{eq:V18-cofinal-assumptions} passes, the physical source has a
      positive-range adjacent-cutoff alignment pass.  Run the independent Version~V11
      posterior pair on one predeclared physical shell width.  A strict radial
      loss returns contraction; a near-unit positive-width radial channel
      returns the positive-range boundary survivor.
\item If the old/fine mixed residual is bounded away from zero, return a typed
      cutoff-transport obstruction before invoking radial survival.  If only
      the sufficient Hellinger interval is inconclusive, return
      \(\mathsf{STOP}\) at the exact mixed scalar rather than calling the
      interval an obstruction.
\item A contact-scale survivor remains possible only for a separately loaded
      source family whose physical support radius tends to zero.  The present
      four rectangles have fixed physical radius by
      \eqref{eq:V18-rectangle-lift}.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the remaining linear branch is not a request for a larger local
Peter--Weyl theorem.  It is the conjunction of one actual adjacent-cutoff
law-alignment Read and the already isolated radial posterior Read.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first item is \Cref{thm:V17-sublinear-extinction}.  The second is
\Cref{thm:V18-one-link-optimality,lem:V18-path-lift}.  The third follows from
\Cref{cor:V18-cofinal-old-fine} and the Version~V11 Bayes-reverse identity.
The fourth is the definition of the exact mixed Gram together with the
one-sided nature of \eqref{eq:V18-Schur-upper}.  The fifth is the physical
support statement in \Cref{lem:V18-path-lift}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Spatial cutoff incidence is not the OS semigroup]
\label{fire:V18-not-OS}
The dyadic source incidence compares the same fixed-physical Wilson rectangles
at two ultraviolet cutoffs.  The radial posterior compares nested spatial
Markov blankets at one cutoff.  Neither map is the reflected-time transfer
operator.  A positive-range cutoff thread and a near-unit radial shell channel
therefore remain insufficient for an Osterwalder--Schrader mass unless the
separate reflected-time, full centre-neutral complement, and continuum
transport rows are populated.
\end{firewall}

\section{Exact finite replay, proof ledger, and export}
\label{sec:V18-certificate}
% =============================================================================

\begin{certificate}[Version V18 dyadic law-transport verifier]
\label{cert:V18-verifier}
The accompanying program
\begin{center}
\path{Renewal_YM_Boundary_Sector_V18_dyadic_law_transport_certificate.py}
\end{center}
