\section{Version V19 direction: factor the law row through the physical source record}
\label{sec:V19-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V18 proves that the four selected physical rectangle writers have
exact dyadic incidence.  The fine writer is the ordered two-edge lift of the
coarse writer, so the old/fine source comparison has no path-shape or support
birth.  Its remaining exact scalar is the law-aligned overlap between the
fine balanced source and the transported old balanced source.

The sufficient estimate of Version~V18 controls that overlap by the complete
Hellinger distance between the natural coarse law and the induced blocked
fine law.  That estimate is valid, but it does not identify where a failed
law row lives.  A discrepancy may already be visible in the four physical
Wilson rectangles, or it may remain hidden inside configurations having the
same four-loop record.  These two mechanisms have different physical
meanings and must not be charged as one undifferentiated cutoff defect.

The present continuation moves one arrow upstream.  It factors the canonical
density-square-root incidence through the actual source record
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr S_M
 :=\sigma(\mathbf O_M),
 \qquad
 \mathbf O_M=(\mathcal O_{11,M},\mathcal O_{00,M},
               \mathcal O_{10,M},\mathcal O_{01,M})^{\mathsf T}.}
 \label{eq:V19-source-record}
\end{equation}
The resulting contraction has an exact conditional-Hellinger multiplier.  It
then yields a nested Pythagoras which splits the old/fine Schur residual into
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{hidden conditional-fibre loss}\\
 {}+\;\text{visible source-record line mismatch}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V19-two-stage-slogan}
\end{equation}
The two terms are positive and nonduplicating.  Their simultaneous vanishing
is exactly the old/fine alignment pass.

\begin{firewall}[No replacement of the physical mixed row]
\label{fire:V19-no-mixed-row-replacement}
The decomposition below does not infer an unpopulated Wilson expectation.
For the scalar old/fine verdict, the direct mixed value of Version~V18 remains
target minimal.  The new two-stage card is used when the mixed row is to be
acquired from positive conditional quantities or when a failure must be
attributed to a source-record defect rather than to hidden cutoff fibres.
Separate source-record marginals do not determine the full physical overlap;
an exact counterexample is proved below.

\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The action-level origin of the old/fine Hellinger bridge}
\label{sec:V19-action-midpoint}
% =============================================================================

The source-record factorization below is most useful after the full-law bridge
has itself been placed on the actual Wilson action.  Let $m_N$ and $m_M$ be
normalized product Haar measure on the fine and coarse link cylinders, and
retain the dyadic block map $B=B_{N\to M}$ with $N=2M$.  Since each coarse link
is the ordered product of one disjoint fine-link pair,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{B_*m_N=m_M.}
 \label{eq:V19-Haar-pushforward}
\end{equation}
Choose a regular Haar disintegration
\begin{equation}
 m_N(\dd U)=m_M(\dd W)\,\kappa_W(\dd U),
 \qquad W=B(U).
 \label{eq:V19-Haar-disintegration}
\end{equation}
For the selected fine Wilson action $S_N(U)=\beta_NA_N(U)$, define its exact
blocked conditional partition and effective action by
\begin{equation}
 Q_{N\downarrow M}(W)
 :=\int e^{-S_N(U)}\,\kappa_W(\dd U),
 \qquad
 S_0(W):=-\log Q_{N\downarrow M}(W).
 \label{eq:V19-block-effective-action}
\end{equation}
Let $S_1(W)=\beta_MA_M(W)$ be the natural coarse Wilson action.  Then the
induced law $\nu$ and natural law $\mu$ of Version~V18 are exactly the Gibbs
laws of $S_0$ and $S_1$ with respect to the same $m_M$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact geometric midpoint action and mixed source insertion]
\label{thm:V19-midpoint-action}
Put
\begin{equation}
 S_t=(1-t)S_0+tS_1,
 \qquad
 Z_t=\int e^{-S_t}\,\dd m_M,
 \qquad
 \dd\pi_t=Z_t^{-1}e^{-S_t}\,\dd m_M.
 \label{eq:V19-action-path}
\end{equation}
Thus $\pi_0=\nu$ and $\pi_1=\mu$.  The full-law Hellinger affinity and the exact
balanced old/fine mixed source scalar are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{\rm full}
 =\frac{Z_{1/2}}{\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}},
 \qquad
 c_{Y/X}
 =\mathcal A_{\rm full}
  \mathbb E_{\pi_{1/2}}[F_\nu F_\mu].}
 \label{eq:V19-midpoint-action-card}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_{Y/X}
 =\frac{
  \displaystyle\int F_\nu(W)F_\mu(W)
   e^{-[S_0(W)+S_1(W)]/2}\,m_M(\dd W)}
 {\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}}.}
 \label{eq:V19-midpoint-unnormalized}
\end{equation}
Hence one positive midpoint action cylinder and one source-product insertion
populate the same scalar as the direct common-cylinder Gram of Version~V18.
The affinity and insertion are factors of one mixed entry and are not charged
as two independent defects.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V19-Haar-pushforward} follows because products of
independent Haar variables are Haar and the coarse-link pairs are disjoint.
Disintegration gives
\[
 \int f(BU)e^{-S_N(U)}\,m_N(\dd U)
 =\int f(W)Q_{N\downarrow M}(W)\,m_M(\dd W)
\]
for every bounded coarse writer $f$, proving that $S_0$ generates the blocked
fine law.  The geometric mean of the two endpoint densities is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{\dd\nu}{\dd m_M}\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd m_M}}
 =\frac{e^{-(S_0+S_1)/2}}{\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}}.
\]
Integrating once, and then after multiplication by $F_\nu F_\mu$, proves
\eqref{eq:V19-midpoint-action-card}--\eqref{eq:V19-midpoint-unnormalized}.
\end{proof}

Put $\Delta=S_1-S_0$ and $\Phi(t)=\log Z_t$.

\begin{theorem}[Integrated action-curvature identity]
\label{thm:V19-action-curvature}
The bridge path satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Phi'(t)=-\mathbb E_{\pi_t}\Delta,
 \qquad
 \Phi''(t)=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\Delta)\ge0.}
 \label{eq:V19-action-derivatives}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 -2\log\mathcal A_{\rm full}
 =\int_0^1\min\{t,1-t\}
   \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\Delta)\,\dd t.}
 \label{eq:V19-action-curvature}
\end{equation}
The symmetric endpoint relative entropy is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm KL}(\nu\|\mu)+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|\nu)
 =\int_0^1\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\Delta)\,\dd t.}
 \label{eq:V19-Jeffreys-curvature}
\end{equation}
The weighted integral in \eqref{eq:V19-action-curvature} vanishes exactly when
$S_1-S_0$ is constant $m_M$-almost everywhere, equivalently when
$\mu=\nu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiation under the compact finite-dimensional integral gives
\eqref{eq:V19-action-derivatives}.  Taylor's formula about $t=1/2$ gives
\[
 \Phi(0)+\Phi(1)-2\Phi(1/2)
 =\int_0^{1/2}t\Phi''(t)\,\dd t
  +\int_{1/2}^1(1-t)\Phi''(t)\,\dd t.
\]
The left side is $-2\log\mathcal A_{\rm full}$ by
\eqref{eq:V19-midpoint-action-card}.  For the relative entropies, their sum is
$\mathbb E_{\pi_0}\Delta-\mathbb E_{\pi_1}\Delta$, while
$\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\mathbb E_{\pi_t}\Delta
=-\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\Delta)$.  This proves both identities.  Full
support of every $\pi_t$ gives the equality statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Action-path sufficient law-alignment row]
\label{cor:V19-action-path-pass}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal V_{Y/X}^{\rm act}
 :=\int_0^1\min\{t,1-t\}
   \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(S_1-S_0)\,\dd t.
 \label{eq:V19-action-debit}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak h_{\rm full}^2
 =2\left(1-e^{-\mathcal V_{Y/X}^{\rm act}/2}\right).}
 \label{eq:V19-action-Hellinger}
\end{equation}
In particular, the Version~V18 sufficient old/fine interval becomes
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \le\min\left\{1,
 \frac{\left[
 6(e^{\delta_{\log W}}-1)
 +7\sqrt{2(1-e^{-\mathcal V_{Y/X}^{\rm act}/2})}
 \right]^2}{\sigma_\nu^2}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V19-action-Schur-bound}
\end{equation}
Thus
$\mathcal V_{Y/X}^{\rm act}\to0$,
$\delta_{\log W}\to0$, and
$\inf\sigma_\nu^2>0$ imply adjacent-cutoff source alignment.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the Hellinger convention of Version~V18 together with
\eqref{eq:V19-action-curvature}.  Substitute it into
\eqref{eq:V18-log-transport-bound} and \eqref{eq:V18-Schur-upper}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Action gauge and scope]
\label{ass:V19-action-gauge}
Adding independent constants to $S_0$ and $S_1$ changes the three partition
functions by cancelling scalar factors and leaves every $\pi_t$, affinity,
mixed source scalar, and variance in this section unchanged.  This is the
correct gauge for the normalized cutoff source angle.  It also proves that
the present action path does not populate YM--A's separate unnormalized
partition-curvature germ.  No locality or finite-range property of
$S_0=S_{N\downarrow M}^{\rm eff}$ is asserted.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The conditional square-root source router}
\label{sec:V19-source-router}
% =============================================================================

Retain the two equivalent finite Gibbs laws of Version~V18,
\begin{equation}
 \mu=\mu_{M,\beta_M}^{\rm nat},
 \qquad
 \nu=(B_{N\to M})_*\mu_{N,\beta_N}^{\rm nat},
 \qquad
 h=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}}.
 \label{eq:V19-mu-nu-h}
\end{equation}
Let $P_{\mathscr S}$ denote conditional expectation in $L^2(\nu)$ onto
$L^2(\mathscr S_M,\nu)$.  Denote the source-record pushforwards by
\begin{equation}
 \mu_{\mathscr S}:=(\mathbf O_M)_*\mu,
 \qquad
 \nu_{\mathscr S}:=(\mathbf O_M)_*\nu.
 \label{eq:V19-source-pushforwards}
\end{equation}
Since the two full laws have strictly positive densities, the two pushforwards
are equivalent.  Define the source-record likelihood root, projected full
likelihood root, and conditional-fibre survival by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 h_{\mathscr S}
 :=\left(\mathbb E_\nu[h^2\mid\mathscr S_M]\right)^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathscr S}
 :=\mathbb E_\nu[h\mid\mathscr S_M],
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathscr S}
 :=\frac{\kappa_{\mathscr S}}{h_{\mathscr S}}.}
 \label{eq:V19-h-kappa-rho}
\end{equation}
All three are strictly positive almost everywhere.

\begin{theorem}[Exact conditional-Hellinger source router]
\label{thm:V19-source-router}
The source-record Radon--Nikodym derivative and its square root are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}}
 =\mathbb E_\nu[h^2\mid\mathscr S_M]
 =h_{\mathscr S}^2.}
 \label{eq:V19-source-RN}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{0<\rho_{\mathscr S}\le1.}
 \label{eq:V19-rho-contraction}
\end{equation}
For every real $\mathscr S_M$-measurable
$f\in L^2(\mu)$, the canonical full-law incidence followed by source-record
projection is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal K_{\mathscr S}f
 :=P_{\mathscr S}(hf)
 =\kappa_{\mathscr S}f
 =\rho_{\mathscr S}h_{\mathscr S}f.}
 \label{eq:V19-router-factorization}
\end{equation}
Thus
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal K_{\mathscr S}
 =M_{\rho_{\mathscr S}}U_{h_{\mathscr S}}:
 L^2(\mu_{\mathscr S})\longrightarrow L^2(\nu_{\mathscr S}),}
 \label{eq:V19-router-operator}
\end{equation}
where $U_{h_{\mathscr S}}f=h_{\mathscr S}f$ is unitary and
$M_{\rho_{\mathscr S}}$ is a positive contraction.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathcal K_{\mathscr S}f\|_{L^2(\nu)}
 \le\|f\|_{L^2(\mu)}.}
 \label{eq:V19-router-contraction}
\end{equation}

For regular conditional laws $\mu_s,\nu_s$ over the source record,
$\rho_{\mathscr S}$ is the conditional Hellinger affinity:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \rho_{\mathscr S}(s)
 =\int\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu_s}{\dd\nu_s}}\,\dd\nu_s
 =\int\sqrt{\dd\mu_s\,\dd\nu_s}.}
 \label{eq:V19-conditional-affinity}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every bounded $\mathscr S_M$-measurable $\varphi$,
\[
 \int\varphi\,\mathbb E_\nu[h^2\mid\mathscr S_M] \,\dd\nu
 =\int\varphi h^2\,\dd\nu
 =\int\varphi\,\dd\mu.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:V19-source-RN}.  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz gives
$\kappa_{\mathscr S}^2\le h_{\mathscr S}^2$, proving
\eqref{eq:V19-rho-contraction}.  If $f$ is source-record measurable, it may be
pulled through conditional expectation, which gives
\eqref{eq:V19-router-factorization}.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V19-source-RN} makes $U_{h_{\mathscr S}}$ an isometry, and
\eqref{eq:V19-rho-contraction} makes multiplication by
$\rho_{\mathscr S}$ contractive.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V19-router-operator}--\eqref{eq:V19-router-contraction}.

The configuration spaces are compact standard Borel spaces, so regular
conditional laws exist.  On a source fibre, the full density ratio factors as
\[
 \frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}
 =\frac{\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}}(s)
  \frac{\dd\mu_s}{\dd\nu_s}.
\]
Taking square roots and integrating with respect to $\nu_s$ gives
\eqref{eq:V19-conditional-affinity}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Meaning of the router]
\label{ass:V19-router-meaning}
The factor $h_{\mathscr S}$ aligns the two laws on the four-loop source
record.  The multiplier $\rho_{\mathscr S}$ records the fidelity of the
remaining conditional link configurations after that same record is fixed.
The latter is one exactly defined cutoff-incidence row.  It is not a new
source, and it is not determined by the four-loop marginal laws alone.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact Hellinger chain and source-record sufficiency}
\label{sec:V19-Hellinger-chain}
% =============================================================================

Define the full and source-record affinities by
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal A_{\rm full}:=\mathbb E_\nu h,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{\mathscr S}:=\mathbb E_{\nu_{\mathscr S}}h_{\mathscr S},
 \label{eq:V19-two-affinities}
\end{equation}
and the corresponding squared Hellinger distances by
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak h_{\rm full}^2:=2(1-\mathcal A_{\rm full}),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak h_{\mathscr S}^2:=2(1-\mathcal A_{\mathscr S}).
 \label{eq:V19-two-Hellingers}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Visible/hidden Hellinger chain]
\label{thm:V19-Hellinger-chain}
One has the exact decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak h_{\rm full}^2
 =\mathfrak h_{\mathscr S}^2
 +2\,\mathbb E_{\nu_{\mathscr S}}
   \left[h_{\mathscr S}(1-\rho_{\mathscr S})\right].}
 \label{eq:V19-Hellinger-chain}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\le\mathfrak h_{\mathscr S}
 \le\mathfrak h_{\rm full}.}
 \label{eq:V19-Hellinger-data-processing}
\end{equation}
The square-root likelihood fibre residual is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\rm fib}^{0}
 :=\|h-\kappa_{\mathscr S}\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2
 =1-\mathbb E_{\mu_{\mathscr S}}\rho_{\mathscr S}^2.}
 \label{eq:V19-null-fibre-residual}
\end{equation}
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item $\mathbb C_{\rm fib}^{0}=0$;
\item $h$ is $\mathscr S_M$-measurable;
\item $\rho_{\mathscr S}=1$ almost everywhere;
\item $\mu_s=\nu_s$ for almost every source record $s$.
\end{enumerate}
Thus $\mathbb C_{\rm fib}^{0}$ is the exact residual for sufficiency of the
four-loop record with respect to the old/fine law change.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:V19-router-factorization},
$\mathbb E_\nu h=\mathbb E_{\nu_{\mathscr S}}
(\rho_{\mathscr S}h_{\mathscr S})$.  Subtracting this identity from
$\mathcal A_{\mathscr S}$ proves \eqref{eq:V19-Hellinger-chain}; positivity of
the second term proves \eqref{eq:V19-Hellinger-data-processing}.

Conditional-expectation Pythagoras and $\|h\|_2^2=1$ give
\[
 \mathbb C_{\rm fib}^{0}
 =1-\|\kappa_{\mathscr S}\|_2^2.
\]
Using $\kappa_{\mathscr S}=\rho_{\mathscr S}h_{\mathscr S}$ and
$h_{\mathscr S}^2\,\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}=\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}$ proves
\eqref{eq:V19-null-fibre-residual}.  Equality in conditional
Cauchy--Schwarz holds exactly when $h$ is constant on almost every source
fibre.  By \eqref{eq:V19-conditional-affinity}, this is equivalent to
conditional Hellinger affinity one, hence to equality of the two conditional
probability laws.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source-weighted fibre loss]
\label{cor:V19-source-weighted-fibre}
For every bounded source-record writer $f$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb D_{\rm fib}(f)
 &:=\|hf-\mathcal K_{\mathscr S}f\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2
 \label{eq:V19-Dfib-def}\\
 &=\int f(s)^2\bigl(1-\rho_{\mathscr S}(s)^2\bigr)
        \,\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}(s)
 \label{eq:V19-Dfib-rho}\\
 &\le\|f\|_\infty^2\mathbb C_{\rm fib}^{0}.
 \label{eq:V19-Dfib-bound}
\end{align}
In particular, for the balanced old Creutz source of Version~V18,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb D_{\rm fib}(F_\mu)
 \le9\mathbb C_{\rm fib}^{0}.}
 \label{eq:V19-Creutz-fibre-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Since $f$ is source-record measurable,
\[
 hf-\mathcal K_{\mathscr S}f
 =f(h-\kappa_{\mathscr S}).
\]
The conditional variance of $h$ is
$h_{\mathscr S}^2-\kappa_{\mathscr S}^2
=h_{\mathscr S}^2(1-\rho_{\mathscr S}^2)$.
Integrating proves \eqref{eq:V19-Dfib-rho}; the supremum bound gives
\eqref{eq:V19-Dfib-bound}.  Version~V18 proves
$\|F_\mu\|_\infty\le3$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact two-stage Pythagoras for the old/fine source Gram}
\label{sec:V19-two-stage-Pythagoras}
% =============================================================================

Set
\begin{equation}
 X:=hF_\mu,
 \qquad
 M:=P_{\mathscr S}X=\mathcal K_{\mathscr S}F_\mu,
 \qquad
 G:=F_\nu.
 \label{eq:V19-XMG}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \|X\|_2^2=\sigma_\mu^2,
 \qquad
 \|G\|_2^2=\sigma_\nu^2,
 \qquad
 \langle G,X\rangle=\langle G,M\rangle=c_{Y/X}.
 \label{eq:V19-XMG-Gram}
\end{equation}
Let $P_G$ be the orthogonal projection onto the line spanned by $G$, with
$P_G=0$ when $G=0$.

\begin{theorem}[Nonduplicating fibre/visible decomposition]
\label{thm:V19-two-stage-Pythagoras}
Assume $\sigma_\mu>0$ and $\sigma_\nu>0$.  Define
\begin{align}
 \mathbb D_{\rm fib}
 &:=\|(I-P_{\mathscr S})X\|_2^2
 =\sigma_\mu^2-\|M\|_2^2,
 \label{eq:V19-Dfib}\\
 \mathbb D_{\rm vis}
 &:=\|(P_{\mathscr S}-P_G)X\|_2^2
 =\|M\|_2^2-\frac{|c_{Y/X}|^2}{\sigma_\nu^2}.
 \label{eq:V19-Dvis}
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sigma_\mu^2\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =\mathbb D_{\rm fib}+\mathbb D_{\rm vis}.}
 \label{eq:V19-additive-residual}
\end{equation}
Both terms are nonnegative.  If $\|M\|_2>0$, put
\begin{equation}
 r_{\rm fib}:=\frac{\mathbb D_{\rm fib}}{\sigma_\mu^2},
 \qquad
 r_{\rm vis}:=\frac{\mathbb D_{\rm vis}}{\|M\|_2^2}.
 \label{eq:V19-normalized-components}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =r_{\rm fib}+(1-r_{\rm fib})r_{\rm vis}.}
 \label{eq:V19-convex-residual}
\end{equation}
When $M=0$, one has $r_{\rm fib}=1$ and
$\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=1$.

The residual vanishes exactly when both of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item the transported old source $hF_\mu$ is source-record measurable;
\item its source-record descendant $M$ lies in the line spanned by the fine
      source $F_\nu$.
\end{enumerate}
A signed alignment pass additionally requires the oriented cross coefficient
to be positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The fine source $G$ is $\mathscr S_M$-measurable, so
$\operatorname{Ran}P_G\subseteq\operatorname{Ran}P_{\mathscr S}$ and
\[
 I-P_G=(I-P_{\mathscr S})+(P_{\mathscr S}-P_G)
\]
is an orthogonal sum.  Therefore
\[
 \|(I-P_G)X\|_2^2
 =\|(I-P_{\mathscr S})X\|_2^2
  +\|(P_{\mathscr S}-P_G)X\|_2^2.
\]
The left side is
\[
 \sigma_\mu^2-
 \frac{|\langle G,X\rangle|^2}{\sigma_\nu^2}
 =\sigma_\mu^2\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal},
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V19-additive-residual}.  Dividing by
$\sigma_\mu^2$ and using
$\|M\|_2^2/\sigma_\mu^2=1-r_{\rm fib}$ gives
\eqref{eq:V19-convex-residual}.  The equality classification follows from
vanishing of the two orthogonal summands.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal attribution of an old/fine failure]
\label{cor:V19-cofinal-attribution}
Suppose the old and fine source stocks have positive lower bounds along a
cofinal dyadic family.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 r_{\rm fib}\longrightarrow0
 \ \text{and}\ 
 r_{\rm vis}\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:V19-cofinal-equivalence}
\end{equation}
Consequently a nonvanishing adjacent-cutoff residual has, after subsequence
extraction, one of two exact types:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c}
 \text{source-weighted conditional-fibre transport obstruction},\\[0.2em]
 \text{visible four-loop source-direction obstruction}.
 \end{array}}
 \label{eq:V19-two-obstructions}
\end{equation}
The second type is read only after the first component has been accounted for;
the two are not summed as independent full-strength defects.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication follows from nonnegativity in
\eqref{eq:V19-convex-residual}: first $r_{\rm fib}\le\mathbb R$ tends to zero,
then $1-r_{\rm fib}\to1$ forces $r_{\rm vis}\to0$.  The reverse implication is
immediate from the same identity.  Subsequence extraction gives the typed
alternative.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Positive conditional acquisition and an outward interval compiler}
\label{sec:V19-positive-card}
% =============================================================================

The decomposition can be acquired without first assigning a sign to the mixed
coefficient.  Draw a source record from $\nu_{\mathscr S}$ and, conditionally
on it, draw two independent full configurations from the corresponding
$\nu$-fibre.  Put
\begin{equation}
 X_i=h(\omega_i)F_\mu(\mathbf O_M(\omega_i)),
 \qquad i=1,2.
 \label{eq:V19-fibre-leaves}
\end{equation}
Separately, let $(G_1,M_1)$ and $(G_2,M_2)$ be independent copies of
$(G,M)$ under $\nu_{\mathscr S}$, and define the positive source-record area
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak A_{\rm vis}
 :=\mathbb E\left[(G_1M_2-G_2M_1)^2\right].
 \label{eq:V19-visible-area}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact positive four-scalar old/fine card]
\label{thm:V19-positive-card}
The two residual numerators are reconstructed by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb D_{\rm fib}
 =\frac12\mathbb E[(X_1-X_2)^2],}
 \label{eq:V19-Dfib-replica}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb D_{\rm vis}
 =\frac{\mathfrak A_{\rm vis}}{2\sigma_\nu^2}.}
 \label{eq:V19-Dvis-area}
\end{equation}
Therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =\frac{\mathbb D_{\rm fib}}{\sigma_\mu^2}
 +\frac{\mathfrak A_{\rm vis}}
       {2\sigma_\mu^2\sigma_\nu^2}.}
 \label{eq:V19-positive-residual-card}
\end{equation}
The exact domain constraints are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\le\mathbb D_{\rm fib}\le\sigma_\mu^2,
 \qquad
 0\le\mathfrak A_{\rm vis}
 \le2\sigma_\nu^2(\sigma_\mu^2-\mathbb D_{\rm fib}).}
 \label{eq:V19-positive-domain}
\end{equation}
The sign of $c_{Y/X}$ is needed only when oriented line transport, rather than
the unsigned Schur residual, is the target.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional on $\mathscr S_M$, the two leaves are independent with common
mean $M$, so
\[
 \frac12\mathbb E[(X_1-X_2)^2\mid\mathscr S_M]
 =\operatorname{Var}_\nu(X\mid\mathscr S_M).
\]
Averaging gives \eqref{eq:V19-Dfib-replica}.  Independence of the two
source-record copies gives
\[
 \mathfrak A_{\rm vis}
 =2\left(\sigma_\nu^2\|M\|_2^2-|c_{Y/X}|^2\right),
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V19-Dvis-area}.  Substitution in
\eqref{eq:V19-additive-residual} proves
\eqref{eq:V19-positive-residual-card}.  The domain constraints are ordinary
projection Pythagoras and Cauchy--Schwarz.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Denominator-safe interval compiler]
\label{cor:V19-interval-compiler}
Suppose validated outward intervals satisfy
\[
 \underline s_\mu\le\sigma_\mu^2\le\overline s_\mu,
 \qquad
 \underline s_\nu\le\sigma_\nu^2\le\overline s_\nu,
\]
\[
 \underline d\le\mathbb D_{\rm fib}\le\overline d,
 \qquad
 \underline a\le\mathfrak A_{\rm vis}\le\overline a,
\]
with $\underline s_\mu,\underline s_\nu>0$ and all residual endpoints
nonnegative.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{\underline d}{\overline s_\mu}
 +\frac{\underline a}{2\overline s_\mu\overline s_\nu}
 \le\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \le
 \min\left\{1,
 \frac{\overline d}{\underline s_\mu}
 +\frac{\overline a}{2\underline s_\mu\underline s_\nu}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V19-residual-interval}
\end{equation}
A packet incompatible with \eqref{eq:V19-positive-domain} is an input error,
not a Yang--Mills obstruction.  An interval containing both zero and a
positive value is unresolved.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every term in \eqref{eq:V19-positive-residual-card} is monotone increasing in
its nonnegative numerator and decreasing in its positive denominators.  The
stated outward substitutions prove the interval.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Target-minimal versus attribution-complete acquisition]
\label{ass:V19-target-minimal}
For one scalar verdict, the direct packet
\[
 \sigma_\mu^2,\quad\sigma_\nu^2,\quad c_{Y/X}
\]
remains irreducible.  The positive packet
\[
 \sigma_\mu^2,\quad\sigma_\nu^2,
 \quad\mathbb D_{\rm fib},\quad\mathfrak A_{\rm vis}
\]
is attribution complete: it proves the same unsigned residual and states
whether the loss occurs before or after projection to the physical source
record.  No complete link-state reconstruction is required by either target.
\end{assessment}

\section{Sharp nonidentifiability from source-record marginals}
\label{sec:V19-countermodels}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Counterexample: the complete source-record law does not determine the full mixed Gram]
\label{cth:V19-source-marginal-no-full-Gram}
There are two finite old/fine law pairs with:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item identical old and fine source-record marginals;
\item identical source functions and diagonal source stocks;
\item different law-aligned mixed coefficients and different Schur residuals.
\end{enumerate}
Hence even the complete probability laws of the four source writers, taken
separately at the two cutoffs, cannot replace the conditional-fibre incidence
or the direct mixed Read.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let the source record be $T\in\{-1,1\}$ and let $Z\in\{0,1\}$ be a hidden
fibre coordinate.  Take $\nu$ uniform on the four pairs $(T,Z)$ and use the
same source at both cutoffs,
\[
 f(T)=g(T)=T.
\]
For the first old law take $\mu_0=\nu$.  Then
\[
 \sigma_{\mu_0}^2=\sigma_\nu^2=1,
 \qquad c_0=1,
 \qquad\mathbb R_0=0.
\]
For the second old law put, for each $T$,
\[
 \mu_1(T,0)=\frac38,
 \qquad
 \mu_1(T,1)=\frac18.
\]
The $T$-marginal remains uniform, and both diagonal source stocks remain one.
The conditional-fibre affinity is the constant
\begin{equation}
 a=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}.
 \label{eq:V19-counter-a}
\end{equation}
Therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_1=a,
 \qquad
 \mathbb D_{{\rm fib},1}
 =\mathbb R_1
 =1-a^2
 =\frac{2-\sqrt3}{4}>0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb D_{{\rm vis},1}=0.}
 \label{eq:V19-counter-hidden}
\end{equation}
All source-record statistics are identical in the two cards, while their full
law-aligned source Grams differ.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The two failure types are independent]
\label{prop:V19-independent-types}
There is also a finite card with $h=1$, hence
$\mathbb D_{\rm fib}=0$, but with positive visible mismatch.  Take four
uniform source records and
\[
 f=(1,1,-1,-1),
 \qquad
 g=(1,0,-1,0).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sigma_\mu^2=1,
 \qquad
 \sigma_\nu^2=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathbb D_{\rm fib}=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb D_{\rm vis}=\mathbb R=\frac12.}
 \label{eq:V19-counter-visible}
\end{equation}
Thus hidden fibre loss and visible source-direction loss cannot be inferred
from one another.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The two laws are equal, so $h=\rho_{\mathscr S}=1$.  Direct averaging gives
$\langle f,g\rangle=1/2$ and the displayed norms.  Substitution in
\eqref{eq:V19-Dvis} gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Source quotient versus physical cutoff incidence]
\label{fire:V19-source-quotient-scope}
Replacing the full law incidence by the source-record pushforward incidence is
valid exactly on the branch $\rho_{\mathscr S}=1$.  Outside that branch it
deletes the positive fibre loss in \eqref{eq:V19-additive-residual}.  A
four-loop histogram, separate covariance matrices, or agreement of all
source-record moments therefore does not prove physical adjacent-cutoff
alignment.
\end{firewall}

\section{Application to the dyadic Wilson source and the revised decision order}
\label{sec:V19-YM-application}
% =============================================================================

For the literal dyadic pair, the raw rectangle identity of Version~V18 makes
$\mathscr S_M$ a canonical common bounded record carrying both balanced
source writers once the four mean vectors have been frozen.  The exact old/fine
source channel is consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 L^2(\mu_{\mathscr S})
 \xrightarrow{\ U_{h_{\mathscr S}}\ }
 L^2(\nu_{\mathscr S})
 \xrightarrow{\ M_{\rho_{\mathscr S}}\ }
 L^2(\nu_{\mathscr S})
 \xrightarrow{\ \text{projection onto }F_\nu\ }
 \operatorname{Span}\{F_\nu\}.}
 \label{eq:V19-Wilson-three-arrow}
\end{equation}
The first arrow is an isometric change of source-record law.  The second is
the hidden conditional-fibre survival.  The third is visible source-direction
alignment.  Only their complete product is the physical old/fine coefficient.

\begin{theorem}[Version V19 adjacent-cutoff alternative]
\label{thm:V19-adjacent-alternative}
Retain the exact dyadic writer incidence and positive old/fine source stocks.
For every adjacent selected-root pair, exactly one of the following theorem
statuses is returned.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V19.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5em]
\item \textbf{Alignment pass.}  The direct mixed Gram is positive semidefinite,
      its oriented coefficient is positive, and both normalized losses in
      \eqref{eq:V19-convex-residual} have certified upper endpoints tending to
      zero.
\item \textbf{Conditional-fibre obstruction.}  The source-weighted fibre loss
      has a positive lower endpoint.  The blocked fine and natural coarse laws
      retain physically different link information after the same four-loop
      source record is fixed.
\item \textbf{Visible source-direction obstruction.}  The fibre loss vanishes
      within the certified interval, but the visible area
      \eqref{eq:V19-visible-area} has a positive normalized lower endpoint.
\item \textbf{Unresolved.}  The positive intervals overlap zero and a positive
      residual, or the direct mixed scalar has not been acquired.
\item \textbf{Error.}  The submitted densities, source-record incidence,
      support, or positive-domain identities are inconsistent.
\end{enumerate}
On the passing cofinal branch, the remaining YM--B acquisition is precisely
the independent Bayes-reverse radial source loss of Version~V11 on one
predeclared positive physical shell width.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The alternatives are the finite spectral statuses of the exact positive
identity \eqref{eq:V19-positive-residual-card} together with the oriented sign
of the direct mixed coefficient.  They are exhaustive and mutually exclusive
once interval overlap is assigned to the unresolved status.  The final
statement is the programme order already isolated in Versions~V11 and V18:
adjacent-cutoff source transport and outward radial source retention are
independent physical channels.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal handoff]
\label{cor:V19-cofinal-handoff}
Suppose the adjacent-cutoff alignment pass holds with the already required
stock floors and summable common-screen vector defects.  Then the canonically
balanced physical source has one cofinal old/fine line.  On that line:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item a uniform positive-width Bayes-reverse loss gives the contraction branch;
\item a near-unit radial channel at shrinking physical width gives only the
      contact-scale branch;
\item a near-unit radial channel at physical widths with positive lower limit
      gives the positive-range source survivor.
\end{enumerate}
A failure of the adjacent-cutoff pass is exported with the conditional-fibre
or visible-direction type and is not renamed as radial attenuation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The alignment hypotheses transport the one-dimensional source line through the
dyadic cutoff system.  The three radial alternatives are the inherited
physical-radius trichotomy applied to the transported line.  The final
qualification follows because \eqref{eq:V19-additive-residual} is an
adjacent-cutoff law/source identity, whereas the Version~V11 loss is a
Bayes-reverse outward-shell identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[No temporal or mass-gap promotion]
\label{fire:V19-no-mass}
The record $\mathscr S_M$ is a spatial four-loop source record, and
$\rho_{\mathscr S}$ is a conditional fidelity between two adjacent-cutoff
laws.  Neither is the Osterwalder--Schrader semigroup.  A passing old/fine
source line and a radial positive-range survivor remain source-relative
spatial statements.  They do not prove a vacuum-sector transfer gap or a
continuum Yang--Mills mass.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Version V19 integrated conclusion]
\label{thm:V19-integrated}
Versions~V1--V18 are retained.  Version~V19 additionally proves:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(I\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item the induced fine law is generated by the exact blocked conditional free
      energy, and the old/fine mixed scalar is one geometric-midpoint action
      insertion;
\item the full Hellinger debit is the triangular integral of the blocked-action
      mismatch variance;
\item the exact dyadic law incidence factors through the physical four-loop
      record as a source-record likelihood isometry followed by a conditional
      Hellinger contraction;
\item full Hellinger loss splits into source-record mismatch and hidden
      conditional-fibre mismatch;
\item the physical old/fine source Schur residual has the exact nonduplicating
      Pythagoras \eqref{eq:V19-additive-residual};
\item a positive four-scalar packet reconstructs that residual and an outward
      interval compiler has explicit denominator checks;
\item source-record marginals and diagonal stocks do not determine the full
      mixed Gram;
\item the adjacent-cutoff failure is now typed as conditional-fibre or visible
      source-direction obstruction before the independent radial channel is
      read.
\end{enumerate}
No item assigns the missing Wilson values on a selected dyadic pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Items~\textup{(I1)--(I2)} are
\Cref{thm:V19-midpoint-action,thm:V19-action-curvature}.  Items~
\textup{(I3)--(I4)} are
\Cref{thm:V19-source-router,thm:V19-Hellinger-chain}.  Items~
\textup{(I5)--(I6)} are
\Cref{thm:V19-two-stage-Pythagoras,thm:V19-positive-card,cor:V19-interval-compiler}.
Item~\textup{(I7)} is \Cref{cth:V19-source-marginal-no-full-Gram}; item~
\textup{(I8)} is
\Cref{cor:V19-cofinal-attribution,thm:V19-adjacent-alternative}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V20 direction: the old/fine source line must be oriented}
\label{sec:V20-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V19 factors the exact adjacent-cutoff source Gram into hidden
conditional-fibre loss and visible source-record line loss.  Its scalar Schur
residual is
\[
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=1-|\alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}|^2.
\]
That number is the correct \emph{unoriented} principal-line defect, but it does
not distinguish the two equality cases
\[
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=+1
 \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=-1.
\]
The distinction is immaterial for a one-cutoff variance ratio, but it is
essential when the source is transported cofinally and exported to the
signed reduced-fibre card of YM--A.  The Creutz coefficient convention
$(1,1,-1,-1)$ has already been frozen, so an adjacent sign reversal cannot be
removed by silently changing the source section at one cutoff.

The present continuation therefore moves one arrow upstream of the unsigned
Schur short.  It identifies the canonical signed overlap measure carried by
the two normalized source amplitudes.  Its Jordan positive and negative
parts give two nonnegative midpoint-action channels.  They determine both
the amplitude mismatch and the source orientation, and they show that
complete full-law Hellinger alignment is sufficient but not necessary for
the actual source target.

\begin{firewall}[No new law or radial estimator]
\label{fire:V20-no-new-estimator}
The results below do not replace the unpopulated selected-root Wilson
integral by an abstract value.  They correct the target of that integral:
for a cofinal signed source, the required old/fine output is the oriented
coefficient $\alpha$, not only $1-|\alpha|^2$.  The positive Jordan channels
are an exact decomposition of the same midpoint source insertion already
identified in Version~V19.  The independent Bayes-reverse radial loss of
Version~V11 is not recomputed.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Canonical source-energy measures and the signed overlap measure}
\label{sec:V20-source-energy}
% =============================================================================

Retain the natural coarse law $\mu$, the induced blocked fine law $\nu$, and
\[
 h=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}}.
\]
Let $F_\mu\in L_0^2(\mu;\R)$ and
$F_\nu\in L_0^2(\nu;\R)$ be the two balanced physical Creutz writers, and put
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_\mu^2:=\|F_\mu\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2,
 \qquad
 \sigma_\nu^2:=\|F_\nu\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2.
 \label{eq:V20-source-stocks}
\end{equation}
Throughout this section assume $\sigma_\mu\sigma_\nu>0$.  In the common real
Hilbert space $L^2(\nu)$ define the unit source amplitudes
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \psi_\nu:=\frac{F_\nu}{\sigma_\nu},
 \qquad
 \psi_\mu:=\frac{hF_\mu}{\sigma_\mu}.}
 \label{eq:V20-unit-amplitudes}
\end{equation}
Their oriented overlap is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha:=\langle\psi_\nu,\psi_\mu\rangle_{L^2(\nu)}
 =\frac{c_{Y/X}}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}\in[-1,1].}
 \label{eq:V20-oriented-alpha}
\end{equation}

\begin{definition}[Source-energy probability laws and signed overlap]
\label{def:V20-source-energy-laws}
Define two probability measures on the common cylinder by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dd\rho_\nu:=\psi_\nu^2\,\dd\nu
 =\frac{F_\nu^2}{\sigma_\nu^2}\,\dd\nu,
 \qquad
 \dd\rho_\mu:=\psi_\mu^2\,\dd\nu
 =\frac{F_\mu^2}{\sigma_\mu^2}\,\dd\mu.}
 \label{eq:V20-energy-laws}
\end{equation}
The signed source-overlap measure is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dd\zeta:=\psi_\nu\psi_\mu\,\dd\nu
 =\frac{F_\nu F_\mu}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}
   \sqrt{\dd\nu\,\dd\mu}.}
 \label{eq:V20-signed-overlap-measure}
\end{equation}
Let $\zeta=\zeta^+-\zeta^-$ be its Hahn--Jordan decomposition and put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_+:=\zeta^+(\Omega),
 \qquad
 a_-:=\zeta^-(\Omega),
 \qquad
 A_E:=a_++a_-.}
 \label{eq:V20-Jordan-masses}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-energy polar decomposition]
\label{thm:V20-source-energy-polar}
The total variation of the signed source overlap is the Hellinger affinity of
the source-energy laws:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_E=\|\zeta\|_{\rm TV}
 =\int\sqrt{\dd\rho_\nu\,\dd\rho_\mu}
 =\mathbb E_\nu|\psi_\nu\psi_\mu|
 \in[0,1].}
 \label{eq:V20-energy-affinity}
\end{equation}
The oriented coefficient is the Jordan imbalance
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\alpha=a_+-a_-.}
 \label{eq:V20-alpha-Jordan}
\end{equation}
If $A_E>0$, let $\omega_E$ be the normalized overlap law
\begin{equation}
 \dd\omega_E
 :=A_E^{-1}\sqrt{\dd\rho_\nu\,\dd\rho_\mu}
 \label{eq:V20-overlap-law}
\end{equation}
and let
\begin{equation}
 p_-:=\omega_E(F_\nu F_\mu<0).
 \label{eq:V20-negative-overlap-prob}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_-=A_Ep_-,
 \qquad
 a_+=A_E(1-p_-),
 \qquad
 \alpha=A_E(1-2p_-).}
 \label{eq:V20-alpha-polar}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The measures in \eqref{eq:V20-energy-laws} have total mass one because the
two source amplitudes are unit vectors.  With $\nu$ as a dominating measure,
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{\dd\rho_\nu}{\dd\nu}
             \frac{\dd\rho_\mu}{\dd\nu}}
 =|\psi_\nu\psi_\mu|.
\]
Integration gives \eqref{eq:V20-energy-affinity}; Cauchy--Schwarz gives the
upper bound one.  The positive and negative parts of the density
$\psi_\nu\psi_\mu$ are exactly the Jordan densities of $\zeta$, so their
masses have difference $\int\psi_\nu\psi_\mu\,\dd\nu=\alpha$.  Normalizing
the total-variation measure gives \eqref{eq:V20-alpha-polar}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Oriented and unoriented defect identities]
\label{thm:V20-two-defects}
The squared distance of the two \emph{oriented} unit source amplitudes is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb D_{\rm ori}
 :=\|\psi_\nu-\psi_\mu\|_2^2
 =2(1-\alpha)
 =2(1-A_E)+4a_-.}
 \label{eq:V20-oriented-defect}
\end{equation}
The unsigned Schur residual is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =1-\alpha^2
 =\bigl(1-A_E^2\bigr)+4a_+a_-.}
 \label{eq:V20-unoriented-defect}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak h_E^2:=2(1-A_E)
 \label{eq:V20-energy-Hellinger}
\end{equation}
is the squared Hellinger distance between $\rho_\nu$ and $\rho_\mu$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb D_{\rm ori}=\mathfrak h_E^2+4a_-,
 \qquad
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =\mathfrak h_E^2-\frac14\mathfrak h_E^4+4a_+a_-.}
 \label{eq:V20-Hellinger-orientation}
\end{equation}
The equality cases are:
\begin{align}
 \mathbb D_{\rm ori}=0
 &\iff \psi_\mu=\psi_\nu
 \iff A_E=1\ \hbox{and}\ a_-=0,
 \label{eq:V20-oriented-zero}\\
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=0
 &\iff \psi_\mu=\psi_\nu\ \hbox{or}\ \psi_\mu=-\psi_\nu.
 \label{eq:V20-unoriented-zero}
\end{align}
On the second branch of \eqref{eq:V20-unoriented-zero}, one has
$A_E=a_-=1$, $a_+=0$, and $\mathbb D_{\rm ori}=4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since the two amplitudes are unit vectors,
$\|\psi_\nu-\psi_\mu\|^2=2-2\alpha$.  Substitute
$\alpha=a_+-a_-$ and $A_E=a_++a_-$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:V20-oriented-defect}.  Similarly,
\[
 A_E^2-\alpha^2
 =(a_++a_-)^2-(a_+-a_-)^2
 =4a_+a_-,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V20-unoriented-defect}.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V20-Hellinger-orientation} is algebra.  Equality in
Cauchy--Schwarz for two unit real vectors gives
$\psi_\mu=\pm\psi_\nu$, and the Jordan masses distinguish the two signs.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The physical meaning of the two defects]
\label{ass:V20-defect-meaning}
The Schur residual measures distance between one-dimensional \emph{unoriented}
subspaces.  It is sufficient when only a variance or principal angle is
needed.  The quantity $\mathbb D_{\rm ori}$ measures transport of the frozen
signed Creutz source.  A cofinal export to YM--A either requires
$\mathbb D_{\rm ori}\to0$ or requires an independently loaded cutoff-dependent
$\mathbb Z_2$ orientation section.  The latter is a calibration row, not a
gauge consequence of the unsigned Gram.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Source-record and conditional-fibre factorization of the energy overlap}
\label{sec:V20-record-factorization}
% =============================================================================

Retain the four-loop source record $\mathscr S_M$ and the Version~V19
quantities
\[
 h_{\mathscr S}^2=\frac{\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}
                         {\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathscr S}=\mathbb E_\nu[h\mid\mathscr S_M]
 =\rho_{\mathscr S}h_{\mathscr S},
 \qquad 0<\rho_{\mathscr S}\le1.
\]
Both $F_\mu$ and $F_\nu$ are $\mathscr S_M$-measurable.

\begin{definition}[Record-level source-energy Jordan masses]
\label{def:V20-record-Jordan}
Put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 b_\pm
 :=\frac{1}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}
   \int (\pm F_\nu F_\mu)_+
   \sqrt{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}\,\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}},
 \qquad
 A_{E,\mathscr S}:=b_++b_-.}
 \label{eq:V20-record-Jordan}
\end{equation}
Thus $A_{E,\mathscr S}$ is the Hellinger affinity of the source-energy laws
pushed forward to the four-loop record.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact record/fibre/Jordan factorization]
\label{thm:V20-record-fibre-Jordan}
The full Jordan masses satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_\pm
 =\frac{1}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}
   \int (\pm F_\nu F_\mu)_+\,
   \rho_{\mathscr S}
   \sqrt{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}\,\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}.}
 \label{eq:V20-full-Jordan-record}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\le a_\pm\le b_\pm,
 \qquad
 0\le A_E\le A_{E,\mathscr S}\le1.}
 \label{eq:V20-Jordan-data-processing}
\end{equation}
The hidden source-energy affinity debit is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_{E,\mathscr S}-A_E
 =\frac{1}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}
   \int |F_\nu F_\mu|(1-\rho_{\mathscr S})
   \sqrt{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}\,\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}.}
 \label{eq:V20-hidden-energy-debit}
\end{equation}
It vanishes exactly when $\rho_{\mathscr S}=1$ on the support of the
source-energy overlap measure; equality of the conditional laws is required
only on that target-visible support.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By source-record measurability,
\[
 \mathbb E_\nu[(\pm F_\nu F_\mu)_+h]
 =\mathbb E_{\nu_{\mathscr S}}
  [(\pm F_\nu F_\mu)_+\kappa_{\mathscr S}].
\]
Use $\kappa_{\mathscr S}=\rho_{\mathscr S}h_{\mathscr S}$ and
$h_{\mathscr S}\,\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}
 =\sqrt{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}\,\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:V20-full-Jordan-record}.  The inequalities follow from
$0<\rho_{\mathscr S}\le1$ and Cauchy--Schwarz for the record-level
source-energy probability laws.  Summing the two signs gives
\eqref{eq:V20-hidden-energy-debit}.  A nonnegative integral vanishes exactly
when its integrand vanishes almost everywhere with respect to the displayed
source-energy overlap measure.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Three-stage oriented and unoriented transport ledgers]
\label{thm:V20-three-stage}
The oriented source defect has the exact nonnegative decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb D_{\rm ori}
 ={}&2(1-A_{E,\mathscr S})\\
 &+2(A_{E,\mathscr S}-A_E)\\
 &+4a_-.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V20-three-stage-oriented}
\end{equation}
The unsigned Schur residual has the exact decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 ={}&\bigl(1-A_{E,\mathscr S}^2\bigr)\\
 &+\bigl(A_{E,\mathscr S}^2-A_E^2\bigr)\\
 &+4a_+a_-.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V20-three-stage-unoriented}
\end{equation}
The three rows are, respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item source-energy mismatch already visible in the four-loop record;
\item source-weighted conditional-fibre loss hidden inside that record;
\item counteroriented source overlap.
\end{enumerate}
The last row of \eqref{eq:V20-three-stage-unoriented} detects mixed positive
and negative overlap but, as expected, does not detect a pure global sign
reversal.  The oriented ledger \eqref{eq:V20-three-stage-oriented} detects
both.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert and subtract $A_{E,\mathscr S}$ in
$2(1-\alpha)$ and use $A_E-\alpha=2a_-$.  This gives
\eqref{eq:V20-three-stage-oriented}.  Insert and subtract
$A_{E,\mathscr S}^2$ and $A_E^2$ in $1-\alpha^2$, then use
$A_E^2-\alpha^2=4a_+a_-$.  Every term is nonnegative by
\eqref{eq:V20-Jordan-data-processing}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Target-visible conditional sufficiency]
\label{cor:V20-target-visible-sufficiency}
For the old/fine source target it is unnecessary to prove
$\rho_{\mathscr S}=1$ on source-record fibres on which
$F_\nu F_\mu=0$.  The conditional-fibre row of the oriented and unoriented
source ledgers vanishes exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (1-\rho_{\mathscr S})|F_\nu F_\mu|=0
 \quad
 \sqrt{\dd\nu_{\mathscr S}\,\dd\mu_{\mathscr S}}
 \text{-almost everywhere}.}
 \label{eq:V20-target-visible-sufficiency}
\end{equation}
Thus full source-record sufficiency from Version~V19 is a valid stronger
condition, but it is not logically necessary for this scalar source line.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is the equality condition in
\eqref{eq:V20-hidden-energy-debit}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Two positive midpoint-action channels determine the signed mixed row}
\label{sec:V20-midpoint-Jordan}
% =============================================================================

Retain the exact blocked actions $S_0,S_1$, partition functions $Z_0,Z_1$,
and midpoint law $\pi_{1/2}$ of Version~V19.

\begin{definition}[Positive midpoint source channels]
\label{def:V20-positive-midpoint-channels}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Z_\pm^{\rm src}
 :=\int (\pm F_\nu F_\mu)_+
     e^{-(S_0+S_1)/2}\,\dd m_M.}
 \label{eq:V20-positive-midpoint-partitions}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal Z_\pm^{\rm src}
 =Z_{1/2}\,
   \mathbb E_{\pi_{1/2}}[(\pm F_\nu F_\mu)_+].
 \label{eq:V20-positive-midpoint-expectations}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical positive two-channel old/fine card]
\label{thm:V20-positive-two-channel}
The Jordan masses, mixed scalar, total source-energy affinity, and oriented
coefficient are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_\pm
 =\frac{\mathcal Z_\pm^{\rm src}}
 {\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}\,\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu},}
 \label{eq:V20-midpoint-Jordan-masses}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_{Y/X}
 =\frac{\mathcal Z_+^{\rm src}-\mathcal Z_-^{\rm src}}
       {\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}},
 \qquad
 A_E
 =\frac{\mathcal Z_+^{\rm src}+\mathcal Z_-^{\rm src}}
       {\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}\,\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu},}
 \label{eq:V20-midpoint-signed-total}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha
 =\frac{\mathcal Z_+^{\rm src}-\mathcal Z_-^{\rm src}}
       {\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}\,\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}.}
 \label{eq:V20-midpoint-oriented-alpha}
\end{equation}
Thus the signed old/fine line is determined by two nonnegative midpoint
insertions and the two diagonal stocks.  No separate full-law affinity is
needed.

Moreover, the two measures obtained by restricting the signed midpoint
source measure to the regions $F_\nu F_\mu>0$ and $F_\nu F_\mu<0$ are its
unique Jordan positive and negative parts.  Among all decompositions of that
signed measure into a difference of two positive measures, their total mass
$A_E$ is minimal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Substitute the geometric-mean density from
\eqref{eq:V19-midpoint-unnormalized} into the definitions of $a_\pm$.
Adding and subtracting the two positive parts gives
\eqref{eq:V20-midpoint-signed-total}--\eqref{eq:V20-midpoint-oriented-alpha}.
The uniqueness and minimal-total-mass statement are the Hahn--Jordan theorem:
if $\zeta=\eta_+-\eta_-$ with $\eta_\pm\ge0$, then
$\|\zeta\|_{\rm TV}\le\eta_+(\Omega)+\eta_-(\Omega)$, with equality for the
mutually singular Jordan parts.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No source sign problem in the acquisition]
\label{cor:V20-no-source-sign-problem}
The midpoint source product may be signed, but its two required acquisition
writers
\[
 (F_\nu F_\mu)_+,
 \qquad
 (-F_\nu F_\mu)_+
\]
are nonnegative.  Cancellation occurs only in the final exact difference
$\mathcal Z_+^{\rm src}-\mathcal Z_-^{\rm src}$.  The same two positive
channels also supply the total variation $A_E$, so no separately fitted sign
or absolute-overlap model is introduced.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Immediate from \Cref{thm:V20-positive-two-channel}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Denominator-safe oriented interval compiler]
\label{cor:V20-oriented-interval}
Suppose validated outward intervals satisfy
\[
 0\le \underline B_\pm\le B_\pm\le\overline B_\pm,
 \qquad
 B_\pm:=\frac{\mathcal Z_\pm^{\rm src}}{\sqrt{Z_0Z_1}},
\]
\[
 0<\underline s_\nu\le\sigma_\nu^2\le\overline s_\nu,
 \qquad
 0<\underline s_\mu\le\sigma_\mu^2\le\overline s_\mu.
\]
Put
\begin{equation}
 d_-:=\sqrt{\underline s_\nu\underline s_\mu},
 \qquad
 d_+:=\sqrt{\overline s_\nu\overline s_\mu},
 \label{eq:V20-denominator-interval}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \underline a_\pm:=\frac{\underline B_\pm}{d_+},
 \qquad
 \overline a_\pm:=\min\left\{1,
 \frac{\overline B_\pm}{d_-}\right\}.
 \label{eq:V20-Jordan-intervals}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \underline\alpha
 :=\max\{-1,\underline a_+-\overline a_-\}
 \le\alpha\le
 \min\{1,\overline a_+-\underline a_-\}
 =:\overline\alpha.}
 \label{eq:V20-alpha-interval}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 2(1-\overline\alpha)
 \le\mathbb D_{\rm ori}
 \le2(1-\underline\alpha).}
 \label{eq:V20-oriented-defect-interval}
\end{equation}
If
\[
 m_\alpha=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&0\in[\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha],\\
 \min\{|\underline\alpha|,|\overline\alpha|\},&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 M_\alpha=\max\{|\underline\alpha|,|\overline\alpha|\},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \max\{0,1-M_\alpha^2\}
 \le\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \le\min\{1,1-m_\alpha^2\}.}
 \label{eq:V20-Schur-interval}
\end{equation}
An exact packet must satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{B_++B_-\le\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu.}
 \label{eq:V20-positive-domain}
\end{equation}
If the submitted lower bounds force the reverse strict inequality, the packet
is an input error.  If $\overline\alpha<0$, the card certifies a
counteroriented source line even when the Schur residual interval contains
zero.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V20-Jordan-intervals} is outward division by a positive
denominator interval.  The extrema of $a_+-a_-$ on the resulting rectangle
are the displayed opposite corners, proving
\eqref{eq:V20-alpha-interval}.  The maps
$\alpha\mapsto2(1-\alpha)$ and $\alpha\mapsto1-\alpha^2$ give the remaining
intervals.  The domain condition is $A_E\le1$ from
\eqref{eq:V20-energy-affinity}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Two sharp target-order counterexamples}
\label{sec:V20-counterexamples}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Full-law Hellinger alignment is not necessary for source alignment]
\label{cth:V20-full-law-not-necessary}
There are two different full laws with positive Hellinger distance whose
normalized physical source amplitudes align exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On four points take
\[
 \nu=\left(\frac14,\frac14,\frac18,\frac38\right),
 \qquad
 \mu=\left(\frac14,\frac14,\frac38,\frac18\right),
\]
and use the same centered source under both laws,
\[
 F_\nu=F_\mu=(1,-1,0,0).
\]
Both source stocks equal $1/2$.  The source-energy laws are identical and
supported on the first two points, with the same sign.  Therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{A_E=\alpha=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb D_{\rm ori}=\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=0.}
 \label{eq:V20-invisible-law-mismatch}
\end{equation}
The full-law Hellinger affinity is only
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \int\sqrt{\dd\mu\,\dd\nu}
 =\frac12+\frac{\sqrt3}{4}<1.}
 \label{eq:V20-full-affinity-counter}
\end{equation}
The law mismatch is confined to points on which the source vanishes.  Hence
the Version~V19 full-law action-curvature debit is a sufficient global row,
but the source-energy target is strictly weaker.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The Schur residual alone does not certify oriented transport]
\label{cth:V20-Schur-no-orientation}
There is a card with zero old/fine Schur residual and maximal oriented source
defect.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take one common law on two equiprobable points and set
\[
 F_\nu=(1,-1),
 \qquad
 F_\mu=(-1,1)=-F_\nu.
\]
Both source stocks are one.  Hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 A_E=a_-=1,
 \qquad
 a_+=0,
 \qquad
 \alpha=-1,}
 \label{eq:V20-sign-reversal-data}
\end{equation}
so
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb D_{\rm ori}=4.}
 \label{eq:V20-sign-reversal-defects}
\end{equation}
Thus a zero principal-line defect determines only an unoriented line.  It
cannot select the frozen physical source section.
\end{proof}

\section{Cofinal oriented transport and the sign-cocycle branch}
\label{sec:V20-cofinal-orientation}
% =============================================================================

Assume the inherited dyadic physical incidences and law-alignment isometries
have been composed into one common real Hilbert screen.  Let $\Psi_n$ be the
unit balanced source amplitude at cutoff $n$ after this declared transport,
and put
\begin{equation}
 \alpha_n:=\langle\Psi_{n+1},\Psi_n\rangle,
 \qquad
 d_n^{\rm ori}:=\|\Psi_{n+1}-\Psi_n\|
 =\sqrt{2(1-\alpha_n)}.
 \label{eq:V20-cofinal-increments}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Oriented common-screen criterion]
\label{thm:V20-oriented-common-screen}
If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sum_{n=1}^\infty d_n^{\rm ori}<\infty,}
 \label{eq:V20-oriented-summability}
\end{equation}
then $(\Psi_n)$ is Cauchy and converges strongly to a unique unit source
vector on the common screen.  The sufficient positive-channel condition is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sum_n
 \sqrt{\,2(1-A_{E,n})+4a_{-,n}\,}<\infty.}
 \label{eq:V20-positive-channel-summability}
\end{equation}
In particular, $A_{E,n}\to1$ and $a_{-,n}\to0$ are necessary for an oriented
adjacent-cutoff pass.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $m>n$, the triangle inequality gives
\[
 \|\Psi_m-\Psi_n\|
 \le\sum_{j=n}^{m-1}d_j^{\rm ori}.
\]
The tail of the convergent series tends to zero, so the unit vectors are
Cauchy.  Completeness gives a strong limit, and norm continuity preserves
unit norm.  Equation \eqref{eq:V20-positive-channel-summability} is exactly
\eqref{eq:V20-oriented-defect} at each adjacent pair.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unoriented near-unit transport has a sign alternative]
\label{thm:V20-sign-alternative}
Suppose only
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb R_n=1-\alpha_n^2\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:V20-unoriented-near-unit}
\end{equation}
After discarding finitely many zero overlaps, exactly one of the following
occurs:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item the overlaps are eventually positive and $\alpha_n\to+1$, equivalently
      $d_n^{\rm ori}\to0$;
\item the overlaps are eventually negative and $\alpha_n\to-1$, in which case
      $(d_n^{\rm ori})^2\to4$ and $a_{-,n}\to1$;
\item both signs occur infinitely often; the positive and negative
      subsequences converge respectively to $+1$ and $-1$.
\end{enumerate}
On the eventual nonzero-overlap branch one may algebraically choose signs
$\varepsilon_n\in\{\pm1\}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon_{n+1}\varepsilon_n=\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha_n)
 \label{eq:V20-sign-cocycle}
\end{equation}
so that the reoriented adjacent overlaps are $|\alpha_n|$.  This operation is
a cutoff-dependent $\mathbb Z_2$ source calibration.  It is not physically
licensed by the unsigned Gram and is not applied unless that orientation
section is independently loaded.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V20-unoriented-near-unit} gives
$|\alpha_n|\to1$.  Compactness of the two-point sign set gives the displayed
subsequence alternatives.  The formula for $d_n^{\rm ori}$ proves the second
claim.  On a chain, choose $\varepsilon_1=1$ and define the remaining signs
recursively by \eqref{eq:V20-sign-cocycle}; then
\[
 \langle\varepsilon_{n+1}\Psi_{n+1},
         \varepsilon_n\Psi_n\rangle=|\alpha_n|.
\]
The recursion is mathematical.  The frozen Creutz source convention supplies
no physical Read of the newly chosen $\varepsilon_n$, which proves the final
qualification.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Correct adjacent-cutoff status before the radial Read]
\label{cor:V20-adjacent-status}
On one selected-root dyadic family, the exact old/fine status is now:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item \emph{oriented pass}: $\mathbb D_{\rm ori}\to0$;
\item \emph{source-energy mismatch}: $1-A_E$ has a positive lower limit;
\item \emph{counterorientation}: $a_-$ has a positive lower limit, including
      the pure sign-reversal branch $a_-\to1$;
\item \emph{unresolved}: the positive midpoint intervals contain more than
      one of the preceding branches;
\item \emph{error}: the submitted positive channels violate
      \eqref{eq:V20-positive-domain} or their common-cylinder incidence.
\end{enumerate}
Only item~\textup{(A1)}, or item~\textup{(A3)} together with an independently
loaded sign cocycle, permits a signed cofinal source export.  The independent
Version~V11 radial posterior card is then evaluated at the predeclared
physical shell width.
\end{corollary}
