% =============================================================================
\section{Version V21 direction: law comparison is not transport occurrence}
\label{sec:V21-direction}
% =============================================================================

Versions~V18--V20 construct an exact and useful comparison between the natural
coarse Wilson law and the law induced by blocking the fine Wilson cylinder.
The comparison is the density-square-root unitary
\[
 f\longmapsto h f,
 \qquad
 h=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}},
\]
and its source-energy overlap admits the complete Hellinger, conditional-fibre,
and Jordan decompositions proved above.  Those statements remain exact.

The present continuation audits a logically earlier word in the phrase
``old/fine transport.''  A density-square-root unitary identifies two
Hilbert spaces; it does not by itself describe an occurring stochastic
cutoff route, a common two-cutoff history, or a Markov re-equilibration of the
blocked fine field into a natural coarse field.  Unless the two endpoint laws
coincide, the blocked fine coarse field and a natural coarse field cannot be
the same random variable with both marginals.  A second coarse variable and
an actual coupling kernel are required.

This distinction matters because different couplings of the same endpoint
laws can give source overlaps ranging from perfect alignment to perfect
counterorientation.  The two positive midpoint channels of Version~V20
therefore solve the canonical half-density comparison problem, but they do
not populate a physical coupling which has not occurred.

Version~V21 moves to that upstream incidence.  It proves that the minimum
same-history object for the scalar source target is a coupling of the two
four-loop source records, gives one nonnegative squared-difference writer
which reconstructs the complete oriented mixed Gram on that coupling, and
separates an occurring coupling from an optimally fitted transportation plan.

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the correction]
\label{fire:V21-scope}
No theorem below invalidates the Hellinger and Jordan identities of
Versions~V18--V20.  Their exact scope is the canonical half-density
comparison of two endpoint laws.  Version~V21 proves that this comparison is
not an occurring stochastic cutoff transport unless an additional physical
incidence is supplied.  Conversely, once an actual coupling is supplied, the
one positive squared source difference is target-minimal; the Hellinger
midpoint and its two Jordan channels are not charged again merely to recover
the same coupled scalar.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The half-density unitary is Markov only on the projective-law branch}
\label{sec:V21-half-density}
% =============================================================================

Let $(\Omega,\mathscr F)$ be the common coarse configuration cylinder and let
$\mu,\nu$ be mutually absolutely continuous probability laws.  Put
\begin{equation}
 h:=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}},
 \qquad
 U_h:L^2(\mu)\longrightarrow L^2(\nu),
 \qquad U_hf:=hf.
 \label{eq:V21-half-density-unitary}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Half-density comparison versus a Markov transport]
\label{thm:V21-half-density-not-Markov}
The map $U_h$ is a positive unitary and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{U_h\one=h.}
 \label{eq:V21-half-density-unit}
\end{equation}
It is a unital Markov operator if and only if
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\mu=\nu.}
 \label{eq:V21-half-density-projective}
\end{equation}
More generally, the diagonal geometric-mean measure
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_H(\dd x,\dd y)
 :=\delta_x(\dd y)\sqrt{\dd\mu\,\dd\nu}(x)
 \label{eq:V21-diagonal-Hellinger-measure}
\end{equation}
has total mass equal to the Hellinger affinity
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_H(\Omega^2)
 =\int\sqrt{\dd\mu\,\dd\nu}
 =:\mathcal A_H\le1,
 \label{eq:V21-Hellinger-mass}
\end{equation}
and both of its marginals are the geometric-mean measure.  It is a coupling
of $(\nu,\mu)$ if and only if $\mu=\nu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $f\in L^2(\mu)$,
\[
 \|U_hf\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2
 =\int h^2|f|^2\,\dd\nu
 =\int|f|^2\,\dd\mu,
\]
so $U_h$ is an isometry; multiplication by $h^{-1}$ gives its inverse.
Positivity is immediate.  A Markov operator is unital.  Thus $U_h$ can be
Markov only when $h=1$ $\nu$-almost everywhere, which is equivalent to
$\mu=\nu$.  The converse is the identity operator.

The mass and marginals of $\gamma_H$ follow by integrating the diagonal
kernel.  If it has first marginal $\nu$ and second marginal $\mu$, then the
geometric-mean measure equals both endpoint laws.  Hence their densities
satisfy $\sqrt{pq}=p=q$ relative to any common dominating measure, and
$\mu=\nu$.  The converse is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Correct interpretation of the V18 incidence]
\label{ass:V21-V18-interpretation}
The map $U_h$ is the canonical same-observable comparison and the correct
half-density chart for a normalized old/fine Gram.  It is not a conditional
expectation, a transition kernel, or a random old field generated from the
blocked fine field.  Calling its Gram ``law aligned'' is exact; calling it an
occurring cutoff transport requires an additional physical route.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact dyadic graph obstruction and the minimum re-equilibration kernel}
\label{sec:V21-dyadic-coupling}
% =============================================================================

Let $U_N$ have the selected fine Wilson law $\mu_N$, put
\[
 W_\nu:=B_{N\to M}U_N,
\]
and denote its law by
\[
 \nu=(B_{N\to M})_*\mu_N.
\]
Let $\mu$ be the selected natural coarse Wilson law on the same coarse
configuration cylinder.

\begin{theorem}[A single dyadic coarse variable cannot carry two unequal laws]
\label{thm:V21-single-variable-no-go}
Suppose a common history contains $U_N$ and one coarse variable $W$ such that
\begin{equation}
 W=B_{N\to M}U_N
 \quad\hbox{almost surely},
 \qquad
 \mathcal L(W)=\mu.
 \label{eq:V21-single-variable-claims}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\mu=\nu.}
 \label{eq:V21-single-variable-projective}
\end{equation}
Consequently, when $\mu\ne\nu$, any occurring old/fine history must contain
either a second coarse variable $W_\mu$ or an equivalent physical
reweighting/resampling mark.  In kernel form the missing incidence is a
Markov kernel
\begin{equation}
 K_{Y/X}(w,\dd w')
 \quad\hbox{such that}\quad
 \boxed{\nu K_{Y/X}=\mu.}
 \label{eq:V21-reequilibration-kernel}
\end{equation}
The identity kernel satisfies \eqref{eq:V21-reequilibration-kernel} if and
only if $\mu=\nu$.  A marginal-correct kernel always exists, for example
$K(w,\cdot)=\mu(\cdot)$, but marginal correctness alone supplies no source
transport.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The law of the deterministic image $B_{N\to M}U_N$ is $\nu$ by definition.
The two assertions in \eqref{eq:V21-single-variable-claims} therefore give
$\mathcal L(W)=\nu=\mu$.  The kernel statement is the disintegration of any
joint law of $(W_\nu,W_\mu)$ with first marginal $\nu$ and second marginal
$\mu$.  The identity kernel preserves $\nu$, and hence reaches $\mu$ exactly
when the laws coincide.  The constant kernel has output law $\mu$ for every
input law, proving existence while also showing that mere existence carries
no information about the old/fine source correlation.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Occurring cutoff coupling and coupled source Gram]
\label{def:V21-occurring-coupling}
An occurring adjacent-cutoff coupling is a probability law
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{Y/X}(\dd w,\dd w')
 =\nu(\dd w)K_{Y/X}(w,\dd w')
 \label{eq:V21-coupling-law}
\end{equation}
whose marginals are $\nu$ and $\mu$, and whose kernel or common-cylinder
realization is fixed independently of the source overlap read from it.

Let $F_\nu\in L_0^2(\nu;\R)$ and
$F_\mu\in L_0^2(\mu;\R)$ be the balanced Creutz writers, with nonzero stocks
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_\nu^2=\mathbb E_\nu F_\nu^2,
 \qquad
 \sigma_\mu^2=\mathbb E_\mu F_\mu^2.
 \label{eq:V21-coupled-stocks}
\end{equation}
On the common history put
\begin{equation}
 X:=F_\nu(W_\nu),
 \qquad
 Y:=F_\mu(W_\mu).
 \label{eq:V21-coupled-columns}
\end{equation}
The occurring coupled Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{Y/X}^{\lambda}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
   \sigma_\nu^2&c_\lambda\\
   c_\lambda&\sigma_\mu^2
  \end{pmatrix}\succeq0,}
 \qquad
 c_\lambda:=\mathbb E_\lambda[XY].
 \label{eq:V21-coupled-Gram}
\end{equation}
Its oriented coefficient and unsigned Schur residual are
\begin{equation}
 \alpha_\lambda
 :=\frac{c_\lambda}{\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu},
 \qquad
 \mathbb R_\lambda:=1-\alpha_\lambda^2.
 \label{eq:V21-coupled-alpha}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

% =============================================================================
\section{One positive squared-difference Read reconstructs the oriented coupling}
\label{sec:V21-positive-read}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Target-minimal oriented coupling Read]
\label{thm:V21-positive-oriented-read}
For an occurring coupling define the unnormalized and normalized positive
writers
\begin{equation}
 D_0^\lambda
 :=\mathbb E_\lambda[(X-Y)^2],
 \qquad
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda
 :=\mathbb E_\lambda\left[
  \left(\frac{X}{\sigma_\nu}-\frac{Y}{\sigma_\mu}\right)^2
 \right].
 \label{eq:V21-two-positive-differences}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_\lambda
 =\frac{\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2-D_0^\lambda}{2},}
 \label{eq:V21-cross-from-unnormalized-loss}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_\lambda=1-\frac12D_{\rm ori}^\lambda,}
 \label{eq:V21-alpha-from-oriented-loss}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_\lambda
 =D_{\rm ori}^\lambda-\frac14(D_{\rm ori}^\lambda)^2.}
 \label{eq:V21-Schur-from-oriented-loss}
\end{equation}
Moreover
\begin{equation}
 0\le D_{\rm ori}^\lambda\le4,
 \label{eq:V21-oriented-loss-range}
\end{equation}
and the exact branches are
\begin{equation}
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda=0&\alpha_\lambda=1\quad\text{oriented pass},\\
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda=2&\alpha_\lambda=0\quad\text{orthogonal source lines},\\
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda>2&\alpha_\lambda<0\quad\text{counteroriented coupling},\\
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda=4&\alpha_\lambda=-1\quad\text{exact sign reversal}.
 \end{array}
 \label{eq:V21-oriented-branches}
\end{equation}
Thus one nonnegative same-history writer, together with the two diagonal
stocks, determines the complete signed mixed scalar.  The Version~V20 Jordan
channels need not be acquired again when this occurring coupling Read is
available.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expanding $(X-Y)^2$ and using the two marginal laws gives
\[
 D_0^\lambda
 =\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2-2c_\lambda,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V21-cross-from-unnormalized-loss}.  The normalized
columns have unit norm in $L^2(\lambda)$, so the same expansion gives
\[
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda
 =2-2\alpha_\lambda.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:V21-alpha-from-oriented-loss}.  Substitution in
$1-\alpha_\lambda^2$ gives \eqref{eq:V21-Schur-from-oriented-loss}.
Cauchy--Schwarz gives $-1\le\alpha_\lambda\le1$, which is equivalent to
\eqref{eq:V21-oriented-loss-range}; the branch table is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Denominator-safe interval form]
\label{cor:V21-positive-read-interval}
Suppose validated outward intervals satisfy
\[
 0<\underline s_T\le\sigma_T^2\le\overline s_T,
 \qquad T\in\{\nu,\mu\},
\]
and
\[
 0\le\underline D_0\le D_0^\lambda\le\overline D_0.
\]
Put
\begin{equation}
 n_-:=\underline s_\nu+\underline s_\mu-\overline D_0,
 \qquad
 n_+:=\overline s_\nu+\overline s_\mu-\underline D_0,
 \label{eq:V21-numerator-interval}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 d_-:=2\sqrt{\underline s_\nu\underline s_\mu},
 \qquad
 d_+:=2\sqrt{\overline s_\nu\overline s_\mu}.
 \label{eq:V21-denominator-interval}
\end{equation}
Then the sign-safe outward quotient enclosure is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \max\left\{-1,\min_{\substack{n\in\{n_-,n_+\}\\d\in\{d_-,d_+\}}}
                  \frac nd\right\}
 \le\alpha_\lambda\le
 \min\left\{1,\max_{\substack{n\in\{n_-,n_+\}\\d\in\{d_-,d_+\}}}
                  \frac nd\right\}.}
 \label{eq:V21-alpha-interval}
\end{equation}
If the normalized positive writer is acquired directly as
$D_{\rm ori}^\lambda\in[\underline D,\overline D]$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 1-\frac12\overline D
 \le\alpha_\lambda\le
 1-\frac12\underline D.}
 \label{eq:V21-direct-oriented-interval}
\end{equation}
A negative upper endpoint is a certified counterorientation.  A coupling
table whose row or column marginals fail the declared endpoint laws is an
input error rather than a physical obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V21-cross-from-unnormalized-loss} gives a numerator in
$[n_-,n_+]$ and a strictly positive denominator in $[d_-,d_+]$.  The extrema
of $n/d$ on this interval rectangle occur at its four corners, which proves
the sign-safe enclosure \eqref{eq:V21-alpha-interval}.
Equation \eqref{eq:V21-direct-oriented-interval} is the affine identity
\eqref{eq:V21-alpha-from-oriented-loss}.  The final statement is part of the
definition of an occurring coupling.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Endpoint laws and their Hellinger comparison do not determine the coupling}
\label{sec:V21-nonidentifiability}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Same marginals, same Hellinger card, opposite physical transports]
\label{thm:V21-coupling-nonidentifiability}
There are three coupling cards with identical endpoint laws, identical source
functions, identical endpoint moments of every order, and identical
Version~V18--V20 half-density comparison, but with coupled source
coefficients
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\alpha_+=1,\qquad\alpha_0=0,\qquad\alpha_-=-1.}
 \label{eq:V21-three-coupling-values}
\end{equation}

Indeed, let $\Omega=\{-1,+1\}$, let $\mu=\nu$ be uniform, and put
$F_\mu(x)=F_\nu(x)=x$.  Let $\lambda_+$ be the diagonal coupling,
$\lambda_-$ the antidiagonal coupling, and $\lambda_0=\nu\otimes\mu$ the
independent coupling.  The half-density map is the identity and its oriented
coefficient is one, while the three occurring coupling coefficients are
those in \eqref{eq:V21-three-coupling-values}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All endpoint data are fixed because the marginals and source functions are
fixed.  Under $\lambda_+$ one has $Y=X$, under $\lambda_-$ one has $Y=-X$,
and under the product coupling the centered variables are independent.
Their normalized cross moments are respectively $1,-1,0$.  Since
$\mu=\nu$, the Hellinger density is one and the canonical half-density
comparison identifies the two copies pointwise, giving coefficient one in
all three cases.  Hence that comparison cannot determine which coupling
occurred.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The upstream physical residual]
\label{ass:V21-upstream-residual}
The two Jordan midpoint channels determine the signed half-density overlap
exactly.  The theorem above shows that even their exact values do not select
an occurring old/fine coupling.  The first unclosed physical row is therefore
not another refinement of the midpoint integral.  It is the common two-cutoff
cylinder or coupling kernel on which the old and fine source values are read
together.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The four-loop record coupling is target-minimal}
\label{sec:V21-record-coupling}
% =============================================================================

Let
\[
 \mathfrak O_\nu:\Omega_\nu\to\mathscr S,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak O_\mu:\Omega_\mu\to\mathscr S,
 \qquad
 \mathscr S\subset[-1/2,1]^4,
\]
be the four physical rectangle records, and let
\[
 F_\nu=f_\nu\circ\mathfrak O_\nu,
 \qquad
 F_\mu=f_\mu\circ\mathfrak O_\mu.
\]
Denote the record marginals by $\nu_{\mathscr S}$ and
$\mu_{\mathscr S}$.

\begin{theorem}[Record quotient and coupling lift]
\label{thm:V21-record-lift}
Let $\Lambda$ be any coupling of the complete endpoint configuration laws and
let
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{\mathscr S}
 :=(\mathfrak O_\nu,\mathfrak O_\mu)_*\Lambda.
 \label{eq:V21-record-pushforward}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_\Lambda[F_\nu F_\mu]
 =\mathbb E_{\lambda_{\mathscr S}}
   [f_\nu(s)f_\mu(t)].}
 \label{eq:V21-record-sufficiency}
\end{equation}
Conversely, on standard Borel configuration spaces every coupling
$\lambda_{\mathscr S}$ of the two record marginals admits a coupling lift
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Lambda(\dd x,\dd y)
 =\int
  \nu(\dd x\mid s)\,
  \mu(\dd y\mid t)\,
  \lambda_{\mathscr S}(\dd s,\dd t),}
 \label{eq:V21-independent-fibre-lift}
\end{equation}
where regular conditional endpoint laws are used.  This lift has the
required full marginals and reproduces the same source Gram.

Therefore a coupling of the four-loop records is mathematically necessary
and sufficient for the scalar old/fine source target.  A full link-field
coupling is required only when its hidden detail correlations, local action,
or another non-record observable is itself claimed.  The physical occurrence
of either coupling remains an input; the independent conditional lift is not
silently declared to be the Yang--Mills cutoff dynamics.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V21-record-sufficiency} is the pushforward identity because
both source writers factor through the displayed records.  For the converse,
integrating \eqref{eq:V21-independent-fibre-lift} first over $y,t$ gives the
disintegration of $\nu$; integrating first over $x,s$ gives the
disintegration of $\mu$.  Hence $\Lambda$ is a coupling.  The source product
is constant on each conditional fibre pair and therefore has the same
expectation as under $\lambda_{\mathscr S}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Optimal lifting is not occurrence]
\label{fire:V21-lift-not-occurrence}
The existence of the lift \eqref{eq:V21-independent-fibre-lift} is a
mathematical extension theorem.  Selecting that lift, an optimal-transport
coupling, or any other coupling after inspecting the desired source overlap
is a fit.  A physical transport claim requires an independently occurring
joint record, a loaded re-equilibration kernel, or a positive common-cylinder
construction whose two marginals pass the endpoint audit.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{A quantitative physical gluing theorem}
\label{sec:V21-gluing-bound}
% =============================================================================

On an occurring record coupling write
\[
 \mathbf O_\nu:=\mathfrak O_\nu(W_\nu),
 \qquad
 \mathbf O_\mu:=\mathfrak O_\mu(W_\mu),
\]
with means $W^\nu,W^\mu$ and balanced unit coefficient vectors
$u^\nu,u^\mu$.  Thus
\begin{equation}
 F_\nu=(u^\nu)^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_\nu-W^\nu),
 \qquad
 F_\mu=(u^\mu)^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_\mu-W^\mu).
 \label{eq:V21-record-sources}
\end{equation}
Define the physical raw-record gluing cost
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 g_\lambda^2
 :=\mathbb E_\lambda
 \|\mathbf O_\nu-\mathbf O_\mu\|_2^2,}
 \label{eq:V21-record-gluing-cost}
\end{equation}
and the coefficient drift
\begin{equation}
 \delta_u:=\|u^\nu-u^\mu\|_2.
 \label{eq:V21-coefficient-drift}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Record gluing controls the complete oriented source defect]
\label{thm:V21-gluing-theorem}
For every occurring coupling,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|F_\nu-F_\mu\|_{L^2(\lambda)}
 \le3\delta_u+g_\lambda.}
 \label{eq:V21-unnormalized-gluing}
\end{equation}
Let
\[
 \sigma_*:=\min\{\sigma_\nu,\sigma_\mu\}>0.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda
 \le
 \frac{4(3\delta_u+g_\lambda)^2}{\sigma_*^2},}
 \label{eq:V21-normalized-gluing}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_\lambda
 \ge
 1-\frac{2(3\delta_u+g_\lambda)^2}{\sigma_*^2},}
 \label{eq:V21-alpha-gluing-lower}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_\lambda
 \le
 \frac{4(3\delta_u+g_\lambda)^2}{\sigma_*^2}.}
 \label{eq:V21-Schur-gluing-upper}
\end{equation}

If
\[
 \delta_{\log W}
 :=\max_\alpha
 \left|\log W_\alpha^\nu-\log W_\alpha^\mu\right|,
\]
then the inherited balanced-direction estimate gives
\begin{equation}
 \delta_u\le2(e^{\delta_{\log W}}-1),
 \label{eq:V21-logmean-direction}
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm ori}^\lambda
 \le
 \frac{4\left[6(e^{\delta_{\log W}}-1)+g_\lambda\right]^2}
      {\sigma_*^2}.}
 \label{eq:V21-executable-gluing}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every component of a normalized real Wilson trace lies in $[-1/2,1]$.
Its centered range therefore has absolute value at most $3/2$, and hence
\begin{equation*}
 \|\mathbf O_\nu-W^\nu\|_2\le3
 \quad\hbox{pointwise}.
\end{equation*}
Using \eqref{eq:V21-record-sources},
\begin{align*}
 F_\nu-F_\mu
 ={}&(u^\nu-u^\mu)^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_\nu-W^\nu)\\
 &+(u^\mu)^{\mathsf T}
 \left[(\mathbf O_\nu-W^\nu)-(\mathbf O_\mu-W^\mu)\right].
\end{align*}
The first term has $L^2$ norm at most $3\delta_u$.  Put
$D=\mathbf O_\nu-\mathbf O_\mu$.  Since
$\mathbb E_\lambda D=W^\nu-W^\mu$,
\[
 \mathbb E\|D-\mathbb ED\|_2^2
 \le\mathbb E\|D\|_2^2=g_\lambda^2.
\]
The second term is a unit-vector compression of $D-\mathbb ED$ and therefore
has norm at most $g_\lambda$.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V21-unnormalized-gluing}.

Let $e=\|F_\nu-F_\mu\|_{L^2(\lambda)}$.  The reverse triangle inequality
gives $|\sigma_\nu-\sigma_\mu|\le e$.  Hence
\begin{align*}
 \left\|
  \frac{F_\nu}{\sigma_\nu}
  -\frac{F_\mu}{\sigma_\mu}
 \right\|_2
 &\le
 \frac{e}{\sigma_\nu}
 +\sigma_\mu
  \left|\frac1{\sigma_\nu}-\frac1{\sigma_\mu}\right|\\
 &\le\frac{2e}{\sigma_\nu}
 \le\frac{2e}{\sigma_*}.
\end{align*}
Squaring and using \eqref{eq:V21-unnormalized-gluing} proves
\eqref{eq:V21-normalized-gluing}.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V21-alpha-gluing-lower} follows from
$D_{\rm ori}=2(1-\alpha)$.  Since
$1-\alpha^2\le2(1-\alpha)=D_{\rm ori}$,
\eqref{eq:V21-Schur-gluing-upper} follows.  Finally,
\eqref{eq:V21-logmean-direction} is the balanced coefficient estimate of
Version~V18, and substitution gives \eqref{eq:V21-executable-gluing}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact diagonal-record pass]
\label{cor:V21-diagonal-record-pass}
If an occurring record coupling satisfies
\[
 \mathbf O_\nu=\mathbf O_\mu\quad\lambda\text{-almost surely}
\]
and the four means agree, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{F_\nu=F_\mu,\qquad D_{\rm ori}^\lambda=0,
 \qquad\alpha_\lambda=1.}
 \label{eq:V21-diagonal-pass}
\end{equation}
Such a diagonal record coupling can have the prescribed marginals only when
$\nu_{\mathscr S}=\mu_{\mathscr S}$.  Equality of the four means alone is not
sufficient.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The hypotheses give $g_\lambda=0$ and $u^\nu=u^\mu$, so
\eqref{eq:V21-record-sources} gives equality of the source values.  A random
pair supported on the diagonal has equal marginal laws on the record space.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Sharp marginal-only interval and the no-fit rule}
\label{sec:V21-transport-polytope}
% =============================================================================

The actual record values may be evaluated on a finite validated partition or
finite exact quadrature bank.  Let the fine record atoms have probabilities
$p_i$ and normalized source values $x_i$, and the coarse atoms have
probabilities $q_j$ and normalized source values $y_j$.  A coupling table
$\Lambda=(\lambda_{ij})$ belongs to the transportation polytope
\begin{equation}
 \Pi(p,q)
 :=\left\{
 \lambda_{ij}\ge0:
 \sum_j\lambda_{ij}=p_i,
 \ \sum_i\lambda_{ij}=q_j
 \right\}.
 \label{eq:V21-transport-polytope}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp coupling interval from endpoint source marginals]
\label{thm:V21-sharp-coupling-interval}
The set of possible normalized coupling coefficients is the compact interval
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 [\alpha_-,\alpha_+]
 =\left\{
  \sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij}x_i y_j:
  \Lambda\in\Pi(p,q)
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V21-coupling-interval}
\end{equation}
Its endpoints are attained and have the exact linear-programming dual forms
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_+
 =\min_{a_i+b_j\ge x_i y_j}
 \left(\sum_i p_i a_i+\sum_jq_jb_j\right),}
 \label{eq:V21-upper-dual}\\
 \boxed{
 \alpha_-
 =\max_{a_i+b_j\le x_i y_j}
 \left(\sum_i p_i a_i+\sum_jq_jb_j\right).}
 \label{eq:V21-lower-dual}
\end{align}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.4em]
\item if $\alpha_+<0$, every possible coupling is counteroriented;
\item if $\alpha_+\le1-\delta$, no coupling can give an oriented defect below
      $2\delta$;
\item if $\alpha_+$ is close to one, this proves only the existence of a
      favorable coupling, not that it physically occurred;
\item the value of a submitted physical coupling is accepted only after its
      nonnegativity and marginal equations in
      \eqref{eq:V21-transport-polytope} have passed.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The transportation polytope is nonempty, compact, and convex.  The displayed
source coefficient is a linear functional, so its image is a compact
interval and its extrema are attained.  Finite linear-programming duality
for the maximization problem gives \eqref{eq:V21-upper-dual}; applying the
same theorem to the minimization problem gives
\eqref{eq:V21-lower-dual}.  The four conclusions are immediate from
$D_{\rm ori}=2(1-\alpha)$ and from the distinction between existence and
occurrence.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Optimal transport is a bound, not the cutoff route]
\label{fire:V21-optimal-not-physical}
The optimizer attaining $\alpha_+$ is a sharp marginal-only upper benchmark.
It may be used to prove that alignment is impossible for every coupling.  It
may not be selected as the Yang--Mills cutoff transport merely because it
maximizes the desired overlap.  The physical kernel must be declared by the
actual two-cutoff construction before the source product is inspected.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cofinal common-history source landing}
\label{sec:V21-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

Let $(\mu_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a cofinal sequence of endpoint laws.  Suppose each
adjacent physical cutoff route is an occurring coupling
\[
 \lambda_n(\dd x_n,\dd x_{n+1})
 =\mu_n(\dd x_n)K_n(x_n,\dd x_{n+1})
\]
with second marginal $\mu_{n+1}$.  Let $F_n$ be the nonzero balanced source at
cutoff $n$, put $\sigma_n=\|F_n\|_{L^2(\mu_n)}$, and define
\[
 \Psi_n:=F_n(X_n)/\sigma_n.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Actual kernels produce one cofinal source history]
\label{thm:V21-cofinal-coupling}
The kernels $(K_n)$ and initial law $\mu_0$ determine a probability law on the
complete cutoff path $(X_0,X_1,\ldots)$ whose adjacent pair marginal is
$\lambda_n$.  On this common history,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\Psi_{n+1}-\Psi_n\|_{L^2}^2
 =D_{{\rm ori},n}^{\lambda}.}
 \label{eq:V21-path-increment}
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sum_{n=0}^\infty
 \sqrt{D_{{\rm ori},n}^{\lambda}}<\infty,}
 \label{eq:V21-summable-physical-coupling}
\end{equation}
then $(\Psi_n)$ converges strongly in the path $L^2$ space to a unique unit
source $\Psi_\infty$.

If only the half-density comparison defects of Versions~V18--V20 are
summable, while no kernels or common cylinders occur, one obtains an abstract
Hilbert-space identification but not the common cutoff history asserted
here.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The standard iterative kernel construction defines the finite-dimensional
path laws
\[
 \mu_0(\dd x_0)K_0(x_0,\dd x_1)\cdots
 K_{m-1}(x_{m-1},\dd x_m).
\]
They are consistent under terminal marginalization, and hence define the
path law.  By construction its adjacent pair marginal is $\lambda_n$.
Equation \eqref{eq:V21-path-increment} is the definition of the normalized
positive coupling writer.  Under \eqref{eq:V21-summable-physical-coupling},
the triangle inequality shows that $(\Psi_n)$ is Cauchy in $L^2$.  Its limit
has norm one because every $\Psi_n$ does.  Uniqueness follows from completeness
of the Hilbert space.  The final statement is
\Cref{thm:V21-half-density-not-Markov,thm:V21-coupling-nonidentifiability}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Physical trichotomy order]
\label{cor:V21-physical-order}
On a branch satisfying \eqref{eq:V21-summable-physical-coupling}, the balanced
source has an actual oriented cutoff landing.  The independent spatial
radial verdict is then read from the Version~V11 Bayes-reverse source loss on
a predeclared shell width.  Its branches remain:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.4em]
\item strict source-relative radial loss: contraction;
\item a near-unit radial channel at shrinking physical width: contact-scale
      retention;
\item a near-unit radial channel at positive physical width: positive-range
      boundary survival.
\end{enumerate}
If the selected roots are sublinear, Version~V17 already gives the first
branch at every separating shell, regardless of adjacent-cutoff source
alignment.  The spatial cutoff path and radial shell channel remain distinct
from the Osterwalder--Schrader time transfer.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is \Cref{thm:V21-cofinal-coupling}.  The three radial
branches and the sublinear extinction theorem are inherited from
Versions~V11 and V17.  Their physical-radius tags are unchanged by the
present cutoff coupling construction.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Finite certificate and exact next acquisition}
\label{sec:V21-certificate}
% =============================================================================

\begin{certificate}[Transport-occurrence compiler]
\label{cert:V21-transport-occurrence}
On a finite record bank, the submitted adjacent-cutoff packet contains:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.4em]
\item the two endpoint record laws and source values;
\item a nonnegative joint table $\Lambda$ whose row and column sums are the
      endpoint laws, or an independently declared kernel and its common
      history;
\item the two positive source stocks;
\item either the positive normalized squared source difference or the
      unnormalized squared difference.
\end{enumerate}
The certificate returns exactly one of:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(O\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.4em]
\item \textsf{PASS}: the outward oriented-defect interval lies below the
      predeclared transport tolerance;
\item \textsf{OBSTRUCTION}: an outward lower defect exceeds the
      predeclared transport tolerance, or the upper overlap endpoint is
      negative, with the coupling and source witness retained;
\item \textsf{UNRESOLVED}: the interval overlaps both passing and failing
      regions;
\item \textsf{ERROR}: nonnegativity, marginal incidence, stock positivity, or
      a defining identity fails.
\end{enumerate}
The last status is not a theorem verdict.  Separate endpoint laws and the
Hellinger midpoint may be supplied as useful consistency data, but do not
replace item~\textup{(C2)}.
\end{certificate}

\begin{theorem}[Version V21 integrated conclusion]
\label{thm:V21-integrated}
Versions~V1--V20 are retained.  Version~V21 additionally proves:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(I\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item the density-square-root incidence is a positive unitary but a Markov
      transport only when the natural and induced laws coincide;
\item exact dyadic identification of the fine blocked variable with the
      natural coarse variable is possible only on that projective-law branch;
\item an occurring old/fine coupling has an exact oriented source Gram, and
      one positive squared-difference writer reconstructs its signed mixed
      coefficient and Schur residual;
\item endpoint laws, all within-law moments, and the complete Hellinger card
      do not determine the occurring coupling;
\item the four-loop record coupling is sufficient for the scalar source
      target and admits a full conditional-fibre lift;
\item raw-record gluing and coefficient drift give the quantitative oriented
      transport bound \eqref{eq:V21-executable-gluing};
\item the transportation-polytope dual gives the sharp marginal-only range
      without fitting its optimizer as the physical route;
\item actual adjacent kernels produce one common cutoff path, and summable
      positive source differences yield a unique cofinal oriented source.
\end{enumerate}
No item populates the missing selected-root coupling, its positive source
loss, or the subsequent radial posterior loss.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Items~\textup{(I1)--(I2)} are
\Cref{thm:V21-half-density-not-Markov,thm:V21-single-variable-no-go}.
Item~\textup{(I3)} is \Cref{thm:V21-positive-oriented-read}.  Item~
\textup{(I4)} is \Cref{thm:V21-coupling-nonidentifiability}.  Item~
\textup{(I5)} is \Cref{thm:V21-record-lift}.  Item~\textup{(I6)} is
\Cref{thm:V21-gluing-theorem}.  Item~\textup{(I7)} is
\Cref{thm:V21-sharp-coupling-interval}.  Item~\textup{(I8)} is
\Cref{thm:V21-cofinal-coupling}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V22 direction: remove target inflation before reading another transport}
\label{sec:V22-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V21 proves a correct and useful statement: a density-square-root
unitary is not a Markov kernel unless the endpoint laws coincide, and an
actual stochastic re-equilibration route is not determined by its endpoint
marginals.  That theorem remains valid whenever the target includes a common
cutoff history, a transition kernel, or pathwise chronology.

The declared YM--B target is weaker.  It asks first for the old/fine mixed
\emph{source Gram} of the same four physical rectangle writers.  Versions
V18--V20 already place the natural coarse and blocked fine sources in one
Hilbert comparison by the canonical density-square-root incidence.  Requiring
an entire stochastic coupling merely to evaluate this one Gram is therefore a
target inflation unless a stochastic cutoff process is itself being claimed.

The distinction is not semantic.  The exact dyadic path identity of
\Cref{lem:V18-path-lift,cor:V18-no-shape-birth} says that the four rectangle
writers are the same bounded multiplication operators at the two cutoffs.
The correct linear incidence should consequently intertwine multiplication
by every common coarse writer.  Version~V22 proves that there is exactly one
positive unitary with this property: multiplication by
\(
 h=\sqrt{\dd\mu/\dd\nu}
\).
The Markov no-go of Version~V21 then becomes a separation theorem between two
different targets rather than an obstruction to the old/fine source Gram.

The present continuation makes this correction without deleting any earlier
material.  It then supplies two target-native acquisitions:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one positive half-density source-difference writer},\\
 \text{or one integrated source-speed bound along the actual action bridge}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V22-two-acquisitions}
\end{equation}
Either closes the signed module overlap.  A stochastic coupling remains an
optional stronger row for claims about re-equilibration histories.

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the V21 qualification]
\label{fire:V22-V21-scope}
No coupling theorem, transportation-polytope theorem, or common-history
promotion theorem of Version~V21 is withdrawn.  Their scope is the stronger
process target in which an old field and a fine-induced field jointly occur.
For the source-Gram target, however, the first incidence is the unique
positive same-observable module unitary.  A coupling kernel is not charged
unless the intended conclusion mentions a stochastic route, chronology, or
pathwise joint observable.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The unique order-positive same-observable module unitary}
\label{sec:V22-module-unitary}
% =============================================================================

Let \((\Omega,\mathscr F)\) be the common coarse configuration cylinder and
let \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) be mutually absolutely continuous probability laws.
The algebra \(L^\infty(\Omega,\mathscr F)\) acts by multiplication on both
\(L^2(\mu)\) and \(L^2(\nu)\).  Write these actions as
\(
 M_a^\mu
\) and \(
 M_a^\nu
\).

Fix any common dominating probability measure \(m\), and put
\begin{equation}
 p=\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd m},
 \qquad
 q=\frac{\dd\nu}{\dd m}.
 \label{eq:V22-pq}
\end{equation}
Define the amplitude embeddings
\begin{equation}
 J_\mu f=f\sqrt p,
 \qquad
 J_\nu g=g\sqrt q,
 \label{eq:V22-amplitude-embeddings}
\end{equation}
from the endpoint Hilbert spaces into \(L^2(m)\).

\begin{theorem}[Unique order-positive module incidence]
\label{thm:V22-module-uniqueness}
Let
\(
 T:L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\nu)
\)
be an order-positive unitary, meaning that $Tf\ge0$ whenever $f\ge0$, and satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T M_a^\mu=M_a^\nu T
 \quad\text{for every }a\in L^\infty(\Omega,\mathscr F).}
 \label{eq:V22-module-intertwining}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Tf=h f,
 \qquad
 h=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}}.}
 \label{eq:V22-unique-module-unitary}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{T=J_\nu^{-1}J_\mu.}
 \label{eq:V22-module-amplitude-factorization}
\end{equation}
If positivity is omitted but complex unitarity is retained, every module
unitary has the form
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{Tf=\omega h f,
 \qquad |\omega|=1\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.}
 \label{eq:V22-module-phase}
\end{equation}
On a real Hilbert space the phase is a measurable sign.  Positivity fixes the
orientation \(\omega=1\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put \(u=T\one\).  Positivity gives \(u\ge0\).  For every bounded
\(f\in L^2(\mu)\), the module identity gives
\[
 Tf=T(M_f^\mu\one)=M_f^\nu T\one=fu.
\]
Truncation and continuity extend this identity to all of \(L^2(\mu)\).
Unitarity now implies, for every bounded \(f\),
\[
 \int |f|^2u^2\,\dd\nu
 =\|Tf\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2
 =\|f\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2
 =\int |f|^2\,\dd\mu.
\]
Thus the finite measures \(u^2\nu\) and \(\mu\) agree on every bounded
measurable test function.  Hence
\(
 u^2=\dd\mu/\dd\nu
\)
\(\nu\)-almost everywhere.  Positivity gives \(u=h\), proving
\eqref{eq:V22-unique-module-unitary}.  Equations
\eqref{eq:V22-amplitude-embeddings} then give
\eqref{eq:V22-module-amplitude-factorization}.

Without positivity the same argument gives \(|u|=h\).  Writing
\(u=\omega h\) yields \(|\omega|=1\) and proves
\eqref{eq:V22-module-phase}.  Conversely every such multiplier is a module
unitary.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Target-native canonicity of the V18 old/fine Gram]
\label{cor:V22-V18-canonical}
Under the exact dyadic rectangle incidence of Version~V18, the law-aligned
Gram of \Cref{def:V18-old-fine-Gram} is the unique Gram obtained from a
order-positive unitary which preserves every common coarse multiplication writer.
In particular, the positive orientation of the mixed source line is fixed
before its value is read.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The path identity identifies every coarse rectangle writer with its pulled-
back fine writer.  Any positive same-observable Hilbert incidence must
therefore satisfy \eqref{eq:V22-module-intertwining}.  Apply
\Cref{thm:V22-module-uniqueness}.  The mixed entry is then exactly
\(
 \langle F_\nu,hF_\mu\rangle_{L^2(\nu)}
\), which is the entry in \Cref{def:V18-old-fine-Gram}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What unitality does and does not mean]
\label{ass:V22-unitality}
The identity \(U_h\one=h\) of \Cref{thm:V21-half-density-not-Markov} is
unchanged.  It proves that the canonical module unitary is not a Markov
operator when \(\mu\ne\nu\).  Unitality is necessary for a stochastic
transition, but it is not necessary for a unitary comparison of centered
source Hilbert spaces.  The latter is the immediate old/fine Gram target.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{A law-changing Markov route cannot preserve the same writer algebra}
\label{sec:V22-Markov-no-go}
% =============================================================================

The following theorem explains why replacing the module incidence by an
arbitrary coupling changes the target rather than completing it.

\begin{theorem}[Writer-faithful Markov no-go]
\label{thm:V22-Markov-module-no-go}
Let \(K(x,\dd y)\) be a Markov kernel on \((\Omega,\mathscr F)\), and let
\begin{equation}
 P_Kf(x)=\int f(y)K(x,\dd y)
 \label{eq:V22-Markov-operator}
\end{equation}
be its unital positive operator.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 P_KM_a=M_aP_K
 \quad\text{for every }a\in L^\infty(\Omega,\mathscr F),}
 \label{eq:V22-Markov-module}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{K(x,\cdot)=\delta_x
 \quad\text{for almost every }x.}
 \label{eq:V22-Markov-diagonal}
\end{equation}
Consequently a Markov kernel which changes \(\nu\) into a different law
\(\mu\) cannot simultaneously preserve the complete same-observable
multiplication module.

More generally, if \(\mathscr S\subseteq\mathscr F\) is a physical record and
\eqref{eq:V22-Markov-module} is imposed only for
\(a\in L^\infty(\mathscr S)\), then every coupling generated by \(K\) obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{S(Y)=S(X)\quad\text{almost surely}}
 \label{eq:V22-record-diagonal}
\end{equation}
for every bounded record coordinate \(S\).  Thus the two record marginals
must agree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Set \(f=\one\) in \eqref{eq:V22-Markov-module}.  Since \(P_K\one=\one\),
\[
 P_Ka=a
\]
for every bounded measurable \(a\).  Taking \(a=\one_A\) gives
\[
 K(x,A)=\one_A(x)
\]
for every measurable set in a determining class, and hence for every
\(A\in\mathscr F\).  This is \eqref{eq:V22-Markov-diagonal}.  The record
version is the same proof applied to record indicators.  Equality of every
record coordinate follows by bounded approximation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Meaning of the V21 coupling interval]
\label{cor:V22-coupling-meaning}
The multiple coupling coefficients constructed in
\Cref{thm:V21-coupling-nonidentifiability} are genuine values of different
stochastic common histories.  Except for the diagonal case, they are not
same-observable module incidences.  Their variability therefore does not make
the canonical module coefficient ambiguous.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The canonical module coefficient is unique by
\Cref{thm:V22-module-uniqueness}.  A nontrivial coupling kernel cannot obey
the complete multiplication intertwining by
\Cref{thm:V22-Markov-module-no-go}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{One positive half-density source-difference writer}
\label{sec:V22-positive-distance}
% =============================================================================

Retain the balanced endpoint sources \(F_\nu,F_\mu\) and stocks
\(\sigma_\nu^2,\sigma_\mu^2\) of Version~V18.  In the common amplitude space
\(L^2(m)\), put
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_\nu=F_\nu\sqrt q,
 \qquad
 \Phi_\mu=F_\mu\sqrt p.
 \label{eq:V22-source-amplitudes}
\end{equation}
Their norms are the two endpoint stocks.

\begin{definition}[Positive module-distance Read]
\label{def:V22-module-distance}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}
 :=\|\Phi_\nu-\Phi_\mu\|_{L^2(m)}^2
 =\int
  \left(F_\nu\sqrt q-F_\mu\sqrt p\right)^2\dd m.}
 \label{eq:V22-module-distance}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One positive writer reconstructs the signed old/fine Gram]
\label{thm:V22-positive-module-card}
The module distance satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}
 =\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2-2c_{Y/X}.}
 \label{eq:V22-distance-polarization}
\end{equation}
Hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_{Y/X}
 =\frac{\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2-D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}}{2}.}
 \label{eq:V22-cross-from-distance}
\end{equation}
When both stocks are positive,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =\frac{\sigma_\nu^2+\sigma_\mu^2-D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}}
        {2\sigma_\nu\sigma_\mu}.}
 \label{eq:V22-alpha-from-distance}
\end{equation}
The normalized oriented defect and unsigned Schur residual are
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 D_{Y/X}^{\rm ori}
 :=\left\|
 \frac{\Phi_\nu}{\sigma_\nu}
 -\frac{\Phi_\mu}{\sigma_\mu}
 \right\|_2^2
 =2(1-\alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}),}
 \label{eq:V22-oriented-distance}\\
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 =1-(\alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal})^2
 =D_{Y/X}^{\rm ori}
  -\frac14(D_{Y/X}^{\rm ori})^2.}
 \label{eq:V22-Schur-from-distance}
\end{align}
Thus the three nonnegative endpoint quantities
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sigma_\nu^2,
 \qquad
 \sigma_\mu^2,
 \qquad
 D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}}
 \label{eq:V22-three-scalar-card}
\end{equation}
form a complete signed old/fine module card.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand the square in \eqref{eq:V22-module-distance}.  Its diagonal terms are
\[
 \int F_\nu^2q\,\dd m=\sigma_\nu^2,
 \qquad
 \int F_\mu^2p\,\dd m=\sigma_\mu^2,
\]
and its cross term is
\[
 \int F_\nu F_\mu\sqrt{pq}\,\dd m=c_{Y/X}.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:V22-distance-polarization}--
\eqref{eq:V22-alpha-from-distance}.  Expanding the squared distance of the
two unit amplitudes proves \eqref{eq:V22-oriented-distance}.  Substituting
\(\alpha=1-D^{\rm ori}/2\) into \(1-\alpha^2\) proves
\eqref{eq:V22-Schur-from-distance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One bounded positive endpoint-mixture writer]
\label{cor:V22-mixture-writer}
Let
\begin{equation}
 \overline\pi=\frac12(\mu+\nu).
 \label{eq:V22-mixture-law}
\end{equation}
On the set \(p+q>0\), define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr D_{Y/X}^{\rm mix}
 =\frac{2\left(F_\nu\sqrt q-F_\mu\sqrt p\right)^2}{p+q}.}
 \label{eq:V22-mixture-writer}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_{\overline\pi}\mathscr D_{Y/X}^{\rm mix}
 =D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}.}
 \label{eq:V22-mixture-expectation}
\end{equation}
For the balanced four-loop source, \(|F_\nu|,|F_\mu|\le3\), and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{0\le\mathscr D_{Y/X}^{\rm mix}\le36.}
 \label{eq:V22-mixture-bound}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, in the blocked-action notation of Version~V19,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}
 =\int\left(
  \frac{F_\nu e^{-S_0/2}}{\sqrt{Z_0}}
  -\frac{F_\mu e^{-S_1/2}}{\sqrt{Z_1}}
 \right)^2\dd m_M.}
 \label{eq:V22-action-square}
\end{equation}
Thus deterministic integration of one nonnegative common-action insertion,
or one calibrated endpoint-mixture Read, populates the old/fine module Gram
without constructing a stochastic re-equilibration kernel.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The density of \(\overline\pi\) relative to \(m\) is \((p+q)/2\), so the
factors in \eqref{eq:V22-mixture-writer} cancel and give
\eqref{eq:V22-mixture-expectation}.  Moreover,
\[
 2(a-b)^2\le4(a^2+b^2)
\]
with \(a=F_\nu\sqrt q\) and \(b=F_\mu\sqrt p\).  Since
\(a^2+b^2\le9(p+q)\), the pointwise bound follows.  Substituting
\(q=Z_0^{-1}e^{-S_0}\) and \(p=Z_1^{-1}e^{-S_1}\) proves
\eqref{eq:V22-action-square}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Independence of the dominating measure]
\label{prop:V22-dominating-independence}
The amplitudes, module distance, mixed coefficient, oriented defect, and
Schur residual above are independent of the choice of common dominating
measure.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(m'=r m\) with \(r>0\).  The unitary
\[
 V:L^2(m)\longrightarrow L^2(m'),
 \qquad Vg=r^{-1/2}g,
\]
sends
\[
 F_\lambda\sqrt{\frac{\dd\lambda}{\dd m}}
 \quad\text{to}\quad
 F_\lambda\sqrt{\frac{\dd\lambda}{\dd m'}}
\]
for \(\lambda\in\{\mu,\nu\}\).  Hence it preserves all norms and inner
products used in the definitions.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{A sign-safe finite interval certificate}
\label{sec:V22-interval}
% =============================================================================

\begin{certificate}[Target-native module card]
\label{cert:V22-module-card}
Suppose validated outward intervals are available:
\begin{equation}
 \underline s_T\le\sigma_T^2\le\overline s_T,
 \qquad T\in\{\nu,\mu\},
 \qquad
 \underline D\le D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}\le\overline D,
 \label{eq:V22-input-intervals}
\end{equation}
with \(\underline s_\nu,\underline s_\mu>0\).  Put
\begin{equation}
 n_-:=\underline s_\nu+\underline s_\mu-\overline D,
 \qquad
 n_+:=\overline s_\nu+\overline s_\mu-\underline D,
 \label{eq:V22-numerator-interval}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 d_-:=2\sqrt{\underline s_\nu\underline s_\mu},
 \qquad
 d_+:=2\sqrt{\overline s_\nu\overline s_\mu}.
 \label{eq:V22-denominator-interval}
\end{equation}
Then the oriented coefficient belongs to the outward interval
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \in
 \left[
  \min_{\substack{n\in\{n_-,n_+\}\\ d\in\{d_-,d_+\}}}\frac nd,
  \max_{\substack{n\in\{n_-,n_+\}\\ d\in\{d_-,d_+\}}}\frac nd
 \right]\cap[-1,1].}
 \label{eq:V22-alpha-interval}
\end{equation}
The interval for \(D^{\rm ori}=2(1-\alpha)\) follows by reversing endpoints;
the Schur interval is obtained by evaluating \(1-\alpha^2\) at the interval
endpoints and at zero when zero is included.

For exact point data, the Hilbert-domain condition is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (\sigma_\nu-\sigma_\mu)^2
 \le D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}
 \le(\sigma_\nu+\sigma_\mu)^2.}
 \label{eq:V22-Hilbert-domain}
\end{equation}
Violation is an ill-typed input, not a Yang--Mills obstruction.  A strictly
negative upper endpoint for \(\alpha\) is a counterorientation obstruction;
a small upper endpoint for \(D^{\rm ori}\) is an oriented pass; every
remaining overlapping interval is \textsf{UNRESOLVED}.
\end{certificate}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V22-alpha-from-distance} gives a numerator in
\([n_-/2,n_+/2]\) and a positive denominator in
\([\sqrt{\underline s_\nu\underline s_\mu},
  \sqrt{\overline s_\nu\overline s_\mu}]\).
The extrema of \(n/d\) over a rectangle with \(d>0\) occur at its four
corners, proving \eqref{eq:V22-alpha-interval}.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V22-Hilbert-domain} is the triangle and reverse-triangle inequality
for the two amplitude vectors.  The remaining transformations are exact
monotone interval maps on the stated domains.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The exact source speed along the Wilson action bridge}
\label{sec:V22-source-speed}
% =============================================================================

The positive distance of the preceding section is target minimal.  When it
is easier to control the complete interpolation between the blocked and
natural actions, one can instead bound the same endpoint angle by a local
source-speed integral.

Let \(t\mapsto S_t\) be a continuously differentiable action path on the
fixed compact coarse cylinder, with
\begin{equation}
 p_t=Z_t^{-1}e^{-S_t},
 \qquad
 \dd\pi_t=p_t\,\dd m,
 \qquad
 s_t:=\partial_t\log p_t
 =-\dot S_t+\mathbb E_{\pi_t}\dot S_t.
 \label{eq:V22-path-score}
\end{equation}
Let \(F_t\) be a continuously differentiable real centered source family and
assume
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_t^2:=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}F_t^2>0
 \quad(0\le t\le1).
 \label{eq:V22-path-stock}
\end{equation}
Define its unit amplitude in the fixed space \(L^2(m)\) by
\begin{equation}
 \Psi_t:=\frac{F_t\sqrt{p_t}}{\sigma_t}.
 \label{eq:V22-unit-source-path}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact module-Fisher source speed]
\label{thm:V22-source-speed}
Put
\begin{equation}
 G_t:=\dot F_t+\frac12s_tF_t,
 \label{eq:V22-Gt}
\end{equation}
and let \(P_t\) be the rank-one orthogonal projection in \(L^2(\pi_t)\) onto
\(F_t\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\dot\Psi_t\|_{L^2(m)}^2
 =\mathcal E_t^{\rm src},}
 \label{eq:V22-speed-identity}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_t^{\rm src}
 :=\frac{\|(I-P_t)G_t\|_{L^2(\pi_t)}^2}{\sigma_t^2}}
 \label{eq:V22-source-energy-projection}\\
 \boxed{
 \phantom{\mathcal E_t^{\rm src}}
 =\frac{\mathbb E_{\pi_t}G_t^2}{\sigma_t^2}
  -\frac{(\mathbb E_{\pi_t}F_tG_t)^2}{\sigma_t^4}
 \ge0.}
 \label{eq:V22-source-energy-scalar}
\end{align}
Thus \(\mathcal E_t^{\rm src}\) removes the irrelevant instantaneous
rescaling of the source line and measures only motion of its normalized
module direction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the stock:
\[
 \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\sigma_t^2
 =\mathbb E_{\pi_t}(2F_t\dot F_t+s_tF_t^2)
 =2\mathbb E_{\pi_t}(F_tG_t).
\]
Therefore
\(
 \dot\sigma_t=\mathbb E(F_tG_t)/\sigma_t
\).
Differentiating \eqref{eq:V22-unit-source-path} gives
\[
 \dot\Psi_t
 =\frac{\sqrt{p_t}}{\sigma_t}
  \left(
   G_t-\frac{\mathbb E_{\pi_t}(F_tG_t)}{\sigma_t^2}F_t
  \right).
\]
Taking the \(L^2(m)\) norm proves
\eqref{eq:V22-speed-identity}--\eqref{eq:V22-source-energy-scalar}.
Nonnegativity is also the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Explicit balanced four-loop derivative]
\label{prop:V22-balanced-derivative}
On the affine action path of Version~V19, put
\begin{equation}
 W_t=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}\mathbf O_M,
 \qquad
 b_t=D_{W_t}^{-1}\varepsilon_\square,
 \qquad
 u_t=\frac{b_t}{\|b_t\|_2},
 \qquad
 F_t=u_t^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_M-W_t).
 \label{eq:V22-balanced-path}
\end{equation}
Assume every component of \(W_t\) is positive.  Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{\dot W_t=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[\mathbf O_Ms_t],}
 \label{eq:V22-Wdot}\\
 \boxed{
 (\dot b_t)_\alpha
 =-\varepsilon_{\square,\alpha}
   \frac{\dot W_{t,\alpha}}{W_{t,\alpha}^2},}
 \label{eq:V22-bdot}\\
 \boxed{
 \dot u_t
 =\frac{(I-u_tu_t^{\mathsf T})\dot b_t}{\|b_t\|_2},}
 \label{eq:V22-udot}\\
 \boxed{
 \dot F_t
 =\dot u_t^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O_M-W_t)
  -u_t^{\mathsf T}\dot W_t.}
 \label{eq:V22-Fdot}
\end{align}
Hence every entry of \(\mathcal E_t^{\rm src}\) is an expectation of the
four original rectangle writers and the action-path score on the same bridge
law.  No stochastic old/fine kernel is used.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For a fixed bounded writer \(A\), differentiation of
\(\mathbb E_{\pi_t}A\) gives \(\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[As_t]\), proving
\eqref{eq:V22-Wdot}.  The remaining identities are ordinary differentiation
of \(b_t\), its Euclidean normalization, and the centered linear source.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint angle from the source path]
\label{cor:V22-path-angle}
Assume
\(
 F_0=F_\nu
\),
\(
 F_1=F_\mu
\),
\(
 p_0=q
\), and
\(
 p_1=p
\).
Put
\begin{equation}
 L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}
 :=\int_0^1\sqrt{\mathcal E_t^{\rm src}}\,\dd t.
 \label{eq:V22-source-length}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \sqrt{D_{Y/X}^{\rm ori}}
 \le L_{Y/X}^{\rm src},}
 \label{eq:V22-chord-length}\\
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \ge\cos\!\left(\min\{L_{Y/X}^{\rm src},\pi\}\right).}
 \label{eq:V22-angle-length}
\end{align}
In particular, if \(L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}<\pi/2\), then the source is
positively oriented and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
 \le\sin^2 L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}.}
 \label{eq:V22-Schur-length}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The curve \(\Psi_t\) lies on the unit sphere of \(L^2(m)\), and
\Cref{thm:V22-source-speed} identifies its speed.  The chord between its
endpoints is no longer than its arc length, proving
\eqref{eq:V22-chord-length}.  The spherical geodesic distance between the
endpoints is
\(
 \arccos\alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm bal}
\)
and is also no longer than the path length.  Monotonicity of cosine on
\([0,\pi]\) proves \eqref{eq:V22-angle-length}.  The last claim follows from
\(1-\alpha^2\le1-\cos^2L\) on the positively oriented branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite bridge quadrature and cofinal module landing]
\label{cor:V22-bridge-quadrature}
Let
\(
 0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_J=1
\)
be fixed before evaluation, and suppose validated upper bounds
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_t^{\rm src}\le\overline E_j
 \quad(t_{j-1}\le t\le t_j)
 \label{eq:V22-energy-panels}
\end{equation}
are available.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}
 \le\overline L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}
 :=\sum_{j=1}^J(t_j-t_{j-1})\sqrt{\overline E_j}.}
 \label{eq:V22-length-upper}
\end{equation}
A bound \(\overline L<\pi/2\) gives the signed pass interval of
\Cref{cor:V22-path-angle}.

Along a cofinal adjacent-cutoff sequence, assume the inherited exact dyadic
writer incidences and common-screen embeddings.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sum_n\overline L_{n+1/n}^{\rm src}<\infty,}
 \label{eq:V22-length-summability}
\end{equation}
then the unit balanced source amplitudes converge strongly to a unique
oriented unit source on that screen.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is integration of the pointwise upper bounds.  For the
cofinal statement, \eqref{eq:V22-chord-length} bounds every adjacent source
increment by \(\overline L_{n+1/n}^{\rm src}\).  The summability assumption
makes the source amplitudes Cauchy.  Completeness of the common Hilbert screen
gives the strong limit, and every vector has unit norm.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[A sufficient path bound is not a negative verdict]
\label{fire:V22-path-not-obstruction}
The direct positive distance \(D_{Y/X}^{\rm mod}\) is target minimal.  The
bridge length is a sufficient upper bound which may be nonsharp because a
path can turn while its endpoints remain close.  Failure of a finite energy
panel to make \(\overline L\) small is therefore \textsf{UNRESOLVED}; it is
not a cutoff-transport obstruction unless the endpoint distance itself is
bounded below.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Version V22 target-native incidence theorem]
\label{thm:V22-integrated}
Preserving Versions~V1--V21, the following statements are now proved.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V22.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.6em]
\item The exact dyadic rectangle identity determines one common multiplication
      algebra for the old and fine source writers.
\item The density-square-root multiplier is the unique order-positive unitary
      intertwining that algebra.  Its positive orientation is canonical.
\item A law-changing Markov kernel cannot preserve the same complete writer
      algebra.  Stochastic re-equilibration is therefore a stronger target,
      not a missing premise of the source Gram.
\item One positive half-density source-difference writer and the two diagonal
      stocks reconstruct the complete signed old/fine module Gram.
\item The same distance is the expectation of a bounded nonnegative writer on
      the fifty-fifty endpoint mixture, or one positive insertion on the
      common blocked/natural action cylinder.
\item The complete signed interval is denominator safe and distinguishes an
      oriented pass, counterorientation, unresolved overlap, and ill-typed
      Hilbert data.
\item Along the actual action bridge, the normalized source speed is the
      positive projected form \eqref{eq:V22-source-energy-scalar}; its path
      length bounds the endpoint oriented defect and gives a finite
      quadrature compiler.
\item Summable source-bridge lengths give a unique strong cofinal module
      source without constructing a stochastic cutoff history.
\end{enumerate}
No item evaluates a selected-root Wilson integral or the positive-width
radial posterior.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Items~\textup{(V22.1)--(V22.3)} are
\Cref{thm:V22-module-uniqueness,cor:V22-V18-canonical,thm:V22-Markov-module-no-go}.
Items~\textup{(V22.4)--(V22.6)} are
\Cref{thm:V22-positive-module-card,cor:V22-mixture-writer,prop:V22-dominating-independence,cert:V22-module-card}.
Items~\textup{(V22.7)--(V22.8)} are
\Cref{thm:V22-source-speed,prop:V22-balanced-derivative,cor:V22-path-angle,cor:V22-bridge-quadrature}.
The limitation is the absence of the finite Wilson values named below.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Corrected status of the first old/fine row]

\end{assessment}
