\section{Version V23 direction: the endpoint source Gram precedes, but does not transport, the boundary message}
\label{sec:V23-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V22 identified the unique positive same-observable module incidence
between the natural coarse Wilson law and the induced blocked fine law.  Its
positive module distance is exactly the old/fine \emph{source-level} Gram.
That theorem remains correct.  It does not yet say that conditional
expectation onto a physical boundary shell commutes with the change of law,
nor that the native fine shell contains no additional detail beyond the
lifted coarse shell.

This is the first unclosed arrow.  The physical source must be fixed before
boundary conditioning, then propagated through the actual conditional-
expectation map, and only afterward compared at the output.  Re-centering or
rebalancing the source separately in every boundary cell erases the message
by construction and is therefore a different experiment.

The corrected order is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{finite selected-root source and its global coefficient direction}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{native fine shell and lifted coarse shell records}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{fine boundary-detail birth}
 +\text{ shared-record law/conditioning defect}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{complete old/fine boundary-message Gram}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{positive-width Bayes-reverse radial loss and the cofinal trichotomy}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V23-upstream-order}
\end{equation}

The present continuation proves the complete Hilbert-space square behind
this order.  It does not introduce another endpoint Hellinger comparison,
another radial estimator, or a stochastic cutoff history.

\begin{firewall}[The V22 source-level theorem is retained]
\label{fire:V23-V22-retained}
The module incidence and positive distance of Version~V22 continue to be the
canonical comparison of the two complete source amplitudes.  Version~V23
adds the source-to-boundary propagation row needed when the target is the
boundary message itself.  It does not reclassify a source-level pass as a
failure; it proves that such a pass is not, by itself, a boundary-message
transport theorem.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The balanced source is frozen before every boundary decomposition}
\label{sec:V23-fixed-source}
% =============================================================================

Let \((\Omega,\mathscr F,\lambda)\) be one finite selected-root Wilson card,
let
\[
 \mathbf O=(\mathcal O_{11},\mathcal O_{00},
             \mathcal O_{10},\mathcal O_{01})^{\mathsf T}
\]
be the four physical rectangle writers, and put
\begin{equation}
 W:=\mathbb E_\lambda\mathbf O,
 \qquad
 u:=\frac{D_W^{-1}\varepsilon_\square}
          {\|D_W^{-1}\varepsilon_\square\|_2},
 \qquad
 F:=u^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O-W).
 \label{eq:V23-fixed-balanced-source}
\end{equation}
The vector \(u\) is fixed from the complete endpoint law before a boundary
record is exposed.  Let \(\mathscr B\subseteq\mathscr F\) be a physical shell
record and define
\begin{equation}
 W_{\mathscr B}:=\mathbb E_\lambda[\mathbf O\mid\mathscr B],
 \qquad
 M_{\mathscr B}:=\mathbb E_\lambda[F\mid\mathscr B]
 =u^{\mathsf T}(W_{\mathscr B}-W).
 \label{eq:V23-boundary-message-explicit}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-source boundary Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V23-fixed-source-Pythagoras}
The source has the exact orthogonal decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 F=u^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O-W_{\mathscr B})+M_{\mathscr B},}
 \label{eq:V23-fixed-source-split}
\end{equation}
where the first term has zero conditional mean given \(\mathscr B\).  Hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|F\|_{L^2(\lambda)}^2
 =\|u^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O-W_{\mathscr B})\|_2^2
  +\|M_{\mathscr B}\|_2^2.}
 \label{eq:V23-fixed-source-stock-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}

More generally, let \(v_{\mathscr B}\) be any square-integrable
\(\mathscr B\)-measurable coefficient field and define the boundary-retuned
writer
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde F_{\mathscr B}
 :=v_{\mathscr B}^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O-W_{\mathscr B}).
 \label{eq:V23-retuned-source}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_\lambda[\widetilde F_{\mathscr B}\mid\mathscr B]=0,}
 \label{eq:V23-retuned-message-zero}
\end{equation}
while
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \|F-\widetilde F_{\mathscr B}\|_2^2
 ={}&\|M_{\mathscr B}\|_2^2\\
 &+\|(u-v_{\mathscr B})^{\mathsf T}
       (\mathbf O-W_{\mathscr B})\|_2^2.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V23-retuning-distance}
\end{equation}
In particular, even the apparently harmless cellwise re-centering obtained
by taking \(v_{\mathscr B}=u\) deletes exactly the complete boundary-message
stock.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Add and subtract \(W_{\mathscr B}\) in
\eqref{eq:V23-fixed-balanced-source}.  Conditional expectation gives
\eqref{eq:V23-boundary-message-explicit}; the residual is orthogonal to every
\(\mathscr B\)-measurable function, proving
\eqref{eq:V23-fixed-source-stock-Pythagoras}.

Because \(v_{\mathscr B}\) is measurable with respect to the conditioning
record,
\[
 \mathbb E_\lambda[
 v_{\mathscr B}^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf O-W_{\mathscr B})
 \mid\mathscr B]=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 F-\widetilde F_{\mathscr B}
 =M_{\mathscr B}
  +(u-v_{\mathscr B})^{\mathsf T}
    (\mathbf O-W_{\mathscr B}).
\]
The two summands are respectively \(\mathscr B\)-measurable and
conditionally centered, hence orthogonal.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V23-retuning-distance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Boundary retuning is not a radial proof]
\label{ass:V23-no-boundary-retuning}
The coefficients in the physical Creutz source are fixed by the complete
selected-root endpoint law.  Recomputing rectangle means or a balanced
coefficient direction after conditioning defines a new, boundary-dependent
source.  Its vanishing conditional mean is tautological and cannot be used
as evidence of radial contraction of the original source.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The conditional-expectation/module intertwining defect}
\label{sec:V23-conditional-square}
% =============================================================================

Let \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) be mutually absolutely continuous probability laws
on one common coarse configuration cylinder \((\Omega,\mathscr F)\), and let
\(\mathscr B\subseteq\mathscr F\) be the common physical boundary record.
Write
\begin{equation}
 h:=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu}{\dd\nu}},
 \qquad
 h_{\mathscr B}
 :=\left(\mathbb E_\nu[h^2\mid\mathscr B]\right)^{1/2}
 =\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu_{\mathscr B}}
               {\dd\nu_{\mathscr B}}}.
 \label{eq:V23-full-boundary-roots}
\end{equation}
Let \(E_\lambda^{\mathscr B}\) denote conditional expectation under the law
\(\lambda\), and let
\[
 U_hf=hf,
 \qquad
 U_{h_{\mathscr B}}g=h_{\mathscr B}g
\]
be the unique positive full and boundary module unitaries of Version~V22.

\begin{definition}[Conditional-expectation intertwining defect]
\label{def:V23-intertwining-defect}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}
 :=E_\nu^{\mathscr B}U_h
   -U_{h_{\mathscr B}}E_\mu^{\mathscr B}
 :L^2(\mu)\longrightarrow L^2(\nu_{\mathscr B}).}
 \label{eq:V23-intertwining-defect}
\end{equation}
It measures whether transport of a source followed by boundary conditioning
agrees with boundary conditioning followed by transport of the boundary
message.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact conditional square and sharp fibre norm]
\label{thm:V23-conditional-square}
For every \(f\in L^2(\mu)\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 E_\mu^{\mathscr B}f
 =\frac{E_\nu^{\mathscr B}(h^2f)}{h_{\mathscr B}^2},}
 \label{eq:V23-Bayes-conditional}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}f
 =\frac{1}{h_{\mathscr B}}
   E_\nu^{\mathscr B}
   \left[h(h_{\mathscr B}-h)f\right].}
 \label{eq:V23-defect-formula}
\end{equation}

Let \(\mu_b,\nu_b\) be regular conditional laws on the boundary fibre and
write
\begin{equation}
 h=h_{\mathscr B}(b)h_b,
 \qquad
 h_b=\sqrt{\frac{\dd\mu_b}{\dd\nu_b}},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathscr B}(b)
 :=\int h_b\,\dd\nu_b.
 \label{eq:V23-fibre-root-affinity}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}f)(b)
 =h_{\mathscr B}(b)
  \mathbb E_{\mu_b}
  \left[(h_b^{-1}-1)f\right],}
 \label{eq:V23-fibre-functional}
\end{equation}
and the operator norm is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\|_{L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\nu_{\mathscr B})}^2
 =\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{b\sim\mu_{\mathscr B}}
   2\bigl(1-\rho_{\mathscr B}(b)\bigr).}
 \label{eq:V23-sharp-defect-norm}
\end{equation}
Consequently the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item \(\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}=0\);
\item \(h\) is \(\mathscr B\)-measurable;
\item \(\rho_{\mathscr B}=1\) almost everywhere;
\item \(\mu_b=\nu_b\) for almost every physical boundary record.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every bounded \(\mathscr B\)-measurable test function \(a\),
\[
 \int a f\,\dd\mu
 =\int a h^2f\,\dd\nu
 =\int a E_\nu^{\mathscr B}(h^2f)\,\dd\nu.
\]
Since \(\dd\mu_{\mathscr B}=h_{\mathscr B}^2\dd\nu_{\mathscr B}\), this is
\eqref{eq:V23-Bayes-conditional}.  Substitution into
\eqref{eq:V23-intertwining-defect} gives
\[
 E_\nu^{\mathscr B}(hf)
 -\frac{E_\nu^{\mathscr B}(h^2f)}{h_{\mathscr B}}
 =\frac{E_\nu^{\mathscr B}[h(h_{\mathscr B}-h)f]}
        {h_{\mathscr B}},
\]
proving \eqref{eq:V23-defect-formula}.

Disintegration of the Radon--Nikodym derivative gives
\(h=h_{\mathscr B}h_b\) and \(\dd\mu_b=h_b^2\dd\nu_b\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}f(b)
 =h_{\mathscr B}(b)
  \left(\int h_bf\,\dd\nu_b-\int f\,\dd\mu_b\right)
 =h_{\mathscr B}(b)
  \mathbb E_{\mu_b}[(h_b^{-1}-1)f],
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V23-fibre-functional}.

The fibre functional on \(L^2(\mu_b)\) has squared norm
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \int(h_b^{-1}-1)^2\,\dd\mu_b
 &=\int(1-h_b)^2\,\dd\nu_b\\
 &=2\left(1-\int h_b\,\dd\nu_b\right)
 =2(1-\rho_{\mathscr B}(b)).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Moreover,
\(h_{\mathscr B}^2\dd\nu_{\mathscr B}=\dd\mu_{\mathscr B}\).
Thus \(\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\) is the direct integral of these scalar
fibre functionals over \(\mu_{\mathscr B}\), and its norm is the essential
supremum of their norms.  This proves
\eqref{eq:V23-sharp-defect-norm}.  The equality cases are exactly the equality
cases of conditional Hellinger affinity, as in the source-record theorem of
Version~V19.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source-specific conditional-incidence bound]
\label{cor:V23-source-specific-incidence}
For every \(f\in L^2(\mu)\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}f\|_2^2
 \le
 2\int
   \bigl(1-\rho_{\mathscr B}(b)\bigr)
   \mathbb E_{\mu_b}|f|^2\,
   \mu_{\mathscr B}(\dd b).}
 \label{eq:V23-source-specific-bound}
\end{equation}
If \(|f|\le M\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}f\|_2^2
 \le2M^2
 \left[1-\mathbb E_{\mu_{\mathscr B}}
                 \rho_{\mathscr B}^2\right].}
 \label{eq:V23-null-fibre-bound}
\end{equation}
The right side is a conservative use of the Version~V19 conditional-fibre
residual on the present physical boundary record.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to the fibre functional in
\eqref{eq:V23-fibre-functional} and use its squared norm computed in the
proof of \Cref{thm:V23-conditional-square}.  This gives
\eqref{eq:V23-source-specific-bound}.  Since
\(0\le\rho_{\mathscr B}\le1\), one has
\(1-\rho_{\mathscr B}\le1-\rho_{\mathscr B}^2\), proving
\eqref{eq:V23-null-fibre-bound}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The shared-record old/fine boundary-message card}
\label{sec:V23-shared-message}
% =============================================================================

Let \(F_\nu,F_\mu\) be the endpoint balanced sources, with positive stocks
\(\sigma_\nu^2,\sigma_\mu^2\), and put
\begin{equation}
 \psi_\nu:=F_\nu/\sigma_\nu,
 \qquad
 \psi_\mu:=F_\mu/\sigma_\mu.
 \label{eq:V23-unit-endpoint-sources}
\end{equation}
Their endpoint oriented module defect is the Version~V22 quantity
\begin{equation}
 d_{\rm src}
 :=\|\psi_\nu-h\psi_\mu\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2
 =D_{Y/X}^{\rm ori}.
 \label{eq:V23-endpoint-source-defect}
\end{equation}
Define the two boundary messages and the transported old message by
\begin{equation}
 m_\nu:=E_\nu^{\mathscr B}\psi_\nu,
 \qquad
 m_\mu:=E_\mu^{\mathscr B}\psi_\mu,
 \qquad
 \widetilde m_\mu:=h_{\mathscr B}m_\mu.
 \label{eq:V23-three-boundary-messages}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-to-message rectangle]
\label{thm:V23-source-message-rectangle}
Put
\begin{equation}
 a_{\mathscr B}
 :=E_\nu^{\mathscr B}(\psi_\nu-h\psi_\mu),
 \qquad
 c_{\mathscr B}
 :=\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\psi_\mu.
 \label{eq:V23-two-message-defects}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 m_\nu-\widetilde m_\mu
 =a_{\mathscr B}+c_{\mathscr B}.}
 \label{eq:V23-message-rectangle}
\end{equation}
The positive matrix
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\mathscr B}^{\rm rect}
 :=\begin{pmatrix}
   \|a_{\mathscr B}\|_2^2&
   \langle a_{\mathscr B},c_{\mathscr B}\rangle\\
   \langle c_{\mathscr B},a_{\mathscr B}\rangle&
   \|c_{\mathscr B}\|_2^2
  \end{pmatrix}\succeq0}
 \label{eq:V23-rectangle-Gram}
\end{equation}
contains the complete interference between endpoint source motion and the
conditional-incidence defect.  In particular, with
\begin{equation}
 d_{\rm int}:=\|c_{\mathscr B}\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\rm sh}:=\|m_\nu-\widetilde m_\mu\|_2^2,
 \label{eq:V23-shared-defects}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\sqrt{d_{\rm sh}}-\sqrt{d_{\rm int}}\right|
 \le\sqrt{d_{\rm src}},}
 \label{eq:V23-shared-defect-sandwich}
\end{equation}
and hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \bigl(\max\{0,\sqrt{d_{\rm int}}-\sqrt{d_{\rm src}}\}\bigr)^2
 \le d_{\rm sh}
 \le(\sqrt{d_{\rm int}}+\sqrt{d_{\rm src}})^2.}
 \label{eq:V23-shared-defect-interval}
\end{equation}
Thus, after the endpoint module distance tends to zero, the shared-boundary
message defect is asymptotically exactly the conditional-expectation
intertwining defect.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By the definition of \(\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\),
\[
 E_\nu^{\mathscr B}(h\psi_\mu)
 =h_{\mathscr B}E_\mu^{\mathscr B}\psi_\mu
  +\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\psi_\mu.
\]
Subtract this identity from \(m_\nu\), proving
\eqref{eq:V23-message-rectangle}.  The displayed matrix is the Gram of the
two vectors in \eqref{eq:V23-two-message-defects}.  Conditional expectation
is contractive, so
\(
 \|a_{\mathscr B}\|_2\le\sqrt{d_{\rm src}}
\).
The reverse triangle inequality applied to
\eqref{eq:V23-message-rectangle} gives
\eqref{eq:V23-shared-defect-sandwich}; squaring its two one-sided forms gives
\eqref{eq:V23-shared-defect-interval}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One positive shared-record writer gives the boundary Gram]
\label{cor:V23-shared-boundary-Gram}
Define the source-relative visible stocks
\begin{equation}
 i_\nu:=\|m_\nu\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 i_\mu:=\|m_\mu\|_2^2
          =\|\widetilde m_\mu\|_{L^2(\nu_{\mathscr B})}^2.
 \label{eq:V23-shared-visible-stocks}
\end{equation}
Then the complete shared-record mixed entry is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_{\mathscr B}^{\rm msg}
 =\langle m_\nu,\widetilde m_\mu\rangle
 =\frac{i_\nu+i_\mu-d_{\rm sh}}{2}.}
 \label{eq:V23-shared-cross-from-distance}
\end{equation}
If \(i_\nu i_\mu>0\), its oriented coefficient is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{\mathscr B}^{\rm msg}
 =\frac{i_\nu+i_\mu-d_{\rm sh}}
        {2\sqrt{i_\nu i_\mu}}.}
 \label{eq:V23-shared-message-angle}
\end{equation}
Thus the target-minimal shared-record card is the two visible stocks plus the
one nonnegative writer \(|m_\nu-\widetilde m_\mu|^2\).  The two-component
Gram \eqref{eq:V23-rectangle-Gram} is needed only when attribution between
source motion and conditional incidence is part of the target.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The boundary module multiplier \(h_{\mathscr B}\) is unitary from
\(L^2(\mu_{\mathscr B})\) to \(L^2(\nu_{\mathscr B})\).  Expanding the
squared distance in \eqref{eq:V23-shared-defects} gives
\eqref{eq:V23-shared-cross-from-distance}; normalization gives
\eqref{eq:V23-shared-message-angle}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Native fine boundary detail and the complete two-row message Pythagoras}
\label{sec:V23-fine-detail}
% =============================================================================

Let \((\widehat\Omega_Y,\widehat\nu_Y)\) be the native fine Wilson card,
let
\[
 \pi=B_{Y\to X}:\widehat\Omega_Y\longrightarrow\Omega_X
\]
be the exact dyadic block map, and let \(\nu=\pi_*\widehat\nu_Y\).  The
exact rectangle identity of Version~V18 gives
\begin{equation}
 \psi_Y=\psi_\nu\circ\pi.
 \label{eq:V23-fine-source-lift}
\end{equation}
Let \(\mathscr B_X\) be the physical coarse shell record and assume the
native fine shell has been chosen so that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X\subseteq\mathscr B_Y.}
 \label{eq:V23-boundary-record-nesting}
\end{equation}
This is a literal incidence condition on the two shell geometries, not an
automatic consequence of the source path identity.

Define
\begin{equation}
 m_Y^{\rm nat}
 :=\mathbb E_{\widehat\nu_Y}[\psi_Y\mid\mathscr B_Y],
 \qquad
 m_Y^{\downarrow}
 :=\mathbb E_{\widehat\nu_Y}
       [\psi_Y\mid\pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X]
 =(m_\nu\circ\pi).
 \label{eq:V23-native-blocked-messages}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Fine boundary-detail birth]
\label{thm:V23-fine-detail-birth}
The native fine visible stock splits exactly as
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 i_Y^{\rm nat}
 :=\|m_Y^{\rm nat}\|_2^2
 =i_\nu+\mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial},}
 \label{eq:V23-fine-visible-split}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 :=\|m_Y^{\rm nat}-m_Y^{\downarrow}\|_2^2
 \ge0.}
 \label{eq:V23-fine-detail-stock}
\end{equation}
The detail stock vanishes if and only if the native fine boundary message is
already measurable from the lifted coarse shell record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two conditional expectations in
\eqref{eq:V23-native-blocked-messages} are orthogonal projections onto nested
subspaces by \eqref{eq:V23-boundary-record-nesting}.  Therefore
\(m_Y^{\rm nat}-m_Y^{\downarrow}\) is orthogonal to
\(m_Y^{\downarrow}\).  Pythagoras gives
\eqref{eq:V23-fine-visible-split}.  Equality is equivalent to equality of the
two projections on the selected source.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete cutoff-message Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V23-complete-message-Pythagoras}
Transport the natural coarse boundary message to the induced-fine boundary
record by \(U_{h_{\mathscr B}}\), and then pull it back through \(\pi\).  The
complete native-fine versus natural-coarse boundary-message distance is
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 :=\left\|
 m_Y^{\rm nat}-(\widetilde m_\mu\circ\pi)
 \right\|_{L^2(\widehat\nu_Y)}^2.
 \label{eq:V23-total-message-distance}
\end{equation}
It has the exact nonduplicating decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 =\mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}+d_{\rm sh}.}
 \label{eq:V23-two-row-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 \le
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 +(\sqrt{d_{\rm src}}+\sqrt{d_{\rm int}})^2.}
 \label{eq:V23-total-message-upper}
\end{equation}

The actual old/fine boundary-message Gram at the selected physical radius is
therefore reconstructed by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 c_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 =\frac{i_Y^{\rm nat}+i_\mu-
             \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}}{2}.}
 \label{eq:V23-total-message-cross}
\end{equation}
If \(i_Y^{\rm nat}i_\mu>0\), the oriented message coefficient is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 =\frac{i_Y^{\rm nat}+i_\mu-
             \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}}
        {2\sqrt{i_Y^{\rm nat}i_\mu}}.}
 \label{eq:V23-total-message-angle}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Using \eqref{eq:V23-native-blocked-messages}, write
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 m_Y^{\rm nat}-\widetilde m_\mu\circ\pi
 ={}&\bigl(m_Y^{\rm nat}-m_Y^{\downarrow}\bigr)\\
 &+\bigl(m_\nu-\widetilde m_\mu\bigr)\circ\pi.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first summand is orthogonal to every
\(\pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X\)-measurable function, while the second is measurable
with respect to that record.  Their squared norms are respectively
\(\mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}\) and \(d_{\rm sh}\), because pullback through
\(\pi\) is an isometry from \(L^2(\nu)\) to
\(L^2(\widehat\nu_Y)\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:V23-two-row-Pythagoras}.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V23-total-message-upper} follows from
\Cref{thm:V23-source-message-rectangle}.  Finally, expand the squared distance
between the two boundary messages to obtain
\eqref{eq:V23-total-message-cross}--\eqref{eq:V23-total-message-angle}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[The original old/fine mixed row is now fully typed]
\label{ass:V23-complete-row-meaning}
The endpoint module card of Version~V22 compares complete sources.  The
actual boundary-message card additionally requires exactly two rows:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \text{native fine boundary-detail birth}
 \quad+\quad
 \text{shared-record source/law-conditioning transport}.}
 \label{eq:V23-two-physical-rows}
\end{equation}
The first is a nesting residual for physical shell records.  The second is a
same-record module distance, whose upstream causes are the endpoint source
motion and the conditional-expectation square defect.  These rows are
orthogonal in \eqref{eq:V23-two-row-Pythagoras} and are never charged twice.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Two exact independence witnesses}
\label{sec:V23-countermodels}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Countertheorem: exact source-module alignment need not transport a boundary message]
\label{cth:V23-source-pass-no-message-pass}
There are two equivalent finite endpoint laws with equal boundary marginals
and exactly aligned unit source amplitudes, but with a nonzero shared-record
boundary-message defect.

Let
\[
 \Omega=\{(j,z):j\in\{0,1,2\},\ z\in\{0,1\}\},
 \qquad \mathscr B=\sigma(j),
\]
and put, for every \(j\),
\begin{equation}
 \nu(j,0)=\frac5{24},
 \qquad
 \nu(j,1)=\frac18,
 \qquad
 h(j,0)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 h(j,1)=\frac32,
 \qquad
 \mu=h^2\nu.
 \label{eq:V23-six-state-laws}
\end{equation}
Define the old source by
\begin{equation}
 \begin{array}{c|rr}
 j&f_\mu(j,0)&f_\mu(j,1)\\ \hline
 0&1&0\\
 1&-1&1\\
 2&0&-1
 \end{array}
 \qquad
 f_\nu=hf_\mu.
 \label{eq:V23-six-state-source}
\end{equation}
Then both sources are centered and have stock \(2/3\), while their endpoint
module distance is zero.  The boundary likelihood root is one and the
conditional affinity is \(7/8\) on every cell.  Nevertheless the unnormalized
boundary messages are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 m_\mu=\left(\frac5{32},\frac{11}{16},-\frac{27}{32}\right),
 \qquad
 m_\nu=\left(\frac5{16},\frac14,-\frac9{16}\right).}
 \label{eq:V23-six-state-messages}
\end{equation}
After source normalization,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 i_\mu=\frac{619}{1024},
 \qquad
 i_\nu=\frac{61}{256},
 \qquad
 d_{\rm sh}=d_{\rm int}=\frac{151}{1024},
 \qquad
 c_{\mathscr B}^{\rm msg}=\frac{89}{256}.}
 \label{eq:V23-six-state-card}
\end{equation}
Thus
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{\mathscr B}^{\rm msg}
 =\frac{178}{\sqrt{37759}}
 =0.9160301333883965\ldots<1,}
 \label{eq:V23-six-state-angle}
\end{equation}
although \(D_{Y/X}^{\rm ori}=0\).  The sharp squared norm of
\(\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\) is \(1/4\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All quantities follow by direct rational summation.  Each boundary cell has
mass \(1/3\) under both laws, so \(h_{\mathscr B}=1\).  Its conditional
\(\nu\)-weights are \((5/8,3/8)\), giving affinity
\((5/8)(1/2)+(3/8)(3/2)=7/8\).  The sources satisfy
\(f_\nu=hf_\mu\), which proves exact endpoint module alignment.  Conditional
expectation gives \eqref{eq:V23-six-state-messages}; polarization gives
\eqref{eq:V23-six-state-card}.  Finally
\eqref{eq:V23-sharp-defect-norm} gives
\(2(1-7/8)=1/4\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Countertheorem: fine boundary detail is independent of the shared-record row]
\label{cth:V23-detail-independent}
There is a four-point uniform fine card with unit centered source
\[
 \psi=(-1,-1,1,1),
\]
for which the lifted coarse boundary record is trivial and the native fine
boundary record reveals the sign of \(\psi\).  Take the natural and induced
coarse endpoint laws and sources to be identical.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{\rm src}=d_{\rm int}=d_{\rm sh}=0,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}=1,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}=1.}
 \label{eq:V23-detail-countermodel}
\end{equation}
Hence no endpoint source Gram or shared-record message Gram determines the
fine boundary-detail birth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation onto the trivial record is zero, while conditional
expectation onto the sign record is \(\psi\) itself.  Their squared difference
is one.  Equality of the endpoint laws and sources makes every shared-record
module defect vanish.  Equation \eqref{eq:V23-two-row-Pythagoras} gives the
last identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The three upstream defects are logically independent]
\label{cor:V23-three-independent-defects}
The following data cannot be inferred from one another without an additional
physical theorem:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{\rm src},
 \qquad
 d_{\rm int},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}.}
 \label{eq:V23-three-defects}
\end{equation}
The endpoint source direction may align while the conditional square fails,
and both may align while the native fine shell carries a new detail message.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first countermodel has \(d_{\rm src}=0\) and \(d_{\rm int}>0\).  The
second has the first two defects zero and the detail birth positive.  V22
already gives endpoint cards with positive source-module distance, completing
the logical separation.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cofinal boundary-message landing and the revised radial handoff}
\label{sec:V23-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Summable three-row cutoff-message landing]
\label{thm:V23-cofinal-message-landing}
Consider a cofinal adjacent dyadic sequence with the exact rectangle lifts,
physical boundary-record nesting, and common-screen incidences fixed before
any source value is read.  For the \(n\)-th adjacent pair let
\[
 d_{{\rm src},n},
 \qquad
 d_{{\rm int},n},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak B_n^{\partial}
\]
be the three defects of \eqref{eq:V23-three-defects}.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
 \left(
  \sqrt{d_{{\rm src},n}}
  +\sqrt{d_{{\rm int},n}}
  +\sqrt{\mathfrak B_n^{\partial}}
 \right)<\infty,}
 \label{eq:V23-three-row-summability}
\end{equation}
then the source-normalized physical boundary messages form a Cauchy sequence
on the declared common screen.

If their visible stocks satisfy a uniform lower bound
\begin{equation}
 i_n\ge i_*>0,
 \label{eq:V23-message-visibility-floor}
\end{equation}
then their unit boundary-message directions converge strongly and their
adjacent oriented coefficients tend to one.  If instead a subsequence has
\(i_n\to0\), the output is source-relative boundary-message extinction on
that subsequence, not an oriented survivor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:V23-two-row-Pythagoras} and
\eqref{eq:V23-shared-defect-interval},
\[
 \sqrt{\mathfrak D_{n}^{\rm msg}}
 \le
 \sqrt{\mathfrak B_n^{\partial}}
 +\sqrt{d_{{\rm src},n}}
 +\sqrt{d_{{\rm int},n}}.
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:V23-three-row-summability} makes the adjacent boundary-message
increments summable on the common screen, hence Cauchy.  If both vectors in
an adjacent comparison have norm at least \(\sqrt{i_*}\), then
\[
 \left\|\frac{x}{\|x\|}-\frac{y}{\|y\|}\right\|
 \le\frac{2}{\sqrt{i_*}}\|x-y\|.
\]
The unit messages are therefore Cauchy as well.  Their limiting norm is one,
and the adjacent inner products tend to one.  The final branch is simply the
definition of collapse of the source-relative visible stock.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Typed failure after an endpoint source pass]
\label{cor:V23-typed-failure}
Suppose \(d_{{\rm src},n}\to0\).  If the complete boundary-message defect
does not tend to zero, then after subsequence extraction at least one of
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \limsup_n\mathfrak B_n^{\partial}>0,
 \qquad
 \limsup_n d_{{\rm int},n}>0}
 \label{eq:V23-two-upstream-obstructions}
\end{equation}
holds.  These are respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a native fine boundary-detail birth absent from the lifted coarse shell;
\item a conditional-fibre law/conditioning obstruction on the shared shell.
\end{enumerate}
Neither is a gauge redundancy merely because the endpoint source lines align.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If both quantities in \eqref{eq:V23-two-upstream-obstructions} tended to
zero, \eqref{eq:V23-total-message-upper} and
\(d_{{\rm src},n}\to0\) would force
\(\mathfrak D_n^{\rm msg}\to0\), a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Correct handoff to the spatial radial trichotomy]
\label{ass:V23-radial-handoff}
The old/fine boundary-message row and the within-cutoff radial row are now
separate and ordered.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item First freeze the global source, verify the native/lifted shell nesting,
      and evaluate \(\mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}\), or its two positive
      summands.
\item On an oriented, source-visible cutoff-message branch, acquire the
      Version~V11 Bayes-reverse loss across one predeclared positive physical
      shell width.
\item A uniform positive radial loss gives contraction.  A near-unit radial
      channel with a positive visibility floor and positive physical width
      gives the positive-range boundary survivor.
\item A shrinking-width packet is contact scale and is not promoted to a
      positive-range survivor.
\end{enumerate}
On the sublinear-root branch, Version~V17 already gives extinction at every
separating shell, so the radial conclusion is terminal irrespective of the
adjacent-cutoff source comparison.
\end{assessment}

\section{Version V24 direction: the conditional action is upstream of the message distance}
\label{sec:V24-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V23 isolated the complete old/fine boundary-message distance as
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 =\mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}+d_{\rm sh}.}
 \label{eq:V24-inherited-message-split}
\end{equation}
The first term is source information visible in the native fine boundary but
absent from the lifted coarse boundary.  The second is the shared-record
natural-coarse versus induced-fine message distance.  Direct acquisition of
these two quantities remains target minimal.

The related programmes identify one useful upstream alternative when the
complete conditional cylinders already occur.  The action and the global
source are frozen before any phase or shell decomposition, and the source is
then propagated through the actual conditional law before an output short is
taken.  Thus the first analytic substitute for an unpopulated message distance
is not another endpoint Gram.  It is the oscillation, modulo normalizing
constants, of the fixed conditional Hamiltonians which produce the message.
The admissible order is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{globally frozen source and fixed endpoint actions}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{shared-boundary conditional-action mismatch}
 +\text{ fine-detail boundary-action sensitivity}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{complete cutoff-message distance}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{oriented message transport and the independent radial Read}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V24-upstream-order}
\end{equation}

This continuation proves a sharp Gibbs-cylinder comparison, an exact
source-to-message Duhamel identity, and a complete one-sided action-level
compiler for \eqref{eq:V24-inherited-message-split}.  Conversely, after
endpoint source motion is controlled, a persistent direct message defect
returns a shared-fibre action mismatch, a native fine boundary-pair mismatch,
or a source-normalization obstruction.

% =============================================================================
\section{Sharp comparison of two finite Gibbs cylinders}
\label{sec:V24-Gibbs-cylinder}
% =============================================================================

Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,m)\) be a probability space and let
\begin{equation}
 \dd\gamma_i
 =\frac{e^{-H_i}}{Z_i}\,\dd m,
 \qquad
 Z_i=\int e^{-H_i}\,\dd m,
 \qquad i=0,1,
 \label{eq:V24-two-Gibbs-laws}
\end{equation}
with strictly positive finite densities.  Define the Hamiltonian oscillation
modulo constants by
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon(H_1,H_0)
 :=\inf_{c\in\R}\|H_1-H_0-c\|_{L^\infty(m)}.
 \label{eq:V24-Hamiltonian-oscillation}
\end{equation}
Use the total-variation convention
\begin{equation}
 \|\rho-\lambda\|_{{\rm TV},*}
 :=\sup_{\|f\|_\infty\le1}|\rho(f)-\lambda(f)|
 =\int\left|\frac{\dd\rho}{\dd\lambda}-1\right|\dd\lambda.
 \label{eq:V24-TV-convention}
\end{equation}
Its maximum is two.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp Gibbs-cylinder Hellinger and total-variation bounds]
\label{thm:V24-sharp-Gibbs-comparison}
If \(\varepsilon(H_1,H_0)\le\varepsilon\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \int\sqrt{\dd\gamma_0\,\dd\gamma_1}
 \ge \operatorname{sech}\!\left(\frac\varepsilon2\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-sharp-Hellinger}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\gamma_1-\gamma_0\|_{{\rm TV},*}
 \le2\tanh\!\left(\frac\varepsilon2\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-sharp-TV}
\end{equation}
Both constants are sharp for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put \(r=\dd\gamma_1/\dd\gamma_0\).  After subtracting a constant from
\(H_1-H_0\), the unnormalized likelihood ratio lies in
\([e^{-\varepsilon},e^{\varepsilon}]\).  Normalization multiplies it by one
positive scalar, so
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\operatorname*{ess\,sup}r}
      {\operatorname*{ess\,inf}r}
 \le R:=e^{2\varepsilon}.
 \label{eq:V24-likelihood-ratio-range}
\end{equation}
Write \(m_0\le r\le M_0\), with \(m_0\le1\le M_0\) and
\(M_0/m_0\le R\).  Convexity of \(x\mapsto|x-1|\) and the secant through
\(m_0,M_0\) give
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{\gamma_0}|r-1|
 \le\frac{2(M_0-1)(1-m_0)}{M_0-m_0}.
 \label{eq:V24-TV-secant}
\end{equation}
The right side is maximized when \(M_0=Rm_0\) and
\(m_0=R^{-1/2}\); its value is
\[
 2\frac{\sqrt R-1}{\sqrt R+1}
 =2\tanh(\varepsilon/2),
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V24-sharp-TV}.

For the Hellinger affinity put \(X=\sqrt r\), with
\(0<a\le X\le b\).  Then \(b/a\le e^\varepsilon\) and
\(\mathbb E_{\gamma_0}X^2=1\).  The pointwise inequality
\((X-a)(b-X)\ge0\) yields
\(
 \mathbb E X^2\le(a+b)\mathbb E X-ab
\).
Maximizing the resulting ratio gives the Kantorovich estimate
\[
 \frac{\mathbb E X^2}{(\mathbb E X)^2}
 \le\frac{(a+b)^2}{4ab}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_{\gamma_0}\sqrt r
 \ge\frac{2\sqrt{ab}}{a+b}
 \ge\frac{2e^{\varepsilon/2}}{1+e^\varepsilon}
 =\operatorname{sech}(\varepsilon/2).
\]

For sharpness take the two-point laws
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_0
 =\left(\frac{e^\varepsilon}{1+e^\varepsilon},
         \frac1{1+e^\varepsilon}\right),
 \qquad
 \gamma_1
 =\left(\frac1{1+e^\varepsilon},
         \frac{e^\varepsilon}{1+e^\varepsilon}\right).
 \label{eq:V24-two-point-extremizer}
\end{equation}
Then \(r=(e^{-\varepsilon},e^\varepsilon)\), and both inequalities are
equalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Small-oscillation forms]
\label{cor:V24-small-oscillation}
For every \(\varepsilon\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
 0\le2\left(1-\operatorname{sech}(\varepsilon/2)\right)
 \le\min\left\{2,\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}\right\},
 \label{eq:V24-Hellinger-quadratic}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 0\le2\tanh(\varepsilon/2)\le\min\{2,\varepsilon\}.
 \label{eq:V24-TV-linear}
\end{equation}
Thus the conditional Hellinger loss is quadratic, while the conditional mean
spread is linear, at small fixed-action modulus.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use \(1-\operatorname{sech}x\le x^2/2\) and
\(\tanh x\le x\) for \(x\ge0\), together with the trivial range bounds.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Shared-boundary conditional actions control the V23 square defect}
\label{sec:V24-shared-action}
% =============================================================================

Retain the natural coarse law \(\mu\), the induced blocked-fine law \(\nu\),
and one common physical boundary record \(\mathscr B\).  Let
\(\mu_b,\nu_b\) be their regular conditional interior laws.  On a common
conditional Haar cylinder write
\begin{equation}
 \dd\mu_b
 =Z_{\mu,b}^{-1}e^{-\mathcal H_\mu(z\mid b)}\,\dd m_b(z),
 \qquad
 \dd\nu_b
 =Z_{\nu,b}^{-1}e^{-\mathcal H_\nu(z\mid b)}\,\dd m_b(z).
 \label{eq:V24-shared-conditional-actions}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon_{\rm sh}(b)
 :=\inf_{c\in\R}
 \|\mathcal H_\mu(\cdot\mid b)
   -\mathcal H_\nu(\cdot\mid b)-c\|_\infty,
 \label{eq:V24-shared-action-modulus-point}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \overline\varepsilon_{\rm sh}
 :=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{b\sim\mu_{\mathscr B}}
   \varepsilon_{\rm sh}(b).
 \label{eq:V24-shared-action-modulus}
\end{equation}
No locality of the blocked effective action is assumed; this modulus is read
from its complete conditional cylinder.

Let \(\rho_{\mathscr B}(b)\) be the V23 conditional-fibre Hellinger affinity,
let \(\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\) be the conditional-expectation/module
commutator, and let \(\psi_\mu\) be the unit natural-coarse source.  Put
\begin{equation}
 d_{\rm int}
 :=\|\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\psi_\mu\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V24-dint-recall}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Source-weighted conditional-action bound]
\label{thm:V24-shared-action-bound}
The source-specific square debit obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{\rm int}
 \le2\int
 \left[1-\operatorname{sech}
       \!\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{\rm sh}(b)}2\right)\right]
 \mathbb E_{\mu_b}|\psi_\mu|^2\,
 \dd\mu_{\mathscr B}(b).}
 \label{eq:V24-weighted-dint}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{\rm int}
 \le2\left[1-\operatorname{sech}
       \!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_{\rm sh}}2\right)\right].}
 \label{eq:V24-uniform-dint}
\end{equation}
The bound is sharp on a two-point boundary fibre.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Version~V23 gives
\[
 (\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}f)(b)
 =h_{\mathscr B}(b)
  \mathbb E_{\mu_b}[(h_b^{-1}-1)f],
 \qquad
 h_b=\sqrt{\dd\mu_b/\dd\nu_b}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mu_b}(h_b^{-1}-1)^2
 =2(1-\rho_{\mathscr B}(b))
\]
give the same integrand with \(1-\rho_{\mathscr B}(b)\).  Since
\(h_{\mathscr B}^2\dd\nu_{\mathscr B}=\dd\mu_{\mathscr B}\), integration
and \Cref{thm:V24-sharp-Gibbs-comparison} prove
\eqref{eq:V24-weighted-dint}.  The uniform form uses
\(\|\psi_\mu\|_2=1\).  The two-point extremizer, with source along the Riesz
representer \(h_b^{-1}-1\), gives equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Static shared-message bound]
\label{cor:V24-static-shared-message}
Let \(d_{\rm src}\) be the V22 endpoint source-module distance and
\(d_{\rm sh}\) the V23 shared-record message distance.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sqrt{d_{\rm sh}}
 \le\sqrt{d_{\rm src}}
 +\sqrt{2\left[1-\operatorname{sech}
       \!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_{\rm sh}}2\right)\right]}.}
 \label{eq:V24-static-shared-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the exact V23 rectangle
\(
 m_\nu-h_{\mathscr B}m_\mu
 =a_{\mathscr B}+\mathfrak C_{\mathscr B}\psi_\mu
\), contractivity of conditional expectation, and
\Cref{thm:V24-shared-action-bound}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The exact source-to-message Duhamel identity}
\label{sec:V24-message-Duhamel}
% =============================================================================

Let \(t\mapsto\pi_t\) be a positive differentiable action path on one fixed
compact cylinder,
\begin{equation}
 \dd\pi_t=p_t\,\dd m,
 \qquad
 s_t=\partial_t\log p_t,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\pi_t}s_t=0,
 \label{eq:V24-action-path}
\end{equation}
and let \(\psi_t\) be a differentiable real source family with
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{\pi_t}\psi_t^2=1.
 \label{eq:V24-unit-source-path}
\end{equation}
Every source coefficient is fixed on the full cylinder and is independent of
the boundary cell.  Put
\begin{equation}
 g_t:=\dot\psi_t+\frac12s_t\psi_t,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_t^{\rm src}:=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}g_t^2.
 \label{eq:V24-global-source-velocity}
\end{equation}
This is the V22 normalized source-amplitude velocity.

For one fixed physical boundary record \(\mathscr B\), put
\begin{equation}
 m_t:=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[\psi_t\mid\mathscr B],
 \qquad
 s_{\mathscr B,t}:=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[s_t\mid\mathscr B].
 \label{eq:V24-message-and-boundary-score}
\end{equation}
Let \(p_{\mathscr B,t}\) be the boundary marginal density relative to a fixed
boundary reference and define
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_t:=m_t\sqrt{p_{\mathscr B,t}}.
 \label{eq:V24-boundary-amplitude}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-to-message Duhamel derivative]
\label{thm:V24-message-Duhamel}
Define
\begin{equation}
 a_t:=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[g_t\mid\mathscr B],
 \label{eq:V24-projected-source-speed}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 c_t:=\frac12\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}
       (\psi_t,s_t\mid\mathscr B)
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{\pi_t}
   [(\psi_t-m_t)(s_t-s_{\mathscr B,t})\mid\mathscr B].
 \label{eq:V24-conditional-Duhamel-column}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dot\Phi_t
 =\sqrt{p_{\mathscr B,t}}\,(a_t+c_t).}
 \label{eq:V24-message-derivative}
\end{equation}
The complete instantaneous Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_t^{\rm msg}
 =\mathbb E_{\pi_{\mathscr B,t}}
 \begin{pmatrix}
 a_t^2&a_tc_t\\
 a_tc_t&c_t^2
 \end{pmatrix}
 \succeq0,}
 \label{eq:V24-message-speed-Gram}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\dot\Phi_t\|_2^2
 =(1\;1)\mathbb G_t^{\rm msg}\binom11.}
 \label{eq:V24-complete-message-speed}
\end{equation}
The two columns interfere and are not separately charged after the complete
speed is known.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a differentiable writer \(f_t\),
\begin{equation}
 \partial_t\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[f_t\mid\mathscr B]
 =\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[\dot f_t\mid\mathscr B]
  +\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(f_t,s_t\mid\mathscr B).
 \label{eq:V24-conditional-derivative}
\end{equation}
Also
\(
 \partial_t\log p_{\mathscr B,t}=s_{\mathscr B,t}
\).
Differentiate \eqref{eq:V24-boundary-amplitude}, use
\eqref{eq:V24-conditional-derivative}, and add and subtract
\(\frac12\mathbb E[s_t\psi_t\mid\mathscr B]\).  The result is exactly
\eqref{eq:V24-message-derivative}.  The remaining identities are the squared
norm of the two-column sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Positive conditional source--score action]
\label{cor:V24-conditional-source-score}
Put
\begin{equation}
 v_{\psi,t}:=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\psi_t\mid\mathscr B),
 \qquad
 v_{s,t}:=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(s_t\mid\mathscr B),
 \label{eq:V24-two-conditional-variances}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_t^{\rm cond}
 :=\frac14\mathbb E_{\pi_{\mathscr B,t}}[v_{\psi,t}v_{s,t}].
 \label{eq:V24-conditional-action}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \|a_t\|_2^2\le\mathcal E_t^{\rm src},
 \label{eq:V24-projected-speed-bound}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \|c_t\|_2^2\le\mathcal E_t^{\rm cond},
 \label{eq:V24-conditional-speed-bound}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\dot\Phi_t\|_2
 \le\sqrt{\mathcal E_t^{\rm src}}
     +\sqrt{\mathcal E_t^{\rm cond}}.}
 \label{eq:V24-total-speed-bound}
\end{equation}
The new row is the conditional covariance between hidden source and hidden
action score; it is not a second source birth.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation is an orthogonal contraction.  Conditional
Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(|c_t|^2\le v_{\psi,t}v_{s,t}/4\).  Apply the triangle
inequality to \eqref{eq:V24-message-derivative}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Affine fixed-action bridge]
\label{cor:V24-affine-message-bridge}
Suppose
\begin{equation}
 S_t=(1-t)S_0+tS_1,
 \qquad
 \Delta:=S_1-S_0,
 \label{eq:V24-affine-action-bridge}
\end{equation}
and define
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon_{\mathscr B}^{\rm path}
 :=\inf_{q\in L^\infty(\mathscr B)}\|\Delta-q\|_\infty.
 \label{eq:V24-path-action-modulus}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_t^{\rm cond}
 \le\frac14(\varepsilon_{\mathscr B}^{\rm path})^2.}
 \label{eq:V24-path-cond-bound}
\end{equation}
If the path joins the induced-fine and natural-coarse sources and
\begin{equation}
 L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}
 :=\int_0^1\sqrt{\mathcal E_t^{\rm src}}\,\dd t,
 \label{eq:V24-inherited-source-length}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sqrt{d_{\rm sh}}
 \le L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}
     +\frac12\varepsilon_{\mathscr B}^{\rm path}.}
 \label{eq:V24-dynamic-shared-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For the affine Gibbs path,
\[
 s_t-s_{\mathscr B,t}
 =-(\Delta-\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[\Delta\mid\mathscr B]).
\]
If \(|\Delta-q|\le\varepsilon_{\mathscr B}^{\rm path}\) with \(q\) boundary
measurable, then every conditional variance of \(\Delta\) is at most
\((\varepsilon_{\mathscr B}^{\rm path})^2\).  Moreover
\(
 \mathbb E v_{\psi,t}\le1
\).  This proves \eqref{eq:V24-path-cond-bound}.  Integrate
\eqref{eq:V24-total-speed-bound}; the endpoint boundary amplitudes are exactly
the V23 shared-record messages in a common half-density chart.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Static and dynamic routes are alternatives]
\label{ass:V24-static-dynamic-not-additive}
The static estimate \eqref{eq:V24-static-shared-bound} uses endpoint source
motion and the sharp endpoint conditional Hellinger deficit.  The dynamic
estimate \eqref{eq:V24-dynamic-shared-bound} uses the complete source path and
one conditional source--score action.  They are alternative upper routes to
the same \(d_{\rm sh}\); they are not added as independent losses.  A large
upper bound from either route is unresolved, not a transport obstruction.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Fine-detail boundary pairs and their exact action modulus}
\label{sec:V24-fine-detail}
% =============================================================================

Let \(\mathscr C=\pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X\) be the lifted coarse boundary record
and \(\mathscr D=\mathscr B_Y\) the native fine record, with
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr D.
 \label{eq:V24-record-nesting}
\end{equation}
Let \(\psi_Y\) be the globally frozen unit fine source and put
\begin{equation}
 M_D:=\mathbb E[\psi_Y\mid\mathscr D],
 \qquad
 M_C:=\mathbb E[\psi_Y\mid\mathscr C].
 \label{eq:V24-two-fine-messages}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}=\|M_D-M_C\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V24-detail-birth-recall}
\end{equation}

For a lifted coarse record \(x\), let \(y,y'\) range over occurring native
fine records above \(x\).  Write their conditional source-interior laws as
\begin{equation}
 \dd\kappa_y(z)
 =Z_y^{-1}e^{-\mathcal H_Y(z\mid y)}\,\dd m_x(z),
 \label{eq:V24-fine-conditional-laws}
\end{equation}
and define
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon_\partial(x)
 :=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{y,y'\mid x}
 \inf_{c\in\R}
 \|\mathcal H_Y(\cdot\mid y)
  -\mathcal H_Y(\cdot\mid y')-c\|_\infty.
 \label{eq:V24-fine-detail-modulus}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Boundary-pair writer and sharp fine-detail bound]
\label{thm:V24-fine-detail-bound}
Let \(D_1,D_2\) be conditionally independent copies of the native fine record
given \(\mathscr C\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 =\frac12\mathbb E
  \left[(M_D(D_1)-M_D(D_2))^2\right].}
 \label{eq:V24-detail-pair-read}
\end{equation}
If \(K_Y:=\|\psi_Y\|_\infty<\infty\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 \le K_Y^2\mathbb E\left[
  \tanh^2\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon_\partial(\mathscr C)}2\right)
 \right].}
 \label{eq:V24-detail-action-bound}
\end{equation}
In particular, if
\(\varepsilon_\partial\le\overline\varepsilon_\partial\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 \le K_Y^2
 \tanh^2\!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_\partial}2\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-detail-uniform-bound}
\end{equation}
The constant is sharp on a two-boundary, two-interior-state card.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional-expectation Pythagoras gives
\[
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 =\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(M_D\mid\mathscr C).
\]
For two conditionally independent copies, half their squared difference is
the same conditional variance.  By
\Cref{thm:V24-sharp-Gibbs-comparison}, any two conditional laws above \(x\)
satisfy
\[
 \|\kappa_y-\kappa_{y'}\|_{{\rm TV},*}
 \le2\tanh(\varepsilon_\partial(x)/2).
\]
Their source means therefore differ by at most
\(
 2K_Y\tanh(\varepsilon_\partial(x)/2)
\).  Popoviciu's variance bound is one quarter of the squared range diameter.
Integrate over \(x\).  The sharp two-point Gibbs pair with source values
\((-K_Y,K_Y)\) and equally weighted fine labels attains equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced Creutz specialization]
\label{cor:V24-balanced-detail-bound}
For the canonically balanced four-loop source \(F_Y\),
\begin{equation}
 |F_Y|\le3.
 \label{eq:V24-balanced-source-bound}
\end{equation}
If \(\sigma_Y^2=\|F_Y\|_2^2>0\) and
\(\psi_Y=F_Y/\sigma_Y\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 \le\frac9{\sigma_Y^2}
 \tanh^2\!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_\partial}2\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-balanced-detail-stock}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every real normalized Wilson trace lies in \([-1/2,1]\), so each centered
raw-loop coordinate has range length at most \(3/2\).  The balanced
coefficient vector has Euclidean norm one, hence \(|F_Y|\le3\).  Divide by
\(\sigma_Y\) and apply \Cref{thm:V24-fine-detail-bound}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Complete specification-first cutoff-message certificate}
\label{sec:V24-complete-certificate}
% =============================================================================

Define the two alternative shared-record upper bounds
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{\rm sh}^{\rm stat}
 :=\left(
 \sqrt{d_{\rm src}}
 +\sqrt{2\left[1-\operatorname{sech}
       \!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_{\rm sh}}2\right)\right]}
 \right)^2,
 \label{eq:V24-static-upper}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{\rm sh}^{\rm dyn}
 :=\left(
 L_{Y/X}^{\rm src}
 +\frac12\varepsilon_{\mathscr B}^{\rm path}
 \right)^2.
 \label{eq:V24-dynamic-upper}
\end{equation}
Use only a route whose hypotheses have been physically populated, and use the
minimum when both are available.  Denote the resulting quantity by
\(\Delta_{\rm sh}^{\rm act}\).

\begin{theorem}[Specification-first complete message bound]
\label{thm:V24-complete-message-bound}
Assume literal nesting
\(\pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X\subseteq\mathscr B_Y\), a positive fine source stock,
and the conditional action cylinders above.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 \le\frac9{\sigma_Y^2}
 \tanh^2\!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_\partial}2\right)
 +\Delta_{\rm sh}^{\rm act}.}
 \label{eq:V24-complete-action-bound}
\end{equation}
Hence
\begin{equation}
 \inf_n\sigma_{Y_n}^2>0,
 \quad
 \overline\varepsilon_{\partial,n}\to0,
 \quad
 \Delta_{{\rm sh},n}^{\rm act}\to0
 \label{eq:V24-action-pass-assumptions}
\end{equation}
imply
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{Y_n/X_n}^{\rm msg}\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V24-message-distance-pass}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine the exact V23 Pythagoras
\eqref{eq:V24-inherited-message-split}, the fine-detail estimate
\eqref{eq:V24-balanced-detail-stock}, and either the static or dynamic shared
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Visible-stock oriented pass]
\label{cor:V24-visible-oriented-pass}
Let \(x,y\) be the two common-screen message amplitudes and suppose
\begin{equation}
 \|x\|_2^2,\|y\|_2^2\ge i_*>0,
 \qquad
 \|x-y\|_2^2=\mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}.
 \label{eq:V24-visible-floor}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \left\|
 \frac{x}{\|x\|_2}-\frac{y}{\|y\|_2}
 \right\|_2^2
 \le\frac{4\mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}}{i_*},
 \label{eq:V24-unit-message-bound}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 \ge1-\frac{2\mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}}{i_*},}
 \label{eq:V24-alpha-lower}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 \le\frac{4\mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}}{i_*}.}
 \label{eq:V24-message-Schur-bound}
\end{equation}
Thus \eqref{eq:V24-message-distance-pass} plus a visible-stock floor is an
oriented message-transport pass.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For nonzero Hilbert vectors,
\[
 \left\|\frac{x}{\|x\|}-\frac{y}{\|y\|}\right\|
 \le\frac{2\|x-y\|}{\min\{\|x\|,\|y\|\}}.
\]
Square and use \eqref{eq:V24-visible-floor}.  The squared unit-vector distance
is \(2(1-\alpha)\), while \(1-\alpha^2\le2(1-\alpha)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Summable conditional-action landing]
\label{cor:V24-summable-action-landing}
Suppose the adjacent message amplitudes live on one common screen,
\(\sigma_{Y_n}^2\ge s_*>0\), and
\begin{equation}
 \sum_n\left[
 \frac3{\sqrt{s_*}}
 \tanh\!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_{\partial,n}}2\right)
 +\sqrt{d_{{\rm src},n}}
 +\sqrt{2\left(1-\operatorname{sech}
       \!\left(\frac{\overline\varepsilon_{{\rm sh},n}}2\right)\right)}
 \right]<\infty.
 \label{eq:V24-summable-static-moduli}
\end{equation}
Then the message amplitudes are Cauchy.  The same conclusion holds with the
last two terms replaced by
\(
 L_{Y_n/X_n}^{\rm src}+
 \varepsilon_{\mathscr B,n}^{\rm path}/2
\).
With a uniform visible-stock floor, the unit message directions converge
strongly and retain their orientation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Bound the square root of the exact two-row distance by the sum of the square
roots of its nonnegative rows, use the preceding estimates, and apply the
Cauchy criterion.
\end{proof}

\section{A persistent message defect returns an action-level witness}
\label{sec:V24-obstruction}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative action-modulus obstruction alternative]
\label{thm:V24-action-obstruction}
Suppose on one finite card
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}\ge\delta>0,
 \qquad
 d_{\rm src}\le\eta,
 \qquad
 \|\psi_Y\|_\infty\le K<\infty.
 \label{eq:V24-obstruction-data}
\end{equation}
Then at least one of the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(O\arabic*)},leftmargin=4em]
\item If \(\sqrt{\delta/2}<K\), the fine-detail action modulus obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \overline\varepsilon_\partial
 \ge2\operatorname{artanh}
 \left(\frac{\sqrt{\delta/2}}{K}\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-detail-obstruction}
\end{equation}
If the ratio is at least one, the assumed finite \(K\) and strictly positive
finite Gibbs cylinder exclude this branch.
\item Put
\begin{equation}
 r_{\delta,\eta}
 :=\left(\sqrt{\delta/2}-\sqrt\eta\right)_+.
 \label{eq:V24-r-delta-eta}
\end{equation}
If \(r_{\delta,\eta}>0\), the shared-boundary action modulus obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \overline\varepsilon_{\rm sh}
 \ge2\operatorname{arcosh}
 \left(\frac1{1-r_{\delta,\eta}^2/2}\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-shared-obstruction}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
If no uniform \(K\) exists because \(\sigma_Y\to0\), the output is the
already named source-normalization or visibility obstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:V24-inherited-message-split}, either
\(
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}\ge\delta/2
\)
or \(d_{\rm sh}\ge\delta/2\).  The first case and
\eqref{eq:V24-detail-uniform-bound} give
\eqref{eq:V24-detail-obstruction}.  In the second case,
\eqref{eq:V24-static-shared-bound} gives
\[
 \sqrt{2\left(1-\operatorname{sech}
   (\overline\varepsilon_{\rm sh}/2)\right)}
 \ge r_{\delta,\eta}.
\]
Rearrange and invert the decreasing \(\operatorname{sech}\) function.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Literal fine-boundary pair]
\label{cor:V24-boundary-pair-extraction}
If \(\mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}\ge b>0\) and
\(\|\psi_Y\|_\infty\le K\), then on the finite card there are a lifted coarse
record \(x\) and two occurring fine records \(y,y'\) above it such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |\mathbb E_{\kappa_y}\psi_Y-
   \mathbb E_{\kappa_{y'}}\psi_Y|
 \ge2\sqrt b,}
 \label{eq:V24-mean-pair-witness}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\kappa_y-\kappa_{y'}\|_{{\rm TV},*}
 \ge\frac{2\sqrt b}{K}.}
 \label{eq:V24-TV-pair-witness}
\end{equation}
Thus positive detail birth has an attained finite boundary-pair witness.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Some coarse fibre has conditional variance at least \(b\).  The diameter of a
real random variable is at least twice the square root of its variance, giving
\eqref{eq:V24-mean-pair-witness}.  Total-variation duality gives
\eqref{eq:V24-TV-pair-witness}.
\end{proof}

\section{Exact finite replay}
\label{sec:V24-replay}
% =============================================================================

The verifier uses three independent finite cards.  For
\begin{equation}
 \nu=\left(\frac45,\frac15\right),
 \qquad
 \mu=\left(\frac15,\frac45\right),
 \label{eq:V24-replay-two-laws}
\end{equation}
the likelihood ratio is \((1/4,4)\), the modulus is \(\log4\), and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \rho=\frac45
 =\operatorname{sech}\!\left(\frac{\log4}{2}\right),
 \qquad
 \|\mu-\nu\|_{{\rm TV},*}=\frac65
 =2\tanh\!\left(\frac{\log4}{2}\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-replay-sharp-comparison}
\end{equation}
The Riesz source saturates the square norm
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{2(1-\rho)=\frac25.}
 \label{eq:V24-replay-square-norm}
\end{equation}

Two equally likely fine records carrying these conditional laws in reverse
order and source values \((-1,1)\) have means \((3/5,-3/5)\), so
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 =\frac9{25}
 =\tanh^2\!\left(\frac{\log4}{2}\right).}
 \label{eq:V24-replay-detail-sharp}
\end{equation}

A four-state exponential family with action exponents \((0,1,2,0)\), boundary
cells \((0,0,1,1)\), and raw writer \((-2,1,0,2)\) verifies
\eqref{eq:V24-message-derivative} symbolically.  At the neutral parameter the
raw centered stock is \(35/16\).  In the first boundary cell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dot\Phi_0=\frac{593\sqrt{70}}{19600},
 \quad
 a_0=\frac{173\sqrt{35}}{9800},
 \quad
 \operatorname{Cov}(\psi,s\mid B=0)=\frac{3\sqrt{35}}{35}.}
 \label{eq:V24-replay-Duhamel-first}
\end{equation}
Omitting the half conditional covariance leaves the nonzero residual
\(3\sqrt{70}/140\); in the second cell the residual is
\(-\sqrt{70}/35\).

The orthogonal direct sum of the sharp shared-record and fine-detail cards
gives
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{\rm src}=0,
 \qquad
 d_{\rm sh}=\frac25,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{\partial}=\frac9{25},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}=\frac{19}{25}.}
 \label{eq:V24-replay-complete}
\end{equation}
Deleting the fine-detail row returns \(2/5\) and fails the V23 Pythagoras.

The verifier and output are
\begin{center}
\path{Renewal_YM_Boundary_Sector_V24_conditional_action_message_certificate.py},\\
\path{Renewal_YM_Boundary_Sector_V24_conditional_action_message_certificate.json}.
\end{center}
Their SHA--256 digests are
\begin{center}\scriptsize\ttfamily
681c96c7cf4eeaee4a26828ca1a5091a7a52c007b0935bc24bb0ae395dd5cadf,\\
2263f73b930e569daab06d652cbcc11fcb92e3d2d8792c3fb296a27d0fd87024.
\end{center}
Ordinary and optimized executions produce byte-identical JSON.  Mutations of

\begin{theorem}[Version V24 conditional-action/message theorem]
\label{thm:V24-integrated}
Preserving Versions~V1--V23, Version~V24 proves:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V24.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.8em]
\item the sharp conditional Hellinger floor
      \(\operatorname{sech}(\varepsilon/2)\) and total-variation bound
      \(2\tanh(\varepsilon/2)\);
\item a source-weighted shared-boundary action bound for the V23 conditional
      module-square debit;
\item an exact source-to-message Duhamel derivative with projected global
      source speed and conditional source--score columns;
\item an exact positive boundary-pair representation and sharp action bound
      for native fine detail birth;
\item a complete one-sided action-level compiler for the two-row cutoff-
      message distance;
\item conversion of a vanishing complete message distance and visible-stock
      floor into oriented old/fine message transport;
\item a quantitative inverse alternative returning a fine-boundary or shared-
      fibre action witness whenever a direct message defect persists after
      endpoint alignment.
\end{enumerate}
No item evaluates either action modulus on the selected Wilson cylinder or
supplies the subsequent positive-width radial posterior.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The assertions are
\Cref{thm:V24-sharp-Gibbs-comparison,thm:V24-shared-action-bound,thm:V24-message-Duhamel,thm:V24-fine-detail-bound,thm:V24-complete-message-bound,cor:V24-visible-oriented-pass,thm:V24-action-obstruction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{openproblem}[Version V25: evaluate one direct message card or its fixed-action modulus]
\label{op:V24-V25}
Preserve Version~V24 and every frozen source, action, dyadic, shell,
orientation, and physical-radius convention.  Proceed only in this order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V25.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item Freeze one adjacent selected-root pair and one literal native/lifted
      boundary pair.  Verify
      \(\pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X\subseteq\mathscr B_Y\).
\item Choose one route before reading values:
      \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
      \item read \(\mathfrak D_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}\) and the visible stocks; or
      \item acquire endpoint source distance or source-speed panels, the
            shared-boundary action modulus, the fine-detail action modulus,
            and a fine source-stock floor.
      \end{enumerate}
      Do not charge both routes as independent defects.
\item On the action route, apply \eqref{eq:V24-complete-action-bound}.  An
      inconclusive upper interval remains unresolved unless the direct distance
      or inverse obstruction theorem is populated.
\item If a direct defect survives endpoint alignment, return the shared-fibre
      or fine-boundary witness of \Cref{thm:V24-action-obstruction}; do not open
      another endpoint Gram.
\item Only on an oriented, source-visible message branch acquire the V11
      Bayes-reverse source loss across one positive physical width.
\item Export uniform radial contraction or the positive-range survivor and
      terminate YM--B.  A shrinking-width packet remains contact scale.
\item On a sublinear selected-root branch retain the V17 complete source-
      relative shell extinction theorem as terminal.
\end{enumerate}
No cellwise source retuning, new conditional-action representation, enlarged
phase bank, stochastic cutoff process, representation bank, or further radial
parametrization is licensed before one of the two literal routes is populated.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{assessment}[Version V24 termination]
\label{ass:V24-termination}
The related programmes sharpened the upstream interpretation of the V23 card.
The relevant analytic object is the fixed conditional action which propagates
the already loaded source to the boundary record.  Its shared-fibre and fine-
detail oscillations now give a complete one-sided certificate, and a
persistent direct message defect returns one of those action-level witnesses.
The attachments contain neither modulus nor the direct selected-root message
distance.  The exact status is therefore \(\mathsf{STOP}\) at a finite
conditional-cylinder acquisition, not another abstract source or shell
construction.
\end{assessment}
