% =============================================================================
\section{Version V25 direction: shell incidence is upstream of every conditional-action comparison}
\label{sec:V25-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V23 proved the boundary-message Pythagoras under the explicit
incidence hypothesis
\[
 \pi^{-1}\mathscr B_X\subseteq\mathscr B_Y,
\]
and Version~V24 then bounded the two resulting message rows through fixed
conditional actions.  Both theorems remain exact at those hypotheses.  The
literal inherited link shells, however, had not yet been checked against the
dyadic block map.

That geometric row is logically prior to the conditional-action modulus.  If
the pulled-back coarse record is not measurable from the proposed fine shell,
then no comparison of conditional laws on that single shell can instantiate
the square used in Versions~V23--V24.  Enlarging the action estimate does not
create the missing record incidence.

The present continuation performs the exact finite audit on the first literal
adjacent physical source pair,
\[
 M=32,\qquad N=64,
\]
and proves that the source contours lift exactly but a coarse separating shell
does not lift into one fine separating shell.  It splits across the two
consecutive shells
\[
 \Sigma_{64,2R}\quad\text{and}\quad\Sigma_{64,2R+1}.
\]
Consequently the first valid common refinement is a dyadic two-shell bracket,
not one native shell.  The corrected order is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{frozen source contours and inherited plaquette collars}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{exact dyadic shell-incidence audit}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{one block-complete two-shell record}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{shared-record action/message comparison}
 +\text{ native-shell incidence innovation}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{positive-width radial posterior and the cofinal trichotomy}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V25-upstream-order}
\end{equation}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the correction]
\label{fire:V25-scope}
The abstract nested-record theorems of Versions~V23--V24 are not withdrawn.
They apply after a record satisfying their inclusion hypothesis has actually
been constructed.  Version~V25 proves that a single inherited fine shell is
not such a record on the literal \(32\to64\) card, constructs two minimal
link-coordinate completions, and replaces the invalid one-row application by
a common-refinement rectangle.  It does not evaluate a selected root, a
Wilson expectation, a conditional-action modulus, or a radial posterior.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The inherited collars and the exact dyadic link lift}
\label{sec:V25-geometry}
% =============================================================================

For a lattice size \(K\in16\mathbb N\), let
\(\mathcal C_K^\square\) be the union of the four unoriented edge supports of
the centered rectangles with side pairs
\[
 \left(\frac K4,\frac K4\right),\quad
 \left(\frac K4,\frac{3K}{8}\right),\quad
 \left(\frac{3K}{8},\frac K4\right),\quad
 \left(\frac{3K}{8},\frac{3K}{8}\right).
\]
Retain the inherited collar construction:
\begin{align}
 \mathscr P_{K,0}^\square
 &:=\{p:\partial p\cap\mathcal C_K^\square\ne\varnothing\},
 \label{eq:V25-P0}\\
 \mathscr P_{K,R+1}^\square
 &:=\mathscr P_{K,R}^\square
   \cup\{q:\partial q\cap\partial p\ne\varnothing
             \text{ for some }p\in\mathscr P_{K,R}^\square\},
 \label{eq:V25-collar-expand}\\
 \Sigma_{K,R}
 &:=\{e:e\subset\partial p\cap\partial q
       \text{ for some }p\in\mathscr P_{K,R}^\square,
       \ q\notin\mathscr P_{K,R}^\square\}.
 \label{eq:V25-shell-definition}
\end{align}
The shell record is
\[
 \mathscr B_{K,R}:=\sigma(U_e:e\in\Sigma_{K,R}).
\]

Let \(N=2M\).  The dyadic block map sends the two fine children of the coarse
positive link \(e=(x,\mu)\) to the coarse link matrix
\begin{equation}
 (B_{N\to M}U)_e
 =U_{e^{(0)}}U_{e^{(1)}},
 \qquad
 e^{(0)}=(2x,\mu),\quad
 e^{(1)}=(2x+\widehat\mu,\mu).
 \label{eq:V25-child-product}
\end{equation}
Write
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Ch}(e):=\{e^{(0)},e^{(1)}\},
 \qquad
 L_R:=\bigcup_{e\in\Sigma_{M,R}}\operatorname{Ch}(e).
 \label{eq:V25-lifted-shell-support}
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Exact lift of the four source contours]
\label{lem:V25-source-lift}
For \(M=32\) and \(N=64\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C_{64}^\square
 =\bigsqcup_{e\in\mathcal C_{32}^\square}
   \operatorname{Ch}(e).}
 \label{eq:V25-source-lift}
\end{equation}
The coarse source has ninety-six positive-link supports and the fine source
has one hundred ninety-two.  Every rectangle path, orientation, and physical
side length is preserved by ordered two-link multiplication.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A coarse horizontal or vertical side of length \(m\) starts at an even fine
vertex after multiplication of every coordinate by two.  Replacing each
coarse link by the ordered pair in \eqref{eq:V25-child-product} gives the
corresponding fine side of length \(2m\).  The four side lengths
\((8,8),(8,12),(12,8),(12,12)\) therefore become
\((16,16),(16,24),(24,16),(24,24)\).  The child map is injective on positive
coarse links, so the union is disjoint and the cardinalities double.  The
standalone integer replay checks the four complete contours rather than only
their side lengths.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The literal coarse shell occupies a two-shell fine bracket}
\label{sec:V25-two-shell}
% =============================================================================

For the literal pair \(32\to64\), define
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_R^{0}:=L_R\cap\Sigma_{64,2R},
 \qquad
 \Delta_R^{1}:=L_R\cap\Sigma_{64,2R+1}.
 \label{eq:V25-two-child-levels}
\end{equation}
The index \(2R\) has the same inherited physical-radius tag as the coarse
index \(R\), because
\[
 a_{64}(2R)=a_{32}R.
\]
The index \(2R+1\) is one fine lattice spacing farther out.

\begin{theorem}[Exact two-shell incidence on the first four literal radii]
\label{thm:V25-two-shell-incidence}
For \(R=0,1,2,3\), the lifted coarse shell has the disjoint decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 L_R=\Delta_R^{0}\sqcup\Delta_R^{1}
 \subseteq\Sigma_{64,2R}\sqcup\Sigma_{64,2R+1}.}
 \label{eq:V25-two-shell-partition}
\end{equation}
Neither inclusion
\begin{equation}
 L_R\subseteq\Sigma_{64,2R},
 \qquad
 L_R\subseteq\Sigma_{64,2R+1}
 \label{eq:V25-single-shell-fail-set}
\end{equation}
holds.  The exact cardinalities are
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r|r|r}
R&|\Sigma_{32,R}|&|L_R|&|\Delta_R^0|&|\Delta_R^1|
 &\#(0,2)&\#(1,1)\\
\hline
0&  992& 1984&  512& 1472& 480& 512\\
1& 3424& 6848& 2208& 4640&1216&2208\\
2& 7256&14512& 5024& 9488&2232&5024\\
3&12192&24384& 8720&15664&3472&8720
\end{array}
 \label{eq:V25-shell-count-table}
\end{equation}
Here \((j_0,j_1)\) means that one coarse shell link has \(j_0\) children in
\(\Sigma_{64,2R}\) and \(j_1\) children in
\(\Sigma_{64,2R+1}\).  Thus every coarse link is of type \((0,2)\) or
\((1,1)\); no coarse link has both children in the exact-radius fine shell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is a finite theorem in the integer cubical incidence structure.  Starting
from the four contours, construct \(\mathscr P_{K,0}^\square\) by listing the
six plaquettes incident to every source link, iterate
\eqref{eq:V25-collar-expand}, and apply
\eqref{eq:V25-shell-definition}.  For each of the
\(|\Sigma_{32,R}|\) coarse links, form its two children and test membership in
the two displayed fine shells.

The resulting lifted-child counts are the four rows of
\eqref{eq:V25-shell-count-table}.  In every row the two child counts sum to
\(2|\Sigma_{32,R}|\), their intersection is empty, and the complement in
\(L_R\) is empty.  Both columns are nonzero, proving
\eqref{eq:V25-single-shell-fail-set}.  The final two columns result from the
same exhaustive parent-by-parent classification.  The verifier uses packed
integer vertices, links, and plaquettes and checks the complete sets and their
SHA--256 fingerprints; no floating-point or random test enters the proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What the table means physically]
\label{ass:V25-radius-bracket}
The exact-radius fine shell \(\Sigma_{64,2R}\) and the one-step-outer fine
shell \(\Sigma_{64,2R+1}\) form a bracket of physical thickness \(a_{64}\).
The lifted coarse shell is not a third shell between them: each coarse link is
an ordered product of two fine factors whose locations are distributed across
the bracket.  The thickness tends to zero on a cofinal dyadic sequence, but
the bracket may sit at either contact or positive physical radius according
to the separately retained tag \(a_{32}R\).  No radial survivor type is
assigned from the thickness alone.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{A single native fine shell cannot carry the pulled-back coarse record}
\label{sec:V25-measurability}
% =============================================================================

The pulled-back coarse shell sigma-algebra is
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr C_R
 :=B_{64\to32}^{-1}\mathscr B_{32,R}
 =\sigma\!\left(
   U_{e^{(0)}}U_{e^{(1)}}:e\in\Sigma_{32,R}
  \right).
 \label{eq:V25-pulled-coarse-record}
\end{equation}
Define two link-coordinate completions:
\begin{align}
 \mathscr D_R^{0}
 &:=%
 \mathscr B_{64,2R}
 \vee\sigma(U_f:f\in\Delta_R^{1}),
 \label{eq:V25-even-completion}\\
 \mathscr D_R^{1}
 &:=%
 \mathscr B_{64,2R+1}
 \vee\sigma(U_f:f\in\Delta_R^{0}).
 \label{eq:V25-odd-completion}
\end{align}
The first preserves the exact physical-radius shell and adds the missing
one-step-outer children.  The second preserves the outer fine shell and adds
the missing inward children.

\begin{theorem}[Exact record incidence and coordinate minimality]
\label{thm:V25-record-incidence}
For every \(R=0,1,2,3\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr C_R\subseteq\mathscr D_R^{0},
 \qquad
 \mathscr C_R\subseteq\mathscr D_R^{1}.}
 \label{eq:V25-completion-inclusions}
\end{equation}
For every finite Wilson coupling \(\beta\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr C_R\not\subseteq\mathscr B_{64,2R},
 \qquad
 \mathscr C_R\not\subseteq\mathscr B_{64,2R+1}.}
 \label{eq:V25-single-shell-nonmeasurable}
\end{equation}
Moreover, among sigma-algebras generated by a native fine shell together with
additional individual fine-link coordinates, the added sets in
\eqref{eq:V25-even-completion}--\eqref{eq:V25-odd-completion} are minimal:
every link in the displayed \(\Delta\)-set is necessary to make all coarse
shell matrices in \eqref{eq:V25-child-product} measurable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The set partition \eqref{eq:V25-two-shell-partition} shows that both factors
of every coarse product belong to either completion, proving
\eqref{eq:V25-completion-inclusions}.

For the exact-radius shell, every coarse parent has at least one child in
\(\Delta_R^1\), because the only parent types are \((0,2)\) and \((1,1)\).
For the outer shell, every type-\((1,1)\) parent has one missing child in
\(\Delta_R^0\), and the last column of
\eqref{eq:V25-shell-count-table} is positive.

Fix one missing child \(f\) and its unique coarse parent \(e\).  Condition on
all other fine links.  At finite coupling the conditional law of \(U_f\) has
a strictly positive continuous density relative to Haar measure.  With the
other child fixed, the map
\[
 U_f\longmapsto U_{e^{(0)}}U_{e^{(1)}}
\]
is a left or right translate of \(U_f\) and is therefore nonconstant on every
full-Haar support.  The coarse shell matrix is not measurable without
\(U_f\).  This proves both noninclusions and, because the child map is
injective, the coordinate-minimality claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The first V23 incidence hypothesis fails for one inherited shell]
\label{cor:V25-V23-hypothesis}
On the literal \(32\to64\) shell pairs above, neither choice
\[
 \mathscr B_Y=\mathscr B_{64,2R}
 \quad\text{nor}\quad
 \mathscr B_Y=\mathscr B_{64,2R+1}
\]
satisfies the V23 nesting hypothesis
\(\mathscr C_R\subseteq\mathscr B_Y\).
The V23--V24 nested-record theorems become physically instantiated after
\(\mathscr B_Y\) is replaced by either block-complete record
\(\mathscr D_R^0\) or \(\mathscr D_R^1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is exactly \eqref{eq:V25-single-shell-nonmeasurable} together with
\eqref{eq:V25-completion-inclusions}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The correct Hilbert geometry for incomparable native and coarse records}
\label{sec:V25-common-refinement}
% =============================================================================

The preceding geometry forces a common-refinement square rather than a nested
one.  The following theorem is independent of the finite lattice counts and
therefore applies to every future dyadic card once its incidence sets are
verified.

Let \((\Omega,\mathscr F,\lambda)\) be a probability space, let
\(\mathscr B,\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr F\) be two
possibly incomparable records inside one common refinement, and let
\(P_B,P_C,P_D\) be their conditional-expectation projections.  For a centered
source \(\psi\in L^2(\lambda)\), put
\begin{equation}
 m_B=P_B\psi,
 \qquad
 m_C=P_C\psi,
 \qquad
 m_D=P_D\psi,
 \label{eq:V25-three-messages}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \eta_B=m_D-m_B,
 \qquad
 \eta_C=m_D-m_C.
 \label{eq:V25-two-incidence-innovations}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Two-record common-refinement rectangle]
\label{thm:V25-common-refinement-rectangle}
The innovations satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \eta_B\perp L^2(\mathscr B),
 \qquad
 \eta_C\perp L^2(\mathscr C),
 \qquad
 m_B-m_C=\eta_C-\eta_B.
 \label{eq:V25-innovation-relations}
\end{equation}
Their incidence Gram
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{B,C\mid D}^{\rm inc}
 :=\begin{pmatrix}
 b_B&\chi\\
 \overline\chi&b_C
 \end{pmatrix}
 :=\begin{pmatrix}
 \|\eta_B\|_2^2&\langle\eta_B,\eta_C\rangle\\
 \langle\eta_C,\eta_B\rangle&\|\eta_C\|_2^2
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0}
 \label{eq:V25-incidence-Gram}
\end{equation}
contains the complete failure of nesting.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{B,C}:=\|m_B-m_C\|_2^2
 =b_B+b_C-2\operatorname{Re}\chi,}
 \label{eq:V25-two-record-distance}
\end{equation}
so
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (\sqrt{b_B}-\sqrt{b_C})^2
 \le d_{B,C}
 \le(\sqrt{b_B}+\sqrt{b_C})^2.}
 \label{eq:V25-two-record-interval}
\end{equation}
If \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr B\), one may take
\(\mathscr D=\mathscr B\), so \(b_B=0\) and the ordinary nested Pythagoras is
recovered.  Without nesting the cross term \(\chi\) cannot be discarded.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since \(P_BP_D=P_B\) and \(P_CP_D=P_C\), each difference in
\eqref{eq:V25-two-incidence-innovations} is orthogonal to the corresponding
smaller subspace.  Subtracting the two identities
\(m_D=m_B+\eta_B=m_C+\eta_C\) gives
\eqref{eq:V25-innovation-relations}.  Taking the squared norm gives
\eqref{eq:V25-two-record-distance}.  Positivity of the Gram and
Cauchy--Schwarz give \(|\chi|\le\sqrt{b_Bb_C}\), which yields
\eqref{eq:V25-two-record-interval}.  The nested specialization is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Positive acquisition of both incidence innovations]
\label{cor:V25-positive-incidence}
The two diagonal innovations have exact conditional-replica forms.  If
\(D_1,D_2\) are independent copies of the \(\mathscr D\)-record conditional
on \(\mathscr B\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 b_B
 =\frac12\mathbb E
   \left[
    \bigl(m_D(D_1)-m_D(D_2)\bigr)^2
   \right].}
 \label{eq:V25-bB-replica}
\end{equation}
The analogous identity with copies conditional on \(\mathscr C\) gives
\(b_C\).  The complete cross term may be acquired directly, or reconstructed
from the additional positive writer \(|m_B-m_C|^2\) by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\operatorname{Re}\chi=\frac{b_B+b_C-d_{B,C}}2.}
 \label{eq:V25-cross-from-distance}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Because \(m_B=\mathbb E[m_D\mid\mathscr B]\), conditional two-copy variance
gives \eqref{eq:V25-bB-replica}.  The second statement is the same identity
with \(\mathscr C\), and the last formula rearranges
\eqref{eq:V25-two-record-distance}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Corrected native-fine versus natural-coarse message transport}
\label{sec:V25-corrected-message}
% =============================================================================

Choose one of the two block-complete records in
\eqref{eq:V25-even-completion}--\eqref{eq:V25-odd-completion} and denote it by
\(\mathscr D\).  Let \(\mathscr B\) be its native-shell subrecord and let
\(\mathscr C\) be the pulled-back coarse shell record.  On the common fine law
let
\[
 m_B=P_B\psi_Y,
 \qquad
 m_C=P_C\psi_Y,
 \qquad
 m_D=P_D\psi_Y.
\]
Let \(y_C\in L^2(\mathscr C)\) be the natural-coarse boundary message after
the V22 boundary-law module incidence.  Put
\begin{equation}
 d_{\rm sh}:=\|m_C-y_C\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_D:=\|m_D-y_C\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_B:=\|m_B-y_C\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V25-three-old-fine-distances}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Block-complete Pythagoras and native-shell rectangle]
\label{thm:V25-corrected-message}
With \(b_B,b_C\) from \eqref{eq:V25-incidence-Gram},
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{D_D=b_C+d_{\rm sh}.}
 \label{eq:V25-block-complete-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
Thus the V23--V24 nested-record compiler is exact on the block-complete
record.  The native-shell distance is instead
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_B=d_{B,C}+d_{\rm sh}
 +2\operatorname{Re}\omega,}
 \qquad
 \omega:=\langle m_B-m_C,m_C-y_C\rangle,
 \label{eq:V25-native-old-rectangle}
\end{equation}
with the sharp interval
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \bigl(\sqrt{d_{B,C}}-\sqrt{d_{\rm sh}}\bigr)^2
 \le D_B
 \le
 \bigl(\sqrt{d_{B,C}}+\sqrt{d_{\rm sh}}\bigr)^2.}
 \label{eq:V25-native-old-interval}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, comparison through the common refinement gives
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\sqrt{D_B}-\sqrt{b_B}\right|
 \le\sqrt{b_C+d_{\rm sh}}.}
 \label{eq:V25-completion-native-sandwich}
\end{equation}
No sum of the nonnegative diagonal rows is equal to the native-shell distance
unless the corresponding cross term is proved to vanish.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since \(m_D-m_C=\eta_C\perp L^2(\mathscr C)\) and
\(m_C-y_C\in L^2(\mathscr C)\), Pythagoras gives
\eqref{eq:V25-block-complete-Pythagoras}.  The identity
\[
 m_B-y_C=(m_B-m_C)+(m_C-y_C)
\]
gives \eqref{eq:V25-native-old-rectangle}; Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\eqref{eq:V25-native-old-interval}.  Finally,
\[
 m_B-y_C=(m_D-y_C)-(m_D-m_B)
\]
and the reverse triangle inequality give
\eqref{eq:V25-completion-native-sandwich}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Terminating attribution after a block-complete pass]
\label{cor:V25-attribution}
Suppose along adjacent dyadic cards that
\[
 D_D\longrightarrow0.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\sqrt{D_B}-\sqrt{b_B}\right|\longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V25-native-defect-is-bridge}
\end{equation}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item if \(b_B\to0\), the native-shell message also passes;
\item if \(\liminf D_B>0\), the complete surviving defect is the native-shell
      incidence innovation \(b_B\), not another endpoint source or
      shared-boundary law mismatch.
\end{enumerate}
Conversely, if \(b_B\to0\) but \(D_B\) stays positive, then the
block-complete transport distance \(D_D\) stays positive and the V24
shared-fibre/action alternative remains the correct upstream diagnosis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is \eqref{eq:V25-completion-native-sandwich}.  The two
alternatives follow by taking limits.  The converse is the reverse triangle
inequality in the same formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[No double charging]
\label{ass:V25-no-double-charge}
The exact-radius shell, the one-step-outer shell, and the pulled-back coarse
record are three records on one fine cylinder.  Their innovations are not
three source births.  The source is frozen once; \(b_B,b_C\), and the cross
term only record how the same source is resolved by incomparable boundary
records.  The V24 action modulus may bound the block-complete row
\(D_D=b_C+d_{\rm sh}\), while \(b_B\) is the separate incidence cost of
returning to the chosen native shell.  These quantities are assembled before
any positive radial loss is declared.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cofinal consequences and the revised physical acquisition}
\label{sec:V25-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

For a general dyadic pair \(M\to N=2M\), define the finite geometric audit
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak E_{N/M,R}
 :=L_R\setminus
   \bigl(\Sigma_{N,2R}\cup\Sigma_{N,2R+1}\bigr).
 \label{eq:V25-geometric-defect}
\end{equation}
The literal \(32\to64\) certificate proves
\(\mathfrak E_{64/32,R}=\varnothing\) for \(R=0,1,2,3\).
At every later cutoff and every growing physical radius, the same finite set
audit must be run before a nested conditional expectation is used.  A nonzero
\(\mathfrak E\) is an exact shell-incidence obstruction and is not repaired by
an action estimate.

\begin{theorem}[Cofinal shell-bracket transport criterion]
\label{thm:V25-cofinal-criterion}
Consider a cofinal dyadic family for which the geometric defects
\(\mathfrak E_{N/M,R}\) vanish and choose one block-complete record at each
step.  Let
\[
 b_{B,n},\quad b_{C,n},\quad d_{{\rm sh},n}
\]
be the two incidence innovations and the shared-boundary old/fine defect.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sqrt{D_{B,n}}
 \le
 \sqrt{b_{B,n}}
 +\sqrt{b_{C,n}+d_{{\rm sh},n}}.}
 \label{eq:V25-cofinal-upper}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 b_{B,n}+b_{C,n}+d_{{\rm sh},n}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 D_{B,n}\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:V25-cofinal-pass}
\end{equation}
If the square roots in \eqref{eq:V25-cofinal-upper} are summable after
transport to one common screen, the native boundary-message amplitudes have a
unique strong Cauchy landing.

If the two native and old message stocks have a common positive lower bound,
\(D_{B,n}\to0\) implies that their oriented mixed coefficients tend to one.
If a message stock tends to zero, the output is source-relative message
extinction, not a survivor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first inequality is \eqref{eq:V25-completion-native-sandwich} together
with \eqref{eq:V25-block-complete-Pythagoras}.  The vanishing implication is
immediate.  Summability gives the Cauchy criterion by composing the declared
adjacent incidences.  For positive stocks, expansion of the squared distance
gives the oriented mixed coefficient; convergence of the distance forces the
norms and the normalized angle to agree.  A vanishing stock has no unit
message direction and is therefore retained as extinction.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The one-step bracket is not a radial verdict]
\label{fire:V25-bracket-not-radial}
The bracket thickness is \(a_N\), but its base radius is \(a_MR\), which may
tend to zero or remain positive.  A persistent incidence innovation is
therefore typed by its actual physical-radius sequence.  It is not declared a
contact survivor merely because the two compared fine shells are adjacent,
and it is not declared a positive-range survivor before the source stock and
the V11 positive-width Bayes-reverse channel are read.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V26 direction: the least common record precedes a link-coordinate completion}
\label{sec:V26-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V25 repaired a genuine geometric defect: the pulled-back coarse shell
record is not measurable from either inherited single fine shell.  It then
constructed two link-coordinate completions and used a common-refinement
rectangle.  Those results remain exact.  The next upstream question is
whether the completed record contains only the information required by the
old/fine message target.

The answer is generally no.  To compare one native fine shell with the
pulled-back coarse shell, the required record is only their least common
sigma-algebra.  Revealing every missing fine child link is a stronger
experiment whenever a coarse parent has no child in the chosen native shell:
the parent product is required, but the relative factorization of that
product is not.

This distinction is operationally important.  A larger completion increases
both incidence diagonals and their mixed entry by the same positive stock.
That stock cancels from the native/coarse message distance only when the mixed
entry is retained.  If it is instead labelled as a new boundary source, the
same relative-child information is charged twice.

The corrected order is therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{frozen global source and literal native fine shell}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{pulled-back coarse parent-product record}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{least product join }\mathscr B\vee\mathscr C
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{direct native/old message distance}
 \\
 \Downarrow\quad
 \begin{matrix}
 \text{minimal-join attribution only if the direct target does not decide,}\\[-0.1em]
 \text{then the independent positive-width radial posterior.}
 \end{matrix}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V26-upstream-order}
\end{equation}

\begin{firewall}[No target inflation]
\label{fire:V26-no-target-inflation}
The native/old scalar message Gram does not require a link-field coupling, a
complete fine state, or an individually readable factorization of every
coarse block product.  Such stronger records remain legitimate when their
hidden detail is itself the target.  They are not prerequisites for the
source-message angle.  Version~V26 therefore does not discard either
Version~V25 completion; it identifies and shorts the common overresolution
which one of them may contain.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The least native-shell/coarse-product join}
\label{sec:V26-product-join}
% =============================================================================

Let \(N=2M\), fix a coarse radius \(R\), and assume for the moment that the
V25 two-shell geometric defect vanishes.  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), put
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr B_j:=\mathscr B_{N,2R+j},
 \qquad
 \mathscr C:=B_{N\to M}^{-1}\mathscr B_{M,R},
 \qquad
 \boxed{\mathscr D_j^{\times}:=\mathscr B_j\vee\mathscr C.}
 \label{eq:V26-minimal-product-join}
\end{equation}
The superscript \(\times\) records that \(\mathscr C\) exposes the ordered
parent products, not their individual fine factors.

For a coarse shell link \(e\), define
\begin{equation}
 n_j(e):=
 \#\bigl(\operatorname{Ch}(e)\cap\Sigma_{N,2R+j}\bigr)
 \in\{0,1,2\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_j:=\{e:n_j(e)=0\}.
 \label{eq:V26-parent-types}
\end{equation}
The set \(\mathcal A_j\) consists of coarse parents whose two fine children
are both absent from the chosen native shell.  Let
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr D_j^{\rm link}
 :=\mathscr B_j\vee
   \sigma\!\left(
      U_f:f\in L_R\setminus\Sigma_{N,2R+j}
   \right)
 \label{eq:V26-link-completion}
\end{equation}
be the corresponding V25 link-coordinate completion.

\begin{theorem}[Exact product/relative-child factorization]
\label{thm:V26-product-relative-factorization}
For each \(e\in\mathcal A_j\), choose the first child as a relative coordinate,
\[
 R_e:=U_{e^{(0)}}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr D_j^{\rm link}
 =\mathscr D_j^{\times}
  \vee\sigma(R_e:e\in\mathcal A_j).}
 \label{eq:V26-link-product-factorization}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr D_j^{\rm link}=\mathscr D_j^{\times}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal A_j=\varnothing}
 \label{eq:V26-link-product-equality}
\end{equation}
at every finite Wilson coupling.

When \(\mathcal A_j\ne\varnothing\), the inclusion is strict and each absent
parent carries one residual \(\SU(3)\) factorization fibre.  More precisely,
with
\[
 W_e=U_{e^{(0)}}U_{e^{(1)}},
\]
the fibre over a fixed \(W_e\) is parametrized by
\begin{equation}
 (U_{e^{(0)}},U_{e^{(1)}})
 =\bigl(g,g^{-1}W_e\bigr),
 \qquad g\in\SU(3).
 \label{eq:V26-relative-fibre}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If \(n_j(e)=2\), both children are already in \(\mathscr B_j\).  If
\(n_j(e)=1\), the native shell gives one child and the product record gives
\(W_e\).  The missing child is then recovered exactly as
\[
 U_{e^{(1)}}=U_{e^{(0)}}^{-1}W_e
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 U_{e^{(0)}}=W_eU_{e^{(1)}}^{-1},
\]
according to which child is known.  If \(n_j(e)=0\), the product record gives
only \(W_e\); adjoining \(R_e=U_{e^{(0)}}\) recovers
\(U_{e^{(1)}}=R_e^{-1}W_e\).  Since different coarse positive links have
disjoint child pairs, these reconstructions assemble simultaneously and
prove \eqref{eq:V26-link-product-factorization}.

If \(\mathcal A_j=\varnothing\), no relative coordinate is needed.  Conversely,
fix \(e\in\mathcal A_j\) and condition on every other fine link and on
\(W_e\).  Product Haar measure disintegrates along
\eqref{eq:V26-relative-fibre} with Haar fibre coordinate \(g\).  At finite
Wilson coupling the Gibbs density is continuous and strictly positive, so
the conditional fibre law has full Haar support.  A nonconstant bounded
function of \(g\) is therefore not measurable from
\(\mathscr D_j^{\times}\).  Hence the inclusion is strict.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The product join is the unique target-minimal completion]
\label{cor:V26-target-minimal-join}
The sigma-algebra \(\mathscr D_j^{\times}=\mathscr B_j\vee\mathscr C\) is the
unique least record containing both the native shell and every pulled-back
coarse shell matrix.  Any completion that reveals the individual child pair
of a parent in \(\mathcal A_j\) contains an additional relative-child record
not required by the old/fine source-message target.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A join is, by definition, the least sigma-algebra containing its two
arguments.  The additional statement is
\Cref{thm:V26-product-relative-factorization}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Completion-gauge invariance of the incidence rectangle}
\label{sec:V26-completion-gauge}
% =============================================================================

The next theorem is independent of lattice geometry and identifies exactly
what changes when a larger common refinement is used.

Let \(\mathscr B,\mathscr C\) be two records on one probability space, put
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr D_*:=\mathscr B\vee\mathscr C,
 \label{eq:V26-abstract-minimal-join}
\end{equation}
and let \(\widetilde{\mathscr D}\supseteq\mathscr D_*\).  For a centered
\(\psi\in L^2\), write
\[
 m_A:=\mathbb E[\psi\mid\mathscr A].
\]
For a common refinement \(\mathscr D\), define
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 b_B(\mathscr D)&:=\|m_D-m_B\|_2^2,\\
 b_C(\mathscr D)&:=\|m_D-m_C\|_2^2,\\
 \chi(\mathscr D)&:=
 \langle m_D-m_B,m_D-m_C\rangle.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:V26-completion-dependent-rows}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact completion-gauge Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V26-completion-gauge}
Put
\begin{equation}
 r_{\widetilde D}:=m_{\widetilde D}-m_{D_*},
 \qquad
 \varrho_{\widetilde D}:=\|r_{\widetilde D}\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V26-overresolution-stock}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 b_B(\widetilde{\mathscr D})
 &=b_B(\mathscr D_*)+\varrho_{\widetilde D},\\
 b_C(\widetilde{\mathscr D})
 &=b_C(\mathscr D_*)+\varrho_{\widetilde D},\\
 \chi(\widetilde{\mathscr D})
 &=\chi(\mathscr D_*)+\varrho_{\widetilde D}.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V26-completion-gauge-three}
\end{equation}
Consequently the native/coarse record distance is completion invariant:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|m_B-m_C\|_2^2
 =b_B(\mathscr D)+b_C(\mathscr D)
  -2\operatorname{Re}\chi(\mathscr D)}
 \label{eq:V26-completion-invariant-distance}
\end{equation}
for every \(\mathscr D\supseteq\mathscr D_*\).

If \(y_C\in L^2(\mathscr C)\) is an old-law message on the common screen and
\[
 D(\mathscr D):=\|m_D-y_C\|_2^2,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D(\widetilde{\mathscr D})
 =D(\mathscr D_*)+\varrho_{\widetilde D}.}
 \label{eq:V26-completion-gauge-old-distance}
\end{equation}
Thus the least join simultaneously minimizes both incidence diagonals and the
block-complete old/fine distance among all common refinements.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since \(\mathscr D_*\subseteq\widetilde{\mathscr D}\), conditional-expectation
Pythagoras gives
\[
 r_{\widetilde D}\perp L^2(\mathscr D_*).
\]
Both \(m_{D_*}-m_B\) and \(m_{D_*}-m_C\) belong to
\(L^2(\mathscr D_*)\).  Expanding
\[
 m_{\widetilde D}-m_B
 =r_{\widetilde D}+(m_{D_*}-m_B),
\]
and the analogous \(C\)-identity proves the two diagonal formulas.  Expanding
the mixed inner product leaves the same additional term
\(\|r_{\widetilde D}\|_2^2\), proving the third.  Its cancellation gives
\eqref{eq:V26-completion-invariant-distance}.  Finally,
\(m_{D_*}-y_C\in L^2(\mathscr D_*)\), so the same orthogonal decomposition
proves \eqref{eq:V26-completion-gauge-old-distance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Relative-child information is not a second source birth]
\label{cor:V26-relative-not-birth}
For the dyadic records of \Cref{thm:V26-product-relative-factorization}, put
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak r_{R,j}^{\rm rel}
 :=\left\|
   \mathbb E[\psi\mid\mathscr D_j^{\rm link}]
   -\mathbb E[\psi\mid\mathscr D_j^{\times}]
  \right\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V26-relative-source-stock}
\end{equation}
Then every V25 incidence diagonal and the block-complete old/fine distance
computed on \(\mathscr D_j^{\rm link}\) equals its target-minimal value plus
\(\mathfrak r_{R,j}^{\rm rel}\), while the native/coarse message distance is
unchanged after the mixed entry is assembled.

On the audited outer-shell branch of
\Cref{thm:V26-outer-minimal-next-pair},
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak r_{R,1}^{\rm rel}=0}
\]
identically for every source.  On an exact-radius branch with absent parents,
the record-level relative projection is nonzero, although its value on one
particular physical source may still vanish.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:V26-completion-gauge} with
\(\mathscr D_*=\mathscr D_j^{\times}\) and
\(\widetilde{\mathscr D}=\mathscr D_j^{\rm link}\).  The outer-shell statement
is \eqref{eq:V26-outer-minimal-equality}.  Strictness of the record inclusion
when absent parents occur is
\Cref{thm:V26-product-relative-factorization}; it guarantees a nonzero
orthogonal projection on some bounded writer, not necessarily on the chosen
Creutz source.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Qualification of the V25 diagonal attribution]
\label{ass:V26-V25-attribution}
Version~V25 correctly warned that the two diagonal innovations cannot be
added without their mixed term.  Version~V26 sharpens the reason.  On a
nonminimal completion, both diagonals and their cross contain the same common
overresolution stock.  Only the least-join values are intrinsic incidence
rows.  A link-coordinate value is still usable if its mixed entry is retained
or if the relative-child stock is shorted first.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The direct native/old message Gram is the primary target}
\label{sec:V26-direct-target}
% =============================================================================

Let \(m_B\) be the native fine-shell source message and let \(y_C\) be the
natural-coarse message after the already fixed law incidence.  Put
\begin{equation}
 i_B:=\|m_B\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 i_X:=\|y_C\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_B:=\|m_B-y_C\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:V26-direct-three-scalars}
\end{equation}
These objects are defined on the common fine cylinder even though
\(\mathscr B\) and \(\mathscr C\) are incomparable.

\begin{theorem}[Completion-free reconstruction of the selected message Gram]
\label{thm:V26-completion-free-Gram}
The complete signed native/old message Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 i_B&c_B\\ c_B&i_X
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 c_B=\frac{i_B+i_X-D_B}{2}.}
 \label{eq:V26-direct-message-Gram}
\end{equation}
If \(i_Bi_X>0\), its oriented coefficient is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_{Y/X}^{\rm msg}
 =\frac{i_B+i_X-D_B}{2\sqrt{i_Bi_X}}.}
 \label{eq:V26-direct-message-angle}
\end{equation}
No common refinement is required to determine this scalar target.

A common refinement is required only for attribution.  On the least join
\(\mathscr D_*\), put
\[
 b_B^*:=b_B(\mathscr D_*),
 \qquad
 D_*:=\|m_{D_*}-y_C\|_2^2.
\]
Then the sharp V25 comparison becomes the intrinsic estimate
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\sqrt{D_B}-\sqrt{b_B^*}\right|
 \le\sqrt{D_*}.}
 \label{eq:V26-intrinsic-native-sandwich}
\end{equation}
Every larger completion replaces both \(b_B^*\) and \(D_*\) by values with
the same additional overresolution stock and therefore gives a weaker
attribution bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The polarization identity gives \eqref{eq:V26-direct-message-Gram} and
normalization gives \eqref{eq:V26-direct-message-angle}.  For the last
statement write
\[
 m_B-y_C=(m_{D_*}-y_C)-(m_{D_*}-m_B)
\]
and apply the reverse triangle inequality.  Minimality follows from
\eqref{eq:V26-completion-gauge-three} and
\eqref{eq:V26-completion-gauge-old-distance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Target-minimal acquisition hierarchy]
\label{cor:V26-acquisition-hierarchy}
On one selected adjacent-cutoff boundary card, proceed in the following
order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item Acquire \(i_B,i_X,D_B\).  If their outward intervals decide
      \eqref{eq:V26-direct-message-angle}, stop the cutoff-message row without
      constructing a completion diagnostic.
\item If a nonzero direct defect requires attribution, use only the least join
      \(\mathscr D_*\) and acquire \(b_B^*\) and \(D_*\), or its already
      isolated shared-fibre/action components.
\item A larger link-coordinate completion is charged only when relative-child
      information is itself a declared target.  Otherwise its stock is shorted
      by \eqref{eq:V26-completion-gauge-old-distance}.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, a failure of a sufficient action-modulus upper bound remains
unresolved unless the direct message distance or a lower witness is acquired.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first item is \Cref{thm:V26-completion-free-Gram}.  The second and third
are \Cref{thm:V26-completion-gauge}.  The last statement is the usual
one-sided status discipline: failure of an upper certificate is not a lower
obstruction.
\end{proof}

\section{Cofinal handoff after the target-minimal correction}
\label{sec:V26-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Minimal-join cutoff-message alternative]
\label{thm:V26-cofinal-alternative}
Consider a cofinal dyadic sequence with source directions frozen before shell
conditioning.  On each adjacent pair, let \(D_{B,n}\) be the direct
native/old message distance and let \(i_{B,n},i_{X,n}\) be its two message
stocks.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item If \(D_{B,n}\to0\) and
      \(\inf_n\min\{i_{B,n},i_{X,n}\}>0\), then
      \(\alpha_{Y_n/X_n}^{\rm msg}\to1\).  Summability of
      \(\sqrt{D_{B,n}}\) on the declared common screens gives a unique strong
      oriented boundary-message landing.
\item If either message stock tends to zero, the branch is source-relative
      message extinction and no unit message survivor is formed.
\item If \(\limsup_nD_{B,n}>0\), compute the attribution only on
      \(\mathscr D_{*,n}=\mathscr B_n\vee\mathscr C_n\).  A vanishing
      \(D_{*,n}\) forces the surviving defect into the intrinsic native-shell
      incidence row \(b_{B,n}^*\); a vanishing \(b_{B,n}^*\) forces it into the
      shared-fibre/action row.  No relative-child overresolution is a third
      physical branch.
\item If the two-shell geometric defect is nonzero, the missing child support
      is the shell-incidence obstruction and the message comparison stops
      before an action bound is used.
\end{enumerate}
Only after branch~\textup{(a)} has passed is the V11 positive-width
Bayes-reverse radial loss acquired.  Its strict loss gives radial contraction;
a near-unit channel at a positive limiting physical width gives the
positive-range retained-source packet.  A shrinking-width packet remains
contact scale.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For positive stock floors, \eqref{eq:V26-direct-message-angle} and
\(D_{B,n}\to0\) force the oriented coefficient to one; summability is the
Hilbert-space Cauchy criterion.  A vanishing stock has no normalized message
line.  The attribution statements follow from
\eqref{eq:V26-intrinsic-native-sandwich} and its reverse-triangle companion.
The geometric and radial statements retain the V25 and V11 audit order.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Spatial message transport is not reflected-time mass]
\label{fire:V26-not-mass}
The source, shell, product-join, and Bayes-reverse cards are spatial Wilson
boundary objects.  Their contraction or survival does not identify the
Osterwalder--Schrader semigroup, the full centre-neutral vacuum carrier, or a
continuum mass.  Those conclusions retain the independent YM--A action,
reflection, phase, source-metric, tail, and full-core rows.
\end{firewall}

\begin{openproblem}[Version V27: read the direct message card before another completion theorem]
\label{op:V26-V27}
Preserve Versions~V1--V26 and every frozen source, action, dyadic, shell,
gauge, orientation, and physical-radius convention.  Proceed only in this
order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V27.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item On one predeclared selected adjacent dyadic pair, run the finite bracket
      audit and form the least product join
      \(\mathscr B_Y\vee B_{Y\to X}^{-1}\mathscr B_X\).
\item Acquire the two native/old message stocks and the direct positive distance
      \(D_B\).  Return the signed interval from

      panel.
\item If the direct interval passes, continue immediately to the V11
      positive-width Bayes-reverse source loss.  If it obstructs and a cause is

      already isolated action components.
\item Do not use an exact-radius link completion without shorting its
      relative-child stock.  On the audited next pair the one-step-outer
      completion is already target minimal.
\item Return oriented cutoff-message alignment, intrinsic shell-incidence
      innovation, shared-fibre/action obstruction, message extinction,
      geometric failure, an unresolved interval, or an ill-typed input.
\item After an oriented source-visible pass, export radial contraction or a
      positive-range retained-source packet and terminate YM--B.  Retain the
      V17 extinction result on every sublinear selected-root branch.
\end{enumerate}
No additional common refinement, endpoint Hellinger decomposition, source
atlas, representation bank, stochastic cutoff process, or radial
reparametrization is admissible before the direct physical message card is
populated.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{assessment}[Version V26 termination]
\label{ass:V26-termination}
The remaining circularity was the assumption that a coordinate-complete
fine record was needed before the scalar old/fine message Gram could be read.
The least product join is the canonical diagnostic record, and the direct
native/old distance is even weaker and target complete.  The geometry of the
next literal dyadic pair selects the one-step-outer completion without an
expectation-dependent choice.  Since no selected-root message value is
present in the attachments, the exact status remains
\[
 \boxed{\mathsf{STOP}\quad
 \text{at the three-scalar direct cutoff-message Read}.}
\]
This is a physical population boundary, not evidence that the message
transport fails.
\end{assessment}

\section{Version V27 direction: replace a worst-exterior coefficient by the actual side transfer}
\label{sec:V27-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V26 identified the irreducible scalar cutoff-message card: two
message stocks and one direct positive distance.  That card remains the
smallest exact acquisition of the signed old/fine message Gram.  No supplied
selected-root cylinder populates it, however.  Replacing it by another
polarization, Hellinger, replica, or completion formula would be circular.

There is one earlier Wilson-specific object which has not yet been used.
Versions~V16--V17 bounded every one-link conditional heat bath by a uniform
worst-exterior coefficient and multiplied that coefficient along a physical
rectangle side.  Version~V18 proved that the order of such a uniform estimate
is optimal: at linear or faster coupling, no further worst-exterior
one-link theorem can force the product to zero.  This does not imply that the
\emph{actual} Wilson heat baths occurring along the selected source side
saturate the worst exterior.

Version~V27 therefore retains the same minimum Peter--Weyl bank
\(\mathfrak R_2\) and replaces the uniform number
\(q_{\rm PW}(\beta)\) by the actual conditional mean matrices.  Their ordered
product is a gauge-covariant finite object on the original Wilson cylinder.
Its norm gives a direct sufficient contraction card.  More importantly, its
failure has an exact positive decomposition into one-link conditional colour
variances and therefore returns a concrete long colour-line corridor.

The corrected order is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{frozen Wilson source contour and its actual one-link heat baths}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{ordered side-transfer matrices in the existing bank }\mathfrak R_2
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \begin{matrix}
 \text{actual source-relative shell contraction,}\\[-0.1em]
 \text{or a positive-range conditional colour-line corridor}
 \end{matrix}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{only then the target-minimal direct message Read and radial posterior.}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V27-upstream-order}
\end{equation}

\begin{firewall}[The actual heat-bath panel is not a new source]
\label{fire:V27-heat-bath-not-source}
Every matrix below is a conditional expectation under the already occurring
Wilson law, with the source contour and representation bank fixed before the
selected-root value is inspected.  The panel is a response coefficient of the
existing source, not a second source birth, a fitted stochastic cutoff
process, or a replacement action.  Failure of its sufficient contraction
bound is not by itself failure of the direct message card.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{The actual one-link Wilson mean and strict finite-card contraction}
\label{sec:V27-one-link}
% =============================================================================

Fix one finite periodic Wilson card, one oriented link \(e\), and all links
other than \(e\).  After orienting the six incident staples consistently, the
conditional law of \(U_e\in\SU(3)\) has the form
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dd\nu_{e,\omega}(U)
 =\frac{1}{Z_e(H_e)}
   \exp\!\left[
    \frac{\beta}{3}\operatorname{ReTr}(UH_e(\omega))
   \right]\dd U,}
 \label{eq:V27-one-link-law}
\end{equation}
where \(H_e\) is the sum of the incident oriented staple matrices and
\(\dd U\) is normalized Haar measure.  For a finite-dimensional unitary
representation \(\rho\), put
\begin{equation}
 A_{e,\rho}^{+}(\omega)
 :=\int\rho(U)\,\dd\nu_{e,\omega}(U),
 \qquad
 A_{e,\rho}^{-}(\omega)
 :=\int\rho(U^{-1})\,\dd\nu_{e,\omega}(U)
 =\bigl(A_{e,\rho}^{+}(\omega)\bigr)^*.
 \label{eq:V27-one-link-mean}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[One-link partition-gradient realization]
\label{prop:V27-partition-gradient}
For every complex matrix direction \(X\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D_X\log Z_e(H)
 =\frac{\beta}{3}
  \mathbb E_{\nu_{e,H}}\operatorname{ReTr}(UX).}
 \label{eq:V27-partition-gradient}
\end{equation}
Consequently the defining-representation mean matrix is reconstructed by the
first matrix derivatives of the actual one-link partition function.  The
remaining matrices for \(\rho\in\mathfrak R_2\) are finite matrix insertions
in the same one-link cylinder.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The group is compact and the integrand is smooth in the finite-dimensional
parameter \(H\), so differentiation under the integral is valid.  Dividing
\(D_XZ_e\) by \(Z_e\) gives \eqref{eq:V27-partition-gradient}.  Polarization
in the real and imaginary matrix entries recovers the defining mean.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Mean-unitary conditional variance identity]
\label{lem:V27-mean-unitary-variance}
Let \(R\) be a random unitary operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space,
let \(A=\mathbb ER\), and let \(v\) be any vector.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E\norm{Rv-Av}^2
 =\norm v^2-\norm{Av}^2.}
 \label{eq:V27-mean-unitary-variance}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Expand the square.  Since \(R\) is unitary,
\(\mathbb E\norm{Rv}^2=\norm v^2\), while
\(\mathbb E\ip{Rv}{Av}=\ip{Av}{Av}\).  The two cross terms therefore remove
one of the two copies of \(\norm{Av}^2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict finite-card contraction in every nontrivial irreducible]
\label{thm:V27-strict-one-link}
At finite \(\beta\), for every exterior configuration and every nontrivial
finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation \(\rho\) of
\(\SU(3)\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\norm{A_{e,\rho}^{\pm}}_{\rm op}<1.}
 \label{eq:V27-strict-one-link}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The density in \eqref{eq:V27-one-link-law} is continuous and strictly
positive on the whole group.  Suppose \(\norm{A_{e,\rho}^{+}v}=\norm v=1\)
for some unit vector.  By \Cref{lem:V27-mean-unitary-variance},
\(\rho(U)v=A_{e,\rho}^{+}v\) for almost every \(U\).  Full support and
continuity make this identity valid for every \(U\in\SU(3)\).  At the
identity the common vector is \(v\), so \(v\) is invariant under \(\rho\),
contradicting nontrivial irreducibility.  Compactness of the unit sphere then
gives a strict operator-norm bound.  The inverse-orientation mean is the
adjoint and has the same norm.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Factorized physical-side transfer and its exact positive action}
\label{sec:V27-side-transfer}
% =============================================================================

Let \(C\) be one of the four frozen physical rectangles.  Let
\(S=(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\) be an oriented straight side of \(C\) such that no
plaquette contains two selected links.  This is the long-side geometry
certified in Versions~V15 and V17.  Condition on
\(\mathscr F_{S^c}\), the sigma-algebra generated by all unselected links.

\begin{lemma}[Exact conditional factorization]
\label{lem:V27-side-factorization}
Conditionally on \(\mathscr F_{S^c}\), the selected links are independent and
have the one-link laws \eqref{eq:V27-one-link-law}.  For every unitary
representation \(\rho\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[\rho(U(C))\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 =T_{C,S,\rho}
 :=V_mA_{e_m,\rho}^{\epsilon_m}V_{m-1}\cdots
   V_1A_{e_1,\rho}^{\epsilon_1}V_0,}
 \label{eq:V27-side-transfer}
\end{equation}
where \(\epsilon_j\in\{+,-\}\) records the traversal orientation and every
\(V_j\) is a unitary matrix determined by the unselected links.  Hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left|\mathbb E[\chi_\rho(U(C))\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]\right|
 \le(\dim\rho)\,t_{C,S,\rho},
 \qquad
 t_{C,S,\rho}:=\norm{T_{C,S,\rho}}_{\rm op}.}
 \label{eq:V27-character-transfer-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every Wilson plaquette term contains at most one selected link.  After all
unselected links are fixed, the action is therefore a sum of functions of
the individual \(U_{e_j}\), proving conditional independence.  Expanding the
ordered loop word between consecutive selected links and integrating one
selected link at a time gives \eqref{eq:V27-side-transfer}.  The trace of a
matrix is bounded by its dimension times its operator norm.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Actual side action]
\label{def:V27-side-action}
For the transfer in \eqref{eq:V27-side-transfer}, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak A_{C,S,\rho}(\omega)
 :=1-t_{C,S,\rho}(\omega)^2\in(0,1].}
 \label{eq:V27-side-action}
\end{equation}
It is the conditional colour information lost while crossing the selected
physical side in the representation \(\rho\).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact colour-line action and telescoping]
\label{thm:V27-side-action-telescope}
For each fixed complement configuration, choose a unit vector \(v_0\) and
define the propagated vectors by inserting the matrices in
\eqref{eq:V27-side-transfer} in their displayed order.  At the \(j\)-th
heat-bath step write \(w_{j-1}\) for the incoming vector and
\(w_j=V_jA_{e_j,\rho}^{\epsilon_j}w_{j-1}\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{w_{j-1}}^2-\norm{w_j}^2
 =\int
  \norm{\rho(U^{\epsilon_j})w_{j-1}
       -A_{e_j,\rho}^{\epsilon_j}w_{j-1}}^2
  \,\dd\nu_{e_j,\omega}(U).}
 \label{eq:V27-local-colour-action}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 1-\norm{T_{C,S,\rho}v_0}^2
 =\sum_{j=1}^{m}
   \int
    \norm{\rho(U^{\epsilon_j})w_{j-1}
         -A_{e_j,\rho}^{\epsilon_j}w_{j-1}}^2
    \,\dd\nu_{e_j,\omega}(U).}
 \label{eq:V27-side-action-telescope}
\end{equation}
Minimizing the right side over unit \(v_0\) gives exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak A_{C,S,\rho}
 =\min_{\norm{v_0}=1}
   \sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathfrak a_{e_j,\rho}(w_{j-1}).}
 \label{eq:V27-side-action-variational}
\end{equation}
The minimum is attained.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The fixed matrices \(V_j\) are unitary.  Apply
\Cref{lem:V27-mean-unitary-variance} to the random unitary
\(\rho(U^{\epsilon_j})\) and the incoming vector \(w_{j-1}\), obtaining
\eqref{eq:V27-local-colour-action}.  Summing telescopes all intermediate
norms and gives \eqref{eq:V27-side-action-telescope}.  For unit \(v_0\), the
right side equals \(1-\norm{T v_0}^2\); its minimum is therefore
\(1-\norm T_{\rm op}^2\).  The unit sphere is compact.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gauge covariance and invariant side stock]
\label{cor:V27-gauge-covariance}
Under a lattice gauge transformation, the open factors in
\eqref{eq:V27-side-transfer} transform by endpoint unitaries and the closed
rectangle transfer transforms by conjugation at its base vertex.  Therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 t_{C,S,\rho},\qquad
 \mathfrak A_{C,S,\rho},\qquad
 \text{and every value in \eqref{eq:V27-side-action-variational}}
 }
 \label{eq:V27-gauge-invariant-stocks}
\end{equation}
are gauge invariant when the propagated colour line is transformed
covariantly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A path holonomy transforms by left multiplication at its initial vertex and
right multiplication by the inverse gauge matrix at its terminal vertex.
The conditional heat-bath mean obeys the same covariance by Haar change of
variables.  Internal endpoint factors cancel in the ordered product, while a
closed path is conjugated at its basepoint.  Unitary conjugation preserves
singular values and all norm differences in the telescoping identity.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The actual heat-bath attenuation card}
\label{sec:V27-actual-card}
% =============================================================================

For each rectangle label \(\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square\), freeze one
admissible long side \(S_\alpha\).  For every ordered pair
\(\alpha\ne\gamma\), freeze the pair-private side
\(S_{\alpha\mid\gamma}\) supplied by Version~V15.  Define the actual
side-survival scalar
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 r_N^{\rm hb}:=\max\Biggl\{&
 \max_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square\\
                  \rho\in\mathfrak R_2}}
 \left(\mathbb E t_{\alpha,\rho}^2\right)^{1/2},\\
 &\max_{\alpha\ne\gamma}
 \left(\mathbb E t_{\alpha\mid\gamma,\mathbf3}^2\right)^{1/2}
 \Biggr\}.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V27-actual-attenuation}
\end{equation}
All expectations use the original Wilson law.  Every integrand lies in
\([0,1]\) and is a deterministic function of the actual one-link heat-bath
insertions.

\begin{theorem}[Actual first, second, mixed, and message bounds]
\label{thm:V27-actual-loop-bounds}
Let \(\Sigma_N\) be the raw covariance of the four normalized real Wilson
loops and let \(K_{N,R}\) be the covariance of their centered messages at any
separating shell.  Put \(r=r_N^{\rm hb}\).  Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \left\|\Sigma_N-\frac1{18}I_4\right\|_{\rm op}
 \le\frac{143}{18}r,}
 \label{eq:V27-actual-covariance-window}\\
 \boxed{
 0\preceq K_{N,R}\preceq16r^2I_4.}
 \label{eq:V27-actual-message-window}
\end{align}
The bounds are uniform over separating shell radii, but use the actual
selected-card value \(r\), not a worst-exterior function of \(\beta\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:V27-side-factorization} and the tower property,
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mid B_{N,R}]}_2
 \le\norm{t_{\alpha,\mathbf3}}_2\le r,
 \qquad
 |W_{\alpha,N}|\le r.
 \label{eq:V27-actual-first-bound}
\end{equation}
Use the exact character identity of
\Cref{lem:V17-character-square}.  The nonconstant representation dimensions,
with the adjoint counted twice, add to
\[
 3+3+6+6+2\cdot8=34.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and \eqref{eq:V27-actual-attenuation} therefore give
\[
 \left|\mathbb E\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}^2-\frac1{18}\right|
 \le\frac{17}{18}r.
\]
For \(\alpha\ne\gamma\), integrate the pair-private side of
\(C_\alpha\); the second loop is independent of those selected links and has
absolute value at most one.  Thus
\[
 |\mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mathcal O_{\gamma,N}]|
 \le r.
\]
After centering,
\[
 \left| (\Sigma_N)_{\alpha\alpha}-\frac1{18}\right|
 \le\frac{35}{18}r,
 \qquad
 |(\Sigma_N)_{\alpha\gamma}|\le2r.
\]
The maximum absolute row sum is \(143r/18\), proving
\eqref{eq:V27-actual-covariance-window}.

For the centered message component
\(m_\alpha=\mathbb E[\mathcal O_\alpha\mid B_{N,R}]-W_\alpha\),
\eqref{eq:V27-actual-first-bound} gives \(\norm{m_\alpha}_2\le2r\).
Hence for every coefficient vector \(a\),
\[
 \norm{\sum_\alpha a_\alpha m_\alpha}_2^2
 \le\norm a_2^2\sum_\alpha\norm{m_\alpha}_2^2
 \le16r^2\norm a_2^2,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:V27-actual-message-window}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Actual source-relative shell contraction]
\label{thm:V27-actual-source-contraction}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_{N,\rm hb}^2
 :=\begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \frac{288(r_N^{\rm hb})^2}{1-143r_N^{\rm hb}},
 &143r_N^{\rm hb}<1,\\[0.8em]
 1,&143r_N^{\rm hb}\ge1,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \widehat\kappa_{N,\rm hb}^2:=\min\{1,\kappa_{N,\rm hb}^2\}.
 \label{eq:V27-actual-kappa}
\end{equation}
Then every nonzero normalized four-loop contrast satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{
  \norm{\mathbb E[a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\mid B_{N,R}]}_2^2
 }{
  \norm{a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N}_2^2
 }
 \le\widehat\kappa_{N,\rm hb}^2.}
 \label{eq:V27-actual-source-ratio}
\end{equation}
In particular, if
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{r_N^{\rm hb}\longrightarrow0,}
 \label{eq:V27-actual-r-vanishes}
\end{equation}
then the complete normalized four-loop source message vanishes uniformly at
every separating shell, with no assumption on the growth rate of
\(\beta_N\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
When \(143r<1\), \Cref{thm:V27-actual-loop-bounds} gives
\[
 \Sigma_N\succeq\frac{1-143r}{18}I_4,
 \qquad
 K_{N,R}\preceq16r^2I_4
 \preceq\frac{288r^2}{1-143r}\Sigma_N.
\]
Congruence by the diagonal Wilson-loop normalization gives the same order for
the normalized source metric and its visible message metric.  On the
complementary branch, conditional expectation gives the universal ratio at
most one.  Scalar compression proves \eqref{eq:V27-actual-source-ratio}; the
cofinal assertion follows immediately.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Version V17 is the uniform envelope]
\label{cor:V27-V17-envelope}
For the side choices above,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_N^{\rm hb}(\beta)
 \le r_N^{\rm PW}(\beta).}
 \label{eq:V27-uniform-envelope}
\end{equation}
Thus Version~V17 is recovered by replacing every actual one-link mean by its
worst-exterior Peter--Weyl bound.  Version~V27 can be strictly stronger on a
linear or superlinear selected-root branch because it retains the actual
staple environments.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:V17-one-link-PW-contraction} bounds every factor in every
transfer product by \(q_{\rm PW}(\beta)\).  Each selected side has at least
\(N/4\) links, so the pointwise transfer norm is at most
\(q_{\rm PW}^{N/4}=r_N^{\rm PW}\).  Take the indicated \(L^2\) norms and
maxima.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{A surviving message forces a positive-range colour-line corridor}
\label{sec:V27-corridor}
% =============================================================================

The actual side panel is useful even when it does not prove contraction.  It
then exposes the normalized extremizer of the failed thermalization estimate.

Let \(\mathbf X_N=\mathbf O_N-\mathbb E\mathbf O_N\) and let
\(u_N\in\R^4\) be a unit coefficient vector, in particular the canonically
balanced Creutz direction of Version~V15.  Put
\begin{equation}
 G_N^{\rm raw}=u_N^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Nu_N,
 \qquad
 I_{N,R}^{\rm raw}=u_N^{\mathsf T}K_{N,R}u_N.
 \label{eq:V27-raw-source-stocks}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Positive-probability coherent colour-line corridor]
\label{thm:V27-colour-corridor}
Let \(N_n\to\infty\).  Suppose that on one subsequence
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{N_n})\ge s_*>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{I_{N_n,R_n}^{\rm raw}}{G_{N_n}^{\rm raw}}\ge\delta>0.
 \label{eq:V27-surviving-message-assumptions}
\end{equation}
Set
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{a:=\frac{\delta s_*}{16}\in(0,1].}
 \label{eq:V27-corridor-a}
\end{equation}
Then for every \(n\) there is one physical rectangle side
\(S_n=(e_{n,1},\ldots,e_{n,m_n})\), with \(m_n\ge N_n/4\), such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\,t_n^2\ge a,
 \qquad
 t_n:=t_{C_n,S_n,\mathbf3}.
 \label{eq:V27-transfer-stock-lower}
\end{equation}
Moreover the complement event
\begin{equation}
 E_n:=\{t_n^2\ge a/2\}
 \label{eq:V27-corridor-event}
\end{equation}
has probability
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb P(E_n)\ge\frac{a}{2-a}.}
 \label{eq:V27-corridor-probability}
\end{equation}
For every complement configuration in \(E_n\), there is a propagated colour
line \((\widehat v_{n,j})_{j=0}^{m_n}\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \norm{v_{n,j}}^2\ge\frac a2
 \qquad(0\le j\le m_n)
 \label{eq:V27-chain-noncollapse}
\end{equation}
and, with the normalized one-link conditional dispersions in the defining representation
\begin{equation}
 d_{n,j}
 :=\int
 \norm{\rho_{\mathbf3}(U^{\epsilon_j})\widehat v_{n,j-1}
       -A_{e_{n,j},\mathbf3}^{\epsilon_j}
        \widehat v_{n,j-1}}^2
 \,\dd\nu_{e_{n,j}}(U),
 \label{eq:V27-local-normalized-dispersion}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sum_{j=1}^{m_n}d_{n,j}\le\frac2a.}
 \label{eq:V27-corridor-total-dispersion}
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every \(\tau>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac1{m_n}
 \#\{j:d_{n,j}>\tau\}
 \le\frac{2}{a m_n\tau}.}
 \label{eq:V27-corridor-density}
\end{equation}
In particular, with \(\tau_n=m_n^{-1/2}\), a proportion tending to one of
the links has conditional colour dispersion at most \(m_n^{-1/2}\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first assumption in \eqref{eq:V27-surviving-message-assumptions} gives
\(G_{N_n}^{\rm raw}\ge s_*\), so
\(I_{N_n,R_n}^{\rm raw}\ge\delta s_*\).  Let
\(m_\alpha=\mathbb E[X_{\alpha,N_n}\mid B_{N_n,R_n}]\).  Since
\(\norm{u_n}=1\),
\[
 I_{N_n,R_n}^{\rm raw}
 \le\operatorname{tr}K_{N_n,R_n}
 =\sum_\alpha\norm{m_\alpha}_2^2.
\]
The first-moment part of \Cref{thm:V27-actual-loop-bounds}, before taking the
maximum over \(\alpha\), gives
\[
 \norm{m_\alpha}_2
 \le2\left(\mathbb E t_{\alpha,\mathbf3}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Therefore some \(\alpha\) satisfies
\(\mathbb E t_{\alpha,\mathbf3}^2\ge\delta s_*/16=a\), proving
\eqref{eq:V27-transfer-stock-lower}.  Since \(0\le t_n^2\le1\), writing
\(p=\mathbb P(E_n)\) gives
\[
 a\le\mathbb E t_n^2
 \le\frac a2(1-p)+p,
\]
which rearranges to \eqref{eq:V27-corridor-probability}.

On \(E_n\), choose a unit right singular vector \(v_{n,0}\) attaining
\(\norm{T_nv_{n,0}}=t_n\), and propagate it through the ordered factors.
All factors are contractions, so every intermediate norm is at least the
terminal norm \(t_n\ge\sqrt{a/2}\), proving
\eqref{eq:V27-chain-noncollapse}.  Let \(\ell_{n,j}\) be the unnormalized
local loss in \eqref{eq:V27-local-colour-action}.  The telescoping theorem
gives \(\sum_j\ell_{n,j}=1-t_n^2\le1\).  Since
\(\ell_{n,j}=\norm{v_{n,j-1}}^2d_{n,j}\) and every preceding norm squared is
at least \(a/2\),
\[
 \sum_jd_{n,j}\le\frac2a\sum_j\ell_{n,j}\le\frac2a.
\]
Markov counting proves \eqref{eq:V27-corridor-density}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Physical meaning of the corridor]
\label{ass:V27-corridor-meaning}
The selected side has a nonvanishing fraction of the frozen physical
rectangle length.  The theorem therefore returns a positive-physical-range
conditional colour transport corridor on an event of uniformly positive
probability.  It is not an abstract Hilbert-space soft vector.  It is also not
yet the positive-range boundary-source survivor of the original radial
trichotomy: that conclusion still requires the source-visible boundary
message and the positive-width Bayes-reverse channel.
\end{assessment}

\section{Gauge-visible closed-line fork}
\label{sec:V27-gauge-fork}
% =============================================================================

For a nonzero closed transfer \(T\) and a unit right singular vector \(v\)
with \(\norm{Tv}=\norm T_{\rm op}=t\), put \(P_v=vv^*\) and define
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak h(T,v)
 :=\frac{|\ip v{Tv}|^2}{t^2},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak q(T,v)
 :=\frac{\norm{(I-P_v)Tv}^2}{t^2}.
 \label{eq:V27-line-fork-def}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Closed-line turning Pythagoras]
\label{prop:V27-line-turning}
The two quantities in \eqref{eq:V27-line-fork-def} are gauge invariant and
obey
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\mathfrak h(T,v)+\mathfrak q(T,v)=1.}
 \label{eq:V27-line-turning-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
After subsequence extraction, every corridor from
\Cref{thm:V27-colour-corridor} has one of two further outcomes:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},leftmargin=4.2em]
\item \(\limsup\mathfrak q>0\): the closed physical rectangle carries a
      projective colour-line turn;
\item \(\mathfrak q\to0\): the maximal conditional colour line is
      asymptotically invariant under the closed transfer, and its remaining
      eigenphase or centre/toron character is the next gauge-invariant Read.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Orthogonally decompose \(Tv=P_vTv+(I-P_v)Tv\) and divide the squared norm by
\(t^2\).  Under a gauge transformation, \(T\) is conjugated and \(v\) is
rotated by the same basepoint unitary, so both summands are unchanged.  The
subsequence alternative is ordinary compactness of \([0,1]\).
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[A conditional colour line is not yet a mass or a gauge artefact]
\label{fire:V27-corridor-scope}
A positive projective-turning stock is a gauge-invariant nonabelian holonomy
witness for the conditional transfer.  An asymptotically invariant line may
instead be flat, centre valued, toroidal, or carried by another harmonic
sector.  Neither branch is identified with a Yang--Mills particle, an
Osterwalder--Schrader excitation, or a continuum mass.  The theorem prevents
the unresolved linear-coupling branch from being reported merely as
``failure of a bound''; it does not skip the subsequent physical classifier.
\end{firewall}

\section{Version V27 integrated alternative and stopping boundary}
\label{sec:V27-integrated}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Actual-side contraction or coherent-corridor alternative]
\label{thm:V27-integrated}
Preserving every theorem and limitation of Versions~V1--V26, the following
finite and cofinal statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V27.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.7em]
\item The actual one-link Wilson heat baths on the frozen physical sides
      determine finite gauge-covariant transfer matrices in the already
      existing bank \(\mathfrak R_2\).
\item Their loss has the exact positive telescoping action
      \eqref{eq:V27-side-action-variational}; no local loss is charged twice.
\item The single finite scalar \(r_N^{\rm hb}\) gives the complete four-loop
      covariance and boundary-message bounds
      \eqref{eq:V27-actual-covariance-window}--
      \eqref{eq:V27-actual-message-window}.
\item If \(r_N^{\rm hb}\to0\), every normalized four-loop source message
      vanishes at every separating shell, regardless of the growth of
      \(\beta_N\).
\item If the raw source frame retains a floor and a source-relative shell
      message retains a fixed fraction, then a physical long side carries the
      positive-probability density-one coherent colour-line corridor of
      \Cref{thm:V27-colour-corridor}.
\item The closed-line Pythagoras separates a projective holonomy turn from an
      asymptotically invariant line requiring a phase/centre/harmonic Read.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the unresolved linear-or-faster selected-root branch is reduced to a
literal actual-heat-bath alternative.  No further universal one-link or
larger finite-representation theorem is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Items~\textup{(V27.1)--(V27.2)} are
\Cref{lem:V27-side-factorization,thm:V27-side-action-telescope,cor:V27-gauge-covariance}.
Items~\textup{(V27.3)--(V27.4)} are
\Cref{thm:V27-actual-loop-bounds,thm:V27-actual-source-contraction}.
Item~\textup{(V27.5)} is \Cref{thm:V27-colour-corridor}, and the final item is
\Cref{prop:V27-line-turning}.
\end{proof}

\begin{openproblem}[Version V28: populate the actual side transfer before another universal estimate]
\label{op:V27-V28}
Preserve Versions~V1--V27 and every frozen source, action, dyadic, shell,
orientation, representation, and physical-radius convention.  Proceed only
in this order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V28.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item On one predeclared selected-root card, evaluate the actual one-link
      insertion matrices \(A_{e,\rho}^{\pm}\) along the frozen long and
      pair-private sides.  Do not replace them by a new worst-exterior bound.
\item Acquire the positive side survival stocks
      \(\mathbb E t_{C,S,\rho}^2\) and form \(r_N^{\rm hb}\).
\item If \(r_N^{\rm hb}<r_{\rm c}\), export the strict source-relative shell
      contraction.  If \(r_N^{\rm hb}\to0\), export complete separating-shell
      extinction and terminate that branch.
\item If a source-visible message survives with a raw-frame floor, extract the
      corridor vectors from \Cref{thm:V27-colour-corridor} and evaluate the
      closed-line turning/phase fork.  Return the resulting holonomy or
      harmonic candidate instead of opening another representation bank.
\item Use the V26 direct message triple only when the actual-side sufficient
      panel is inconclusive for the target.  On an oriented passing branch,
      acquire the V11 positive-width Bayes-reverse source loss.
\item Export radial contraction, a positive-range retained-source packet, a
      typed colour-line/holonomy obstruction, source-frame softening, an
      unresolved interval, or an ill-typed input.
\end{enumerate}
No additional uniform one-link theorem, larger Peter--Weyl bank, endpoint
Hellinger decomposition, common-refinement completion, stochastic cutoff
process, or radial reparametrization is admissible before this actual Wilson
side panel is populated.
\end{openproblem}

\begin{assessment}[Version V27 termination]
\label{ass:V27-termination}
The direct three-scalar message card remains target minimal, but its absence
no longer leaves the linear selected-root branch as an unnamed missing
number.  The actual heat-bath side transfer is an earlier Wilson coefficient.
It either contracts the complete source frame or produces a gauge-covariant,
positive-physical-range colour corridor with an exact local action budget.
Since the supplied files contain neither the selected-root side insertions nor
the direct message values, the current physical status is
\[
 \boxed{\mathsf{STOP}\quad
 \text{at the actual heat-bath side-transfer panel}.}
\]
This is not evidence for a surviving corridor.  It is the first physical
value whose two outcomes are now both mathematically typed.
\end{assessment}
