% =============================================================================
\section{Version V28 direction: acquire the scalar side survival before the full one-link matrix path}
\label{sec:V28-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V27 moved upstream from the still unpopulated direct cutoff-message
triple to the actual Wilson heat-bath propagation along the already frozen
physical rectangle sides.  Its matrix-valued coefficient is exact and its
coherent-corridor alternative remains valid.  The Version~V28 mandate,
however, asked first for every one-link insertion matrix and then for the
operator norm of their ordered product.  That packet is stronger than the
immediate source-moment target.

The four-loop covariance and boundary-message estimates do not require the
maximal colour-line survival itself.  They require only bounds on traces of
the conditional side transfer in the finite degree-two representation bank.
Those traces are controlled by the normalized Hilbert--Schmidt survival,
which has an exact positive two-replica realization on the original Wilson
cylinder.  Thus the correct target-native order is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one frozen complement and two conditionally independent side replicas}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{one relative side holonomy and three positive character losses}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{the complete four-loop covariance/message contraction card}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \begin{matrix}
 \text{source-relative contraction, or}\\[-0.1em]
 \text{a low-loss representation corridor requiring the V27 classifier.}
 \end{matrix}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V28-upstream-order}
\end{equation}

This does not discard the Version~V27 matrices.  They remain the correct
stronger data when the extremizing colour line, its linkwise dispersion, or
its closed-line phase is itself required.  Version~V28 proves that they need
not be populated merely to decide the scalar source-moment contraction.

\begin{firewall}[A replica identity does not manufacture replica occurrence]
\label{fire:V28-replica-occurrence}
The positive writer below is physically sampled only when two side interiors
are conditionally resampled over the same frozen complement, or when the
same conditional integral is evaluated deterministically.  Two unrelated
full Wilson configurations do not give the same quantity.  The common
complement is an incidence row, not a notation which may be dropped after
marginalization.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{One shared-complement relative-holonomy writer}
\label{sec:V28-relative-holonomy}
% =============================================================================

Fix one of the physical rectangle sides used in Version~V27 and condition on
\(\mathscr F_{S^c}\), the complete complement of the selected side.  Draw two
conditionally independent side configurations and denote the resulting
closed loop holonomies by
\begin{equation}
 G_1=G_{C,S}^{(1)},
 \qquad
 G_2=G_{C,S}^{(2)}
 \qquad\text{in }\SU(3).
 \label{eq:V28-two-side-holonomies}
\end{equation}
For a finite-dimensional unitary representation \(\rho\), write
\begin{equation}
 d_\rho=\dim\rho,
 \qquad
 R_a^\rho=\rho(G_a),
 \qquad
 T_\rho
 =\mathbb E[R_a^\rho\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}].
 \label{eq:V28-rep-transfer}
\end{equation}
The last matrix is the same conditional side transfer as
\eqref{eq:V27-side-transfer}.

\begin{definition}[Relative-holonomy replica loss]
\label{def:V28-relative-loss}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_\rho(G_1,G_2)
 :=\frac{1}{2d_\rho}
   \norm{R_1^\rho-R_2^\rho}_{\rm HS}^2
 =1-\frac1{d_\rho}
   \operatorname{Re}\chi_\rho(G_1^{-1}G_2).}
 \label{eq:V28-relative-loss}
\end{equation}
It is gauge invariant and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0\le \mathscr L_\rho\le2
 \label{eq:V28-loss-range-sample}
\end{equation}
sample by sample.
\end{definition}

\begin{proof}
Unitarity gives
\[
 \norm{R_1-R_2}_{\rm HS}^2
 =2d_\rho-2\operatorname{Re}\Tr(R_1^*R_2),
\]
and \(R_1^*R_2=\rho(G_1^{-1}G_2)\).  The character bound
\(\abs{\chi_\rho(g)}\le d_\rho\) proves the range.  A lattice gauge
transformation conjugates both closed holonomies at the common basepoint, so
it conjugates \(G_1^{-1}G_2\); the character is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact conditional replica identity]
\label{thm:V28-replica-identity}
For every finite-dimensional unitary representation,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[
  \mathscr L_\rho(G_1,G_2)
  \mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 =1-\frac1{d_\rho}\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \label{eq:V28-conditional-replica-identity}
\end{equation}
Consequently, with
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)}
 :=\mathbb E\mathscr L_\rho(G_1,G_2),
 \qquad
 q_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)\,2}
 :=\frac1{d_\rho}
   \mathbb E\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}^2,
 \label{eq:V28-global-loss-survival}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\le\Lambda_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)}\le1,
 \qquad
 q_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)\,2}
 =1-\Lambda_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)}.}
 \label{eq:V28-global-replica-identity}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac1{\sqrt{d_\rho}}\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}
 \le\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm op},}
 \label{eq:V28-HS-op-comparison}
\end{equation}
so the new normalized Hilbert--Schmidt survival is no larger than the
Version~V27 maximal-line survival.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional independence gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(R_1^\rho)^*R_2^\rho\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}]
 =T_\rho^*T_\rho.
\]
Taking the real trace in \eqref{eq:V28-relative-loss} proves
\eqref{eq:V28-conditional-replica-identity}.  Averaging gives
\eqref{eq:V28-global-replica-identity}; its range follows because a
normalized Hilbert--Schmidt square of a contraction lies in \([0,1]\).
Finally, the root-mean-square of the singular values is at most their
maximum, proving \eqref{eq:V28-HS-op-comparison}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What has been reduced]
\label{ass:V28-reduced-acquisition}
The scalar \(\Lambda_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)}\) is one nonnegative same-complement
expectation.  It reconstructs the exact normalized Hilbert--Schmidt survival
without first resolving the matrices \(A_{e,\rho}^{\pm}\), their singular
frames, or the maximizing input line.  Those stronger objects are reopened
only on a low-loss branch which requires the V27 corridor or phase witness.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The common complement is an indispensable incidence row}
\label{sec:V28-common-complement}
% =============================================================================

Let
\begin{equation}
 T_\rho(\omega)
 =\mathbb E[\rho(G)\mid\mathscr F_{S^c}](\omega)
 \label{eq:V28-random-transfer}
\end{equation}
be the random transfer indexed by the complement configuration.  There are
two different two-copy experiments.

In the first, both side replicas share the same complement.  In the second,
two complete Wilson configurations, including their complements, are drawn
independently.

\begin{theorem}[Same-complement versus independent-complement Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V28-complement-Pythagoras}
Define
\begin{align}
 Q_{\rm same}
 &:=\frac1{d_\rho}\mathbb E\norm{T_\rho(\omega)}_{\rm HS}^2,
 \label{eq:V28-same-survival}\\
 Q_{\rm ind}
 &:=\frac1{d_\rho}
   \norm{\mathbb E T_\rho(\omega)}_{\rm HS}^2,
 \label{eq:V28-independent-survival}\\
 \Delta_{\rm env}
 &:=\frac1{d_\rho}
   \mathbb E\norm{T_\rho(\omega)-\mathbb ET_\rho}_{\rm HS}^2.
 \label{eq:V28-environment-dispersion}
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{Q_{\rm same}=Q_{\rm ind}+\Delta_{\rm env}.}
 \label{eq:V28-complement-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if \(\Lambda_{\rm same}=1-Q_{\rm same}\) and
\(\Lambda_{\rm ind}=1-Q_{\rm ind}\), then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{\rm ind}
 =\Lambda_{\rm same}+\Delta_{\rm env}.}
 \label{eq:V28-independent-overloss}
\end{equation}
Thus independent full configurations can report strictly more loss than the
physical same-complement side channel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is the Hilbert--Schmidt conditional-expectation Pythagoras
\[
 \mathbb E\norm T_{\rm HS}^2
 =\norm{\mathbb ET}_{\rm HS}^2
  +\mathbb E\norm{T-\mathbb ET}_{\rm HS}^2,
\]
divided by \(d_\rho\).  Subtracting both sides from one gives
\eqref{eq:V28-independent-overloss}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Independent replicas can erase a perfect conditional corridor]
\label{cth:V28-independent-replica-no-go}
Let the complement select the three centre transfers
\begin{equation}
 T_\rho(\omega)
 \in\{I,\rho(\zeta I),\rho(\zeta^2I)\}
 \label{eq:V28-centre-transfer-example}
\end{equation}
with equal probability in the defining representation, where
\(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}\).  Then every conditional transfer is unitary, so
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{Q_{\rm same}=1,\qquad\Lambda_{\rm same}=0.}
 \label{eq:V28-perfect-same-corridor}
\end{equation}
But their unconditional mean is zero, so
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{Q_{\rm ind}=0,\qquad\Lambda_{\rm ind}=1.}
 \label{eq:V28-independent-total-loss}
\end{equation}
Hence unrelated full replicas would falsely replace a perfect conditional
centre corridor by total attenuation.  This is an exact unitary incidence
countermodel; it is not asserted to be attained by a finite-coupling Wilson
heat bath, whose strict contraction was proved in Version~V27.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The three centre phases sum to zero.  The assertions are immediate from
\Cref{thm:V28-complement-Pythagoras}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{One relative holonomy supplies the complete degree-two bank}
\label{sec:V28-character-bank}
% =============================================================================

Write \(\chi_{\mathbf3}(g)=\Tr g\).  The degree-two representations already
frozen in Versions~V17 and V27 satisfy the exact character identities
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi_{\overline{\mathbf3}}(g)
 &=\overline{\chi_{\mathbf3}(g)},\\
 \chi_{\mathbf6}(g)
 &=\frac12\left(
      \chi_{\mathbf3}(g)^2
      +\chi_{\mathbf3}(g^2)
    \right),\\
 \chi_{\overline{\mathbf6}}(g)
 &=\overline{\chi_{\mathbf6}(g)},\\
 \chi_{\mathbf8}(g)
 &=\abs{\chi_{\mathbf3}(g)}^2-1.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V28-SU3-character-identities}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Three positive losses from one shared replica pair]
\label{thm:V28-three-losses-one-pair}
For the single relative holonomy
\begin{equation}
 R_{12}=G_1^{-1}G_2,
 \label{eq:V28-relative-holonomy}
\end{equation}
the three nonnegative writers
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_{\mathbf3}(R_{12}),
 \qquad
 \mathscr L_{\mathbf6}(R_{12}),
 \qquad
 \mathscr L_{\mathbf8}(R_{12})}
 \label{eq:V28-three-positive-writers}
\end{equation}
reconstruct the normalized Hilbert--Schmidt survivals of the entire bank
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak R_2
 =\{\mathbf3,\overline{\mathbf3},
     \mathbf6,\overline{\mathbf6},\mathbf8\}.
 \label{eq:V28-existing-bank}
\end{equation}
Indeed,
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr L_{\overline\rho}
 =\mathscr L_\rho
 \label{eq:V28-conjugate-loss-equality}
\end{equation}
for \(\rho=\mathbf3,\mathbf6\).  No separate side replica is needed for the
conjugate representations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The decompositions
\[
 \mathbf3\otimes\mathbf3
 =\mathbf6\oplus\overline{\mathbf3},
 \qquad
 \mathbf3\otimes\overline{\mathbf3}
 =\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf8
\]
give \eqref{eq:V28-SU3-character-identities}.  Taking real parts in
\eqref{eq:V28-relative-loss} makes the loss invariant under complex
conjugation, proving \eqref{eq:V28-conjugate-loss-equality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite size of the positive side panel]
\label{cor:V28-panel-size}
Freeze one long side for each of the four physical rectangles and one
directed pair-private side for each of the six unordered rectangle pairs.
Then at most ten shared-complement side-replica cylinders produce the complete
positive acquisition:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{side class}&\text{number of replica cylinders}&\text{loss outputs}\\
 \hline
 \text{four long sides}&4&
   \mathscr L_{\mathbf3},\mathscr L_{\mathbf6},\mathscr L_{\mathbf8}\\
 \text{six pair-private sides}&6&
   \mathscr L_{\mathbf3}.
 \end{array}}
 \label{eq:V28-positive-panel-count}
\end{equation}
Thus the scalar covariance target uses ten conditional replica preparations
and eighteen nonnegative scalar expectations, rather than every one-link
matrix along \(O(N)\) side links.
\end{corollary}

% =============================================================================
\section{Trace-averaged side action and exact local telescope}
\label{sec:V28-trace-action}
% =============================================================================

Retain the ordered mean transfer
\begin{equation}
 T_\rho
 =V_mA_mV_{m-1}\cdots V_1A_1V_0
 \label{eq:V28-ordered-mean-transfer}
\end{equation}
from Version~V27, suppressing the representation and orientation labels on
the factors.  Put
\begin{equation}
 X_0=V_0,
 \qquad
 X_j=V_jA_jX_{j-1},
 \qquad
 X_m=T_\rho.
 \label{eq:V28-partial-mean-transfers}
\end{equation}
For the \(j\)-th heat bath, let \(R_j^{(1)},R_j^{(2)}\) be two conditionally
independent copies of the corresponding unitary representation matrix.

\begin{theorem}[Exact trace-averaged colour action]
\label{thm:V28-trace-action-telescope}
The normalized replica loss has the exact local decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 1-\frac1{d_\rho}\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}^2
 ={}&\frac1{2d_\rho}
 \sum_{j=1}^{m}
 \mathbb E
 \norm{
  (R_j^{(1)}-R_j^{(2)})X_{j-1}
 }_{\rm HS}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:V28-trace-action-telescope}
\end{equation}
Every summand is nonnegative and the sum is exact.  It averages the local
conditional colour dispersion over a complete orthonormal input frame; no
maximizing colour line and no minimization are required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For one mean \(A=\mathbb ER\) and one deterministic matrix \(X\), conditional
independence and unitarity give
\begin{equation}
 \frac12\mathbb E\norm{(R_1-R_2)X}_{\rm HS}^2
 =\norm X_{\rm HS}^2-\norm{AX}_{\rm HS}^2.
 \label{eq:V28-one-step-HS-variance}
\end{equation}
The unitary router \(V_j\) does not change the Hilbert--Schmidt norm, so the
right side equals
\(\norm{X_{j-1}}_{\rm HS}^2-\norm{X_j}_{\rm HS}^2\).  Summing telescopes from
\(\norm{X_0}_{\rm HS}^2=d_\rho\) to
\(\norm{X_m}_{\rm HS}^2=\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}^2\), proving the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Relation to the maximal colour-line action]
\label{cor:V28-action-comparison}
Conditionally on the complement, let
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak A_{\rm op}=1-\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm op}^2,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak A_{\rm HS}
 =1-\frac1{d_\rho}\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}^2.
 \label{eq:V28-two-side-actions}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{0\le\mathfrak A_{\rm op}
 \le\mathfrak A_{\rm HS}\le1.}
 \label{eq:V28-action-order}
\end{equation}
The Version~V27 operator action is the least loss over one colour line; the
Version~V28 action is the average loss over a complete orthonormal colour
frame.  They are alternative target levels and are not added.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V28-HS-op-comparison} gives the middle inequality; the
remaining bounds follow because \(T_\rho\) is a contraction.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The complete four-loop contraction from replica losses}
\label{sec:V28-four-loop}
% =============================================================================

Let \(\mathfrak I_\square=\{11,00,10,01\}\).  For each
\(\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square\), freeze the long side \(S_\alpha\) used for
the one-loop and loop-square bounds.  For each unordered pair
\(\{\alpha,\gamma\}\), freeze one of the two already certified directed
pair-private sides and denote it by \(S_{\alpha\mid\gamma}\).

Define the finite panel
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal P_N^{(2)}
 :={}&\{(\alpha,\rho):
        \alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square,
        \rho\in\{\mathbf3,\mathbf6,\mathbf8\}\}\\
 &\cup
 \{(\alpha\mid\gamma,\mathbf3):
        \{\alpha,\gamma\}\subset\mathfrak I_\square,
        \alpha\ne\gamma\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:V28-panel-index}
\end{equation}
For each entry \(p\), let \(\Lambda_{N,p}^{(2)}\) be the expected loss
\eqref{eq:V28-global-loss-survival}, and put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lambda_N^{(2)}
 :=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_N^{(2)}}\Lambda_{N,p}^{(2)},
 \qquad
 r_N^{(2)}
 :=\sqrt{1-\lambda_N^{(2)}}.}
 \label{eq:V28-global-panel-r}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, \(r_N^{(2)}\) is the largest \(L^2\) normalized
Hilbert--Schmidt survival over the finite side panel.

\begin{theorem}[Replica-side raw covariance and boundary-message windows]
\label{thm:V28-replica-loop-bounds}
Let \(\Sigma_N\) be the raw covariance matrix of the four normalized real
Wilson loops and let \(K_{N,R}\) be the covariance of their centered messages
at any separating shell.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\Sigma_N-\frac1{18}I_4}_{\rm op}
 \le\frac{143}{18}r_N^{(2)},}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-covariance-window}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\preceq K_{N,R}
 \preceq16\bigl(r_N^{(2)}\bigr)^2I_4.}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-message-window}
\end{equation}
In particular, when \(143r_N^{(2)}<1\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{1-143r_N^{(2)}}{18}I_4
 \preceq\Sigma_N
 \preceq
 \frac{1+143r_N^{(2)}}{18}I_4.}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-frame-window}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a long side and any retained representation, define the complement-wise
survival
\[
 q_{\alpha,\rho}
 =d_\rho^{-1/2}\norm{T_{\alpha,\rho}}_{\rm HS}.
\]
By \Cref{thm:V28-replica-identity},
\(\norm{q_{\alpha,\rho}}_2^2=1-\Lambda_{\alpha,\rho}^{(2)}\), hence every
such \(L^2\) norm is at most \(r_N^{(2)}\).

The conditional normalized trace obeys
\[
 \left|
 \mathbb E[\mathcal O_\alpha\mid\mathscr F_{S_\alpha^c}]
 \right|
 \le\frac1{3}\abs{\Tr T_{\alpha,\mathbf3}}
 \le q_{\alpha,\mathbf3}.
\]
Taking expectations and conditional expectations gives
\begin{equation}
 |W_{\alpha,N}|\le r_N^{(2)},
 \qquad
 \norm{\mathbb E[\mathcal O_{\alpha,N}\mid B_{N,R}]}_2
 \le r_N^{(2)}.
 \label{eq:V28-first-moment-bound}
\end{equation}
Therefore every centered message coordinate has norm at most
\(2r_N^{(2)}\), and summing four coordinate squares gives
\eqref{eq:V28-replica-message-window}.

For the diagonal raw second moments, use the exact identity
\[
 \mathcal O(g)^2
 =\frac1{18}
 +\frac{
  \chi_{\mathbf3}+\chi_{\overline{\mathbf3}}
  +\chi_{\mathbf6}+\chi_{\overline{\mathbf6}}
  +2\chi_{\mathbf8}}
 {36}.
\]
The trace bound
\(\abs{\Tr T_\rho}\le\sqrt{d_\rho}\norm{T_\rho}_{\rm HS}
=d_\rho q_\rho\) and the total nontrivial dimension weight
\[
 3+3+6+6+2\cdot8=34
\]
give
\[
 \left|
 \mathbb E\mathcal O_\alpha^2-\frac1{18}
 \right|
 \le\frac{17}{18}r_N^{(2)}.
\]
After subtracting \(W_\alpha^2\), the diagonal covariance error is at most
\(35r_N^{(2)}/18\).  On a pair-private side,
\(\mathcal O_\gamma\) is fixed and bounded by one while the selected
\(\mathcal O_\alpha\) has conditional mean bounded by
\(q_{\alpha\mid\gamma,\mathbf3}\).  Hence each off-diagonal raw covariance
has absolute value at most
\(r_N^{(2)}+(r_N^{(2)})^2\le2r_N^{(2)}\).  The maximum row sum is
\[
 \frac{35}{18}r+3(2r)=\frac{143}{18}r,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:V28-replica-covariance-window}; the frame window is
its spectral consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Target-native source-relative contraction]
\label{thm:V28-source-contraction}
Let \(\Gamma_N\) be the complete normalized four-arm source metric and
\(M_{N,R}\) its visible shell-message metric.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\kappa_{N,(2)}^2
 :=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \min\left\{1,
  \frac{288(r_N^{(2)})^2}{1-143r_N^{(2)}}
 \right\},&143r_N^{(2)}<1,\\[1.1em]
 1,&143r_N^{(2)}\ge1.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-kappa}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 M_{N,R}\preceq
 \widehat\kappa_{N,(2)}^2\Gamma_N.}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-source-order}
\end{equation}
Consequently every nonzero normalized four-loop contrast, including the
physical Creutz source, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{
  \norm{\mathbb E[a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N\mid B_{N,R}]}_2^2
 }{
  \norm{a^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Y_N}_2^2
 }
 \le\widehat\kappa_{N,(2)}^2.}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-source-ratio}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{r_N^{(2)}\le r_N^{\rm hb},}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-stronger-than-op}
\end{equation}
so every passing V27 actual-side card also passes through the present scalar
route, while the converse need not hold.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the supported branch, combine
\eqref{eq:V28-replica-frame-window} with
\eqref{eq:V28-replica-message-window} exactly as in
\Cref{thm:V27-actual-source-contraction}.  Diagonal congruence by the four
Wilson-loop normalizations transports the same order to \(\Gamma_N\) and
\(M_{N,R}\).  The universal branch is conditional-expectation contractivity.
The last inequality follows pointwise from
\eqref{eq:V28-HS-op-comparison} before taking the panel maxima.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Executable loss intervals and the coherent-side alternative}
\label{sec:V28-compiler}
% =============================================================================

Suppose each expected positive loss has a validated outward interval
\begin{equation}
 \underline\Lambda_p
 \le\Lambda_{N,p}^{(2)}
 \le\overline\Lambda_p,
 \qquad p\in\mathcal P_N^{(2)}.
 \label{eq:V28-loss-intervals}
\end{equation}
The exact theorem domain is \(0\le\Lambda_{N,p}^{(2)}\le1\).

\begin{theorem}[Finite positive replica-loss compiler]
\label{thm:V28-loss-compiler}
After intersecting every valid interval with \([0,1]\), put
\begin{equation}
 \underline\lambda_N
 :=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_N^{(2)}}\underline\Lambda_p,
 \qquad
 \overline r_N
 :=\sqrt{1-\underline\lambda_N}.
 \label{eq:V28-loss-compiler-r}
\end{equation}
Then \(r_N^{(2)}\le\overline r_N\), and the following outcomes are sound.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C28.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item If
      \begin{equation}
       \overline r_N
       <r_{\rm c}
       :=\frac{\sqrt{21601}-143}{576},
       \label{eq:V28-strict-threshold}
      \end{equation}
      every separating-shell four-loop source channel is strictly
      contractive with the outward coefficient obtained by inserting
      \(\overline r_N\) in \eqref{eq:V28-replica-kappa}.
\item If along a cofinal sequence
      \begin{equation}
       \underline\lambda_N\longrightarrow1,
       \label{eq:V28-loss-to-one}
      \end{equation}
      then every normalized four-loop source message vanishes uniformly at
      all separating shells.
\item If for one side and one representation
      \begin{equation}
       \overline\Lambda_p\le1-a
       \qquad(0<a\le1),
       \label{eq:V28-low-loss-certificate}
      \end{equation}
      then that side has normalized Hilbert--Schmidt survival at least \(a\)
      and carries the positive-probability representation corridor of
      \Cref{thm:V28-replica-corridor} below.
\item If none of these strict inequalities is certified, the sufficient
      side-loss card is unresolved.  Failure of a lower loss bound is not a
      transport obstruction and does not replace the V26 direct message
      triple.
\end{enumerate}
An interval disjoint from \([0,1]\), a negative radius, or loss tables not
acquired over the same declared complement is an ill-typed input rather than
a Yang--Mills verdict.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The interval definition gives
\(\lambda_N^{(2)}\ge\underline\lambda_N\), hence
\(r_N^{(2)}\le\overline r_N\).  The first two conclusions are
\Cref{thm:V28-source-contraction}.  The third follows from
\(q_p^2=1-\Lambda_p\).  The remaining statements are the strict one-sided
certificate semantics of the displayed inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Replica-visible representation corridor]
\label{thm:V28-replica-corridor}
Suppose one physical side in representation \(\rho\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda_{C,S,\rho}^{(2)}\le1-a
 \qquad(0<a\le1).
 \label{eq:V28-corridor-loss-assumption}
\end{equation}
Let
\begin{equation}
 q_\rho(\omega)^2
 :=\frac1{d_\rho}\norm{T_\rho(\omega)}_{\rm HS}^2.
 \label{eq:V28-random-HS-survival}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E q_\rho^2\ge a
 \label{eq:V28-HS-stock-lower}
\end{equation}
and the event
\begin{equation}
 E=\{q_\rho^2\ge a/2\}
 \label{eq:V28-HS-corridor-event}
\end{equation}
has probability
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\mathbb P(E)\ge\frac{a}{2-a}.}
 \label{eq:V28-HS-corridor-probability}
\end{equation}
On every configuration in \(E\),
\begin{equation}
 \norm{T_\rho}_{\rm op}^2
 \ge q_\rho^2\ge a/2,
 \label{eq:V28-op-from-HS}
\end{equation}
so the Version~V27 singular-vector construction gives a propagated
representation line whose normalized linkwise dispersions obey
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\sum_{j=1}^{m}d_j\le\frac2a.}
 \label{eq:V28-replica-corridor-action}
\end{equation}
For \(\rho=\mathbf3\), this is the physical colour-line corridor.  For
\(\rho=\mathbf6\) or \(\mathbf8\), it is a higher-representation corridor
and is not relabelled as a defining colour line.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is \eqref{eq:V28-global-replica-identity}.  Since
\(0\le q_\rho^2\le1\), writing \(p=\mathbb P(E)\) gives
\[
 a\le\mathbb E q_\rho^2
 \le\frac a2(1-p)+p,
\]
which rearranges to \eqref{eq:V28-HS-corridor-probability}.  The largest
singular value dominates the root-mean-square singular value.  The remaining
assertion is the proof of \Cref{thm:V27-colour-corridor} with terminal squared
norm at least \(a/2\).
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Local scalar losses cannot be multiplied through unknown routers}
\label{sec:V28-router-no-go}
% =============================================================================

The new replica writer is attached to the complete ordered side holonomy.
It must not be replaced by a product of scalar one-link survivals.

\begin{theorem}[Identical local singular data, different side survival]
\label{cth:V28-local-scalars-no-side}
Let
\begin{equation}
 A=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&0\\0&1/4\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
 \label{eq:V28-two-step-data}
\end{equation}
Both two-step cards use the same local mean contraction \(A\) at each step
and therefore have the same one-step normalized Hilbert--Schmidt survival
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{q_{\rm step}^2=\frac{5}{16}.}
 \label{eq:V28-step-survival}
\end{equation}
With the aligned router the side transfer is \(T_\parallel=A^2\), while with
the crossed router it is \(T_\times=APA\).  Their complete side survivals are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac12\norm{T_\parallel}_{\rm HS}^2=\frac{41}{256},
 \qquad
 \frac12\norm{T_\times}_{\rm HS}^2=\frac{9}{256}.}
 \label{eq:V28-router-two-survivals}
\end{equation}
The naive product of the local scalar survivals is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{(q_{\rm step}^2)^2=\frac{25}{256},}
 \label{eq:V28-naive-local-product}
\end{equation}
which equals neither answer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct multiplication gives
\[
 A^2=\operatorname{diag}(9/16,1/16),
 \qquad
 APA=\frac3{16}P.
\]
Taking half the squared Hilbert--Schmidt norms yields
\eqref{eq:V28-router-two-survivals}.  The one-step calculation gives
\eqref{eq:V28-step-survival}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Why the side replica is the correct scalar compression]
\label{ass:V28-side-not-local-product}
Per-link scalar deficits forget the relative singular frames and the fixed
Wilson routers between links.  The V27 matrix product retains that information
fully.  The V28 relative-holonomy replica is its target-native scalar
compression because it is evaluated only after the complete ordered side
word has been assembled.  It therefore cannot be replaced by a product or
sum of separately averaged local scalar losses.
\end{assessment}

\section{Cofinal alternative and handoff}
\label{sec:V28-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Replica-side cofinal contraction/corridor alternative]
\label{thm:V28-cofinal-alternative}
Let \(N_n\to\infty\) be a cofinal selected-root sequence and let the ten side
replica cylinders of \Cref{cor:V28-panel-size} be fixed before their values
are inspected.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V28.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.6em]
\item If
      \begin{equation}
       \lambda_{N_n}^{(2)}\longrightarrow1,
       \label{eq:V28-cofinal-loss-one}
      \end{equation}
      the complete normalized four-loop source message vanishes at every
      separating shell.
\item If
      \begin{equation}
       \liminf_n\lambda_{N_n}^{(2)}>1-r_{\rm c}^2,
       \label{eq:V28-cofinal-strict-loss}
      \end{equation}
      the source-to-shell channel has a uniform strict contraction.
\item Suppose instead that the raw source frame has a floor
      \(\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{N_n})\ge s_*>0\) and one normalized source
      message retains a fraction \(\delta>0\).  Then for some physical long
      side in the defining representation,
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \Lambda_{N_n,\alpha,\mathbf3}^{(2)}
       \le1-\frac{\delta s_*}{16}}
       \label{eq:V28-message-forces-low-loss}
      \end{equation}
      along a subsequence.  That side carries the positive-probability
      defining colour corridor of \Cref{thm:V28-replica-corridor}.
\item If the positive loss intervals do not decide these alternatives, the
      target-minimal fallback remains the V26 direct message triple
      \(i_B,i_X,D_{B/X}^{\rm dir}\).  The full V27 one-link matrix path is
      reopened only when an explicit corridor line, local dispersion profile,
      or closed-line phase is required.
\item Only after oriented, source-visible adjacent-cutoff message transport
      passes is the V11 Bayes-reverse source loss acquired over a positive
      physical shell width.  Strict radial loss gives contraction; a near-unit
      positive-width channel gives the positive-range retained-source packet.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first two items are \Cref{thm:V28-source-contraction}.  For the third,
repeat the first-moment portion of the proof of
\Cref{thm:V27-colour-corridor}, replacing the operator survival by the sharper
trace bound used in \Cref{thm:V28-replica-loop-bounds}.  Source-message
survival gives one loop coordinate with
\[
 \mathbb E q_{\alpha,\mathbf3}^2
 \ge\frac{\delta s_*}{16}.
\]
Use \(\Lambda=1-\mathbb E q^2\) and
\Cref{thm:V28-replica-corridor}.  The remaining items retain the already
proved target hierarchy.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The replica-side corridor is spatial and source relative]
\label{fire:V28-not-mass}
A low side-replica loss is a statement about conditional spatial colour
transport through one frozen physical rectangle side.  It does not identify
the Osterwalder--Schrader semigroup, select one DLR vacuum, control the full
centre-neutral source complement, or establish a continuum mass.  Those
claims retain their independent YM--A fixed-action, phase, signed-symbol,
reflection, tail, and full-core rows.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Version V29 direction: the full side complement is finer than the physical shell}
\label{sec:V29-direction}
% =============================================================================

Version~V28 replaced the full one-link matrix path by a positive
same-complement relative-holonomy loss.  Its contraction conclusion remains
valid: a small complement-conditioned transfer bounds every coarser shell
message.  Its low-loss branch, however, was still conditioned on the entire
complement of one physical side.  That record fixes a gauge frame and retains
interior environment information which the actual separating shell does not
contain.

The distinction is load bearing.  A closed Wilson loop is a colour singlet,
whereas the complement-conditioned matrix transfer may contain a traceless
colour frame.  Moreover, even its scalar trace may fluctuate across
complements while disappearing after projection to the shell.  Finally, a
complex fundamental character may survive entirely in its imaginary part,
although the frozen Creutz source uses only real normalized traces.

Version~V29 therefore moves upstream to the actual Markov-blanket record and
separates these effects before interpreting a low-loss side.  The corrected
order is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{globally frozen real Wilson source and physical separating shell}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{shell-preserving interior gauge twirl}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{four gauge-invariant shell character losses with mean subtraction}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{source-relative shell contraction or the direct real message card}
 \\
 \Downarrow
 \\
 \text{only then positive-width radial transmission and the cofinal verdict.}
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V29-corrected-order}
\end{equation}

No theorem below changes the complete V28 source-side covariance bound.  It
shows that its low-loss representation corridor is a statement on an
overconditioned gauge frame until the complement-to-shell debit and the
real-character projection have been passed.

\begin{firewall}[A finer conditioning record is not a stronger physical survivor]
\label{fire:V29-finer-not-survivor}
If \(\mathscr B\subseteq\mathscr C\), then
\(\|\mathbb E[X\mid\mathscr C]\|_2\ge
  \|\mathbb E[X\mid\mathscr B]\|_2\).
The extra norm is information supplied by the finer record.  It may be useful
for an upper contraction estimate, but it cannot be exported as survival at
\(\mathscr B\) until the orthogonal innovation from \(\mathscr B\) to
\(\mathscr C\) is removed.  In particular, a complement-conditioned colour
line is not automatically a boundary-shell colour line.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Rooted closed holonomies and shell-preserving gauge twirling}
\label{sec:V29-shell-twirl}
% =============================================================================

Fix one finite Wilson card, one admissible separating link shell with record
\(\mathscr B\), and one source rectangle \(C\).  Choose a lattice vertex
\(o\) whose incident links do not belong to the shell, and a path \(P\) from
\(o\) to a vertex of \(C\).  Define the rooted closed holonomy
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde U_C
 :=U(P)U(C)U(P)^{-1}.
 \label{eq:V29-rooted-holonomy}
\end{equation}
Its character is independent of the path:
\begin{equation}
 \chi_\rho(\widetilde U_C)=\chi_\rho(U(C)).
 \label{eq:V29-rooted-character}
\end{equation}
On the literal \(N=32\) and \(N=64\) cards through shell radius three, the
origin vertex has shell-disjoint star.  The exact verifier checks all eight
finite rows.  On a later card, existence of such an anchor is retained as a
finite geometry-domain check; it is automatic for a nonwrapping shell which
does not meet every vertex star.

\begin{theorem}[Shell conditional holonomy is colour scalar]
\label{thm:V29-shell-centrality}
Let \(\rho\) be a nontrivial irreducible unitary representation of
\(\SU(3)\), with dimension \(d_\rho\), and put
\begin{equation}
 T_{\mathscr B,\rho}
 :=\mathbb E\!
   \left[\rho(\widetilde U_C)\mid\mathscr B\right].
 \label{eq:V29-shell-matrix-message}
\end{equation}
Then, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T_{\mathscr B,\rho}
 =\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}I_{d_\rho},
 \qquad
 \zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}
 =\frac1{d_\rho}
   \mathbb E[\chi_\rho(U(C))\mid\mathscr B].}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-central-form}
\end{equation}
Consequently the shell-conditioned matrix transfer has no preferred colour
line.  All of its singular values are equal to
\(|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For \(g\in\SU(3)\), perform the lattice gauge transformation which equals
\(g\) at the anchor \(o\) and the identity at every other vertex.  Since no
shell link is incident on \(o\), this transformation leaves the complete
shell record fixed.  Product Haar measure and the Wilson action are gauge
invariant, so every regular conditional interior law given \(\mathscr B\)
is invariant under this transformation.  The rooted holonomy transforms by
\[
 \widetilde U_C\longmapsto g\widetilde U_Cg^{-1}.
\]
Hence \(T_{\mathscr B,\rho}\) commutes with \(\rho(g)\) for every \(g\).
Schur's lemma makes it scalar.  Taking its trace gives the displayed scalar.
For the defining representation, the same conclusion follows directly from
the nine-element exact twirl of \Cref{lem:V8-colour-twirl}; the present
argument applies to every irreducible retained in Version~V28.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No shell-level projective colour turn for a closed loop]
\label{cor:V29-no-shell-colour-turn}
On the physical shell record, the Version~V27 closed-line turning quantity is
zero for the conditional closed-loop matrix whenever the latter is nonzero:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (I-vv^*)T_{\mathscr B,\rho}v=0
 \quad\text{for every unit }v.}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-no-turn}
\end{equation}
Thus a projective colour turn seen only after conditioning on a side
complement belongs to the complement-to-shell innovation.  A nontrivial
adjoint colour mode must be supplied by an adjoint source or score packet,
not by promoting the scalar Wilson-loop message.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use \eqref{eq:V29-shell-central-form}.  A scalar operator preserves every
line.  The final statement is the singlet--adjoint distinction already made
in Version~V8.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The gauge-invariant shell character replica}
\label{sec:V29-character-replica}
% =============================================================================

For a retained irreducible \(\rho\), write the normalized character
\begin{equation}
 Z_\rho
 :=\frac1{d_\rho}\chi_\rho(U(C)).
 \label{eq:V29-normalized-character}
\end{equation}
Conditionally on one shell record, draw two independent complete interiors
and denote their character values by \(Z_\rho^{(1)},Z_\rho^{(2)}\).  Unlike a
matrix relative holonomy across independently gauged interiors, each
character is already gauge invariant.

\begin{theorem}[One nonnegative shell-character loss]
\label{thm:V29-shell-character-loss}
The writer
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_{\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm char}
 :=1-\operatorname{Re}\!
   \left(
    \overline{Z_\rho^{(1)}}Z_\rho^{(2)}
   \right)
 \ge0}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-character-writer}
\end{equation}
is gauge invariant under the independent gauge groups of the two interior
replicas.  Its expectation is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm char}
 :=\mathbb E\mathscr L_{\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm char}
 =1-\mathbb E|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2.}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-character-loss}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 1-\Lambda_{\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm char}
 =\frac1{d_\rho}
   \mathbb E\|T_{\mathscr B,\rho}\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-character-matrix}
\end{equation}
The expected loss lies in \([0,1]\), although the samplewise writer may lie
in the larger interval \([0,2]\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The character bound \(|Z_\rho|\le1\) gives samplewise nonnegativity.  Given
\(\mathscr B\), conditional independence yields
\[
 \mathbb E[
  \overline{Z_\rho^{(1)}}Z_\rho^{(2)}
  \mid\mathscr B]
 =\left|
   \mathbb E[Z_\rho\mid\mathscr B]
  \right|^2
 =|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2.
\]
This is real and nonnegative.  Integrating proves
\eqref{eq:V29-shell-character-loss}.  Equation
\eqref{eq:V29-shell-character-matrix} follows from
\eqref{eq:V29-shell-central-form}, since
\(d_\rho^{-1}\|\zeta I\|_{\rm HS}^2=|\zeta|^2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Positive variance implementation]
\label{rem:V29-positive-variance-implementation}
The same shell survival may also be obtained from two nonnegative quantities:
\begin{equation}
 D_\rho:=\mathbb E|Z_\rho|^2,
 \qquad
 A_{\mathscr B,\rho}
 :=\frac12\mathbb E
   |Z_\rho^{(1)}-Z_\rho^{(2)}|^2,
 \label{eq:V29-two-positive-character-reads}
\end{equation}
for which
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 1-\Lambda_{\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm char}
 =D_\rho-A_{\mathscr B,\rho}.}
 \label{eq:V29-character-variance-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
The single writer \eqref{eq:V29-shell-character-writer} is target minimal;
\eqref{eq:V29-two-positive-character-reads} is an optional all-positive
implementation.
\end{remark}

% =============================================================================
\section{Exact overconditioning Pythagoras}
\label{sec:V29-overconditioning}
% =============================================================================

Let \(\mathscr C=\mathscr F_{S^c}\) be the full complement of one selected
side and retain the inclusion
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr B\subseteq\mathscr C.
 \label{eq:V29-record-inclusion}
\end{equation}
Use a rooted path contained in the complement; changing from the original
loop basepoint then conjugates the Version~V28 conditional transfer by a
\(\mathscr C\)-measurable unitary and does not change its Hilbert--Schmidt
survival.  Put
\begin{equation}
 T_{\mathscr C,\rho}
 :=\mathbb E[\rho(\widetilde U_C)\mid\mathscr C],
 \qquad
 a_{\mathscr C,\rho}
 :=\frac1{d_\rho}\Tr T_{\mathscr C,\rho},
 \label{eq:V29-complement-transfer}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 T_{\mathscr C,\rho}^{\circ}
 :=T_{\mathscr C,\rho}-a_{\mathscr C,\rho}I,
 \qquad
 q_{\mathscr C,\rho}^2
 :=\frac1{d_\rho}
   \mathbb E\|T_{\mathscr C,\rho}\|_{\rm HS}^2.
 \label{eq:V29-complement-parts}
\end{equation}
The corresponding Version~V28 expected loss is
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda_{\mathscr C,\rho}^{(2)}=1-q_{\mathscr C,\rho}^2.
 \label{eq:V29-complement-loss}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Scalar-environment and gauge-frame overconditioning split]
\label{thm:V29-overconditioning-Pythagoras}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm sc}
 :=\mathbb E
   |a_{\mathscr C,\rho}-\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2,
 \label{eq:V29-scalar-environment}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm gf}
 :=\frac1{d_\rho}
   \mathbb E
   \|T_{\mathscr C,\rho}^{\circ}\|_{\rm HS}^2.
 \label{eq:V29-gauge-frame}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 q_{\mathscr C,\rho}^2
 =\mathbb E|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2
  +\mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm sc}
  +\mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm gf}.}
 \label{eq:V29-overconditioning-survival}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm char}
 =\Lambda_{\mathscr C,\rho}^{(2)}
  +\mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm sc}
  +\mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\rho}^{\rm gf}.}
 \label{eq:V29-overconditioning-loss}
\end{equation}
Thus the same-complement loss is a lower bound for the physical shell loss.
Its low-loss branch has no shell-survival interpretation until both displayed
overconditioning debits have been controlled.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The tower property gives
\[
 \mathbb E[T_{\mathscr C,\rho}\mid\mathscr B]
 =T_{\mathscr B,\rho}
 =\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}I.
\]
Taking traces gives
\(\mathbb E[a_{\mathscr C,\rho}\mid\mathscr B]
  =\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}\), while subtracting the scalar part gives
\(\mathbb E[T_{\mathscr C,\rho}^{\circ}\mid\mathscr B]=0\).
Scalar and traceless matrices are orthogonal in Hilbert--Schmidt metric, so
\[
 \frac1{d_\rho}\|T_{\mathscr C,\rho}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =|a_{\mathscr C,\rho}|^2
  +\frac1{d_\rho}
   \|T_{\mathscr C,\rho}^{\circ}\|_{\rm HS}^2.
\]
Conditional-expectation Pythagoras applied to
\(a_{\mathscr C,\rho}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E|a_{\mathscr C,\rho}|^2
 =\mathbb E|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2
  +\mathbb E|a_{\mathscr C,\rho}-\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2.
\]
Combining the two identities proves
\eqref{eq:V29-overconditioning-survival}; subtracting from one proves
\eqref{eq:V29-overconditioning-loss}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided validity of the Version V28 side panel]
\label{cor:V29-V28-one-sided}
Every contraction or extinction conclusion obtained from a small
\(q_{\mathscr C,\rho}\) remains valid at the shell, since
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2
 \le q_{\mathscr C,\rho}^2.}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-below-complement}
\end{equation}
Conversely, for any \(a>0\),
\begin{equation}
 q_{\mathscr C,\rho}^2\ge a
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \max\left\{
  \mathbb E|\zeta_{\mathscr B,\rho}|^2,
  \mathfrak E^{\rm sc},
  \mathfrak E^{\rm gf}
 \right\}\ge\frac a3.
 \label{eq:V29-low-loss-three-way}
\end{equation}
A low complement loss therefore yields a shell scalar, a scalar environment
innovation, or a gauge-frame innovation; it does not select among them.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first statement and the three-term pigeonhole alternative are immediate
from \eqref{eq:V29-overconditioning-survival}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Mean subtraction and the four nonduplicating fundamental channels}
\label{sec:V29-four-way}
% =============================================================================

Return to the defining representation and abbreviate
\begin{equation}
 Z:=\frac13\Tr U(C),
 \qquad
 W:=\mathbb EZ.
 \label{eq:V29-fundamental-character}
\end{equation}
The Wilson action and product Haar measure are invariant under entrywise
complex conjugation.  Since \(Z\) is sent to \(\overline Z\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{W\in\mathbb R.}
 \label{eq:V29-real-unconditional-mean}
\end{equation}
Put \(\zeta_{\mathscr B}=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathscr B]\) and define
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm W}
 &:={\mathbb E}
   (\operatorname{Re}\zeta_{\mathscr B}-W)^2,
 \label{eq:V29-real-Wilson-stock}\\
 \mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm odd}
 &:={\mathbb E}
   (\operatorname{Im}\zeta_{\mathscr B})^2.
 \label{eq:V29-imaginary-character-stock}
\end{align}
The first quantity is the message stock of the centred real normalized Wilson
trace.  The second is a charge-conjugation-odd character message absent from
the frozen real Creutz source.

\begin{theorem}[Complete mean-subtracted complement-survival Pythagoras]
\label{thm:V29-four-way-Pythagoras}
For the fundamental side complement and physical shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 q_{\mathscr C,\mathbf3}^2-W^2
 =\mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm W}
  +\mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm odd}
  +\mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\mathbf3}^{\rm sc}
  +\mathfrak E_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B,\mathbf3}^{\rm gf}.}
 \label{eq:V29-four-way-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the shell excess above the deterministic mean is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 1-\Lambda_{\mathscr B,\mathbf3}^{\rm char}-W^2
 =\mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm W}
  +\mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm odd}.}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-excess-split}
\end{equation}
All four rows in \eqref{eq:V29-four-way-Pythagoras} are nonnegative and no
one of them may be charged as another.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:V29-real-unconditional-mean},
\[
 \mathbb E|\zeta_{\mathscr B}|^2-W^2
 =\mathbb E
   (\operatorname{Re}\zeta_{\mathscr B}-W)^2
  +\mathbb E
   (\operatorname{Im}\zeta_{\mathscr B})^2.
\]
Insert this identity into
\eqref{eq:V29-overconditioning-survival}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A nontrivial complement excess returns one literal carrier]
\label{cor:V29-four-way-pigeonhole}
If
\begin{equation}
 q_{\mathscr C,\mathbf3}^2-W^2\ge\eta>0,
 \label{eq:V29-positive-complement-excess}
\end{equation}
then at least one of the four quantities in
\eqref{eq:V29-four-way-Pythagoras} is at least \(\eta/4\).  The possible
failure objects are therefore exactly:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{a real Wilson boundary message},\qquad
 \text{an imaginary character message},\\
 \text{scalar environment memory},\qquad
 \text{traceless gauge-frame coherence}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:V29-four-failure-objects}
\end{equation}
Only the first is already in the frozen real Creutz source.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the sum of four nonnegative terms in
\eqref{eq:V29-four-way-Pythagoras}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Counterexample: zero complement loss can become complete shell loss]
\label{cth:V29-zero-complement-complete-shell}
There are two exact \(\SU(3)\) cards with
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{\mathscr C,\mathbf3}^{(2)}=0,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\mathscr B,\mathbf3}^{\rm char}=1.}
 \label{eq:V29-zero-to-one-loss}
\end{equation}
In the first, the complement reveals a uniformly random centre phase
\(I,\zeta I,\zeta^2I\); all survival is the scalar environment debit.  In
the second, it reveals the conjugacy orbit
\begin{equation}
 S^b\operatorname{diag}(1,\zeta,\zeta^2)S^{-b},
 \qquad b=0,1,2;
 \label{eq:V29-gauge-orbit-example}
\end{equation}
all survival is the traceless gauge-frame debit.  In both cards every
complement-conditioned matrix is unitary, while the shell conditional mean
is zero.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The three centre phases sum to zero.  In the second card the three cyclic
permutations of the diagonal entries also sum to zero and each matrix is
traceless unitary.  Direct substitution in
\eqref{eq:V29-overconditioning-survival} gives respectively
\((\mathfrak E^{\rm sc},\mathfrak E^{\rm gf})=(1,0)\) and \((0,1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Counterexample: perfect shell character survival can be invisible to the real source]
\label{cth:V29-imaginary-only-shell}
Let the shell record select \(\zeta I\) or \(\zeta^2I\) with equal
probability.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{\mathscr B,\mathbf3}^{\rm char}=0,
 \qquad
 W=-\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm W}=0,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak I_{\mathscr B}^{\rm odd}=\frac34.}
 \label{eq:V29-imaginary-only-values}
\end{equation}
Thus even a perfect shell-conditioned complex character does not imply
survival of the centred real Wilson writer.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Both normalized characters have real part \(-1/2\) and imaginary parts
\(\pm\sqrt3/2\).  Their modulus is one.  Substitute in
\eqref{eq:V29-shell-excess-split}.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{The mean-subtracted four-loss shell card}
\label{sec:V29-four-loss-card}
% =============================================================================

For the four physical rectangles \(\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square\), let
\begin{equation}
 Z_\alpha=\frac13\Tr U(C_\alpha),
 \qquad
 W_\alpha=\mathbb EZ_\alpha\in\mathbb R,
 \label{eq:V29-four-characters}
\end{equation}
and let
\(\Lambda_{\alpha,R}^{\rm char}\) be the shell-character loss
\eqref{eq:V29-shell-character-loss}.  Define the complex shell excess
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 s_{\alpha,R}
 :=1-\Lambda_{\alpha,R}^{\rm char}-W_\alpha^2
 =\left\|
   \mathbb E[Z_\alpha-W_\alpha\mid B_{N,R}]
  \right\|_2^2.}
 \label{eq:V29-shell-excess}
\end{equation}
Let \(\mathbf X_N\) be the four centred real normalized Wilson traces,
\(K_{N,R}\) their shell-message covariance, and let
\begin{equation}
 F_N^{\rm bal}=u_N^{\mathsf T}\mathbf X_N,
 \qquad
 \|u_N\|_2=1,
 \qquad
 G_N^{\rm bal}=\|F_N^{\rm bal}\|_2^2
 \label{eq:V29-balanced-stock}
\end{equation}
be the canonically balanced Creutz source of Version~V15.

\begin{theorem}[Four shell losses bound the complete real source message]
\label{thm:V29-four-loss-source-bound}
For every separating shell,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\preceq K_{N,R}
 \preceq
 \left(\sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square}s_{\alpha,R}\right)I_4.}
 \label{eq:V29-message-matrix-bound}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 I_{N,R}^{\rm bal}
 :=\|\mathbb E[F_N^{\rm bal}\mid B_{N,R}]\|_2^2
 \le
 \sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square}s_{\alpha,R}.}
 \label{eq:V29-balanced-message-bound}
\end{equation}
Whenever \(G_N^{\rm bal}>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\rm bal}}{G_N^{\rm bal}}
 \le
 \min\left\{
  1,
  \frac{\sum_\alpha s_{\alpha,R}}{G_N^{\rm bal}}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V29-direct-shell-ratio}
\end{equation}
Since the original and balanced Creutz writers differ by one nonzero scalar,
the same source-relative ratio holds for the original source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let
\[
 m_{\alpha,R}
 =\mathbb E[
   \operatorname{Re}Z_\alpha-W_\alpha
   \mid B_{N,R}].
\]
By \eqref{eq:V29-shell-excess-split},
\(\|m_{\alpha,R}\|_2^2\le s_{\alpha,R}\).  Since \(K_{N,R}\) is the Gram of
the four real messages,
\[
 K_{N,R}\preceq(\Tr K_{N,R})I_4
 \preceq\left(\sum_\alpha s_{\alpha,R}\right)I_4.
\]
Contract with the unit vector \(u_N\) to obtain
\eqref{eq:V29-balanced-message-bound}; divide by the positive total source
stock.  Scalar rescaling cancels in the ratio.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hybrid denominator from the Version V28 source frame]
\label{cor:V29-hybrid-denominator}
If the source-side Version~V28 panel gives
\(143r_N^{(2)}<1\), then
\begin{equation}
 G_N^{\rm bal}
 \ge\frac{1-143r_N^{(2)}}{18},
 \label{eq:V29-source-frame-floor}
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\rm bal}}{G_N^{\rm bal}}
 \le
 \min\left\{
  1,
  \frac{18\sum_\alpha s_{\alpha,R}}
       {1-143r_N^{(2)}}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V29-hybrid-ratio}
\end{equation}
The source-side complement panel and the shell-character panel enter
different rows: the former supplies a total-source metric floor, while the
latter supplies the physical-shell numerator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply the lower frame inequality
\eqref{eq:V28-replica-frame-window} to the unit coefficient vector \(u_N\),
then use \eqref{eq:V29-balanced-message-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Denominator-safe outward compiler]
\label{thm:V29-four-loss-compiler}
Suppose validated intervals satisfy
\begin{equation}
 0\le\underline\Lambda_\alpha
 \le\Lambda_{\alpha,R}^{\rm char}
 \le\overline\Lambda_\alpha\le1,
 \qquad
 0<\underline W_\alpha
 \le W_\alpha\le\overline W_\alpha\le1,
 \label{eq:V29-loss-mean-intervals}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 G_N^{\rm bal}\ge\underline G>0.
 \label{eq:V29-source-stock-floor}
\end{equation}
Put
\begin{equation}
 \overline s_\alpha
 :=\max\left\{
  0,
  1-\underline\Lambda_\alpha-\underline W_\alpha^2
 \right\}.
 \label{eq:V29-excess-upper}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N,R}^{\rm bal}}{G_N^{\rm bal}}
 \le
 \overline\kappa_{N,R}^2
 :=\min\left\{
  1,
  \frac{\sum_\alpha\overline s_\alpha}{\underline G}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:V29-interval-ratio}
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}
 \underline W_\alpha^2
 >1-\underline\Lambda_\alpha
 \label{eq:V29-domain-violation}
\end{equation}
for any label, the submitted intervals are incompatible with conditional
Jensen and the card is an input error.  If \(\underline G=0\), the result is
source-visibility \(\mathsf{STOP}\), not contraction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:V29-shell-excess} and the monotonicity of
\(1-\Lambda-W^2\) in the positive variables give
\(s_\alpha\le\overline s_\alpha\).  Insert these bounds into
\eqref{eq:V29-direct-shell-ratio}.  Conditional Jensen gives
\(W_\alpha^2\le
  \mathbb E|\mathbb E[Z_\alpha\mid\mathscr B]|^2
  =1-\Lambda_\alpha\), proving the domain check.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal shell extinction with no coupling-growth premise]
\label{cor:V29-cofinal-shell-extinction}
Along any selected-root sequence, if
\begin{equation}
 \inf_nG_{N_n}^{\rm bal}>0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak I_\square}
 s_{\alpha,R_n}\longrightarrow0,
 \label{eq:V29-cofinal-assumptions}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{I_{N_n,R_n}^{\square}}
      {G_{N_n}^{\square}}
 \longrightarrow0.}
 \label{eq:V29-cofinal-extinction}
\end{equation}
This conclusion has no restriction on the growth of the selected bare
coupling.  It is conditional only on the displayed physical shell-character
values and source-stock floor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use \eqref{eq:V29-direct-shell-ratio} and scale invariance between the
balanced and original Creutz sources.
\end{proof}

\section{Reclassification of the complement corridor and the terminating branch order}
\label{sec:V29-reclassification}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Corrected interpretation of Versions V27--V28]
\label{thm:V29-corrected-corridor}
The following statements hold simultaneously.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C29.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item Every strict contraction or extinction conclusion proved from a small
      same-complement survival in Versions~V27--V28 remains valid.
\item A low same-complement loss by itself is not a physical boundary-shell
      survivor.  Its excess above the squared loop mean has the exact four-way
      split \eqref{eq:V29-four-way-Pythagoras}.
\item A complement-conditioned projective colour corridor contributes to the
      shell only through its scalar character component.  The traceless
      component belongs to
      \(\mathfrak E^{\rm gf}_{\mathscr C\mid\mathscr B}\) and vanishes under
      the shell-preserving gauge twirl.
\item Even perfect scalar shell-character survival can lie entirely in the
      imaginary channel and carry zero real Wilson-source message.
\item Therefore a positive-range YM--B survivor requires a lower interval for
      the \emph{real centred shell message}, oriented adjacent-cutoff message
      transport, and the independent positive-width radial posterior.  A
      complement corridor alone is an attribution witness, not that survivor.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Item~\textup{(C29.1)} is
\eqref{eq:V29-shell-below-complement}.  Items~\textup{(C29.2)--(C29.3)} are
\Cref{thm:V29-overconditioning-Pythagoras,thm:V29-four-way-Pythagoras} and
\Cref{thm:V29-shell-centrality}.  Item~\textup{(C29.4)} is
\Cref{cth:V29-imaginary-only-shell}.  The final item is the already frozen
order of the cutoff-message and radial cards after removing the three
non-target debits.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What is now genuinely target native]
\label{ass:V29-target-native}
The first shell-level sufficient Read is no longer the ten-cylinder
same-complement panel.  It is the four gauge-invariant character losses
\(\Lambda_{\alpha,R}^{\rm char}\), the four already required rectangle
means, and one lower interval for the balanced source stock.  This card can
prove contraction or extinction.  It cannot prove a real survivor because
\(s_{\alpha,R}\) also contains the imaginary character message.  On an
inconclusive branch, the next object is therefore the V26 direct real message
triple, not the V27 colour-line path.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[The shell twirl is spatial and does not choose a vacuum phase]
\label{fire:V29-not-time-or-phase}
The local gauge twirl acts inside one finite conditional Wilson cylinder.  It
does not establish DLR uniqueness, choose an extremal phase, identify the
Osterwalder--Schrader semigroup, control the centre-neutral vacuum complement,
or prove a continuum mass.  Those remain the fixed-action, phase,
reflection, signed-symbol, tail, and full-core rows of YM--A.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Version V29 shell-native correction]
\label{thm:V29-terminal}
Preserving every theorem and limitation of Versions~V1--V28, Version~V29
additionally proves:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E29.\arabic*)},leftmargin=5.5em]
\item a rooted closed holonomy conditioned on the physical separating shell
      has a colour-scalar matrix mean in every irreducible representation;
\item one gauge-invariant two-interior character loss reconstructs its exact
      normalized shell survival;
\item the complement-conditioned Hilbert--Schmidt survival is the sum of the
      shell survival, scalar environment dispersion, and traceless gauge-frame
      coherence;
\item after subtracting the global loop mean, the fundamental complement
      survival splits into real Wilson message, imaginary character message,
      scalar environment memory, and gauge-frame coherence;
\item zero complement loss may coexist with complete shell loss, and perfect
      shell character survival may coexist with zero real Wilson message;
\item four shell-character losses, four loop means, and one source-stock floor
      give a denominator-safe source-relative contraction or extinction card;
\item the low-loss side corridor is therefore retyped as a complement-level
      attribution witness until its overconditioning and real-character rows
      pass.
\end{enumerate}
No selected-root physical value is inferred.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}

\Cref{thm:V29-shell-centrality,thm:V29-shell-character-loss}.  Items

item is \Cref{thm:V29-corrected-corridor}.
\end{proof}
